Sports.title: Raheem Sterling had the world at his feet - his decline has been steep and tragic
Sports.content:
It was October 15, 2018, and Raheem Sterling had the world at his feet.

Already a Premier League champion and England regular, that night in Seville, Sterling ripped apart world champions Spain in a performance that will live long in the memory.

Sterling scored twice in the space of 22 minutes as England beat Spain 3-2 in the Nations League in what was a first half masterclass and one of their best performances under Gareth Southgate.

But eight years on, without a club, Sterling has now reached a new low after being given a suspended 12-month prison sentence, a two-year driving ban and 100 hours of unpaid work after pleading guilty to dangerous driving and possessing nitrous oxide.

‌



Sterling won trophies galore with Manchester City, was England’s best player in the Euros back in 2021 and people are quick to forget just what a special player he was at his best. Quick, dazzling, skillful, close control and dynamic.

Chelsea will back Xabi Alonso in January - he has no excuses to miss out on the top four READ MORE :

Bruno Fernandes is in complete denial...Man United are in for a relegation scrap READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best football coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

But sadly, Sterling’s career went downhill fast after his £50m move to Chelsea in 2022 - and it has been in decline ever since.

That was the turning point for Sterling who is still only 31, is 16 months younger than England captain Kane and yet now finds himself without a club and in limbo.

‌



His nadir came in May of this year when he was arrested and then later plead guilty to dangerous driving and possessing nitrous oxide.

Now he crops up on social media with posts about the Raheem Sterling Foundation and The Football Cage project which helps kids play like he used to as a kid. His defence cited his charity work, with the judge going as far to say his character had been "positively exemplary".

Sterling clearly enjoys helping under-privileged kids, some of whom have the same sort of tough upbringing like he did in the shadow of Wembley before he moved up to Liverpool as a teenage sensation.

View 4 Images Sterling was England's talisman at the Euros in 2021

‌



Don't miss John Cross' exclusive newsletter every Friday - just for Mirror+ subscribers - CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP

But what gets forgotten about Sterling behind his driven mindset and footballing brain which took him to the top is that he is also a sensitive soul and there’s a touch of shyness.

This is a player who was also always in the spotlight but became a powerful voice on racism in football and a hugely respected figure within the game.

And like many other players, criticism really hurt him and from the highs of successes with City - he was a driving force in their 2019 domestic Treble - then came the lows at Chelsea.

Sterling was 27 when he left City for Chelsea in the summer of 2022. Thomas Tuchel was in charge and the club sold him a dream.

‌



There was actually a contract on the table at City and he could have stayed in his comfort zone by signing new terms. But Pep Guardiola warned him there might be less playing time. He chose Chelsea.

View 4 Images Sterling won trophies galore during his time with City

For the first two years, it was OK. No more. Tuchel went, Sterling went to the 2022 World Cup where the last of his 82 caps came and yet that tournament was overshadowed for him by a break-in at home and he jetted back to be with his family before returning to Qatar.

But by the summer of 2024, Chelsea completely dropped him. They made it clear he was no longer in their plans, he could go and that sudden change was a massive blow for him.

‌



An unhappy year at Arsenal followed where Mikel Arteta probably failed to deliver on game-time and, having been such a key player for England, he was dropped like a stone by Gareth Southgate.

From being a massive star to being forgotten is hard for anyone to imagine. Suddenly Sterling found himself out in the cold and that is when Feyenoord signed him in February 2026. Robin van Persie actually offered him a multi-year contract but Sterling wanted to prove himself.

View 4 Images After joining Chelsea his career went into a state of decline

Sterling has always been quite reluctant to do interviews. A bit nervous about the press. But I did speak to him shortly after his starring role in Seville.

‌



He was talking about ending that goal drought in Spain. “The main thing now is to keep trying to be a goal threat,” he said.

“When I was a bit younger, I wasn’t too interested in scoring goals, I was all about trying to look nice and show people I’ve got a lot of ability. I think I’m probably more driven now to be able to get on the end of things, being in the box a lot more.

“Before, I was going wide, trying to beat a player and now I’m trying to get on the end of stuff, being around for scraps and trying to make goals for myself.

“I’m much more confident when I’m in and around the penalty area now so I feel the goals will come for England as they have been doing for City.”

‌



Back then, ahead of arguably his best game in an England shirt, there were only dreams and targets. And it’s worth remembering that, before the crash, he achieved almost all of them.

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling arrives at court for sentencing after crashing his Lamborghini while inhaling laughing gas
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling arrives at court for sentencing after crashing his Lamborghini while inhaling laughing gas

Former England footballer Raheem Sterling has arrived at court as he faces sentence for driving his Lamborghini dangerously on the motorway before crashing into a metal gate

View 2 Images Raheem Sterling arrives for sentencing at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

Raheem Sterling has arrived at court to be sentenced after driving dangerously on a motorway before crashing his Lamborghini into a metal gate.

‌



‌



The former England star had pleaded guilty at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court to driving dangerously on the M25. He was seen by other drivers inhaling from a balloon while swerving in and out of lanes, the trial previously heard.

‌



The 31-year-old arrived at the Hampshire court wearing a black top and dark trousers. He has been on unconditional bail and subject to an interim driving ban since he admitted offences in September.

‌



Sterling admitted driving dangerously on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before colliding into the gate on the morning of May 28.

View 2 Images Raheem Sterling is due to be sentenced today (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

‌



He also pleaded guilty to possession of six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.

Police body worn footage of the footballer's arrest at 9.15am shows him in the crashed car with two canisters on his lap as the officer tells him: "You can put that down mate."

‌



Witness Christopher Jennings called 999 at 7.49am after he was driving in parallel to Sterling's car on the M25 was "shocked by what he saw," the court heard. Jennings made clear "he sighted the defendant inhaling from the balloon".

Fiona Jennings, another witness on the M3 southbound at around 8.45am, said she "had genuine concerns the driver might kill someone" after seeing Sterling's Lamborghini "swerving in and out of lanes", the court heard.

Sports.title: Every rule Mauricio Pochettino has scrapped and changes he's made so far at Man Utd
Sports.content:
Every rule Mauricio Pochettino has scrapped and changes he's made so far at Man Utd

Mauricio Pochettino has wasted no time in implementing some major rule changes at Manchester United with fitness at the top of his agenda

View 4 Images Mauricio Pochettino has made changes at Manchester United (Image: Getty)

Mauricio Pochettino has wasted no time in implementing five rule changes at Manchester United. But what lies behind the head coach's decision to shake things up?

‌



‌



The club moved swiftly once it became clear that Michael Carrick's position was no longer sustainable. Pochettino was brought in from the USMNT last week and took his place in the dugout for the first time on Sunday against rivals Liverpool.

‌



His reign got off to a nightmare start, however - an early sending-off leaving United to endure a 4-0 hammering - and it's evident there's plenty of graft ahead. As matters stand, United languish in 19th place in the Premier League.

‌



Yet behind closed doors, Pochettino is already taking steps to reshape United, chiefly through a sweeping fitness revolution. Mirror Football examines all the rules brought in by the new head coach less than a week after his arrival.

Man Utd without two players for Sporting Lisbon but Mauricio Pochettino handed one injury boost READ MORE :

The embarrassing Man Utd transfer budget Mauricio Pochettino will have to work miracles with in January READ MORE :

Post-match days off scrapped

Players will no longer be given a day off following matches at United, as they were under Carrick, in an effort to improve the squad's overall conditioning. Pochettino is renowned for his demanding training sessions and his focus on physical preparation.

View 4 Images Players were in on Monday (Image: Getty)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

United languished near the foot of the table in crucial physical statistics under Carrick, including 19th for total distance covered, 17th for high-speed running distance, and 19th for average maximum speed.

‌



The shift was clear on Monday when, following the 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool, the squad turned up at Carrington an hour earlier than normal to complete recovery work and analyse match footage.

Body-fat tests and mandatory pre-match meals

As well as the additional conditioning work, Pochettino will be closely tracking his players' weight — this forms part of his broader shake-up to tighten standards around player fitness, overseen by his son and sports scientist Sebastiano.

‌



Reports indicate that players will face regular body fat assessments so staff can keep tabs on their physical state. On top of that, compulsory pre-match squad meals have been brought in to keep an eye on players' diets.

View 4 Images Pochettino places value on fitness (Image: Getty)

‌



Managerial role

While Pochettino's official job title is head coach, unlike immediate predecessors Ruben Amorim and Carrick, the Argentine views himself more as a manager, getting involved not just in on-pitch matters but also those away from it. This stance likely stems from his achievements at former clubs, where he had input on signings.

He said in his opening press conference: "I was during all my... when I started in Espanyol, [I was] head coach, [I've been] coach, manager. And, in the end, it's not changing [my role]. It's not changing too much.

‌



"Because I think in the way that we work it is indifferent, the title description. Sometimes, I work much better when I was head coach, than when I was coach, than manager. Not necessarily, [it] is if you are manager, you have all the decisions.

View 4 Images The manager explained his role (Image: MUTV)

‌



"Maybe you are a coach and maybe you have more power in the decisions. It depends on the structure, depends on the communication, the relationship with all the areas. I know that being a head coach, I am the guy that is going to decide the squad for Sunday, and I'm going to pick the starting XI, I'm going to make the changes.

"Of course, in the future, I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that happen on the squad. In the end, Manchester United is a football club, no?"

‌

Social media layout

Perhaps the most minor adjustment Pochettino has brought in concerns the club's social media operation. Previously, when United's matchday line-up was shared across social media platforms, players were listed according to their squad numbers rather than their playing positions.

Article continues below

However, during an appearance on MUTV, Pochettino was quizzed on his preference and, backing positional order, responded: "Different way, no?"

This change is driven entirely by his own personal preference. Nevertheless, United obliged ahead of the fixture against Liverpool, publishing the team sheet in positional order. The tweak was largely welcomed by the club's supporters.

Sports.title: I was invited to Man Utd dressing room after humiliating them - they wanted to sign me
Sports.content:
I was invited to Man Utd dressing room after humiliating them - they wanted to sign me

Mauricio Pochettino will be desperate to mark what has become a commemorative fixture with a maiden win as Manchester United head coach.

View 2 Images Sir Alex Ferguson changed the course of football history in 2003. (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Cristiano Ronaldo would not be so obliged to split his allegiances when Manchester United face Sporting in the Champions League, had he not caught Sir Alex Ferguson’s eye all those years ago. On Wednesday evening, the Al-Nassr striker will sit down to watch his childhood club host his breakout club at the Jose Alvalade Stadium.

‌



‌



Mauricio Pochettino will be desperate to taste victory for the first time as the Reds' head coach, having suffered a humiliating defeat in his first game in charge. Liverpool waltzed to a 4-0 win at Anfield on Sunday afternoon, extending United’s stay in the Premier League relegation zone.

‌



The Reds have won just twice since the end of August, both times in the Champions League, coming against Sabah and Roma, so a victory in Lisbon may not be entirely out of reach.

‌



Sporting, however, will certainly fancy their chances, having won each of their last five games across all competitions. The Portuguese giants strolled to a 4-0 win over Serra in the fourth round of the Taca de Portugal.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Having etched himself into the history of either club, Ronaldo will hope they both give a good account on Wednesday night. Back in August 2019, the Sporting and United legend recalled the famous pre-season friendly in which he caught Sir Alex’s eye.

‌



Ronaldo, aged just 18 at the time, earned himself a breakout transfer when he fired his childhood club to a 3-1 win over the Reds in 2003. Speaking to DAZN, the now-41-year-old said: “It was the first game in the new Sporting stadium.

“I remember it perfectly, as if it were today. I was happy. I was going to play against one of the best teams in the world and the game was spectacular.

‌



View 2 Images Cristiano Ronaldo joined Manchester United from Sporting CP in 2003 (Image: Matthew Peters/Manchester United via Getty Images)

“I mentioned to my friends at the Sporting academy that I would play against Manchester and that I was a bit nervous. Nervousness is a part of being a football player in big games.

‌



“I’m always nervous because I always want to play well and do the best I can for my team and nervousness always plays a part. But when you’re nervous and focused, things usually work out better.

“I was motivated, I was happy and I knew that if I played well it would generate even more interest, not only from Manchester [United], but from other clubs as well because I was being watched.

‌



“I felt that many teams came to watch me and of course watch Sporting too. The game went really well for me. I try to take all big challenges as a big test.

“Not anymore, but when I was younger, it was always a big challenge. Obviously, with maturity, you’re able to control your emotions, but I knew it was an important step in my career.

‌



“There were a lot of clubs interested in me at the time. I always had my feet on the ground and I knew that my future would be in football, that I would be a professional footballer and my life would be around football.

“I was taking it step by step. This time it was about playing, enjoying the game, playing against Manchester [United], a great team, doing my best, trying to play an excellent game and obviously things went well.

‌



“The before and after... I didn’t think about it. I was just thinking about the moment and enjoying the game.”

Ronaldo went on to feature 346 times for United, scoring 145 goals and providing 73 assists, helping Sir Alex win three more Premier League titles and the Champions League.

‌



In 2009, he joined Real Madrid for a then-world-record fee of £80m, arriving as the reigning Ballon d’Or winner. In the nine years that followed, Ronaldo established himself as one of the greatest players of all time.

The former Portugal international then enjoyed a brief spell at Juventus before returning to Old Trafford. After falling out with Erik ten Hag, he had his United contract terminated and joined Al-Nassr on a free transfer in December 2022, where he remains to this day.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta left with familiar feeling as sloppy Arsenal let Borussia Dortmund off the hook
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta left with familiar feeling as sloppy Arsenal let Borussia Dortmund off the hook

ARSENAL 1-1 BORUSSIA DORTMUND: Viktor Gyokeres stunning first-half strike gave Mikel Arteta's men the perfect start but they were unable to kill off Borussia Dortmund

View 3 Images Arsenal had to settle for a point after failing to kill off Borussia Dortmund (Image: Catherine Ivill/AMA)

This is becoming an all too familiar and frustrating story for Arsenal and Mikel Arteta.

‌



The Gunners were so dominant here against Borussia Dortmund but did not take their chances and it feels like "1-0 to the Arsenal" is no longer enough. Viktor Gyokeres put them on course with a first-half screamer but, just like at Newcastle on Saturday, Arsenal were sloppy and allowed themselves to get pegged back when they should have put the game to bed.

‌



The Premier League champions are still in the upper reaches of the Champions League table but this definitely felt like two points dropped.

‌



They were fast out of the blocks at the Emirates - and it was Gyokeres who really made his mark. It has been a frustrating season for Gyokeres. Despite his prolific form for Sweden, Gyokeres has made just one start in the Premier League and most of his chances have come in the Champions League.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

And this was an opportunity he was determined not to let go to waste. After Christos Tzolis wasted an early opening chance, Gyokeres took matters into his own hands. Noni Madueke’s pass gave the ball to Gyokeres and you could see the Sweden striker only had one thought on his mind as he strode towards goal.

‌



Gyokeres was almost winding himself up, getting ready to put all his power into his shot. Then with all of his might, Gyokeres put his full force behind his right-footed 25 yard rocket which dipped, swerved and beat Dortmund keeper Gregor Kobel all ends up.

It was an incredible strike which brought the Emirates to life. Not so long ago, Arsenal seemed to play Dortmund every season and these nights are always special because their fans bring noise, atmosphere and their wall of yellow scarves, shirts and banners.

‌



View 3 Images Viktor Gyokeres scored Arsenal's goal - but also spurned a great golden chance

This felt like a proper European night. Arsenal top of the Premier League, Dortmund top of the Bundesliga and a high quality game.

‌



Tzolis went close with a shot beaten away by Kobel and Madueke’s foillow-up was blocked. Then Declan Rice raced through only for Dortmund defender Nico Schlotterbeck to make a heroic last-ditch tackle.

Jobe Bellingham stood out for Dortmund as the Englishman drove forward. Arsenal do not look nearly as secure at the back with back-up keeper Kepa Arrizabalaga rather than injured first choice David Raya. Sure enough, Arrizabalaga left a big gap at his near post and Dortmund’s Joane Gadou tried his luck only for the Arsenal keeper to react in time and push the ball round for a corner.

‌



Arsenal had a major let-off at the start of the second half after Daniel Svensson played a great low ball into the box and Maxi Beier looked certain to score but inexplicably missed his kick. But Arsenal did not heed the warning - and were soon punished. Gadou strode powerfully forward, Beier then stepped inside Gabriel and smashed a low shot into the bottom corner to level it up.

View 3 Images Maximilian Beier scored a deserved equaliser for Borussia Dortmund

‌



This felt like familiar territory for Arteta’s men. They were dominant in the first half, were guilty of missed chances and then allowed another opponent back into the contest.

Then Arsenal had an almighty scare when Julian Ryerson’s shot was saved by Arrizabalaga, Bellingham put in the rebound only for the offside flag to go up.

‌



This was nervy stuff. Arsenal had lost control. Arteta paced the touchline nervously as he made a raft of substitutions to try and win the game but it had become a very even contest.

Gyokeres was guilty of a huge miss as he guided a diving header wide of the target. Dortmund’s Serhou Guirassy deflected the ball onto his own post in a goalmouth scramble. Rice also hit the post and Arsenal’s night ultimately ended in frustration.

Sports.title: Arsenal drop points in wasteful outing to leave Mikel Arteta with major dilemma
Sports.content:
Arsenal were held for the second time in three Champions League games as Borussia Dortmund came from behind to leave the Emirates with a point.

Jobe Bellingham thought he was poised to be the matchwinner for the German side, but his second-half effort was marginally offside, cutting short his celebrations in front of the travelling supporters.

Viktor Gyokeres' sensational strike from range had put Arsenal in front as last year's beaten finalists looked to further establish themselves in the top eight. However they were made to pay for their wasteful nature as Dortmund appeared from half-time as a side reborn.

Maximilian Beier deservedly had them level as he cooly slotted past Kepa Arrizabalaga, who was filling in for the injured David Raya.

‌



Gyokeres' strike opened the scoring on ten minutes with the Swede hammering home from 20 yards out, on an angle. He'd had a sighter just minutes earlier and made the Germans pay with his second effort, which thundered past Gregor Kobel.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Dortmund headed to London with a dire away record against English teams, losing eight of their last nine on the road. The Bundesliga outfit have enjoyed success at the Emirates previously, securing a 2-1 win in 2013 when Robert Lewandowski scored their winner, but that was a footballing lifetime ago.

‌



Arsenal continued to dominate after taking the lead, but without extending that advantage. Piero Hincapie failed to make the most of a good position, choosing to pass when he perhaps should've shot.

The German side came out with renew belief in the second-half and saw a penalty appeal against Gyokeres waved away. Maximilian Beier also failed to connect with a low cross from Daniel Svensson when the goal was at his mercy.

He would atone shortly after, finishing excellent after a stunning run from Joane Gadou, who travelled from right-back into the final third before finding his striker. Bellingham thought he acted quickest from a Kepa save to complete the turnaround, but he was centimetres the wrong side of the last defender.

Gyokeres spurned a golden opportunity to put Arsenal ahead for a second time whilst Declan Rice saw a late effort come off the post.

‌



Striker wars

You know you're engaged in a personal battle when, each time you do something positive, the cameraman pans to your teammate who is, almost certainly, sitting on the bench.

That is the scenario facing Gyokeres and Kai Havertz, with the former trusted by Arteta on Tuesday night. He showed excellent poise to score in Prague a matter of weeks ago and the Champions League continues to be his favoured stage this season, scoring early on against Dortmund.

View 3 Images Viktor Gyokeres scored a sensational opener

His strike was that of a player brimming with confidence, which hasn't always been the case. I mean how can it when every matchday there's a debate over who should lead the Arsenal line, and rarely if ever do the Gunners start with both men in the same XI.

‌



It means one always has to miss out and Havertz had to watch on against a number of his compatriots. General consensus would be that the signing of Havertz has been a success, the jury however is still out on Gyokeres as he enters his second season.

For all the quality he showed with his opener, the overriding feeling may be one of regret given the chance he missed with 15 minutes remaining. In search of a winner the Swede was found by Martin Odegaard, but he put his header wide of the mark. The reaction of his manager told the story.

Ethan still in limbo

German football has proved an excellent breeding ground for young English talent, with a host of players finding the Bundesliga a far more generous and prosperous place to begin their careers.

View 3 Images Ethan Nwaneri is on loan at Borussia Dortmund, but spent the evening glued to the bench on his return to the Emirates

‌



Dortmund have perhaps been the biggest beneficiaries of that. Jude Bellingham is the biggest success story, Jadon Sancho's best days were with them and now Jobe Bellingham is showcasing his quality, which has landed him an England call-up recently.

But for Ethan Nwaneri his loan switch to the German club has been a mixed bag. Just as he found himself warming the bench for Arsenal at the Emirates last season he was back doing the same thing, but this time wearing yellow.

Of the winger's 13 appearances this season only four have been as a starter. It was the increased competition in north London that led him to leaving, especially with his potential so obvious. The concern for the 19-year-old is the amount of time that is passing him by. He made his debut back in 2022, becoming Arsenal's youngest ever player in the process, and come the end of this season he'll be nearing five years since then.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino reveals Bruno Fernandes complaint as angry Man Utd go to Premier League
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino reveals Bruno Fernandes complaint as angry Man Utd go to Premier League

Manchester United officials have strongly criticised ProRef and Howard Webb after the governing body backed the decision to dismiss Leny Yoro

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino is not happy

Mauricio Pochettino has revealed that Bruno Fernandes complained to the referee about Bradley Barcola's role in the opening goal and hit out at VAR's failure to rule out Liverpool's opening goal against Manchester United. The Red Devils were also angered by Howard Webb and ProRef for defending Leny Yoro's red card, despite the club winning an appeal to overturn his ban.

‌



The United boss has alleged that Dominik Szoboszlai's free kick following the sending-off should have been disallowed, with captain Fernandes raising an issue with referee Sam Barrott at the time. Barcola is said to have made contact with the Red Devils' wall before the ball was struck.

"I think we didn't pay attention, but Bruno was aware, that is why he's the captain and because he's intelligent and perceives and feels what is going on on the field," said Pochettino.

"No one talked about that the goal wasn't legal. Should disallow the goal because Barcola was touching our wall. Eze, last season against Palace, when Eze scored, [it was disallowed]. Why didn't they check the VAR, check the goal? That must be disallowed.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"[I] need to defend my players and my club. Where are the three points? We need to think a little more deep... in the way that we use the technology.

"Now we need to move on. I am so proud of the players and the way they managed all these unfair situations that happened on the field, and our focus now is to improve, to be better and to start winning games, and tomorrow we have a great opportunity here."

Pochettino's fury at the officials - and VAR John Brooks in particular - came after Manchester United chiefs launched a scathing behind-the-scenes attack on Howard Webb and ProRef, who stood by the decision to dismiss Yoro despite the club successfully appealing against the red card.

View 2 Images Leny Yoro's red card was overturned (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images)

Yoro was shown a red card just eight minutes into the match at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak as he bore down on goal. Barrott produced an immediate red card, with United maintaining that the exchange with the VAR official provided 'no meaningful challenge' to the ruling.

ProRef chief Webb has since appeared on the Mic'd Up show, declaring the decision was "certainly not wrong" and lauding the referee for his decisiveness. Webb's remarks have infuriated United officials, particularly given their successful appeal against the sending-off.

A source at Old Trafford described ProRef's interpretation as 'totally wrong', a situation made worse by Webb's refusal to acknowledge the mistake, even after an FA disciplinary panel had quashed the decision.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

United claim they have the evidence to demonstrate that, even had Isak maintained his maximum pace, he still would not have reached the ball before Lammens, meaning Yoro was not denying a clear goalscoring opportunity.

A club insider revealed they intend to raise the issue with the Premier League and ProRef, while Pochettino appeared visibly angered by the incident two days later as he addressed the media ahead of United's Champions League fixture with Sporting in Portugal.

"Very disappointed because I think this type of thing can never happen," said the United head coach. "My question always was the same. Okay, we can accept the referee can make a mistake because of the emotional relationship with the game from the referee, but if we have VAR, what were they doing?".

"Because now are we going to repeat the game? Are we going to have the possibility to play with the similar tools, 11 vs 11? No, the problem is when we were there, and in the moment that I think we need the time to review the situation."

Sports.title: Florian Wirtz opens up on dark days during Liverpool struggles - 'I wasn't happy'
Sports.content:
Florian Wirtz opens up on dark days during Liverpool struggles - 'I wasn't happy'

Florian Wirtz arrived at Liverpool last summer with huge expectations but endured a challenging debut campaign, which led to some difficult personal reflections

View 2 Images Florian Wirtz had underwhelmed in his debut season (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Florian Wirtz concedes "there were days where I wasn't happy with myself" with the Liverpool playmaker now finding consistent form at Anfield.

‌



‌



The German endured a challenging debut season having arrived at the Reds for what was then a British record fee. Much was expected from one of the most highly thought of players to emerge from the Bundesliga, but he regularly struggled to impact games.

‌



Wirtz would score just seven times with his assist numbers a far cry from the most creative players in the Premier League. Those struggles continued into this season and the ex-Bayer Leverkusen man was regularly being hauled off in games.

‌



But in more recent weeks the 23-year-old has looked far more composed and confident on the pitch. He produced a number of sensational touches in the win over Manchester United on Sunday, scoring himself and laying on a goal, but he admits there's been times where he knew he wasn't producing.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



He said: "It's mainly a thing that goes in my own head, it's not about the people who talk about me. It's the goals I set myself and the performances I want to show for myself. I always believed in myself, I knew my qualities and I know them now.

"Sometimes there are phases where you have to work even more to get the output, but I'm just enjoying the moment. I'm really happy at the moment that it's going well, and I'm happy with myself, so I want to continue like that.

‌



"Of course, there were days where I wasn't happy with myself. I always try to work on myself and get better every day but I still believe that it makes no sense to put too much pressure on yourself because that doesn't help in the process. I just believed in myself so I wasn't too annoyed, but of course on some days I wasn't too happy about myself, but now I can only speak about the time I'm having now and I really enjoy it."

View 2 Images The Liverpool star has begun producing his best football since his £116m move

‌



Wirtz has continued to enjoy the backing of new manager Andoni Iraola, who has continued to play the German despite the outside noise. The German has also benefited from his international windows with Wirtz now working with former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp.

The Anfield legend has taken charge of his national team and was always tipped to get the most out of Wirtz - which has proved to be the case as he scored twice in a 5-0 demolition of the Netherlands last week.

‌



He just tries to give me some advice to get success over here, because he has shown how it's done," he said on his interactions with Klopp. "It's really good that he knows a lot about this club, a lot of people here and he can give me some good advice.

"It's always small things, more private things. He's just speaking good about the club, the region here, the people. That helps, to hear someone who has experienced it for a long time. It's a good topic to speak about."

Sports.title: The NFL's biggest game of the season is here - it could break records
Sports.content:
It has become an era-defining rivalry in the NFL, and now the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills will meet yet again in the biggest game of the regular season on one of football's most-watched stages.

Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen will face off for the 11th time when they headline the NFL's Thanksgiving schedule on Thursday night, live on Sky Sports from 1.20am in the early hours of Friday.

Once more they are positioned neck and neck at the forefront of the NFL's playoff race, once more they will trade the greatness that has governed football for the best part of a decade.

Together they have forged modern football's answer to Tom Brady vs Peyton Manning. Two generational quarterbacks, dictating one another's story, time and time again, although Allen would prefer if the outcome had been a little more even by now.

Mahomes, the driver of a Chiefs dynasty and so often the AFC's Super Bowl gateway; and Allen, the starved nearly man banging down on the Championship door only to see dominant talent blunted by his Kansas City counterpart.

Last season's Thanksgiving Day match-up between the Chiefs and the Dallas Cowboys became the most-viewed regular-season NFL game in history with an audience of 57.230 million. This might well shatter that.

Allen arrives 5-1 in their regular-season head-to-head record, while Mahomes leads the rivalry 4-0 where it matters most - in the playoffs. Five of their last six match-ups have also been decided by one score, their most recent seeing the Bills win 28-21 in November 2025.

Mahomes and the Chiefs defeated Allen's Bills in the postseason four times from 2020-2024, including two AFC Championship Games and two Divisional Round match-ups. And when the Chiefs missed out on the playoffs for the first time since 2014 last season, Buffalo failed to capitalise.

Football swings in waves by way of a league that craves parity and a system structured for the purpose of emerging contenders, new storylines, fresh obstacles, unpredictable risers and fallers.

But every once in a while sport throws in a notion of consistency, an unwavering narrative that shall assert itself as the spine of an entire chapter in its history; Mahomes and Allen remain that constant at the forefront of league discussion and debate.

Who is the best? Who is No 1? Mahomes boasts the resume with three Super Bowl rings, five Super Bowl appearances, seven straight AFC Championship Game appearances from 2018-2024 and the angle-defiant, off-script absurdity to arm talent challenging every boundary in the game during that period.

But while Allen lacks the same accolades, the frequency at which he has carried his Bills outfit through the air and on the ground in critical moments as football's most obvious decider, equaliser and game-wrecker has tossed him into perennial MVP status; there may be no team who struggles as dearly were they to lose their quarterback than the Bills with Allen.

Chiefs stats leaders Passing: Patrick Mahomes, 226/337, 2,709 yards, 22 TDs, 4 INTs

Rushing: Kenneth Walker III, 159 carries, 872 yards, 7 TDs

Receiving: Travis Kelce, 41 catches, 586 yards, 4 TDs

Tackles: Nick Bolton, 94

Sacks: George Karlaftis, 8

Interceptions: Nohl Williams, 2

Their rivalry is perhaps best epitomised by January 2022's iconic 13-second miracle. With 1.54 remaining Mahomes connected with Tyreek Hill for a 64-yard touchdown, before Allen hit back with a scoring strike to Gabriel Davis that would see Buffalo lead 36-33 with... 13 seconds left.

The game was over. Until it wasn't. Until teams across the NFL were frightened into ever believing they had beaten Mahomes and his Chiefs until the clock hit zero. It was the greatest lesson in the importance of aggression against a team that, at its peak, thrived in the face of shoot-outs.

Mahomes connected on passes to both Hill and Travis Kelce to put the Chiefs in field goal range, where Harrison Butker broke Bills hearts with a 49-yard kick to send the game to overtime. Kansas City would win the toss and then the game as Mahomes returned to Kelce for the deciding touchdown. Allen had been 13 seconds from the AFC Championship Game, but for those pesky Chiefs.

The Bills are 9-1 as they prepare to host the first game between the two teams at Buffalo's new Highmark Stadium, where the Chiefs will arrive 8-2 in their bounce-back season after last January's playoff omission.

Bills stats leaders Passing: Josh Allen, 194/302, 2,527 yards, 14 TDs, 9 INTs

Rushing: James Cook III, 209 carries, 1,060 yards, 10 TDs

Receiving: Khalik Shakir, 38 catches, 539 yards, 1 TD

Tackles: Terrel Bernard, 67

Sacks: Greg Rousseau, 10

Interceptions: Davison Igbinosun/Dorian Williams, 2

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player All of Mahomes' five touchdowns in the Kansas City Chiefs' win over the Atlanta Falcons

Mahomes and the Chiefs have rediscovered the offensive spark absent for the last two or three years, their quarterback feasting on the back of last December's season-ending surgery-requiring knee injury and Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III having ignited Andy Reid's attack since signing in free agency.

The Chiefs offense ranks No 1 in yards per game through 10 weeks, while sitting fourth in passing, fifth in rushing and seventh in scoring following Sunday's 34-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals.

Mahomes has thrown for a sixth-most 2,709 yards for 22 touchdowns to just four interceptions with a third-ranked passer rating of 108.3. With Sunday's performance he has now gone four straight games without throwing a pick, while combining for 1,235 yards and 13 touchdown passes.

He has looked a scary reminder of his former self with tight-window aggression, off-platform invention and out-of-structure magic to enter the Comeback Player of the Year race.

Allen is, meanwhile, riding a six-game winning streak without, in his eyes, playing his best football. He has gone 194 of 302 passing (64.2 per cent) for 2,527 yards and 14 touchdowns to nine interceptions with a passer rating of 93.5, having thrown two picks in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Miami Dolphins.

Allen also leads all quarterbacks with 290 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns on the ground, though he played a full game without attempting to run the ball for the first time in his career at the weekend.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Buffalo Bills' clash with the Kansas City Chiefs in the Divisional playoff

While it will be the two quarterbacks who take centre stage, defining factors lie elsewhere. Particularly on the ground.

Kenneth Walker III has missed the last two games through injury after spearheading the Chiefs with 872 rushing yards and seven touchdowns in eight games. But in his absence fifth-round rookie Emmett Johnson has emerged as a key contributor with 56 touches, 314 yards and three touchdowns over two weeks.

In the opposite backfield James Cook remains instrumental to Joe Brady's Bills attack with 1,060 rushing yards (second in the NFL) for 10 touchdowns from 209 carries. He enters Thursday having rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in an NFL-record nine successive games, and has now surpassed 1,000 yards in four straight campaigns.

Buffalo's prime question marks this season came on defense and whether they had the unit and the personnel to stop football's best teams in the playoffs.

They hired Jim Leonhard as their new defensive coordinator during the offseason and currently rank 11th in total yards allowed and ninth in scoring having not allowed a touchdown in 43 drives since Derrick Henry's rushing score in their win over the Ravens on November 1, albeit having played the Vikings, Jets and Dolphins since then. Still, it can be considered progress for a defense that shipped 28.5 points on average across the first six games.

Steve Spagnuolo's Chiefs defense is, meanwhile, fifth in yards allowed and second in scoring to underline what is currently one of football's most complete teams.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kansas City Chiefs' Nohl Williams lifts Arizona Cardinals' Elijah Higgins into the air in a WWE-style tackle

With that being said, the Chiefs' only win against a team with a winning record through 10 weeks was back in Week One against the now 8-2 Denver Broncos.

The Bills have played just two teams sitting among the 14 available playoff spots in the Detroit Lions and the Minnesota Vikings, while their last four outings have seen them encounter back-up or third-string quarterbacks in Miami's Kyle McCord, the New York Jets' Cade Klubnik, Minnesota's Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer and Baltimore's Joe Fagnano, who replaced Lamar Jackson following his thumb injury on the first play from scrimmage in Buffalo's 36-10 win.

"You can see Mahomes stand with more conviction in the pocket. He's not as skittish in the pocket as he was initially, which is natural when you're coming back from a lower leg injury like he had," said Sky Sports NFL's Jeff Reinebold.

"Greg Rousseau and Ed Oliver are going to have to dominate the line of scrimmage. That's one place on the field that I would say Buffalo's defense has an edge against Kansas City. Rousseau is having a tremendous year as an edge rusher. They're going to have to find answers for him. And then Ed Oliver gives them that inside push that you always want to have against Patrick Mahomes.

"I think that's going to be the key because I don't know if Buffalo's back end is built to cover the Kansas City receivers and primarily I think Kelsey's going to be the biggest factor because Buffalo plays a lot of zone and when you play a lot of zone, Kelsey can have a night against you."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Buffalo Bills against the Los Angeles Rams from Week 5 of the NFL season

Kansas City's wake-up call was in Week Seven when they suffered a 20-3 loss to the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Mahomes and co now enter a defining period of their own campaign with Matthew Stafford and Myles Garrett's Los Angeles Rams, Joe Burrow's Cincinnati Bengals and Brock Purdy's San Francisco 49ers coming up before the end of the year.

Mahomes leads the NFL with 33,267 passing yards since Allen's first full season as starter in 2019, with the Bills quarterback ranked third behind Jared Goff with 2,640. In that same period Mahomes is first with 239 passing touchdowns followed by Allen's 224, while Allen tops all quarterbacks with 92 wins (126 games) to Mahomes' 90 (119 games).

It is perfectly-scheduled and perfectly-poised as a test of who both teams are entering the home stretch towards the playoffs. It could be the best Thanksgiving Day game ever. It might be the most-watched regular-season NFL game in history.

Sports.title: Sterling given suspended jail sentence for dangerous driving
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court in September and admitted possession of six nitrous oxide cannisters for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen.

Former England player Raheem Sterling has been given a suspended 12-month jail sentence for dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after a crash involving a Lamborghini on the motorway.

Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court in September to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before he crashed on May 28. The sentence is suspended for 18 months.

He has also been handed a two-year driving ban and must undertake 100 hours of unpaid community work.

The 31-year-old admitted possession of six nitrous oxide cannisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.

Sterling scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate's side reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the final of Euro 2020. He came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut.

Sterling, who was born in Kingston, Jamaica, moved to Manchester City in 2015 and won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup in 2019. He left for Chelsea in 2022 but after falling out of favour spent the 2024/25 season on loan at Arsenal.

Sterling joined Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of the 2025/26 season. He is currently without a club.

In the 2021 Queen's Birthday Honours, Sterling was made an MBE for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out strongly against racism on and off the pitch for several years.

It came amid controversy over England fans booing players taking the knee at matches as a gesture against intolerance.

Rinderknech denied the allegation on Instagram, while stressing that he has never taken a banned substance and revealing he has asked for the ​matter to be heard by an independent tribunal.

The ITIA said in a statement: "Following media reports and the player's social media post, we can confirm that Arthur Rinderknech has been charged with refusing a test.

Sports.title: Rodgers benched by Steelers for game with Broncos
Sports.content:
Aaron Rodgers has been benched by the Pittsburgh Steelers for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos with Mason Rudolph to start in the four-time NFL MVP's place.

Rodgers, who turns 43 next week, has struggled during the Steelers' back-to-back defeats to the Cincinnati Bengals and the Philadelphia Eagles.

Pittsburgh confirmed in a statement that the veteran quarterback will be "inactive", despite head coach Mike McCarthy saying on Monday that he remained the starter.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Steelers' defeat to the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11

Rodgers is amid his 22nd and final NFL season, having reunited with McCarthy after the two previously won the Super Bowl together at the Green Bay Packers in 2010.

He was key in McCarthy being hired to take over from Mike Tomlin.

Rudolph has started only 19 games in seven seasons with the Steelers and the Tennessee Titans, so this is a big call from Pittsburgh, even considering Rodger's flagging numbers.

Image: Mason Rudolph has started only 19 games in seven seasons with the Steelers and the Tennessee Titans

Rodgers has completed under 61 per cent of pass attempts this season, marking one of his worst campaigns since he became a full-time starter with Green Bay in 2008.

The quarterback has been sacked 31 times, surpassing last year's total of 21 already, and leads the league with 257 yards lost in those sacks.

Image: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy (pictured) and Rodgers won the Super Bowl with the Green Bay Packers in 2010

Earlier this week, McCarthy said of Rodgers when discussing Pittsburgh's successive defeats: "When you talk about the quarterback position, I think there's things offensively we need to do better and that always benefits and leads into quarterback play.

"I just need him to just keep ploughing away. We got a lot of work to do."

Sports.title: Villeneuve: Verstappen showed 'race craft' edge over Mercedes pair in Vegas
Sports.content:
Former Formula 1 world champion Jacques Villeneuve says Max Verstappen's Las Vegas Grand Prix victory showed that Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and George Russell will not be able to beat the Red Bull driver in next year's championship unless they have a superior car.

Verstappen retained the lead from pole position at the start but was challenged by Russell and then later Antonelli for almost the entire 50-lap race amid near constant changes of position throughout the field, but the Red Bull driver expertly saw off their best efforts before both made late errors to drop down the order.

Antonelli has already been crowned 2026 world champion after Mercedes' dominance early in the season helped him build a significant advantage, but Verstappen is putting together an ominous finish to the year, with the four-time world champion having won four of the last six races and claimed nine successive podiums.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix

Sky Sports F1 pundit and 1997 F1 world champion Villeneuve said after the race: "It was exciting. People will say there was a battery involved [in all the passes], but it doesn't matter.

"We saw some race craft. Max was above and the two Mercedes drivers were lacking in that respect.

"And what it is telling us is that unless next year Mercedes have a car that's superior, they can't win because there's something missing."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell tussles with Max Verstappen and Isack Hadajr at the start of the Las Vegas Grand Prix

A combination of factors, most notably the extreme power of the slipstream effect, meant there were more than 350 overtakes during a breathless race at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit.

The lead changed hands 34 times, but every time Verstappen was overtaken, which on almost every occasion was by a Mercedes, the four-time world champion retook his position within a few corners.

Russell locked up and hit a barrier as he tried to pass Antonelli for second in the closing stages, before the Italian suffered a loss of power at the start of the final lap after incorrectly lifting off the throttle as he was preparing to mount a final challenge to Verstappen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen had a choice few words for long-time foe George Russell after winning the Las Vegas Grand Prix

Villeneuve was also impressed by the drives of seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton and last year's title winner Lando Norris, who took advantage of the Mercedes errors to finish second ahead of his McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri.

Hamilton could have also ended up on the podium had it not been for him spinning in a contentious collision with his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc.

"You could see that Lewis had good race craft as well as Lando," Villeneuve added.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch new angles of the collision between Lewis Hamilton and Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc at the Las Vegas Grand Prix

"It was really fun to see. We saw today a race where you don't need pit stops, you don't need tyres that degrade.

"We had a race where drivers could push like qualifying laps all the time and that allowed them to race. It was great fun."

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling avoids jail for £270,000 Lamborghini crash: England star handed suspended prison sentence after telling court he underwent 12-day rehab stint for laughing gas 'problem'
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling avoids jail for £270,000 Lamborghini crash: England star handed suspended prison sentence after telling court he underwent 12-day rehab stint for laughing gas 'problem'

Raheem Sterling has been given a suspended sentence for dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide - avoiding prison time after it was revealed he spent 12 days in rehab.

The 31-year-old England footballer was sentenced to 12 months in jail, suspended for 18 months, will have to complete 100 hours of community service and has been given a two-year driving ban.

Sterling pleaded guilty after crashing his £270,000 Lamborghini in May while driving under the influence of laughing gas.

During the arrest, Sterling told police he had 'a problem' with the drug after subjecting rush hour motorists to a terrifying 90 minutes of dangerous driving back, in which he zig-zagged on the M25 and M3 motorways before swerving onto a slip road and crashing into a metal gate.

Sterling froze as he waited for the judge to enter the courtroom. Meanwhile, he sat with his back against the wall in the glass dock and kept eye contact with her while she read her sentencing remarks.

District Judge Kirsty Allman Sterling consulted UK addiction services on June 15 and the following day went into rehab for 12 days. She added: 'You are 31 years old and a man of previous good character. I accept your character has been positively exemplary.'

Raheem Sterling pictured arriving at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court on Wednesday - he avoided prison time

Raheem Sterling is seen after being pulled over by police earlier this year while under the influence of laughing gas in his Lamborghini - he later spent 12 days in rehab

She then said the nitrous oxide had 'become a maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period in your career', adding that he was a 'role model' before passing the sentence that saw Sterling avoid serving any time in prison.

Sterling avoided jail time after the law was changed in March 2026, with a custodial sentence of one year or less presumed to be suspended - unless there are specific aggravating features - because of the overcrowded prison population.

He was also ordered to pay a victim surcharge of £187 and prosecution costs of £85.

Prior to sentencing, Sterling's lawyer, Jason Bartfeld KC, said Sterling is 'more concerned not by damage to his reputation' but the 'consequences' it has had for his family, particularly his children.

He added: 'Mr Sterling recognised the various unhealthy coping mechanisms that brought him to this position and has sought to address these in the most positive and effective way and with some success.

'The end point of this is that he is absolutely determined that he will never appear before a criminal court again.'

In May, Sterling was arrested by police who claim he tried to hide laughing gas, from them by moving it to the back seat of his black Lamborghini Urus SUV.

Police bodycam footage showed the moment that Sterling was arrested with canisters and a deflated balloon on his lap.

Sterling was pictured getting out of his taxi ahead of his sentencing and the judge gave him a 12-month prison sentence suspended for 18 months

Image issued by the Crown Prosecution Service shows the damage to the Lamborghini Urus being driven by Sterling

An officer could be heard saying 'you can put that down' to the footballer after opening his car door.

He could then be seen taking the items from his lap and putting them behind his seat.

The former Manchester City and Chelsea star, who won the PFA Young Player of the Year award in 2018-19, was then read his rights as he is arrested after being asked to put his arms behind his back.

His arrest, near the Minley interchange on the M3 in Hampshire, happened four weeks after he had returned to the UK following the end of an abortive attempt to revive his football career at Dutch club Feyenoord.

Sterling, from Berkshire, pleaded guilty in September to dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen after a single vehicle collision at 8.45am on May 28. Police found six cannisters of nitrous oxide in his car.

During that hearing, Basingstoke Magistrates' Court heard that Sterling was so impaired by the laughing gas that he was unable to perform basic police station tests like placing his finger on his nose or placing one foot in front of another.

Barrister Simon Jones, prosecuting, said of Sterling: 'He appeared to be quiet, withdrawn and lethargic and actively fidgeting.

'Eye lids drooping consistent with fatigue or drug impairment. He said he was feeling very cold, despite this being in the middle of a heatwave with 33-degree temperatures.'

The 31-year-old was charged with dangerous driving and possession of laughing gas after swerving his car on the M25 and M3

Motorist Fiona Jennings told police she had looked across to witness the driver of the Lamborghini with a balloon in front of his face which was so big she thought it was an air bag.

It was so big that 'she had no idea how the driver would have been able to see the road ahead,' Mr Jones said. Ms Jennings described Sterling's driving as 'absolutely horrendous' and expressed 'genuine concern that the driver may kill someone.'

Evidence previously presented to court suggested Sterling was also inhaling laughing gas while at the wheel of the Lamborghini a full seven hours before his arrest.

A concerned witness called police after seeing the driver of the same car entering a McDonalds car park alarmingly fast at 1.10am the same morning and seeing the driver holding up 'a pink, inflated balloon.'

By 7.45am that morning, another motorist concerned by the Lamborghini erratically changing lanes, saw the driver placing a white balloon to his mouth and inhaling its contents.

For 30 minutes, that motorist watched the vehicle weave from inside to outside lane and back and come close to smashing into the central reservation.

Sterling will now attempt to put the shameful incident behind him and move on with his life and career having avoided prison time.

Sports.title: 'You can't escape from it': Rasmus Hojlund opens up on the suffocating pressure of playing for Man United - and reveals Bruno Fernandes and Diogo Dalot are 'looking forward to change' under Mauricio Pochettino
Sports.content:
'You can't escape from it': Rasmus Hojlund opens up on the suffocating pressure of playing for Man United - and reveals Bruno Fernandes and Diogo Dalot are 'looking forward to change' under Mauricio Pochettino

Rasmus Hojlund has laid bare the suffocating pressure of playing for Manchester United and given his insight into what Mauricio Pochettino’s squad will be suffering while marooned in the Premier League relegation zone.

The Dane was back in town this week after spending two seasons at United, mocking Manchester City fans when scoring the opener of Napoli’s 2-2 draw at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday night.

Hojlund secured a £38million permanent move away from Old Trafford in the summer but remains in touch with plenty of old team-mates and believes the lack of equilibrium at the club has contributed to a steady decline.

‘There are so many people following the club around the world and you can’t really escape from it,’ Hojlund said.

‘It is almost too high when it is good and almost too low when it is bad. It is all about trying to be in that middle. I had both the highs and the lows there.

‘The pressure is part of the club, it comes with playing for United. There has been a lot of change but hopefully they will get it right with Mauricio.’

Rasmus Hojlund mocked Man City fans after scoring for Napoli at the Etihad on Tuesday night

A United supporter, Hojlund laughed off the idea that the club is in a relegation scrap despite their worst start to a season since 1972. And the 23-year-old revealed that the players were ready for ‘change’ following the sacking of Michael Carrick.

‘I spoke with Bruno [Fernandes] and Diogo [Dalot] during the international break and they were all obviously devastated that Michael was going but also looking forward to some change,’ Hojlund added.

‘I am still speaking with Patrick [Dorgu] and I just wish the guys all the best. I am sure they will turn it around this season. They have got a lot of quality. They have got a great squad, good leaders, good professionals.

‘It is a temporary picture, I think they will get back to the top. The Premier League is like this. I read the other day that Bournemouth was in the relegation zone after a couple of games, now they have won the last five games and are in the top half of the table.’
