Sports.title: 'Class act' Jude Bellingham praised for standing up for female journalist in chaotic post-match press huddle after he scored 'the best goal of my life'
Sports.content:
'Class act' Jude Bellingham praised for standing up for female journalist in chaotic post-match press huddle after he scored 'the best goal of my life'

Jude Bellingham has earned praise after the Real Madrid star insisted a female reporter was able to finish asking her questions in the mixed zone after being interrupted.

Bellingham spoke to media post-match after scoring the 'best goal of my life' in Real Madrid's 5-1 victory over PSV in the Champions League on Tuesday.

The England star had collected a loose ball from around 25 yards outside the box, initially controlling it with his left foot, before flicking it up with his right foot and volleying it with the outside of that boot into the far corner of the PSV goal.

Bellingham's stunning strike meant he was unsurprisingly in-demand post-match, with reporters eager to get his assessment of his goal.

BBC reporter Elizabeth Conway had asked Bellingham in the mixed zone what had gone through his mind when he scored with his sensational effort.

'Yeah, I was a bit surprised honestly,' Bellingham said. 'I knew I could control the ball and get it into my grasp, but normally from there I am looking to see who's on as an option to play through.

Jude Bellingham has earned praise after the Real Madrid star insisted a female reporter was able to finish asking her questions in the mixed zone

BBC reporter Elizabeth Conway had been interrupted by a male reporter when asking her second question, leading to Bellingham's intervention. Source: instagram/@elizabeth.conway_

Jude Bellingham with his second assist of the night 🤝 pic.twitter.com/IIkEKC6SNs — Match of the Day (@BBCMOTD) November 25, 2026

Bellingham (right) had been in-demand after scoring with a stunning volley to inspire Real Madrid to beat PSV Eindhoven

'It popped up nicely and I thought, you know, I am just going to hit it.

'It was a nice goal and important for the team being the second goal and gave us control.'

Conway looked to follow-up with a second question but was interrupted by a male reporter, leading to Bellingham intervening.

'Sorry, she's got one more,' Bellingham said, while pointing to Conway to encourage her to continue her question.

When asked by Conway whether he feels like he is in the form of his life for club and country, Bellingham added: 'My mentality is based more around just focusing on the next game, I think you are only as good as your next one. Your last one doesn't really matter.

'Even this one that has just gone past, it is all well and good and speaking to you guys is fun but my focus has to change now to preparing for the next game.'

Conway later shared the exchange on social media, writing: 'Just Jude waiting for me to finish my questions,' adding a handshake emoji while fans were quick to praise Bellingham for his 'classy' moment.

Speaking post-match, Bellingham was clear where he ranked his goal, declaring: 'I think this was the best goal of my life.'

Bellingham came off the bench to put Real ahead with this beautiful right-footed volley

PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar could only watch on as the ball flew past him and go into the net

Bellingham is in advanced contract talks with Real Madrid over signing an extension until 2031

His brother Jobe, who played in Borussia Dortmund's 1-1 draw with Arsenal on the same night, later joked that Jude's shot had 'come off his shin' before acknowledging it was a 'great goal'.

Bellingham's performance, he also set up Vinicius Jr for the fifth goal, was acknowledged by Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho and captain Fede Valverde, who scored their equaliser, post-match too.

'Obviously Jude is a different type of player and he gave us what we didn't have in the first half,' Mourinho said. 'He changed the game, scored an incredible goal.'

Valverde concurred declaring: 'He did well. We were struggling to keep the ball behind their midfielders and when Jude came in he gave us that tranquillity to control possession.'

The strike comes a day after Daily Mail Sport reported that the 23-year-old is in advanced talks over a new Real Madrid contract that will make him one of the best-paid players in Europe.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Rafa Nadal and his son’s reaction to Jude Bellingham’s ridiculous goal sums up all of us 🤯😆



The tennis legend and member of the Real Madrid board was at the Bernabéu to soak in their win.



↳ UEFA Champions League. Live & Exclusive on Stan Sport.#StanSportAU #UCL pic.twitter.com/DpIzIUoXRy — Stan Sport Football (@StanSportFC) November 24, 2026

Rafael Nadal was seen celebrating Bellingham's stunning goal with his young son from the Real Madrid director's box

Talks were initiated in September over an extension until 2031 and have been progressing well since with sources at Madrid confident they are close to reaching a conclusion.

Bellingham is expected to be handed improved terms to put him on par with team-mate Vinicius Jr, who agreed a new deal last summer reputedly on around £500,000 a week after tax.

Footage shared on social media also showed tennis legend Rafael Nadal and his young son exuberantly celebrating Bellingham's stunning goal against PSV.

Nadal last week was officially elected to Real Madrid's board of directors at the club's Extraordinary General Assembly.

Sports.title: THE BREAKDOWN: How Florian Wirtz suddenly became the most powerful creative force in the Premier League - from Andoni Iraola's perfect tactics to Liverpool's Bradley Barcola effect
Sports.content:
THE BREAKDOWN: How Florian Wirtz suddenly became the most powerful creative force in the Premier League - from Andoni Iraola's perfect tactics to Liverpool's Bradley Barcola effect

After Florian Wirtz trudged off the field just over an hour into Liverpool’s defeat by Manchester City in October, sacrificed following Ryan Gravenberch’s red card, Jamie Carragher had once again seen enough of the £116million man.

‘I think he needs to come out of the team,’ said Carragher post-match. ‘I said that last time out and I'm going to say it again.’

Fast forward six weeks, and Wirtz was running the show for Liverpool as they put four past Manchester United in poor Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge, topping a stellar performance off with a goal and an assist. Carragher hailed the German’s stunning first-half volley as ‘a goal Dennis Bergkamp would have scored’.

How things change. This was a performance, even against an abysmal 10-man United, that showed Wirtz was ready, at last, to seize the big occasions.

Because, for so long, he wasn’t ready. Carragher was not alone in his earlier assessment, one shared by countless frustrated Liverpool fans. There was a feeling that this slight, wispy technician had the tools to flourish in the slower-paced Bundesliga, or even for Liverpool in the Champions League, but would, perhaps, remain unable to shine amid the rough and tumble of the Premier League.

Wirtz managed five goals and four assists in the Premier League last season and added only one assist this term before that City game. Since then, he’s come to life. Four assists and a couple of goals in the league with another one of each in the Champions League, a tally he will hope to add to on Wednesday evening against Club Bruges.

Florian Wirtz has suddenly sprung to life as a Liverpool player and is making his critics eat their words

Wirtz scores a majestic flick against Manchester United on Sunday

Something has clicked at last.

Since that City defeat, Wirtz is getting into dangerous positions more often. He is having more touches in the opposition box, more shots in the opposition box, playing more passes into the opposition box and creating more than twice as many chances from open play.

Wirtz boasts a league-high 29 of those this season, and 20 of the chances have come since that City game.

The last player to create more than the 10 open-play chances Wirtz managed against United was David Silva in 2015. Wirtz created nine against Brentford, too, in the first league match after the City defeat, meaning he’s the only Premier League player on record (since 2003-04) to create nine or more chances from open play in multiple games in the same season. Wirtz did it twice in five weeks.

HOW BIG IS THE KLOPP FACTOR?

Let’s nip this one in the bud early. It is clear, of course, that Jurgen Klopp, the legendary former Liverpool manager now Germany head coach, has got a tune out of Wirtz in recent months. The pair, according to those who follow the national team, are very close.

‘Wirtz is a once-in-a-century talent,’ was Klopp’s assessment last year, while he later remarked that he was ‘shocked’ by how good Wirtz was in their first training session together.

The 23-year-old has shown it in matches, too, with four goals and an assist in his last four games for Germany, including a brace last week against the Netherlands.

This has fed a narrative of how Klopp has been the one to unlock Wirtz’s powers. Klopp deserves credit, naturally, but he is also helped by having the freedom to give Wirtz what he needs: space.

‘What do I need to be at my best? Ideally, a lot of space in every game so I can do what I want!’ said Wirtz after scoring one and setting up the other in Germany’s 2-0 win over Serbia in October.

He was half-joking, laughing as he said it, but he’s right. Technical creators like Wirtz thrive on space. He’s been able to have more of that in international football, with Klopp even playing him as a false nine to give him all the creative freedom he needs. He leads the press but the midfielders behind him do the bulk of the dirty work to allow Wirtz, the star, to shine.

Wirtz’s performances with his country have helped grow his confidence, but it would be deeply unfair on Iraola to suggest Klopp’s blueprint is the one now being copied.

WIRTZ HAS ALWAYS BEEN IRAOLA’S MAN

Even if Liverpool and Germany play a similar style, it is much, much harder to give players freedom in the Premier League.

But if anyone was going to find a way to do it for Wirtz, it was Iraola.

Arne Slot could never work it out. By the end of his tenure, he’d played Wirtz as an attacking midfielder, stuck him on both flanks and thrust him up front. It was a conundrum he just couldn’t solve.

Iraola's Bournemouth side were one of the hardest-working, highest-pressing teams in the division but his system was still able to allow the likes of Justin Kluivert or Junior Kroupi to create and drift into pockets of space to set the attacking tempo.

For Iraola, it was always going to be Wirtz. The German has started every league game, all of them in the No 10 position.

He’s always led the way off the ball – only three players have won possession more often in the final third this season – but Iraola has been finding different ways to get the best out of him with the ball, too. Against Brentford, he shifted Rio Ngumoha inside almost to play as a second No 10 beside Wirtz, which helped create space for him to set up Liverpool's equaliser.

Having Alexis Mac Allister behind him allows Wirtz to concentrate on being the creative heartbeat, while even Dominik Szoboszlai has played noticeably deeper since returning from injury.

Andoni Iraola has started Wirtz in every league game, all of them in the No 10 position

ISAK PARTNERSHIP STARTING TO BLOSSOM

Szoboszlai isn't the only one. Another aspect of Germany's game that has helped Wirtz is lining up alongside strikers who like to drop deep in Kai Havertz and Nick Woltemade, leaving space for Wirtz to attack.

In recent weeks, especially against United, Liverpool striker Alexander Isak has been doing the same. It was Isak doing exactly that which led to Wirtz’s goal.

Isak (below, in possession) drops in, plays the ball out wide to Ngumoha and Wirtz sprints into the box to get on to the end of the cross.

Alexander Isak dropped into midfield and sprayed the ball wide to Rio Ngumoha before Wirtz's goal against United

Isak missed much of last season through injury but his all-round play is much better attuned to Wirtz's game than those who played alongside him for most of 2025-26, including Hugo Ekitike.

GETTING RUNNERS AROUND HIM

One of the most devastating aspects of Iraola’s Bournemouth was how quickly players flooded forward when they attacked.

His Liverpool side is starting to do the same which, in turn, helps get the best out of Wirtz.

Last season under Slot, the likes of Cody Gakpo and Mo Salah would often tuck in instead of bombing forward out wide and Milos Kerkez, one of the most attacking full backs in the division under Iraola at Bournemouth, rarely did the same under Slot.

Now, Liverpool’s wingers are flying. This season under Iraola, Liverpool are averaging more ‘fast breaks’, how Opta define counter attacks, and shots from them than in any campaign under Slot or even the ‘heavy metal’ Klopp.

Wirtz has attempted seven through balls this season, one of the highest tallies in the division. Since the City game in particular, he has tried to play passes with purpose into the box.

Wirtz was creating chances in the first six games of this season but only a few of them were penetrating passes into the box

The German's chances created in the last five games, since the City defeat, show how many balls he is playing into dangerous areas

The rapid Bradley Barcola starting to find his feet since his £123m move has been a huge help to Wirtz.

Of Wirtz’s 20 open-play chances created since the City game, a quarter of them have been for Barcola.

Having those runners out wide like Barcola and Ngumoha is so helpful for the German. As he drives forward with the ball against United (below), he has three runners ahead of him with even Szoboszlai bursting forward. Wirtz has so many options and eventually slips in Isak for a great chance.

Liverpool had wide runners driving forward against United, helping Wirtz create chances and split their defence

You can see from the average position map from the game (below), just how attacking Liverpool’s wingers – and Kerkez – were, albeit, granted, against 10 men for most of the contest.

The average position map of Liverpool's players against United shows how high up the pitch they played

Wirtz has had a run like this before, around this time last year. During December and January, he racked up four league goals and three assists – having not managed a single one until then – only to notch one of each for the rest of the Premier League campaign.

You get the sense, though, with his confidence growing under managers for both club and country who want to play his way, that he might just keep shining this time.

Sports.title: Beauden Barrett on the verge of joining Bristol Bears: NIK SIMON reveals full details of biggest signing in PREM history - and what sensational coup would mean for English rugby
Sports.content:
Bristol Bears are on the verge of signing All Blacks superstar Beauden Barrett. The double World Player of the Year has been offered a two-year contract that would represent a sensational coup for the English club game. Daily Mail Sport understands Barrett has been offered a deal close to £1million a year, which would make him one of the highest-paid players in the league, coming into effect for the start of next season. Bristol would make Barrett their marquee signing but it is understood the Kiwi, who plays fly-half or at full back, is also weighing up an offer from a club in France’s Top 14. Barrett is currently in London for the Nations Championship and it is understood his representatives have spoken at length with Bristol, who are confident of completing the deal. Beauden Barrett is in advanced talks over signing a two-year deal with PREM Rugby side Bristol Bears Barrett currently plays for the Blues in Super Rugby and has also had two spells in Japan, with Suntory Sungoliath and Toyota Verblitz He scored his 51st Test try at Twickenham last Saturday on his 150th cap for the All Blacks, in a disappointing defeat by England

Your browser does not support iframes.

As revealed by Daily Mail Sport last month, the 35-year-old’s services were also offered to Newcastle Red Bulls. Moving overseas would end Barrett’s hopes of playing for the All Blacks but the 150-cap icon has played a reduced role under new coach Dave Rennie. He is unlikely to represent his country beyond next year’s World Cup, which makes it perfect timing for a move to Europe. Despite being in the advanced stages of his career, Barrett would be one of the most exciting players ever to move to England’s domestic league. It is understood Beauden's brother Scott is also exploring a move to Europe, but it would be near impossible for any English club to take both Barretts on within the salary cap. All Blacks forwards Wallace Sititi and Luke Jacobson have already agreed moves to France as players sort out their long-term futures. ANALYSIS BY NIK SIMON Beauden Barrett moving to English rugby would be the equivalent of Lionel Messi joining the Premier League. The All Blacks playmaker is in the twilight of his career but his try against England on Saturday reminded the world of his box-office status. After years of financial decay – watching the likes of Worcester, Wasps and London Irish go bankrupt – the arrival of Barrett would represent a glorious renaissance for the PREM. With Dyson and Red Bull pumping millions into the game, Barrett's arrival would be one of the biggest statements in English rugby history. With the financial backing of billionaire Steve Lansdown, Bristol have a proud history of box-office recruitment. They recently recruited American superstar Ilona Maher to their women’s team and, in recent years, the men’s backline has been studded with stars such as Charles Piutau and Semi Radradra. Pat Lam is the coach who pushed hardest to bring back Louis Rees-Zammit from the NFL and now he is leading the charge for one of rugby’s greatest-ever players. Barrett’s highlights reel is unmatched over the past decade. He has won two World Cups and is one of the modern-day icons of the All Blacks. Let’s hope he takes up Bristol's offer, because it would be priceless for the league’s global footprint.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland sparks fear among fans after concerning TV interview as he admits he is 'questioning everything' after Man City's draw with Napoli
Sports.content:
Manchester City fans have expressed concern over Erling Haaland's despondent interview following their Champions League draw with Napoli, with the star admitting he is 'questioning everything' amid their slump in form.

Enzo Maresca's side rescued a late draw at the Etihad on Tuesday night, with Rayan Cherki equalising in the 86th minute to secure a 2-2 draw with Napoli.

The result, however, continued an underwhelming run of form with Man City having won just twice in their last seven matches – one of which was achieved in a penalty shoot-out against Brighton in the Carabao Cup.

Man City have suffered defeats to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest in the Premier League in the run, as well as drawing with Fulham on the weekend.

Haaland, who captained Man City against Napoli, admitted post-match to TNT Sports that their underwhelming form has left the squad questioning themselves.

'We were not able to control and attack the game in the way we want,' Haaland said. 'Football is easy and difficult. When you win it's easy and you know what to do. When you don't you start questioning everything.

Erling Haaland cut a despondent figure as he admitted to 'questioning everything' after Man City's draw with Napoli continued their underwhelming form

🗣️ "I have no idea what we were missing. You could feel it in the last few games that there's something that's not clicking fully."@Erling reflects on @ManCity's 2-2 draw with Napoli.



🎤 @AndyKerrtv #UCL | #ManCity pic.twitter.com/Cx2Hzieom3 — beIN SPORTS (@beINSPORTS_EN) November 24, 2026

'The perfect thing would be to not think but it's not so easy.

'We have so much quality so it's about getting the quality out in every player. We have to regroup, stay positive and bring energy on the pitch and try to do our best.'

Haaland admitted in another interview with Bein Sports that the run of form 'hurts', with the star having offered a resigned laugh when asked whether the draw against Napoli should be considered a 'good point'.

The 26-year-old was seen looking down throughout the minute and a half interview, while he also rubbed his face with his hand as he looked to find answers for Man City's recent struggles.

'How the game was we managed to come back two times, but we demand more,' Haaland said.

'We have to do better and find some ways to control the game more and perform in a better way.

'I have no idea what we were missing. You could feel it in the last few games that it is not clicking fully and we have to find out, stay positive and get the best out of every single day.

'With and without the armband I feel huge responsibility because all I want to do is perform for this club and win games for Man City and right now we are not doing that. It hurts.'

Fans quickly noted Haaland's downbeat responses to questions and despondent body language during the interview.

Man City fans have expressed concerns over Haaland's downbeat responses and body language in the interview

Fans claimed they have never seen Haaland 'looking this flat' and suggested the star 'looks distraught' amid their underwhelming run

'I've never seen Haaland looking this flat. Not even close to it,' one commented.

'At least he’s being honest with himself. Looks distraught,' a second said, with a third writing 'Extremely concerning.'

'Never seen Erling Haaland look like this before,' another added, while a Man City fan wrote 'You can really tell how confused Haaland is from his expression. They don’t have confidence in their own football.'

One went as far as claiming 'Haaland looks like he’s done with Manchester City…' while sharing footage of his reaction to one of Napoli's goals on the night.

Other fans questioned whether Haaland and his Man City team-mates' recent slump may be related to concerns over the potential punishment the club could face for breaching financial rules.

Man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September. The club have since appealed.

An independent commission ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period with ‘sham’ deals.

Man City were found to have artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

Man City have continued to insist they had 'irrefutable evidence' proving their innocence, but if the club loses its appeal, the Premier League have a range of sanctions at their disposal – including relegation or expulsion.

Man City face Arsenal in a crucial match on Sunday as they look to make inroads in the Gunners six point lead at the top of the Premier League

Haaland had pushed back against suggestions the case had affected their form during the international break, while stressing he was committed long-term to the club.

The forward's first answer to Norwegian broadcaster TV2 had spanned two minutes and 14 seconds, as he reeled off the teams he had represented from 2009 to 2018, the years covered by the charges after he was asked about the club's situation.

'In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list. 2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team,' Haaland said.

'Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

'So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle…

'It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure.'

He continued: 'It's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it.

'I assume the answers will come… I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

'To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.

The Man City star, who signed a nine-and-a-half-year contract in late 2024, told Norwegian television earlier this month that his focus was on helping the team to turn their form around.

The draw against Napoli leaves Man City lying sixth in the Champions League table - which would be enough to see Maresca's side to qualify for the last-16.

Man City face a crucial clash on the weekend when they face reigning champions Arsenal in the Premier League, as they look to halve the six-point gap to the leaders at the top of the table.

Sports.title: Usman Khawaja says he felt 'attacked' by Pat Cummins over explosive Sandpapergate fallout after 'trying to find middle ground' with skipper
Sports.content:
Usman Khawaja has revealed he tried to ‘find a middle ground’ with Pat Cummins in a bid to ‘squash’ the sandpaper controversy – only to be taken aback when Cummins launched a personal attack on him during his 68-minute press conference in Sydney.

With the furore showing little sign of dying down, Khawaja – speaking for the first time since Fox Sports stopped using him and David Warner as pundits during Australia’s T20 series against England – said he texted Cummins a couple of days before Sydney.

Khawaja told The Grade Cricketer podcast: ‘I was hoping he’d be able to find a middle ground that brought everyone in together in this, rather than putting the walls up and creating a bigger division.

‘This is what I was trying to say in my text: “If we could meet in the middle, we could really squash this. You don’t have to concede everything. Just meet in the middle and this can be all over.”

‘And I think people would have respected him for that. This is my issue: Pat was 24 at the time. This wasn’t a Patrick Cummins issue. This was the CA [Cricket Australia] win at all costs. Anybody in the team could have stood up and said: “Let’s stop doing this.” No one in the team did.’

Instead, Cummins used his Sydney appearance to call Khawaja’s claim that everyone knew about the sandpaper plot ‘complete and utter nonsense’, and doubled down on the statement he and Australia’s three others frontline bowlers from the 2018 tour of South Africa released five years ago, in which they denied all knowledge of it.

Usman Khawaja (above) claimed he sent Cricket Australia CEO Todd Greenberg a proposed statement last weekend following his claims about the ball tampering saga

Khawaja (right) said he felt attacked by Pat Cummins (left) during a press conference where he labelled several of Khawaja's accusations 'complete and utter nonsense'

And Khawaja expressed surprise at the personal nature of Cummins’s onslaught, which included the accusation that he had been ‘casual with lives and reputations’ in his explosive autobiography, Sabr.

‘I mentioned Pat two or three times in my book, and they were all singing his praises,’ said Khawaja. ‘I’ve always loved him as a person and a leader. I was never expecting him to attack me personally like he did. He kept going and kept going. I’ve never seen that side of Pat before, and that disappointed me.’

Khawaja also said he had been in touch with CA chief executive Todd Greenberg to suggest a form of words that might help share the blame and bring the matter to a close.

It reads: ‘We accept as a group we were ball tampering by artificially altering the condition of the ball in South Africa in 2018. Whether it was sandpaper or any other means is irrelevant. We knew what we were doing and we take full responsibility as a team and squad for our actions, something we should have done eight years ago.

‘Furthermore, we would like to acknowledge that Steven [Smith], Cameron [Bancroft] and David [Warner] paid an enormous price for the sake of the team, for which we are sorry and eternally grateful.’

Khawaja, who is waiting to hear back from Greenberg, continued to insist that what he wrote in his book is ‘the truth’. He added: ‘I’m not going to hide from it. I can sleep very easily at night. I have told the truth. Cameron Bancroft has told the truth. Chadd Sayers has come out and told the truth.

‘The bowlers then went and put the statement out in 2021, and none of us even knew about it. It just happened. They just did it. It kind of left everyone else with our hands in our pockets. It created this separation. They separated themselves from the rest of the team at that point.

Cummins' (right) gave a 68-minute press conference denying Khawaja's (left) ball-tampering claims

‘I talked to Bancroft about this. I was in touch with him all the way from 2018. He said to me: “That was the loneliest I’ve ever felt in my life.”’

Khawaja said the Australian team, under pressure to get results after losing five Tests in a row in 2016, had been tampering with the ball ‘consistently for a long period of time’.

He added: ‘We were winning games as a team through our tactics with the ball. For me, over such a long period of time, we all knew we were trying to reverse swing the ball and we all know how to reverse swing the ball.

‘That’s the context. You can make up your mind on the rest.’

Sports.title: BBC move Sport Personality of the Year 2026: Salford awards ceremony changed back to a Sunday but will be at 5.45pm and reduced to 90 minutes
Sports.content:
BBC's flagship Sports Personality of the Year awards will have to settle for a reduced spot in the broadcaster's schedule this December, with the annual show swapped out of a primetime slot. The long-running programme is set to air on Sunday, December 13, but will kick off earlier than usual at 5.45pm – and in a format trimmed down to 90 minutes from two hours. Wrapped up by 7.15pm, Sports Personality of the Year will then quickly make way for the final results show of the ballroom dancing contest, with Antiques Roadshow holding onto the 8pm slot. For the past five years, the channel has given more space to a broadcast celebrating the best of British sport, with the 2025, 2024 and 2023 awards all airing from 7pm, with the big winner on the night handed their trophy just after 9pm, with last year's ceremony held on a Thursday. The BBC said in a statement: 'Following the success of last year, we wanted to bring the awards back to a primetime slot on a Sunday evening, making it more accessible so that more people and families can watch and enjoy the celebrations together. 'We’ve made some adjustments to the format to make this work, and we’re looking forward to another fantastic year.' BBC's Sports Personality of the Year awards will run earlier and shorter this year against the backdrop of change at the broadcaster In 2022, Mary Earps won the trophy at 9pm two hours and fifteen minutes after the show started at 6.45pm, with Emma Raducanu announced as the winner at the same time a year earlier. The Corporation argues that Sunday late afternoon is likely to see more families enjoy the awards show, with the shorter format creating a more focused, engaging and accessible show for audiences. The move comes against the backdrop of a number of cut-backs within the BBC's sports output. The department made a slew of unpopular cuts as recently as September, when it was announced that 41 roles were set to be made redundant with a view to making a saving of £2.5million. Equally unsettling was the decision at the end of last season to scrap BBC's Football Focus. At the time, the BBC denied it was part of the money-saving scheme but instead part of 'the continued shift in how audiences engage with football and our commitment to evolving how we deliver content to reach fans wherever they are'. Another programme to have felt the swing of the axe in recent months was winter sports show Ski Sunday, which was cut from the schedule after a nearly 50-year run. During this summer's World Cup, the channel came under fire for the decision to base BBC's punditry team from Salford instead of flying them to North America, as broadcast rivals ITV did. Big names including Gabby Logan, Wayne Rooney and Alan Shearer did not report Stateside until the semi-final stage, in stark contrast to the elaborate studio in New York constructed for ITV. The award was first presented in 1954, when runner Christopher Chataway beat fellow athlete Roger Bannister. For decades, the BBC show was seen as the centre piece of the broadcaster's sporting year. However, SPOTY has suffered from dwindling viewer figures in recent years.

Sports.title: Aidan O’Brien has four chances to break Group 1 world record in Japan and Hong Kong
Sports.content:
Aidan O’Brien has four chances to break Group 1 world record in Japan and Hong Kong

The Ballydoyle maestro saddles Minnie Hauk in Sunday’s Japan Cup and has three possible runners lined up for the Hong Kong International Races

View 3 Images Aidan O'Brien: trying to break own record (Image: Hong Kong Jockey Club)

Aidan O’Brien has four chances to break the Group 1 world record in Japan and Hong Kong.

‌



‌



The Ballydoyle maestro already holds the record of most top level victories in a calendar year, which he set in 2017 when he recorded 28 winners. He equalled the mark at the Breeders’ Cup when Benvenuto Cellini captured the Turf at Keeneland last month.

‌



On Sunday O’Brien is set to saddle Minnie Hauk in the £5.1 million Japan Cup in Tokyo which will feature a strong European contingent headed by defending champion Calandagan, Ombudsman, Goliath and Ethical Diamond, from the Willie Mullins stable.

‌



The Classic-winning mare is also one of the international stars selected for the £12.7m Longines Hong Kong International Races at Sha Tin on December 13. She could also run in the Hong Kong Cup or Vase, while Benvenuto Cellini could line up in the Hong Kong Vase and True Love in the Hong Kong Mile

They feature among a total of 18 individual Group 1 winners nominated for four Group 1 races at the year-end “Turf World Championships”.

View 3 Images Minnie Hauk: tackles the Japan Cup (Image: ©INPHO/Morgan Treacy)

‌



Hong Kong racing’s international flagship will welcome 31 visiting horses at the fixture where Ka Ying Rising aims to become the first triple winner of the Hong Kong Sprint after victories in 2024 and 2025.

The nine-time Group 1-winning sprinter is also bidding to continue his current unbeaten spell in Hong Kong which spans more than 1,000 days, while also giving the race’s most successful jockey, Zac Purton, his sixth victory.

‌



Andrew Harding, Executive Director, Racing, The Hong Kong Jockey Club, said: “We are excited by the quality and depth for the Longines Hong Kong International Races at Sha Tin on Sunday, 13 December.

View 3 Images Benvenuto Cellini: part of O'Brien's Hong Kong contingent (Image: Alan Crowhurst, Getty Images)

Article continues below

“The presence of so many stars of world-class quality, including Benvenuto Cellini and Almaqam, is in keeping with our commitment to sporting excellence.”

Never So Brave, from the Andrew Balding stable, and Lake Forest (William Haggas) are in the Mile. Almaqam (Ed Walker) is set to contest the Cup while Giavellotto (Marco Botti) will attempt to repeat his Turf success from 2024, in which he could be joined by Pride Of Arras (Ralph Beckett).

Sports.title: 'I was there when Jude Bellingham almost joined Man Utd - it's a sad state of affairs'
Sports.content:
'I was there when Jude Bellingham almost joined Man Utd - it's a sad state of affairs'

Jude Bellingham is performing like one of the world's best for Real Madrid but he wasn't far away from signing for Manchester United

View 3 Images Nicky Butt launched into a scathing rant over Manchester United (Image: The Good, The Bad and The Football)

Jude Bellingham snubbed Manchester United when he was just 16 after touring their training ground. And club legend Nicky Butt, who says he was present for the visit, has slammed United's fall from grace.

‌



‌



Real Madrid and England superstar Bellingham issued a reminder in the Champions League on Tuesday that he remains one of the world's finest talents. His 60th-minute goal in a 5-1 thrashing of PSV has to be seen to be believed and he was the conductor of the victory off the bench.

‌



The 23-year-old's journey to the top has taken stops at Birmingham City and Borussia Dortmund. But in 2020, whilst he was still a teenager honing his craft at St Andrew's, United rolled out the red carpet for him at Carrington.

‌



However, Bellingham could not be coaxed into signing and turned down United in favour of a move to Germany. Butt recalls the visit and believes it epitomises where the now-relegation-threatened United currently stand.

"Jude Bellingham. I was there when that happened. I was there when that happened," said Butt on The Good, The Bad & The Football, sponsored by Midnite.

View 3 Images Bellingham scored an outrageous goal mid-week (Image: Getty)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The conversation with fellow United icon Paul Scholes began as Butt admitted he was also present when Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha toured Carrington.

‌



Butt claims the winger - who dominated United in the 4-0 thrashing on Sunday - is a huge United fan, but the club has hit such dire straits that the teenager opted for Anfield when leaving Chelsea in 2024.

"Now, Man United, 20 years back in the day, was the most productive academy in the world, producing players not only for Man United but for all clubs all over the world - and it's a sad state of affairs," said Butt.

‌



"You're looking at that lad [Ngumoha], who was probably man of the match on Sunday and he's a Man United fan playing for Liverpool… It sounds like I'm having a pop, which I am because I love the football club.

"But he's a massive Man United fan, Rio and his family. Massive Man United fan. So, I think it was at 13 or 14, or whatever age it was. He goes and looks around Man United, whether it be Old Trafford or Carrington.

‌



View 3 Images Ngumoha scored Liverpool's third goal against United on Sunday (Image: Getty)

"He's gone with his family to look around that football club and then he's gone to Liverpool and he's picked Liverpool. I know he's a Man United fan and I know he loves Man United.

Article continues below

"He should not be allowed out of that building before he signed that contract. It should never have happened. I'd like to know who's showing him around the football club, who's explaining things? I'd like to think Wayne Rooney or Paul Scholes... I'm being deadly serious. Why is he being allowed out of the training ground?"

United currently find themselves 19th in the Premier League with 11 games played and Mauricio Pochettino has replaced Michael Carrick to fight the fire. A player like Bellingham or even Ngumoha would be worth their weight in gold at Old Trafford in the current climate.

Sports.title: Sporting manager singles out Man Utd star as he drops brutally honest admission
Sports.content:
Sporting manager singles out Man Utd star as he drops brutally honest admission

Manchester United take on Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday night, looking to bounce back after their thrashing by Liverpool in Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge

View 2 Images Paulo Fonseca has given his take on Manchester United (Image: FILIPE AMORIM / AFP via Getty Images)

Sporting Lisbon boss Paulo Fonseca has admitted he has no idea how Manchester United might set up, but used Bruno Fernandes as an example of the obvious threat they continue to carry.

‌



‌



United face Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday night just three days after they were thrashed 4-0 in Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge against Liverpool. Leny Yoro's early red card - which has since been overturned on appeal - left United facing an uphill struggle and they left Anfield with a stinging defeat.

‌



United have won just three games all season and sit 19th in the Premier League thanks largely to the worst defensive record in Europe's top five leagues. Pochettino has had less than a week to implement his ideas on the training pitch after replacing Michael Carrick.

‌



Yet Fonseca, who only joined Sporting on November 4 after leaving Lyon to replace Rui Borges, believes United's freshness under a new coach makes them a difficult proposition to prepare for.

“It is hard to get the measure of this Manchester side,” said Fonseca. “They changed coach and with the sending-off after eight minutes in (against Liverpool), it became impossible to carry out any kind of analysis.

“It is hard to predict, but this will be a very strong Manchester team, featuring very strong players. We expect a motivated opponent under a new manager.”

‌



Fonseca has won both games in charge so far, against Moreirense in the league and Uniao da Serra in the Taca de Portugal. And the experienced Portuguese manager singled out United captain Fernandes as a threat to his side.

“Obviously, United are a team packed with top-class talent, and Bruno stands out, but we don’t prepare for a match based on a single player,” Fonseca added. “We prepare based on the team as a whole and we have tried to prepare for various scenarios.”

‌



Pochettino has desperately been trying to bring his squad together in a short space of time, but is maintaining a positive outlook. “The situation is fragile,” he said in a pre-match press conference. “We are not fragile. We are a strong team, they showed that last season when they finished third and now we are playing in the Champions League.

“Sometimes things happen in football for different reasons. We need to identify why and already we are working on it. I think we are going to turn round the situation. We need to go game-by-game. In the end, being at Manchester United is about winning every single game, one is not more important than another.

“We are Manchester United and we need to believe we have the capacity to turn that situation. We are building our identity and that is the most important thing.”

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola 'embarrassed' by Italy job offer as he drops hint on his 'next step'
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola 'embarrassed' by Italy job offer as he drops hint on his 'next step'

Pep Guardiola left Manchester City at the end of last season and is currently considering his next step, having turned down the opportunity to become Italy manager

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola is enjoying his time away from management (Image: Getty Images)

Pep Guardiola says he was "embarrassed" to turn down the opportunity to become Italy boss, despite knowing that international management is the "next step" in his career.

‌



‌



Guardiola stepped down as Manchester City manager at the end of last season, ending a 10-year stint with the Premier League club. The 55-year-old left City in order to take some time out of the game, but has continued to be linked with jobs.

‌



He was shortlisted by US Soccer as a possible replacement for Mauricio Pochettino after he was poached by Manchester United. And the USA job wasn't the first international role he was considered for, having been in the frame to take charge of Italy in the summer.

‌



Fellow ex-City boss Roberto Mancini ended up taking the reins in July, but only after Guardiola and Andrea Pirlo were lined up. Guardiola has now revealed that he held talks with former Italy technical director Paolo Maldini and advisor Leonardo about the job.

Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"This is the first time I speak about this, but yes, I did talk to them," Guardiola told his former Barcelona teammate Romario on his show Romario TV. "I felt embarrassed to say 'no' to Italy, a country like Italy, it would have been one of the greatest honours of my career to coach the Italian national team.

"But I realized I needed to stop. If they had called two years earlier, I probably would have accepted. But when Paolo Maldini and Leonardo, whom I love dearly, reached out, it was at a point where I simply had to stop.

‌



"I needed some time for myself. After 18 years as a coach, with matches every three days, week in and week out, there comes a moment when you just have to say 'phew.'"

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images Pep Guardiola needs time off before taking another job (Image: Jordan Bank/Getty Images)

Italy were searching for a replacement for Gennaro Gattuso after their failure to qualify for a third straight World Cup. Guardiola rejected the offer before legendary ex-midfielder Pirlo pulled out following controversy over his ties to a Russian betting company. The saga saw Maldini and Leonardo resign and Mancini re-appointed as the Azzurri boss.

‌



Guardiola has been backed for the USA job by Pochettino, who said it was "the perfect moment to arrive" for the Catalan. But the man himself is content with spending some time out of the spotlight for now, despite saying that a national team "is the next step" in his career.

"The truth is, I don't know, I really don't know. But for now, I'm doing fine," Guardiola said. "If I ever return, it will be because my gut tells me to, and because someone wants me, then I we'll go back. But it's been many years, so many matches."

Article continues below

It has been reported that Guardiola wants to take a year out of the game to recharge his batteries before considering a return. He was admired by the Netherlands before they appointed his former Barcelona player Xavi, and by England before they went for Thomas Tuchel.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury 'thought wife and dad were plotting to kill him' as he shares harrowing experience
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury 'thought wife and dad were plotting to kill him' as he shares harrowing experience

Tyson Fury has opened up about the dark places he has been in ahead of his fight against Anthony Joshua

View 2 Images Tyson Fury has emerged from a dark place (Image: The Louis Theroux Podcast)

Tyson Fury has revealed he thought his wife and father were conspiring to try and kill him at the height of his mental health crisis. Ahead of his blockbuster fight with Anthony Joshua in Cardiff next month, the Gypsy King has been opening up about his struggles away from the ring.

‌



‌



In the upcoming Netflix documentary about his life, it emerged that Fury was diagnosed with schizophrenia just a few months after becoming world heavyweight champion. In a subsequent interview on The Louis Theroux Podcast, Fury detailed the extent of his paranoia, including believing his wife Paris, father John and his best friend were plotting to kill him.

‌



He said: "The problem is what state I was in mentally. It got to a point where I couldn't sleep without the light on. I'd go around and check every window and door like 100 times."

‌



When Theroux brought up obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD), he added: "Yeah, and then got to a point where I thought I was like gonna get attacked and people were gonna break into me house all the time.

Paris Fury fears husband Tyson is 'addicted' to boxing and will fight on after Anthony Joshua bout READ MORE :

"And then it got even worser than that. I started hearing voices in me mind. I thought I was being set up by me wife to get me killed. I thought me dad was in on it. I thought me best friend Dave was in on it. I lost it completely, gone."

Asked what the voices were saying, he added: "The voices were telling me to kill meself. Very, very dark, demonic place I never ever wanna return to, ever.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"That was what I was living with constantly. And I thought that I would end up in a padded room and nowhere else or, or dead. Dead was an easy option really, but I thought I was gonna end up in a straightjacket."

‌



On rebuilding his life, Fury added: "I tried to achieve short-term goals, whether it be weight loss, eating a certain diet, whatever. Kept myself busy and active. I kept around people.

"I couldn't be on me own, even when I was making a comeback. Even when I had my first fight back against Sefer Seferi in '18, I still couldn't sleep with the lights off. Seven foot tall world heavyweight champion has to sleep with the light on 'cause he's scared!"

‌



View 2 Images The Furys have been franks about Tyson's mental health struggles (Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

Regarding the schizophrenia diagnosis, Fury told the Netflix documentary: "Words can't explain the darkness I was in. I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100 per cent thought at times I'd end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.

‌



"I was waking up in the night [and] the anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it. Completely gone, and that's when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London.

"She asked me like a gazillion questions and stuff, and I ticked all the boxes, whatever was going on. Depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder…" Paris added: "He's a mild schizophrenic and even then the penny didn't drop."

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho's Aston Villa future is bleak as blunt Unai Emery explains brutal snub
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho's Aston Villa future is bleak as blunt Unai Emery explains brutal snub

Alejandro Garnacho was missing from the Aston Villa squad for their Champions League tie against Galatasaray and Unai Emery appears to be repeating a brutal approach with the Chelsea loanee

View 3 Images Unai Emery handed Alejandro Garnacho a bitter blow with his words (Image: TNT Sports)

Unai Emery has delivered a hammer blow to Alejandro Garnacho's future at Aston Villa after leaving him out of the squad for their Champions League tie at Galatasaray.

‌



‌



Garnacho was conspicuous by his absence on the team sheet in Istanbul, with Emery choosing to name just 11 substitutes, including two goalkeepers, and leave one slot empty. Villa lost the match 1-0 on Tuesday night with Deniz Gul's late header enough to win it for the hosts.

‌



Emery started with Alysson and Johan Manzambi on the wings while Ibrahim Mbaye, Emi Buendia and George Hemmings came off the bench in the second half to no effect.

‌



Garnacho has made seven appearances for Villa this season since joining on a season-long loan from Chelsea, all of which have come from the substitutes' bench. He has been left on the bench as an unused substitute on six occasions, but was completely snubbed by Emery on Tuesday.

When asked about the 22-year-old's absence, the Villa manager replied bluntly: "Today the players were here who I think are the best players to be here with us."

Garnacho's last appearance for Villa came in a three-minute cameo off the bench against Fulham on October 31. And already he is facing an uphill battle to revive his career in Birmingham, with similarities to Harvey Elliott's situation last season clear.

‌



When the 22-year-old joined Villa in July, the club said his move will "become permanent next summer should certain criteria be met". While those criteria have not been made public, they are understood to be straightforward and Chelsea felt confident they had negotiated a permanent exit for the ex-Manchester United man, who would bring in £42million next summer.

View 3 Images Alejandro Garnacho is enduring a tough time at Aston Villa (Image: Marc Atkins/Aston Villa FC via Getty Images)

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Emery was "delighted" with the signing at the time, adding: "He is so talented, young and he showed us his wish to help our project. We are really happy."

‌



But that impression has faded over recent months with Garnacho failing to force his way into the starting XI. Emery took a brutal approach with Liverpool loanee Elliott last season, freezing him out to avoid triggering a £35m obligation to buy clause, and his words in September about Garnacho hint at something similar happening again.

View 3 Images Alejandro Garnacho was missing from the Villa squad in Istanbul (Image: Aston Villa FC via Getty Images)

‌



"[He has to] continue working. Work, work, train, work. When he can have minutes to play, try and play well," Emery said. "George [Hemmings] is playing fantastic, Alysson is also understanding things well and is giving us things I want.

"Alysson is also understanding things well and is giving us things I want. Mbaye also responded well. We want a competitive team and players to compete in the style we have. Garnacho is a little bit behind because of some circumstances we had in pre-season. It is time to be patient for the time he needs."

Article continues below

Chelsea signed Garnacho from United for £40m in the summer of 2025 and his former club are owed 10 per cent of any sell-on fee. The Argentine winger made 43 appearances last season, with eight goals and four assists, before Chelsea decided to move him on once more.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino brutally digs out VAR after Leny Yoro appeal - 'What were they doing?'
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino let rip at VAR after Leny Yoro's early red card against Liverpool at the weekend was overturned.

The Manchester United defender was given his marching orders after just eight minutes by Sam Barrott for bringing down Alexander Isak. Liverpool went on to thrash their depleted arch-rivals 4-0 in Pochettino's first game at the helm, leaving the Red Devils rooted in the Premier League relegation zone after just one win from 11 games.

The Football Association confirmed on Tuesday that Yoro's red card, given for the denial of a goalscoring opportunity, had been overturned "following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal".

And Pochettino expressed his frustration at the costly decision following Manchester United's successful appeal, questioning why VAR failed to intervene at the time.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

“Very disappointed because this kind of thing can never happen,” said the Argentine following the outcome of Yoro's appeal in his pre-Sporting Lisbon press conference.

“We can accept the referee can make a mistake, but if we have VAR, what were they doing? Are we going to repeat the game 11 v 11? When we were, you need to take your time to review the situation.”

Howard Webb, the chief of Ref Pro, defended Barrott's decision to send Yoro off despite it being rescinded, saying it was "not wrong" for him to do so.

‌



Speaking on Mic'd Up, he said: “We know it’s clearly a foul. I don’t think there’s any dispute about that. And we also know that it’s outside the penalty area. We’re thinking about the sanction, aren’t we? That’s why we’re talking about this.”

View 3 Images Yoro was sent off after just eight minutes at Anfield (Image: Martin Rickett/Press Association)

“Is it a denial of an obvious goal scoring opportunity? Four considerations officials have to think about. direction of play, it’s definitely going towards the goal. It’s not going out wide. Proximity from goal, well, it’ just outside the penalty area. the location of other defenders. Well, there’s only Yoro there. The keeper is moving back towards his own goal.

“He has to put the brakes on and possibly come back out. the reason we’re talking about it is the fourth consideration, that’s control or likelihood of keeping on or gaining control of the ball. Isak’s got control of the ball, he’s got possession, he’s got the touch, he knocks it past Yoro. He’smoving at pace at that moment, and a foul comes in and knocks him down.

‌



“And there’s a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Senne Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.

View 3 Images Howard Webb defended the decision to send Yoro off (Image: Sky Sports)

“That was the referee’s call made on the field, and then the var checks that to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn’t, that if there was any doubt, then it was doubt.

“It wasn’t going to be something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed that decisive on-field decision to stand. and i think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but i think it’s a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.”

‌
