World.title: Sinner uncertain for Australian Open after undergoing knee surgery
World.content:
The five-time Grand Slam champion has not played a match since winning Wimbledon in July.

Jannik Sinner risks missing the Australian Open in January after confirming that he has undergone surgery on his troublesome right knee.

The five-time Grand Slam champion has not played a match since winning Wimbledon for the second time in July, with less than two months until the start of the first major tournament of the season in Melbourne.

“Over the past few months, together with my team we’ve tried everything to treat my injury without surgery,” Sinner said in a statement on Tuesday.

“After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn’t respond as we had all hoped, that’s why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band.”

The procedure, which had been reported earlier in the day by broadcasters RAI and Sky Sport, and sports daily La Gazzetta dello Sport, was performed by knee injury specialist Lasse Lempainen at a clinic in Finland.

Another knee specialist, Fabrizio Terrone at the Isokinetic centre in Turin, told Sky Sport that Sinner’s absence could last “at least three to four months”.

That means the earliest Sinner might be back on court with a racket in hand would be during the American hard-court swing, at Indian Wells and Miami Masters.

The 25-year-old admitted recently that the worst injury of his career left him barely able to move.

“The worst part for me about this injury is that I cannot compete, I cannot play tennis,” said Sinner in a recent video.

“Also, my life outside of tennis is a bit more limited because of a simple fact that I cannot do things that I really like, because I want to protect my knee.”



Sinner, a two-time champion at the Australian Open which begins on January 17, recently said that he will make his comeback at the “Six Kings Slam” tournament in Saudi Arabia, which has been rescheduled for late December due to the conflict with Yemen’s Houthis.

But that now looks impossible and a difficult start to 2027 seems in store for the man who has in recent years risen to be, alongside Spanish star Carlos Alcaraz, the pre-eminent force in men’s tennis.

Sinner was having a brilliant campaign before being stopped by his knee problem, with five Masters 1000 titles going alongside his triumph at Wimbledon.

The Italian’s 94 percent winning record in 2026 is the best of his career, even beating his figures from the previous two seasons in each of which he won two Grand Slams and the ATP Finals.

He suffered a major disappointment at the French Open when, leading Argentina’s Juan Manuel Cerundolo by two sets and 5-1 ahead in the third, he succumbed to heatstroke and was eliminated in the second round.

Sinner recently lost top spot in the men’s world rankings to losing Wimbledon finalist Alexander Zverev, who has taken advantage of injury problems for both Sinner and Alcaraz to win Roland Garros and the US Open.

World.title: After Brexit, is Britain heading back to the EU?
World.content:
Ten years after Britain voted to leave the European Union, London and Brussels have struck a deal to bring their economies closer.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham says Brexit “has not worked” and would like to see Britain rejoin in his lifetime.

But not in this parliament, and he is sticking to the Labour Party’s red lines on the single market, the customs union and free movement.

Critics say he has no mandate to reopen the debate. Burnham says it is up to voters.

United States President Donald Trump welcomed the Brexit vote. Now his tariffs are one reason Britain and the EU see more to gain together.

World.title: Zidane was much better than me: Bellingham after Real Madrid wonder goal
World.content:
Jude Bellingham admits he had ‘no idea’ what he’d done after scoring a goal that drew comparisons with Zinadine Zidane.

Share Zidane was much better than me: Bellingham after Real Madrid wonder goal on social media

Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham has brushed aside comparisons with football great Zinedine Zidane following his sensational goal against PSV in the Champions League.

The England international came on at half-time with Los Blancos trailing and inspired a sensational second-half display, including a magnificent effort from distance, at the Santiago Bernabeu on Tuesday.

Bellingham said he “did not know” how he scored his brilliant goal, flicking the ball up on the edge of the box and slicing a stunning effort inside the far post.

Having seen an acrobatic volley blocked minutes earlier, the England midfielder controlled Kylian Mbappe’s pass with two touches in the air and curled a superb shot into ⁠⁠the far corner from well outside the area.

“I have no idea what I did,” Bellingham told RMTV. “I had the ball in a good position and thought about shooting.”

The 23-year-old, upon joining Real Madrid, took Zidane’s number five shirt in “homage” to the Frenchman, whom he admired, and some have compared his goal to a Zidane-style strike.

“I do things that you guys think are similar to Zidane, but he was much better than me,” Bellingham told reporters.

Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho hailed Bellingham’s game-changing display as the midfielder gave Mourinho credit for helping him find arguably the best form he has enjoyed at Madrid in recent weeks, with Los Blancos winning a 10th straight match, but the coach said the midfielder only had himself to thank.

“I think the main figure responsible for what Jude is today is Jude, and his teammates. I try to help a little,” said the Portuguese coach.



“He’s an absolutely extraordinary player who has everything – he has physicality, he has technique, he has tactical understanding of the game, he has ambition, he has absolutely everything and today, obviously not by himself, but he changed the direction of the match.”

“He’s an absolutely extraordinary player and for me, without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world,” Mourinho said.

Madrid’s victory over the Dutch champions maintained their 100 percent start to the league phase, in which they are provisional leaders.

Mourinho reiterated his view that it was a “scandal” that Bellingham was not ranked in the top 10 players in the world at this year’s Ballon d’Or ceremony.

Mbappe netted twice to put Real out of sight before Vinicius Jr got in on the act with a late goal, having struck the post twice earlier in the game.

World.title: Israeli strike kills Hamas official, his wife and children
World.content:
Share Israeli strike kills Hamas official, his wife and children on social media

An Israeli air attack on Gaza has killed a senior Palestinian security official and his wife and daughters, according to a statement from the enclave’s Ministry of Interior.

In a statement posted on its Telegram channel on Wednesday, the ministry identified the official as Muhammad Majid Abu al-Awf, 47, director of the Internal Security Service in northern Gaza.

Noura Ezzat Abual-Awf, his wife, aged 41, and his children, Yusra Mohammed Abu al-Awf, 15, and Jana Mohammed Abu al-Awf, 13, were also killed in the strike, the statement added.

The ministry described the killings as a “horrific massacre perpetrated by the Israeli occupation forces when they bombed [the family’s] residence in the Shati refugee camp, west of Gaza City, at dawn today”.

The attack is part of “ongoing attempts to undermine the security apparatus in the Gaza Strip in an effort to spread chaos within Palestinian society”, it added.

The strike comes less than 24 hours after the killing of the Internal Security Service’s director general, Brigadier-General Naim Abu Nahal.

Israeli attacks continue

Israeli strikes reported overnight killed several people, according to medical sources.

A source at al-Shifa Hospital confirmed to Al Jazeera that four people from the same family were killed and several others were wounded in an Israeli attack on a residential apartment in the Shati refugee camp.

Separately, medical sources at the Nasser Medical Complex reported that a Palestinian girl was shot by Israeli forces in areas outside their control in Khan Younis, in the southern Gaza Strip.



Daily violations of the so-called “ceasefire” in Gaza have been recorded since October 2025, with Israeli air attacks regularly targeting the enclave and at least 1,680 people killed and more than 6,000 injured as Israel’s genocidal war continues.

Hamas called on the guarantor states of the “ceasefire” deal to intervene immediately “to rein in the occupation, impose a halt to its crimes, and obligate it to adhere to the agreement’s path”.

World.title: ‘People are going hungry’: Guinea’s gold mining crackdown
World.content:
NewsFeed ‘People are going hungry’: Guinea’s gold mining crackdown

The gold mining crackdown in Guinea has forced thousands of people to flee the country into neighbouring Mali. 300,000 people who are attracted to Guinea come West Africa, rely on unauthorised mining.

World.title: Shakib, Mustafizur not among Bangladeshi players on 2027 IPL auction list
World.content:
Eleven Bangladeshi players have entered their names for the December 16 IPL auction, a year after Mustafizur Rahman’s expulsion from the league.

Former captain Shakib Al-Hasan and fast bowler Mustafizur Rahman are notable absentees on the list of 11 Bangladeshi cricketers who have registered for the Indian Premier League’s (IPL) upcoming player auction, as tensions continue to simmer between the South Asian neighbours.

Top-order batter Towhid Hridoy leads the players, named on a list released on Wednesday, who are seeking a place in the world’s most lucrative cricket franchise league, a year after Mustafiz’s controversial removal from the IPL.

The 11 Bangladeshis feature on an initial list of 1,220 players for the December 16 mini auction in Goa, although the pool will be trimmed before franchises make their selections, the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) said.

“With 184 players already retained or picked by the franchises ahead of the auction, a maximum of 66 slots, including 25 overseas slots, are available to be filled,” the BCCI said in a statement.

Apart from Hridoy, who is enjoying great run-scoring form, Hasan Mahmud, Parvez Hossain Emon, Ripon Mondol, Rishad Hossain, Saif Hassan, Shak Mahedi Hasan, Shamim Hossain, Shoriful Islam, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, and Taskin Ahmed are on the list, according to cricket news outlet Cricinfo.

The presence of Bangladeshi names on the draft auction comes as a surprise, months after the country’s expulsion from the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup, cohosted by India.

The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) refused to send its team to India over security concerns, which followed a fallout over star pacer Mustafizur’s removal from the Kolkata Knight Riders’ roster upon the BCCI’s instructions.



Though the BCCI gave no clear reason for his expulsion, the board said it was due to “developments all around” – an apparent reference to the tensions between India and Bangladesh that soared following the ouster of former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in 2024, who then received exile in New Delhi.

The relationship between India and Bangladesh remains tense over Dhaka’s extradition request for Hasina, which New Delhi has yet to comply with.

Among the more than 1,000 players listed for auction, England all-rounder Ben Stokes is among the high-profile names, with a base price of $216,900.

Indian players dominate the initial list, accounting for 939 registrations.

Australia leads the overseas contingent with 53 players, followed by South Africa (40), West Indies (36), New Zealand (25) and Afghanistan (23).

The list also includes players from emerging cricket nations, with 13 registrations from the United States, and 10 each from the United Arab Emirates and Nepal.

Franchises will finalise their squads after the auction, which will determine the player pool for next year’s edition of the competition.

World.title: The cost of Nigeria’s power failures for one small business
World.content:
The cost of Nigeria’s power failures for one small business

NewsFeed The cost of Nigeria’s power failures for one small business

Fashion business owner Aderayo Soile says unreliable electricity is holding back her business. Despite paying for the country’s highest electricity supply tier, she has to buy fuel for a generator to keep operating and wants the next president to make reliable power a priority.

World.title: Who is Chen Jining, China’s latest Politburo member under investigation?
World.content:
Chen is the fourth high-ranking Politburo member to be pushed out in two years.

Share Who is Chen Jining, China’s latest Politburo member under investigation? on social media

The Chinese Communist Party has launched investigations into the party’s Shanghai secretary Chen Jining for alleged “serious violations of discipline and law” – usually code for corruption.

The anticorruption watchdog, the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, announced the probe in a brief statement on Tuesday, according to Xinhua News Agency, but did not give more details.

It comes amid widespread purges in the Political Bureau, one of the top bodies of the CCP, as the party prepares for its next congress in the second half of 2027, where President Xi Jinping is expected to clinch his fourth five-year term.

Xi, who has pushed greater party discipline and anticorruption, has for years pursued a long, intense purge on a scale not seen since the rule of Mao Zedong, experts say.

Chen is the fourth high-ranking Politburo member to be pushed out in two years.

The Shanghai Communist Party’s leaders have backed the move, with its standing committee stating it firmly supported the decision to investigate Chen and that it showed Beijing’s determination to continue its anticorruption campaign.

“The takedown again shows that Xi Jinping’s anticorruption campaign has no limits,” Mingda Qiu, a senior analyst at Eurasia Group, told The Associated Press news agency. “The pattern is unprecedented.” Here’s what we know:

Who is Chen Jining?

Chen, 62, joined the CCP as a 20-year-old environmental engineering student at the highly-rated Tsinghua University. After spending a decade researching in the United Kingdom, the scientist and academic returned to Tsinghua, where he was eventually appointed one of its youngest presidents in 2012.



He went on to serve as the Minister of Environmental Protection from 2015 to 2017, and led efforts to cut pollution in Beijing. He was later appointed Mayor of Beijing in 2018.

In 2022, he was appointed party secretary of Shanghai, the country’s financial hub, amid Xi’s push to install people with strong scientific backgrounds in key roles.

Chen was widely seen as Xi’s protege. His post is usually seen as a stepping stone to party leadership; President Xi previously held the position of Shanghai Party Secretary in 2007.

Chen hosted some of China’s most prominent diplomatic visitors, including former US Secretary of State Antony Blinken, former British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.

He led the opening ceremony of the World AI Conference held earlier this year in Shanghai.

Who else has been targeted?

Other senior party officials have been purged in recent months, especially in the military.

General Zhang Youxia , the senior vice chair of the powerful Central Military Commission (CMC), was investigated for the same “serious violations of discipline and law”, China’s Defence Ministry said in January. The commission is the top military body and is chaired by Xi, making Zhang the military’s number two. He was part of the informal “Shaanxi clique”, a network of political leaders who share ancestral ties to Shaanxi Province with Xi.

The commission is the top military body and is chaired by Xi, making Zhang the military’s number two. He was part of the informal “Shaanxi clique”, a network of political leaders who share ancestral ties to Shaanxi Province with Xi. Liu Zhenli, another CMC member who served as the chief of staff of its Joint Staff Department, was being investigated by the CCP, the Defence Ministry also said in January.

He Weidong, the other vice chair of the military commission, was expelled last October on allegations of “serious misconduct” and violations involving “exceptionally large amounts of money”. Eight other senior military members were also dismissed. He was part of the “Fujian clique”, a tight circle of officials who have long been allied with President Xi since his time as Fujian governor from 1999.

Miao Hua, former head of the political work department in the military commission and another member of the Fujian clique, was removed in June 2025.

Ma Xingrui, former party secretary of Xinjiang, was charged with accepting “exceptionally large” bribes in November. Ma’s investigation was first announced in April.

Why is this happening?

The military shakeups and wider purge are part of Xi’s years-long anticorruption drive that has seen hundreds of senior and junior government officials investigated, prosecuted or dismissed since Xi first came to power in 2012.



Analysts believe the purges are designed to reform the military and to ensure unwavering loyalty to Xi.

Some military expulsions have been linked to suspicions of political divergence. Official sources, for example, described additional allegations against He Weidong, the former vice chairman of the military commission, as being a “loss of chastity,” a rare phrase which, in CCP speak, refers to political disloyalty and ideological collapse.

The takedowns reveal how Chinese politics often depends on shifting circumstances, with even officials possessing the qualifications Xi wants being vulnerable to removal, said Joseph Torigian, a professor at the Washington-based American University.

“On paper,” they appear to be “individuals Xi would appreciate,” Torigian told the AP. But afterwards, “we could easily come up with hypotheses for why he got rid of them”.

World.title: Russia's own figures show it has lost almost 500,000 people in Ukraine war
World.content:
At least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died since the start of the war in Ukraine in 2022, according to Russian government statistics analysed by the BBC.

The leaked Rosstat data reveal how the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has fundamentally changed mortality patterns in Russia, and show the high cost paid in human life in a war that Vladimir Putin had assumed would last only days but is now almost five years old.

BBC Russian has had access to more than 11 million death records from 2021 to September 2026, after a hack by Belarusian group Cyber Partisans BY and Ukraine's Silent Crow.

Russia's statistics agency admitted to a cyber-attack, but denied any protected information had been leaked.

Together with independent Russian outlet Mediazona, BBC Russian has compared the Rosstat data with its own list of confirmed military deaths, pulled from open sources since the start of the invasion, and it has found matches for 90% of the records.

Military experts estimate that the BBC's list of 290,012 deaths, gleaned from official reports, social media, new memorials and graves, may account for 45-55% of the true death toll, which would range from 527,295 to 644,471.

World.title: My family died in Ukraine. My mum blamed Zelensky's troops - the truth is complicated
World.content:
If you are outside of the UK, listen to the Who Killed My Family podcast here

Watch our YouTube documentary here, external

As for my grandparents, my investigations suggested the events surrounding their deaths may have been more complicated.

Their house, on the eastern side of Dachne, had been destroyed. Neighbours told me they had escaped to another home on the same street.

I eventually reached a woman I'll call Lina, who lived nearby and was the last person, as far as I know, who saw my grandparents alive.

She could not recall what this date was, but knew it was in the second half of January.

At this time, she said, "the Russians were fully advancing - the edges of the village were being shelled. Then the Ukrainian soldiers moved from the edge of the village into the centre. They hid in people's yards and used side streets to avoid drones."

She said two soldiers entered her property. They had not been wearing any identifying insignia but had been speaking Ukrainian, she said - a language that Lina described as "Bandera", a derogatory term for Ukrainians.

"You're going to have to leave. Why are you still here?" Lina said they had asked her.

She said one had pointed a machine gun at her as she had stood outside her house, while another had gone to see my grandparents. She told me she had feared for her life and then fled her house for the night.

The following day, she told me she had returned to my grandparents' street to check on them.

She had found the door to the house they had been staying in open, she said, despite the freezing conditions.

With drones buzzing overhead, Lina said she had not dared look inside, but had later heard from neighbours that my grandparents had been found dead. She believed it had been the Ukrainian soldiers who visited her house who had shot them.

Another neighbour, who I will call Maria, described discovering their bodies - my grandmother in bed, covered in a blanket, and my grandfather lying on the floor in a pool of now-dried blood.

Maria also believed Ukrainian soldiers had killed them - because, she said, that she too had felt threatened by Ukrainian troops at the time.

"If they had seen me they would have killed me too."

Her theory was that my grandparents had irritated the troops in some way.

"Your grandparents caught them in a bad mood because your grandfather was always asking to be evacuated. And [the soldiers] were, you know, high. They were taking drugs. So your grandparents got in their way," she told me.

Most of the other people in the village I spoke to also believe Ukrainian soldiers killed them, though their testimony is not based on direct evidence.

The new local mayor, appointed by the Russian occupiers when they finally took control of Dachne in February, said she had been present at my grandparents' burial the following month, and said half of my grandmother's skull was missing.

These accounts of how they might have died in January 2025 were deeply disturbing, though no-one had witnessed their deaths and the information I was given could not be independently verified.

The villagers I spoke to - now living in occupied territory - did say there had been some tensions between themselves and Ukrainian troops at the time, because the soldiers had viewed those who remained in Dachne as supporters of Russia.

The clinical causes of my grandparents' deaths are unclear.

Their bodies were not exhumed for nearly 20 months, when the local authorities sent them to a morgue in the occupied region, where a basic autopsy was carried out by a forensics expert.

He told me that my grandmother had died of an explosives injury to the skull - but could not specify its cause.

As for my grandfather, it said his body had shown no obvious signs of injury.

I compared two satellite images of the house in which their bodies were found - from just before and just after when they are believed to have died - and could detect no significant damage to the building in the second image.

I also spoke to a villager who said he had buried my grandparents.

He said he did not know anything about who killed them.

"I wasn't there. But why would you kill old people?" he asked.

World.title: US attorney general dodges questions about Nvidia investigation
World.content:
US Attorney General Todd Blanche has backed Nvidia as a "good corporate citizen" while refusing to comment on whether the AI chipmaker was under federal investigation.

Blanche said he had no information about newly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang's security clearance status, as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's comeback.

Huang was given his job back less than two weeks after being forced to resign over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

Asked several times on Tuesday if the justice department or FBI had investigated Huang, Blanche responded: "I don't know what you're talking about."

Huang is still set to appear before Congress next week, where he will be questioned about national security concerns over his relationship with an alleged China spy who led Megaspeed, a Singapore-based corporate customer of Nvidia.

Trump has said he would consider pardoning Huang for any potential criminal activity, though he does not think it will come to that.

"It's always an option, I guess, but I don't think it'll be necessary," Trump told the New York Post in an interview published on Tuesday.

World.title: Close-up images to be revealed of asteroid deliberately hit to test ability to protect Earth
World.content:
A spacecraft has arrived at an asteroid to investigate the damage caused by an unprecedented cosmic crash.

In what may sound like the plot of a disaster movie, Nasa's Dart spacecraft deliberately smashed into the space rock in 2022 to knock it off course.

The Nasa craft was obliterated on impact. Four years on, a European Space Agency (ESA) mission, called Hera, is scouring the scene to fully assess the aftermath of the collision - with the first images set to be released later on Wednesday.

The asteroid poses no threat, instead this was the first ever test of our planetary defences to see what action we could take if a space rock was heading for our planet.

"Hera is a sort of Inspector Columbo going back to the crash scene to investigate what is the outcome of this impact," said Patrick Michel, principal investigator of ESA's Hera mission.

World.title: Thomas Markle charged in US for possessing child sex abuse images
World.content:
Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex has been charged by a federal grand jury in Los Angeles with possessing child sex abuse images.

Markle, who remains in custody in Florida, allegedly possessed materials that include at least one image involving a prepubescent minor and a minor under 12 years old, court documents filed in California show.

The 82-year-old has denied possessing images of child sex abuse.

Last week, a judge in Florida declared Prince Harry's father-in-law mentally competent to stand trial.

The FBI arrested Markle on 6 November at an elderly care home in Florida on a single federal charge of possessing child sexual abuse material. He now faces two counts.

US attorney Bill Essayli said Markle faces a maximum of 20 years in prison on each count if convicted.

His arrest came after a search of a storage unit he had allegedly rented in Los Angeles for almost two decades uncovered the abuse material.

Markle was initially released on conditional bail but was then ordered to stay in jail pending trial after allegedly removing a location monitoring device.

World.title: US preparing to unveil plan for new tariffs on global trading partners
World.content:
The US is preparing to announce plans for new tariffs on several countries as early as Wednesday, the BBC understands.

The new import taxes would hit many of America's biggest trading partners, with China, the European Union and Japan among at least 14 jurisdictions affected.

The move comes after the White House's so-called "Section 301" investigation. It was launched in March after the US Supreme Court ruled that President Donald Trump's Liberation Day tariffs were illegal.

Trump has made tariffs a signature policy of his presidency, arguing that they will help boost American manufacturing and create jobs.

The president sent shockwaves around the world when he unveiled sweeping tariffs on global trading partners in April 2025 shortly after his return to the White House.

While the tariffs were later struck down, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer argued then that overproduction abroad was displacing American manufacturing and deterring investment.

Under the new tariffs, countries will face different import tax rates depending on the deals that they have previously struck with Trump.

The announcement is likely to increase tensions between the US and China, the world's two biggest economies, which remain locked in a trade dispute.

Despite last week's meeting between Trump and President Xi Jinping, the two sides have yet to fully resolve their difference with an interim agreement set to expire on 10 January.

World.title: Colombian police storm supermarket to free 20 held hostage for 17 hours
World.content:
Residents living near the supermarket reported hearing explosions as the security forces moved into the building.

Police later confirmed that officers had used stun grenades to overpower the hostage takers.

One was killed in the operation and four have been arrested.

De la Espriella described it as "an extraordinary joint operation", which he said had been carried out "flawlessly".

He flew into the northern city to oversee the operation.

In footage released since then, he can be seen, with a handgun strapped to his belt, flanked by the commanders of the operation.

Speaking after the successful rescue of the hostages, he said that the gunmen had been given the chance to hand themselves in, which they had refused.

Earlier in the day, the assailants had freed 10 of their hostages, among them elderly women.

But they continued to hold around 20, even as a police helicopter hovered above and special forces teams prepared to enter the building, which is located in a popular shopping mall.

Local media said that as well as asking for safe passage out of the supermarket, the gunmen also demanded nearly $2m (Â£1.5m) and armoured vehicles.

According to President De la Espriella, they had no political affiliations but had taken the hostages once their plan to rob an armoured car carrying money had been foiled.

"It's not that a terrorist group carried out a kidnapping - no, these are criminals who were caught off guard, had no way out, and then kidnapped a group of people," he said.

Photos taken during the rescue operation show armed soldiers inside the building as people are kneeling with their hands behind their heads.

It is not clear from the photos whether those kneeling are hostages or the hostage-takers.

Local media are reporting that the authorities feared that some of the gunmen may have tried to pass themselves off as hostages as the rescue mission unfolded.

The identities of the four arrested have not yet been released.

The hostages are being reunited with their families after being checked over by medical teams, according to the mayor of Cartagena.

Many anxious relatives had spent hours waiting for news outside the perimeter place around the supermarket by security forces.

A woman called Sandra told news site Caracol that her 76-year-old mother was one of those being held hostage.

Sandra's mother - among a group of elderly people released after six hours - was reunited with her daughters and grandchildren.

Footage recorded by local media showed bystanders cheering as some of those freed were escorted to ambulances waiting nearby.

But with around 20 people still inside the building, tension outside rose and police said they had to stop some of the relatives from breaching the perimeter.

World.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
World.content:
Huawei has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but not guilty of the more serious overarching racketeering charge in a landmark case in the US.

In a two-month trial, prosecutors accused the Chinese technology and telecommunications giant of lying, cheating and stealing to gain any competitive advantage.

Huawei's defence team argued that prosecutors had decided Huawei was a criminal organisation and built its case from there, but the firm's success was due to its own innovation.

Huawei said, external the racketeering acquittal "confirms that these allegations lack factual basis", adding that it would "take all necessary legal actions to defend our rights and interests".

Jurors in a Brooklyn court found Huawei guilty of 10 out of 12 counts, which included conspiracy to violate US sanctions.

However, the jury declined to convict Huawei of the racketeering conspiracy charge, which required members to find the firm acted like a criminal enterprise.

Federal prosecutors first announced the charges against Huawei in 2019, after the dramatic arrest in late 2018 of senior executive Meng Wanzhou in Canada.

Meng, also known as Cathy Meng, was held for three years in Canada before she was released to return to China through a deal with US prosecutors.

During closing arguments last week, assistant US attorney Meredith Arfa told jurors Huawei spent 20 years doing whatever it took to expand its business, including lying to banks about its business dealings in Iran and stealing technology secrets from rival firms to ensure it had a competitive edge.

"For decades, Huawei and three of its subsidiaries conducted their business in the United States on the basis of lies and theft," US Attorney General Todd Blanche said in statement, external.

"Thanks to the work of the FBI and our federal prosecutors, those who engaged in these criminal activities will be held accountable."

The Chinese government hit out at what it called the US "suppression" of Chinese companies and said it supports Chinese firms protecting their interests.

Defence attorney Brian Heberlig said it was by dint of hard work that Huawei's business had expanded with operations in 170 countries and more than 200,000 staff.

Following the verdict, Heberlig told the BBC that Huawei was gratified that the jury had rejected the racketeering charge.

"The RICO [Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act] count that alleged that Huawei was a corrupt organisation, with a corporate culture and policy of committing crime. That was, in our view, a significant overreach, and the jury soundly rejected it," he said.

"Of course, we have mixed emotions about the rest of the verdict ... [we] thought that Huawei was deserving of acquittals across the board."

Sentencing is planned for September 2027. Heberlig said there will be "significant advocacy" to achieve the lowest sentence possible. Following that, he said he fully expects Huawei to appeal.

"If I know Huawei, that fight will continue, and the company's not going to rest until it's pursued every last argument it can through appeal, and hopefully, ultimately toward vindication," he said.

World.title: Babachir accuses Atiku of seeking subsidy return to loot public funds, slams ADC takeover
World.content:
Former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Babachir Lawal, has accused former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of campaigning to restore the fuel subsidy to reopen avenues for public looting.

In a statement on Facebook titled “Kachalla Series No. 4: Nigeria Ronu – Shine Your Eyes,” Mr Lawal said the statement was a reply to Atiku’s social media supporters, whom he accused of repeatedly attacking him over the defunct grass-cutting scandal despite his discharge on a no-case submission.

Mr Lawal described the former vice president, with whom he was briefly in the African Democratic Congress (ADC), as unqualified to lead Nigeria, citing criticisms from former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s memoirs that Atiku lacked loyalty, transparency, and judgement.

“In thus attacking me, they seek to defend a man who himself could be considered a ‘Mr Corruption’ in Nigeria. A man whom his former immediate boss, President Olusegun Obasanjo, once described in his book as having ‘propensity to corruption’, ‘tendency to disloyalty’, ‘a shameless liar’, and ‘willingness to sacrifice integrity and national interest for personal gains’.

“Obasanjo goes on further to argue that Atiku lacks sound judgement, transparency, and the necessary understanding of the demands of the presidency, stating that choosing him as a running mate was his ‘biggest mistake’. This was from his boss of eight years; nevertheless, you want us to ignore this evaluation of Kachalla Abubakar by his boss and vote him in as our president? This man who ‘lacks sound judgement, transparency, and the necessary understanding of the demands of the presidency’? Haba, Atikulates!”, Mr Lawal stated.

Mr Lawal also cited past domestic and international corruption allegations involving the Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF), the Siemens bribery scandal, investigations involving former U.S. Congressman William Jefferson, and the Special Purpose Vehicles (SPV) controversy, arguing that Atiku escaped prosecution only because of constitutional immunity while in office.

“This is a man of whom the ICC Arbitration panel flagged a $500,000 payment to his wife as raising “significant red flag”. There are many more such “red flags”—a $20 million unauthorized payment by PTDF; a US Senate committee investigation that traced over $40 million in suspected funds linked to him and his wife; the Siemens bribery scandal; allegations tied to former US Congressman William Jefferson; SPVs and Atikugate in which his former SA claims he channeled public funds including a ₦100 million diversion from the Ecological Funds to this SPV; and so on and so on”, Mr Lawal stated.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Turning to internal party politics, Mr Lawal—who resigned from the ADC in June after Atiku won the party’s presidential primary—accused Atiku’s faction of infiltrating and hijacking the ADC after falling out with the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, in the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

He alleged that the ADC had become a “one-man dictatorship” while other members remained passive.

“The ADC was initially conceived to be a party of patriotic democrats with a left-leaning, ideological bent until Atiku’s faction of the PDP, on the run from the rapacious Nyesom Wike, infiltrated it, subterraneanly taking it over and turning it into a one-person tyrannical dictatorship in Atiku Abubakar, egged on by a coven of yes-men. But instead of fighting to resist this fraudulent takeover of their party, the rest of the party members wholesomely chose to surrender to a state of “sit-down-look” and cognitive paralysis”, Mr Lawal said.

Mr Lawal further claimed that Atiku’s 2027 campaign rallies rely on rented crowds and focus on only two themes: reversing the fuel subsidy removal and asserting his Fulani identity.

He criticised Atiku’s public declaration of his Fulani heritage during a visit to Kebbi State as insensitive, noting that communities in the state and neighbouring areas suffer from banditry and terror attacks by groups such as Lakurawa, Boko Haram, and ISWAP offshoots.

Mr Lawal pointed out that suspected terrorists murdered the late Emir of Gobir, Isa Bawa, in the area, arguing that residents needed concrete security solutions rather than ethnic posturing.

“This declaration of his Fulaniness was first made in Kebbi State, of all places. Reports have it that the Lakurawas, an Islamist militant group that is alleged to be allied with Islamic State Sahel Province (ISSP), operates in Kebbi State. It is also reported that the Mamudawa, Boko Haram and ISWP have offshoots operating in Kebbi State.

“I would have thought that what the people of Kebbi State needed to hear is how he will tackle the pervasive insecurity of the area and not a declaration that he comes from the same tribe as that of most of the terrorists.

“Nigerians need to be made aware of who this ADC presidential wannabe and his coven actually represent. Atiku has only two messages to Nigerians which he delivers at his rallies: removal of fuel subsidy and a declaration of his Fulaniness. Aside from declaring these at his rallies of rented crowds, he has chosen to occupy himself with a campaign of harassment of Bola Tinubu, a man of similar bent who beat him to the presidency. Needless to say, this anti-Tinubu drive is occasioned by an Othello syndrome, a sort of delusional jealousy,” Mr Lawal stated.

On the economy, he alleged that Atiku’s opposition to President Tinubu’s May 2023 fuel subsidy removal is driven by self-interest rather than public welfare.

Citing NNPC expenditure figures before May 2023, alongside an August 2026 Federal Ministry of Finance report stating that subsidy removal generated ₦15.8 trillion in revenue for the federation, Mr Lawal maintained that the subsidy regime was a conduit for fraud through fake invoices and ghost deliveries.

“The oil subsidy is a scam. This is probably what the subsidy return means to Atiku and his coven. “The oil subsidy is a scam. This is probably what the subsidy return means to Atiku and his coven. They want a return to the open looting of the oil revenue,” Mr Lawal stated.

“I will now comment on his fixation on oil subsidy removal and portraying it as if he is planning to do so with altruistic motives. To understand this fixation, you need to look at the figures. Before Bola Tinubu removed it on 29th May, 2023, NNPC reported spending ₦4.39 trillion in 2022 and ₦1.829 trillion between January and May 2023. To quote from Bola Tinubu’s inauguration speech: “What is the past is the past, fuel subsidy is in our past, no more corruption, no more falsification of invoices, no more lies, and no more smuggling of fuel.”

“Also, a 2022 motion in the House of Representatives alleged that nearly $10 billion was defrauded from the subsidy fund. The Federal Minister of Finance in August 2026 reported that removing the fuel subsidy generated ₦15.8 trillion in revenue for the Federation. This scam was achieved through fake invoices, ghost shipments and phantom deliveries,” Mr Lawal stated

He also attributed Atiku’s opposition to President Tinubu to frustration over the prevailing political consensus favouring a Southern presidency to complete an eight-year term.

“First, Bola Tinubu’s presidency has further distanced Atiku from his ambition to one day be a President. This is because, aside from the overwhelming agreement among Nigerians that the Presidency should remain in Southern Nigeria to complete its eight years in the seat, old age is playing a trick on him. Hence, he is livid and resorts to the courts and foreign interests to stop Bola from being on the ballot rather than defeating him at the general elections. Desperation is a stinky cologne indeed,” Mr Lawal added.

The former Vice-President is yet to respond to Mr Lawal’s allegations. His spokesperson, Paul Ibe, could not be reached by our reporter Wednesday morning to comment on the allegations.

World.title: Afrilition: Exploring alternatives for the systemic transformation of the future, By Adéwálé Àjàdí
World.content:
…what and how does an African alternative offer a new systemic pathway in the United States and Brazil? This is in the face of deep and significant resistance to Africa and what it represents, including the legitimate pains of ancestral betrayal, deep orientations and socialisation into White Supremacy, in spite of daily resistance to its racism, the intergenerational condition to react, as opposed to the creative disposition to alternatives and the amplification of intention.

The last few days have been blessed, with layers of positive news almost daily. First, Afrilition won a Literary Titan Silver Award, then Brazil returned Lula da Silva to its Presidency, thereafter the Nigerian Under-17 women’s team won the FIFA World Cup, and the US midterm elections shifted the right-wing tide of US representation towards a balance, or dynamic equilibrium, by returning its Senate and House to Democrats. Among these good news stories, Nigeria’s FIFA World Cup is the indisputable confirmation of excellence. All the others have a history that might make them flatter to deceive.

The recent US midterm elections were a powerful expression of the resilience and capacity of African Americans to lead resistance against oppression and marginalisation within the United States. It is no small feat against the most entrenched and effective system of indoctrination into White Supremacy currently in the world. This has been since the horrible dehumanisation and mass murders of enslavement, with the crowning genocide of indigenous people. The system has always been designed as a settler-colonial capitalism operating to reward European hegemony. It has adapted and adjusted its Zeitgeist, especially if you follow the Reconstruction after the Civil War, with corresponding progress for free and emancipated people in their political and economic lives, despite a hostile environment, especially in the Southern United States.

Many attributed the setbacks and murder of Jim Crow to Andrew Johnson’s rollback of Black progress. It, however, seems like the system just recalibrated, finding ways to renew the deep mental model of Caste and Racial Hierarchy that is foundational to the country — rekindling wholesale and retail debauchery and the destruction of black lives. The United States did not become a full democracy until its Voting Rights Act of 1965. Since then, there has been a pattern of periodic dilution of the voting potential and representation, especially of African Americans. There is the regular gerrymandering of votes and the periodic voter correction of emerging Black representation, as if to ensure effective and continued subjugation of Black representation within the institutions of governance.

Black women in the US have created a leadership system blended with identity and based on years of resilience. They have been fashioned by the intergenerational memory of the cruelty of enslavement and systematic vilification, along with the epigenetics of the stress of daily invalidation. The generations of rape, sexual exploitation, and casual cruelty of racism have become the kiln for the political wisdom and leadership service delivery.

This time we might be seeing a very different and more sustainable phenomenon in political activism and the fight for representation and inclusion. First, the leadership of Black Women as a voting bloc to capture the Democratic Party and lead resistance against the Right. No voting block seems further in character and disposition from the Billionaire class which shamelessly now expresses sponsorship, power and control over most public and governance spaces in the country.

Black women in the US have created a leadership system blended with identity and based on years of resilience. They have been fashioned by the intergenerational memory of the cruelty of enslavement and systematic vilification, along with the epigenetics of the stress of daily invalidation. The generations of rape, sexual exploitation, and casual cruelty of racism have become the kiln for the political wisdom and leadership service delivery.

Out of all these, including false and sometimes real narratives of schism in the Black family has generated a warrior spirit now emerging from the cauldron of the MAGA vengefulness. This is not just for this season but the expression of a spirit that refuses to be denied life’s purpose. It is not different from the symbol of the 21-year-old Ana Elisa Santos Silva in Brazil; the most voted woman in the history of Minas Gerais for the Chambers of Deputies. She helped advise and revamp Lula’s digital and social media strategy that made him overturn his first round second place.

For the future, these African communities should consider the understanding of the systems their countries run and why they thrive on the denial of their full and fruitful contributions. These victories can be short-lived once the system recalibrates and is able to revert to its structures and institutions that are leveraging the embedded mental model. In the way the Obama administration was a prelude to Trump’s first time and Dilma Rousseff/ Michel Temer before Bolsonaro in Brazil.

Stacey Abrams’ Fair Fight action was the structural catalyst for transforming the political landscape from blueprint to the effect of including the registration and management of the marginalised and ignored. In both Brazil and the US, the amplification of the inclusion of poorly represented and largely non-participating voters has changed representation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

For the future, these African communities should consider the understanding of the systems their countries run and why they thrive on the denial of their full and fruitful contributions. These victories can be short-lived once the system recalibrates and is able to revert to its structures and institutions that are leveraging the embedded mental model. In the way the Obama administration was a prelude to Trump’s first time and Dilma Rousseff/ Michel Temer before Bolsonaro in Brazil. The settler colonies thrive on Racial Hierarchy and the patterns of regular resistance do not transform or disturb the systemic direction. So even though these waves have the power of institutional disruption, until the transformative battle that people like Malcolm X and Paul Robeson stood for is joined, we will return to the back-and-forth.

So what and how does an African alternative offer a new systemic pathway in the United States and Brazil? This is in the face of deep and significant resistance to Africa and what it represents, including the legitimate pains of ancestral betrayal, deep orientations and socialisation into White Supremacy, in spite of daily resistance to its racism, the intergenerational condition to react, as opposed to the creative disposition to alternatives and the amplification of intention. In all these, Afrilition is an exploration of what the best systemic transformation for the future is and what sustainable legacy we give to our posterity.

Adéwálé Àjàdí, a lawyer, creative consultant and leadership expert, is author of the newly released Afrilition: 21st Century African Manifesto, and Omoluwabi 2.0: A Code of Transformation in 21st Century Nigeria.

World.title: Police arrest suspected grave robber in Kebbi
World.content:
The police in Kebbi State have arrested a 30-year-old man, Tapro Tareza, for allegedly digging into a fresh grave at Machika Cemetery in Ribah.

The suspect, a resident of Changu village, via Gwazawa, in Kanya District, was apprehended by local youths on 10 November.

The state police spokesperson, Bashir Usman, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, two weeks after the incident.

Mr Usman, a superintendent of police, said the police had mounted surveillance in collaboration with local youths following earlier reports of grave vandalism at the cemetery.

“On 10th November 2026, at about 1915hrs, shortly after the burial of a newly deceased person, the suspect was caught digging into the grave. He was immediately apprehended by the vigilant youths, who promptly alerted the Police,” the spokesperson said.

Previous incidents

Mr Usman said preliminary investigations indicated that the suspect allegedly removed items from the bodies of the deceased.

READ ALSO: Police deploy tactical teams to Borgu after deadly attacks

He said Mr Tareza had also allegedly admitted involvement in previous incidents of grave desecration at the cemetery, including one in which he reportedly removed a burial shroud.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The statement did not disclose the suspect’s motive, the number of graves allegedly desecrated or whether any human remains had been removed.

“Investigation is ongoing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incidents and to ensure that the suspect faces appropriate legal action,” Mr Usman said.

The command commended residents for their vigilance and cooperation but warned against taking the law into their own hands.

It urged members of the public to report suspicious activities through its telephone lines: 09039911876 and 07081974395.

World.title: Police deploy tactical teams to Borgu after deadly attacks
World.content:
The Deputy Inspector-General of Police, Operations, Umar Nadada, has assured residents of Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State of an enhanced security presence following last week’s deadly attacks in Lumma Ba’are and Wawa communities.

Mr Nadada gave the assurance during an operational visit to the area on Monday to assess the security situation and engage affected communities.

The DIG, accompanied by the state Commissioner of Police, Salisu Fago, and other tactical commanders, also paid a condolence visit to the Emir of Borgu, Muhammed Dantoro, at his palace in New-Bussa.

He said the visit was at the instance of the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, to convey the police leadership’s condolences to the emirate council and residents over the loss of lives and destruction of property.

Mr Nadada said security agencies, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders, were working to address the security challenges, warning that communal violence and reprisal attacks could further undermine efforts to restore peace.

He said the visit was aimed at assessing the situation firsthand, engaging affected communities and identifying their immediate security needs.

The DIG assured the emirate council that additional operational assets and tactical personnel would be deployed to strengthen security, prevent further attacks and restore normalcy.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He also said requests earlier submitted through the local government chairman would receive the necessary attention from police authorities.

In his response, the Emir of Borgu commended the Inspector-General for deploying the DIG to assess the situation.

The monarch expressed confidence that the security challenges facing the area would receive sustained attention, noting the IGP’s longstanding relationship with the Borgu community.

He condemned the incidents and highlighted the Emirate Council’s efforts to address communal conflicts and promote peaceful coexistence, while reaffirming the community’s support for security agencies.

The delegation subsequently visited Lumma Ba’are, where the initial attack occurred on 21 November.

Suspected armed men reportedly invaded the community, killing the village head, Malam Bawa Muhammad, and other residents, while several houses were set ablaze.

The state government and police initially reported five deaths, including the village head, while other media reports put the casualty figure higher. Five people were also reported injured and evacuated to the General Hospital in New-Bussa.

The attack reportedly occurred amid lingering intercommunal tensions in the area, prompting the deployment of joint security teams and calls for residents to remain calm and avoid reprisals.

The violence subsequently spread to other communities, including Wawa, where suspected reprisal attacks were reported against residents.

Reports on the attacks in Wawa and neighbouring communities gave varying casualty figures, with some accounts reporting dozens of deaths. The figures had not been independently verified by authorities at the time of the DIG’s visit.

The delegation, during its visit to Lumma Ba’are, observed houses burnt in the attack and engaged residents, assuring them of the police command’s commitment to restoring peace.

The DIG announced plans for additional tactical personnel to complement joint security teams already operating in the area.

The delegation also proceeded to Wawa, where it held a stakeholders’ meeting following the suspected reprisal attack.

Residents presented their accounts of the incident and denied that the attack originated from the Wawa community, attributing it to other groups. They also submitted security-related requests for police intervention.

Mr Nadada expressed condolences to the Dodo of Wawa and residents over the incident and assured them of increased security deployment.

He urged residents to cooperate with security agencies, stressing that maintaining peace and security required collective responsibility.

World.title: Delta NDC Killings: Ex-lawmaker, human rights activist, party chieftain among victims
World.content:
The killing of a former Delta State lawmaker, a prominent Urhobo rights activist and a chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has emerged as part of the human cost of the violence that disrupted the party’s campaign rally in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

The three victims were identified as Moses Anaughe, Efemena Umukoro (popularly known as Comrade Akima), and Nyoren Okoro.

Their deaths followed an attack by armed men on Monday during a campaign tour of Uduere community by Ovie Omo-Agege, a former deputy Senate president and the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 elections.

The Nigeria Police Force subsequently confirmed that six people were killed and several others injured in the violence, revising the initial casualty figure of four announced by the Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation.

However, the police have not publicly released the identities of all six victims.

Mr Obi, the NDC presidential candidate, identified Messrs Anaughe, Umukoro and Okoro in a statement condemning the attack. He said a fourth victim had yet to be identified. This leaves two of the six deaths confirmed by the police without publicly established identities in the accounts reviewed by PREMIUM TIMES.

Who were the victims?

Moses Anaughe

Mr Anaughe was a former member of the Delta State House of Assembly, where he represented Ughelli North II Constituency.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He subsequently served as the Federal Commissioner representing Delta State at the Federal Character Commission, having been confirmed by the Senate in June 2020.

He was also an aide to Mr Omo-Agege and was among the two campaign officials initially identified by the campaign organisation as having been killed.

His brother, Godwin Anaughe, in a statement on Tuesday, said he was shot twice at close range during the attack.

Describing him as a peaceful man who served Delta State with dedication, Mr Godwin said his brother left behind a wife, two children and their 95-year-old mother.

He called on the police to arrest those responsible for the killing.

The family alleged that Oghenegueke Ugbarugba, popularly known as Gueke, an aide to Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta State, and Jaro Egbo, the chairman of Ughelli North Local Government, were involved in the attack.

The allegations have not been independently established. The police have commenced an investigation into the incident.

Efemena Umukoro (Comrade Akima)

Mr Umukoro was a prominent Urhobo youth activist, human rights campaigner and former president of the youth wing of the Urhobo Progress Union, a socio-cultural organisation of the Urhobo people.

He was also a member of the NDC and an outspoken advocate for the rights of young people in Delta.

Lawyer Inibehe Effiong, in a tribute, described him as one of the reliable activists in the state who defended young people against injustice, particularly police oppression and extortion.

Mr Effiong said Mr Umukoro had previously appeared in court to show solidarity with his client in a “politically motivated” criminal defamation case.

He described his killing as a tragic loss to Nigeria’s human rights community.

The Anti-Cult Volunteer Corps Nigeria also mourned him, describing him as a committed human rights defender who stood up for vulnerable people and those whose rights had been violated.

Mr Umukoro reportedly left behind children and other family members. His killing has triggered protests by youths and residents of his hometown, Orogun, who have demanded justice.

Nyoren Okoro

Mr Okoro was identified by Mr Obi as an NDC chieftain killed in the attack.

However, details about his political activities, personal background and circumstances surrounding his death were not immediately available.

World.title: ‘One of Africa’s most recognisable thespians’ – Tinubu mourns Pete Edochie
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has expressed grief over the death of veteran actor Pete Edochie, joining other Nigerians to mourn the Nollywood icon.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that Edochie died in Enugu on Wednesday following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer.

In a statement by Bayo Onanuga, his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Mr Tinubu said the news had left him deeply saddened.

The president paid tribute to the actor, describing him as an exceptional talent whose contributions helped lay the foundation for Nigeria’s thriving film industry.

He added that Edochie commanded admiration through his remarkable screen presence and personality.

He said: “He was one of Africa’s most recognisable thespians. For decades, he plied his craft, bringing joy, laughter, and charm to many homes. ​I recall his unforgettable portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s evergreen novel, Things Fall Apart, in the 1980s, and his many brilliant performances afterwards.

“Through memorable performances in productions such as Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart, he helped shape the evolution and international visibility of

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Nollywood. His portrayal of traditional institutions, family structures, African values, and the complexities of human relationships helped project Nigeria’s cultural heritage and storytelling traditions to audiences worldwide.”

Legacy

Mr Tinubu further praised Edochie’s versatility, noting that he excelled as an actor, administrator, broadcaster and journalist.

The former Lagos State governor also prayed for God to grant the deceased eternal rest.

He extended the government’s sympathies to the Edochie family and everyone affected by the veteran’s death, including his friends, associates and colleagues in the film industry.

“His place in the pantheon of those who shaped the film industry, our common norms, and popular culture remains indisputable. ​As I mourn the passing of this legendary actor, I also reflect on his life. Pete Edochie lived well. He played his part and exited gracefully.

“​In his works, he lives forever. Many generations will talk about the life and work of Chief Edochie in the arts industry and academia, in barbershops and marketplaces, and indeed wherever people gather”, Mr Tinubu said.

Backstory

Mr Tinubu joined Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah, the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN) and other Nollywood stakeholders in paying tribute to Edochie.

This newspaper reported that they praised the late actor as an icon, a patriot and a towering personality whose death had left a void in Nollywood and the wider African entertainment industry.

They highlighted his commanding performances, distinctive diction, rich use of proverbs and memorable expressions, and his contributions to broadcasting.

Edochie, 79, spent decades building a career in broadcasting and filmmaking, as this newspaper previously reported.

World.title: Tight security in Maiduguri as Tinubu leads APC rally
World.content:
Security has been beefed up across Maiduguri ahead of President Bola Tinubu’s visit and the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-East zonal rally scheduled for Wednesday.

The heightened security presence, accompanied by road closures and traffic diversions, has disrupted movement in parts of the metropolis as security personnel deploy to strategic locations ahead of the presidential visit.

Roads affected include Airport Road, Kashim Ibrahim Road, Bulumkutu, Teachers’ Quarters Phase II, GSM Village, International Conference Centre, Mai Doki Roundabout, West End Roundabout, Shehu’s Palace, Dandal Roundabout, Bolori Roundabout and Government House.

Security personnel deployed include operatives of the Police, Army, Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Civilian Joint Task Force (CJTF) and vigilante groups, among others.

The restrictions have prompted calls for residents to exercise caution, avoid unnecessary movements and use alternative routes to minimise inconvenience.

Retired Col. Bukar Gujubawo, a security expert, advised residents to avoid roads leading to the rally venue and other areas designated for presidential activities.

He also urged motorists to allow extra time for their journeys, maintain a low profile, remain vigilant and comply with directives from security personnel to ensure a smooth and peaceful event.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Abdulaziz Abdulaziz, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Public Enlightenment and Coordinating Secretary of the Media Committee of the Presidential Campaign Council, said Borno was ready to receive Mr Tinubu.

Mr Abdulaziz urged APC supporters and loyalists to remain calm, conduct themselves peacefully and turn out en masse to welcome the President.

Mr Tinubu is also expected to inaugurate two projects in Maiduguri, including the Maiduguri International Conference Centre and the NYSC Female Corps Members’ Quarters.

The rally has attracted many party supporters, political stakeholders and residents from across the North-East.

(NAN)

World.title: Life coaches’ association to checkmate social media quacks
World.content:
The Life Coaches Association of Nigeria (LCAN) says it is building an online membership directory to help Nigerians verify qualified coaches and avoid uncertified practitioners on social media.

The association announced this on Tuesday during a media parley in Lagos to kick off the eighth edition of Africa Coaching Week (ACW), under the theme “Activating the Future: Data-Driven Coaching Across Africa.”

Fake ‘Instagram coaches’

LCAN President Omawumi Ogbe said low entry barriers have made it easy for people to take online courses and label themselves coaches on social media.

“Because there is a low barrier to entry, it is easy for anybody just to call themselves a coach or put ‘Instagram coach’ on top of their bio.

“People clearly need to start asking where you were certified, because it is your life. You do not just get dumped on,” Ms Ogbe said.

She said the association is creating a public directory where prospective clients can check whether a practitioner is properly trained and accredited before paying for sessions.

“We are working to create a membership directory so that when someone tells you they are a coach, you can go on our directory to check if they are there,” she said. “We need to call out fakes and quacks and the people who are pretending to be coaches.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ms Ogbe said proper coaching brings real results, noting that trained members of the association have helped struggling companies get out of debt and become profitable.

Coaching different from motivational speaking

Speakers at the parley said coaching relies on tools and measurable outcomes, unlike motivational speaking, counselling, or therapy.

Quoting pioneer Nigerian life coach Lanre Olusola, Ms Ogbe said coaching has been widely misunderstood in Nigeria.

“What doesn’t get measured doesn’t get done,” Ms Ogbe said.

“For too long, coaching in many quarters has really been about instinct, inspiration, and motivation. People here do not understand it. They think it is about motivation. But coaching is a set of tools, and we really just wanted to look at measurable outcomes and help people see how to get return on investment,” she added.

Also speaking at the event, pioneer Nigerian life coach and Chairman of the LCAN Advisory Board, Lanre Olusola, compared understanding coaching to tasting Jollof rice, saying people need to experience it to know the difference.

“There is no way I can describe to you how Jollof rice tastes. There are no words to describe it until you taste my jollof rice. Likewise, there is no other way for you to experience and know the power of coaching until you taste it. That is why every year we offer coaching for free,” Mr Olusola said.

Mr Olusola said LCAN sets up free coaching booths every year and is running over 30 coaching sessions for managers and leaders at PwC this year.

Incoming LCAN President Abiola Salami said top company executives need coaches to perform well. He added that the title of “coach” has been “intellectually bastardised” in Nigeria by people who use it loosely for colleagues without proper training.

“Executive coaching is working with a certified, qualified, results-driven professional with proof of sustained performance,” Mr Salami said.

“Once you get into a mid-level supervisory function and want to get to the very top of your career, whether locally or globally, it is important to engage the services of a certified executive coach.”

Why Western coaching models fail

LCAN executives also spoke about “Afro-coaching,” a coaching model developed by Mr Olusola and South African coach Dr Mongezi Makhalima, President of the Africa Board for Coaching, Consulting and Coaching Psychology (ABCCCP).

According to Mr Olusola, PwC data ranks coaching as the second fastest-growing industry globally after ICT, valued at about $50 billion. He said Western coaching models often fail in Nigeria because foreign coaches do not understand the country’s culture and economic realities.

“The West cannot provide what we need because we are different,” Mr Olusola said.

“We have had many organisations and banks that signed up international coaches and paid serious money, but they didn’t get value. They had to come back and hire indigenous coaches.”

He noted that Nigerians act as their own social security system and often spend a significant chunk of their earnings sending younger siblings to school and looking after their parents.

“You cannot separate a human being from his culture and his environment.

“Afro-coaching is African coaches coaching Africans, and that is the future of coaching. Now we want to export it, because there are Black people across the world,” Mr Olusola added.

Ms Ogbe said that while foreign coaching models work to an extent, coaches must adapt them to African culture and ways of thinking to get results. She added that LCAN is working with 11 Afro-coaching competencies to help African coaches.

Eighth Africa Coaching Week

Ms Ogbe said the association named the event Africa Coaching Week rather than Nigeria Coaching Week to reflect its continental vision. This year’s programme brings together speakers from Africa, Asia, the Americas, Europe, and Australia.

Based on feedback from past editions, LCAN replaced large panel sessions with one-on-one LinkedIn podcast interviews. The week also includes a workshop on artificial intelligence and a partnership that gives members access to The Deal Coach, a platform created by an LCAN member to help coaches anticipate changes and measure problems.

Ms Ogbe said coaching is not meant only for wealthy people. She noted that LCAN offers free sessions and low flat fees during partnerships so that the average Nigerian can participate.

“Coaching is not something for just rich people,” she said. “It is really for everyone. Coaching really takes you from where you are to where you want to be. It is a partnership, and as a coachee, you also do the work.”

Mr Salami also urged coaches to register with the association.

“If you are a coach and you are not a member of LCAN, you may become irrelevant soon,” he said.

World.title: Kwara begins ₦2bn gratuity payments to 2018–2019 retirees, clears ₦7bn backlog
World.content:
AbdulRazaq

The Kwara State Local Government Staff Pension Board has commenced the payment of over ₦2 billion in outstanding gratuities to retired local government and Local Government Education Authority (LGEA) workers who left service between 2018 and 2019.

The Chairman of the Local Government Service Commission and Local Government Staff Pension Board, Alhaji Umar Danladi Shero, disclosed this while briefing journalists on developments in the commission and efforts to address outstanding pension obligations.

Shero said beneficiaries in the 2018–2019 retirement category had started receiving their payments following the completion of verification and screening exercises.

He explained that the latest payment was part of the state government’s efforts to settle inherited gratuity liabilities and improve the welfare of retired local government and LGEA workers.

According to him, the state government expended over ₦7 billion between July and October on gratuity payments to local government and LGEA retirees covering the 2011–2017 period.

He said the ongoing disbursement of over ₦2 billion to the 2018–2019 beneficiaries represented a continuation of the exercise to clear outstanding gratuity obligations.

The pension board chairman commended Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq for his support and interventions in addressing the welfare concerns of retired workers at the local government, SUBEB and state levels.

He said the governor’s interventions had supported regular pension payments and the gradual settlement of outstanding gratuities inherited from previous administrations.

Shero assured pensioners that arrangements had been made to ensure a seamless and transparent payment process, adding that verified beneficiaries would receive their entitlements directly into their designated bank accounts.

He reaffirmed the board’s commitment to ensuring that all eligible retirees received their entitlements, urging beneficiaries to remain patient and cooperate with the board where necessary.

He added that the government remained committed to ensuring that no eligible pensioner was left out as efforts continued to clear outstanding gratuity liabilities.

World.title: UCTH: Group presses for immediate CMD advert
World.content:
UCTH

…alleges plot to install acting head

…Ikpeme dismisses claim as “falsehood”

By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR

A socio-political group, Good Governance Initiative (GGI), has accused the management of the University of Calabar Teaching Hospital (UCTH) of stalling the recruitment of a new Chief Medical Director (CMD), alleging a scheme to install an acting head and ease in a preferred successor.

The Chief Medical Director, Prof. Ikpeme Ikpeme, has rejected the allegation.

GGI’s Convener, Mr Bassey Okoi, made the demand in a statement in Calabar on Wednesday, calling for the immediate  of the position, which falls vacant on April 16, 2027, when Ikpeme’s second tenure ends.

Okoi said the vacancy should have been advertised in national newspapers six months before the incumbent’s tenure expires.

The group had expected the process to start on November 1, he said, but there was no sign of it.

He alleged that the delay was meant to tilt the succession in favour of a candidate from Cross River’s southern senatorial district.

Okoi insisted that the central senatorial district should produce the next CMD under a long-standing zoning arrangement among the three senatorial districts.

He recalled that Prof. Thomas Agan, from the northern district, served eight years before the office moved to the south.

According to him, allowing the central district to produce the next CMD is the fairest course, and the incumbent appears determined to disrupt the arrangement.

He stressed that zoning was not meant to undermine competence but to promote fairness, inclusiveness and a sense of belonging.

He warned that manipulating the process could cause tension and damage institutional harmony.

Okoi urged the Federal Ministry of Health to ensure that the recruitment was transparent, credible and consistent with regulations.

He also appealed to stakeholders to back an equitable process, saying no individual or interest group should predetermine the outcome.

When contacted, Prof. Ikpeme dismissed the claims and said he had already begun the process of appointing his successor ahead of time.

He advised the group’s sponsors to stop wasting energy on what he called falsehood and to draw up a programme for taking the hospital to the next level instead.

He said the group should take its concerns to the Federal Ministry of Health, the appropriate authority on such appointments.

Pointing to the reforms he had carried out to reposition the hospital, Ikpeme said he was no party to the dispute. “I am not a contestant,” he said.

World.title: Abia CP vows crackdown on attacks against police, boosts Yuletide security
World.content:
By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — The new Commissioner of Police in Abia State, Sylvester Edobanya Adaji, has vowed a crackdown on attacks, assaults and provocations against police officers, warning that hostility towards law enforcement personnel would no longer be tolerated.

Adaji, who assumed duty as the 36th Commissioner of Police in the state, said assaulting police officers amounted to an attack on government authority, urging residents to channel their grievances through lawful means rather than resort to mob action or taking the law into their hands.

Speaking during the handover ceremony at the Police Command headquarters in Umuahia on Wednesday, the new CP declared that it was time to end the harassment, embarrassment, attacks and killing of police officers.

“Enough is enough,” he warned.

He, however, assured residents that the command would remain guided by professionalism, proportionality, accountability, legality and respect for fundamental human rights in carrying out its duties.

Adaji pledged to strengthen intelligence gathering, community collaboration and inter-agency cooperation, stressing that effective policing depended largely on public trust and actionable information from residents.

“Without that trust, nobody would be ready to come forward to provide credible, workable, actionable information to enable us to discharge our duties,” he said.

The new police chief said he would consolidate the security strategies introduced by his predecessor, AIG Wilfred Afolabi, particularly intelligence-driven policing, visibility patrols and community security partnerships.

He also promised to deploy his experience in operations and intelligence management to reduce crime and criminality to the barest minimum, assuring residents that the command would not relent in its responsibility to protect lives and property.

Adaji warned motorists and other road users against provoking law enforcement officers or violating traffic regulations, insisting that complaints against the police should be addressed through the courts and other lawful channels.

He said the command would intensify public enlightenment on citizens’ responsibilities while reinforcing internal discipline and compliance with standard operating procedures among personnel.

On security during the festive season, the CP announced plans for heavy police deployment and increased visibility policing across the state to ensure the safety of residents and visitors during the Yuletide.

He said existing patrol arrangements would be strengthened, including motorcycle patrols in difficult terrains and areas inaccessible to conventional patrol vehicles.

Earlier, the outgoing Commissioner, Afolabi, who was recently promoted to Assistant Inspector-General of Police, said intelligence-led policing, motorcycle patrols, crime mapping and community partnerships were among the strategies introduced during his tenure to tackle crime.

Afolabi disclosed that when he assumed office, many police divisions lacked dedicated intelligence operatives, prompting him to train and deploy intelligence officers across divisions and area commands.

He said the initiative improved intelligence gathering and processing, making the command’s operations more intelligence-driven.
