The former CP also explained that motorcycle patrols were introduced to improve police visibility in communities inaccessible to patrol vehicles, while personnel were trained in crime mapping and crime-pattern analysis to identify crime-prone locations and improve patrol deployment.

He added that a cybercrime unit was established and equipped in Aba in response to the rising incidence of cyber-related offences, while a monitoring team was set up to investigate misconduct among police personnel.

Afolabi, however, identified inadequate patrol vehicles, poor radio communication infrastructure, unfenced police facilities, insufficient fortification of police stations and the need for continuous personnel training as major challenges confronting the command.

He urged his successor to address the gaps, particularly the shortage of operational vehicles and effective communication equipment, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The outgoing CP warned that inadequate mobility could hamper security deployment in identified flashpoints during the elections.

He said mutual trust between the police and communities had improved through stakeholder engagements and joint activities, expressing confidence that Adaji would sustain the gains and further strengthen the state’s security architecture.

World.title: Bayern confirm Musiala’s neurological symptoms began in 2025, pledge recovery support
World.content:
(FILES) Bayern Munich’s German midfielder #10 Jamal Musiala receives medical attention during the UEFA Champions League second-leg, semi-final football match between FC Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) in Munich, southern Germany on May 6, 2026. Bayern Munich midfielder Jamal Musiala was taken off the pitch after collapsing in a pre-season friendly on August 18, 2026, three days after a similar incident in Munich. (Photo by Odd ANDERSEN / AFP)

By Adegboyega Adeleye

Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala’s management have reaffirmed their support for the midfielder’s recovery and clarified that he was first examined for neurological symptoms on April 22, 2025, immediately after they appeared.

In a joint statement after talks on Tuesday, the club and 11WINS, the agency representing Musiala, said: “Both sides agree that the player’s health comes first. Jamal Musiala has their full support on his road to recovery.”

Addressing speculation about the midfielder’s health, they added: “Jamal Musiala was first examined for absence-like symptoms on April 22, 2025. This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical department immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared.”

The statement said Bayern and Musiala’s management had agreed to continue discussions “in a spirit of partnership and confidentiality”.

Musiala has said he was diagnosed with “easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction” after collapsing twice in four days during pre-season.

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl described Tuesday’s meeting as “very, very constructive” and said the club’s priority was helping Musiala return after a muscle injury sustained during the international break.

“That’s the only task FC Bayern has currently, to give Jamal this trust and not some topics about money or something,” Eberl said.

The talks follow debate over the Germany international’s form and his contract, which runs until 2030. Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen had questioned the lucrative extension if Musiala did not return to his best, while former chief executive Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the deal might need to be renegotiated.

Players’ union FIFPRO criticised the club’s public comments, saying an injury or dip in form was no reason to reopen agreed contract terms. Honorary president Uli Hoeness had said Musiala might never regain his previous performance level.

Musiala has made five appearances this season, scoring twice.

World.title: Musawa mourns Pete Edochie, hails cultural legacy
World.content:
The Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musa Musawa, has expressed grief over the death of veteran actor and broadcaster, Chief Pete Edochie, describing him as a national treasure and an outstanding custodian of Nigerian culture.

Edochie reportedly died in the early hours of Wednesday, November 25, 2026, in Enugu, at the age of 79.

In a condolence message, Musawa described the late actor as an “iroko” whose contributions to Nigeria’s film industry, cultural heritage and storytelling tradition would remain indelible.

“I received with great shock and deep sadness the news of the passing of Chief Pete Edochie. This is a painful loss, not only for his family and the creative industry, but for the entire nation. An iroko has fallen,” she said.

The minister said Edochie was more than an actor, noting that he was also a broadcaster, cultural ambassador, teacher and father figure to generations of artists.

She singled out his portrayal of Okonkwo in the film adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart, describing it as one of the most memorable performances in African storytelling.

According to her, Edochie’s interpretation of the character brought Achebe’s literary creation to life for audiences across the world.

Musawa said the actor’s performances in roles portraying traditional rulers, fathers and elders helped project African values, proverbs, wisdom and identity.

“Chief Edochie was a lover of tradition and culture, and the epitome of an African man. From his commanding roles as a traditional ruler, father and elder, he gave voice to our proverbs, our wisdom, our dignity and our identity. He carried Nigeria with pride on screens across Africa and the world,” she said.

The minister noted that Edochie’s death came at a significant moment as Nigeria hosts the 2026 National Festival of Arts and Culture (NAFEST) in Enugu, a celebration of the cultural heritage he spent much of his career promoting.

She said his death in Enugu, during the national cultural festival, underscored his enduring connection to the traditions and heritage of the people.

Musawa added that his legacy would endure through Nigerian films, theatre, language and the young creatives he inspired.

On behalf of the Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy and the National Council for Arts and Culture, the minister extended condolences to Edochie’s wife, Barrister Josephine Edochie; his children, including Leo Edochie; his extended family; the people of Nteje in Anambra State; the Enugu State Government and people; the Actors Guild of Nigeria; and the wider Nollywood community.

“We stand with the family in this moment of grief. We pray for strength and comfort for them, and for the peaceful repose of his soul. Nigeria will honour him, and we will ensure that his contributions to our arts, culture and national identity are never forgotten,” she said.

The condolence statement was signed by Nneka Ikem Anibeze, Special Adviser on Media and Publicity to the minister, and dated November 25, 2026.

World.title: Security operatives bar journalists from Tinubu’s Maiduguri rally
World.content:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

Journalists accredited to cover President Bola Tinubu’s visit and the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally in Maiduguri, Borno State, were on Wednesday denied access to the designated press pavilion by security operatives.

The journalists, drawn from various media organisations, including Vanguard, Daily Trust, Punch, Leadership, The Nation, News Agency of Nigeria (NAN), TVC, News Central, TV360 and Voice of Nigeria, were reportedly prevented from entering the El-Kanemi Sports Centre despite presenting their organisational identity cards and accreditation tags.

The incident occurred as preparations reached their peak ahead of Tinubu’s arrival in the state for the APC rally, where he was scheduled to formally launch his campaign for a second term.

The security personnel involved reportedly comprised operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS) and the Nigerian Army.

Efforts by some senior Borno State Government officials, including the Commissioner for Youth, Sports and Poverty Alleviation, Saina Buba, and the Governor’s Special Adviser, Malam Dauda Iliya, to secure access for the journalists were unsuccessful.

The security operatives reportedly issued conflicting instructions before eventually refusing the journalists entry.

Tension heightened when a soldier allegedly confronted members of the press corps and warned them against insisting on gaining access.

“I have respect for you. You are not going in, you should leave this place before I get angry. I’m a mad man,” the soldier reportedly told the journalists.

Following the confrontation and perceived threat to their safety, the journalists returned to their waiting bus and left the area.

Iliya, who reportedly spent hours trying to negotiate their entry, urged the stranded journalists to remain patient, saying efforts were being made to resolve the situation.

“Sai hakuri (be patient), efforts are being made to sort things out,” he told them before the journalists decided to withdraw from the venue.

Meanwhile, security was significantly tightened across Maiduguri ahead of the presidential visit, with major roads blocked and restrictions imposed on movement.

Schools and businesses were shut, while key routes were largely deserted under the watch of security personnel drawn from the police, Army, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps and the Civilian Joint Task Force.

Ahead of the visit, the Borno State Police Command, through its Public Relations Officer, ASP Nahum Daso, issued a traffic advisory urging residents to avoid major routes and limit non-essential movements.

The advisory listed Airport Road, Kashim Ibrahim Road, Bulumkutu, the International Conference Centre, Shehu’s Palace and Dandal Roundabout among the areas affected by the movement restrictions.

Despite the security measures, a large crowd of APC supporters from the state’s 27 local government areas converged on the El-Kanemi Sports Centre for the rally.

The stadium reportedly filled to capacity, with supporters displaying posters and banners bearing the images of Tinubu, Vice-President Kashim Shettima and Borno State Governor Babagana Zulum, alongside party insignia.

Reacting to the denial of access, Chairman of the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Borno State, Inusa Ndahi, described the incident as unfortunate.

Ndahi said members of the chapel had completed accreditation to cover the event but were prevented by security personnel from accessing the designated press pavilion.

“It’s our constitutional right to cover any political rallies. Sadly, we were forcefully prevented from accessing the press pavilion,” he said.

World.title: Ughelli Killings: Obidient Movement faults police, urges probe
World.content:
Nigeria Police

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Obidient Movement has condemned the November 23 attack on the campaign team of former Deputy President of the Senate and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Delta Central Senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, which reportedly left four persons dead and several others injured.

The movement expressed concern over the security situation in the state, accusing the Nigeria Police Force of failing to prevent attacks on political supporters and calling for an independent investigation into the conduct of officers deployed to the campaign ground.

In a statement on Wednesday signed by its Director of Media and Communications, Onyeka Dike, the movement urged Nigerians to take their personal security seriously while calling on security agencies to ensure the protection of citizens irrespective of their political affiliations.

It alleged that the police had failed to adequately protect opposition supporters during attacks in Delta State and accused some officers of showing bias in their handling of politically related incidents.

The movement said it was particularly concerned that armed attackers reportedly operated at the campaign venue despite the presence of several truckloads of police personnel.

The statement read, “The Obidient Movement strongly condemns the murderous attack on Senator Ovie Omo-Agege and members of his NDC campaign team in Uduere, Ughelli North, Delta State, by APC thugs on November 23, 2026, which left several people dead and others seriously injured, including outspoken activist, Comrade Efemena Umukoro (Akima) and Senator Omo-Agege’s aide, Comrade Moses Anuaghe.”

The movement alleged that the attacks on NDC supporters in Delta State had continued despite the presence of security personnel.

“We are particularly outraged by the conduct of the Nigeria Police Force during yesterday’s attack. Six truckloads of policemen were reportedly at the campaign ground, yet they failed to stop armed men from attacking and killing innocent Nigerians. What exactly were they deployed there to do?” it queried.

It also cited Omo-Agege’s reported suspicion that the policemen deployed to the venue were not there to protect him but to supervise an attempt on his life.

The movement further alleged that the same security personnel had previously taken a different approach when NDC supporters confronted an attacker during an earlier incident.

It also cited allegations by the Omo-Agege campaign organisation identifying Ughelli North Local Government Chairman, Jaro Egbo, as the leader of the attackers, and called for an investigation into the allegation.

The movement claimed that political violence in the state was not an isolated development, recalling an earlier incident in which an AK-47 rifle was reportedly recovered from a suspected political thug.

It questioned the handling of the earlier incident and called for accountability where offences had been established.

The statement also criticised a remark it attributed to President Bola Tinubu that “all is fair in politics”, arguing that political leaders should avoid statements capable of encouraging hostility among supporters.

Calling on the Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, to intervene, the movement demanded the immediate investigation of individuals implicated in the Ughelli attack, including Egbo.

It also requested an independent investigation into the deployment of the six truckloads of police personnel to the campaign venue, including the identities of their commanders and the instructions they received.

The movement said the investigation should establish whether the officers discharged their responsibilities appropriately and whether any lapses contributed to the reported casualties.

It further urged the police to guarantee the safety of political gatherings and ensure that those found culpable in attacks were brought to justice.

The statement added that Nigerians should take reasonable and lawful steps to protect themselves while insisting that the responsibility for maintaining public safety remained with security agencies.

It warned against using political affiliation as a basis for denying citizens their democratic rights, saying no political party or government should tolerate violence against people for supporting opposition candidates.

The movement called on the police leadership to demonstrate impartiality in addressing politically motivated violence and ensure that all allegations arising from the Ughelli incident received an independent and transparent investigation.

World.title: Adesina urges Tinubu to lead $50bn Africa space fund
World.content:
By Peter Oyedele

ABUJA — Former President of the African Development Bank (AfDB), Dr Akinwumi Adesina, has urged President Bola Tinubu to lead efforts to mobilise $50 billion for investment in Africa’s space economy.

Adesina also proposed the establishment of a $50 billion Africa Space Future Fund, with an initial capitalisation target of $5 billion, to finance space science, research, innovation, technology and infrastructure across the continent.

He made the proposal while delivering a keynote address titled, “Financing Africa’s Space Future: Mobilising Capital for Space Science, Innovation and Technology”, at the Africa Space Economy, Innovation and Communication Conference in Abuja.

The conference, organised by the Nigerian Space Research and Development Agency (NASRDA), attracted space agency officials, astronauts, investors and other stakeholders in the global space industry.

Adesina said Africa needed to increase investment in its space sector to avoid being left behind in an industry offering enormous economic and technological opportunities.

He disclosed that Africa had 321 active commercial space companies across 36 countries, generating approximately $373 million in revenue in 2024.

However, he said government allocations to the continent’s space sector stood at about $828 million, compared with approximately $24.4 billion allocated to the United States’ National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) in 2026.

He said the funding disparity highlighted the need for African countries to pool resources and develop the infrastructure and technological capacity required to compete globally.

Commending Tinubu’s ambition to build a $1 trillion Nigerian economy, Adesina also praised the President’s approval of four new satellites for the country’s space programme.

He described the approval as a demonstration of the administration’s recognition of science, technology and innovation as drivers of economic transformation.

“I particularly commend your commitment to Nigeria’s space programme. Your approval of four new Nigerian satellites sends a powerful message. It demonstrates your conviction that science, technology and innovation must drive our economic transformation,” he said.

Tinubu, Kagame, el-Sisi to lead initiative

Adesina called on Tinubu, Rwandan President Paul Kagame and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi to provide the founding political leadership for the proposed Africa Space Future Fund.

He proposed that the three leaders convene a Founding Presidential Summit on Financing Africa’s Space Future to secure political backing, attract initial investment commitments and establish the institutional framework for the initiative.

He also recommended setting up a high-level continental task force, working with the African Union and the African Space Agency, to develop the financial and institutional framework for raising the initial $5 billion.

The proposed fund would attract contributions and investments from African governments, sovereign wealth funds, development finance institutions, pension funds, insurance companies, private investors, international partners and the African diaspora.

Its investment priorities would include satellite communications, broadband connectivity, Earth observation, scientific research, satellite manufacturing, artificial intelligence, robotics and support for African technology startups.

Adesina stressed that the fund should operate with independent governance, professional investment management and transparent accountability.

“This is not a request for charity. It is an investment proposition,” he said.

Africa must own space infrastructure

The former AfDB president also proposed Africa Link, a continental satellite connectivity programme aimed at expanding affordable and reliable internet access through shared infrastructure and strategic partnerships with international satellite operators.

He argued that African countries must move beyond dependence on foreign-owned satellite networks and develop the capacity to own and manage critical space infrastructure.

“We must move from renting the infrastructure of the digital future to owning a meaningful share of it,” he said.

Adesina identified agriculture, food security, telecommunications, climate resilience, disaster management, infrastructure development and natural resource management as sectors where space technology could accelerate economic growth.

Recalling his experience as Nigeria’s Minister of Agriculture in 2012, he explained how satellite imagery and remote sensing helped the government assess the impact of devastating floods and develop a dry-season agricultural programme that helped avert a predicted food crisis.

He said Africa needed to move beyond launching satellites to developing indigenous technologies, manufacturing capacity and businesses capable of generating wealth from the global space economy.

To achieve this, he advocated blended finance, African Space Bonds, public-private partnerships, venture capital and development finance as funding mechanisms.

In a direct appeal to Tinubu, Adesina urged the President to extend his economic transformation ambition to Nigeria’s space programme.

“Mr President, you conquered the Atlantic! With your vision and boldness, why stop there? Now, Mr President, conquer space!” he said.

He expressed optimism that an African would eventually walk on the Moon, adding that he hoped a Nigerian would achieve the historic feat.

Adesina also called for sustained investment in universities, research institutions, young innovators and technological infrastructure, insisting that Africa must transition from consuming imported space technology to developing and exporting its own. He summarised his vision for the continent’s space future in three words: “OWN. CREATE. EXPORT.”

World.title: 2027: South-west Muslims Urged to Vote for President Tinubu
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

As Nigeria prepares for the general election in January 2027, the Chairman, Presidential Campaign Council (Islamic religious affairs), Sheik Abdullah Olohunlomerue, has called on Muslims in the South-west to vote for President Bola Hammed Tinubu.

In a statement issued yesterday, Olohunlomerue said: “Every individual has the right to vote for any candidate of his or her choice; Muslims in the Southwest should consider the following reasons to vote for President Bola Hammed Tinubu.”

He noted that: “In the history of Nigeria, President Bola Hammed Tinubu is the first Muslim to attain the position of president from the entire Southern Nigeria; before him, no Muslim from the Southern Nigeria has ever been President or Vice President in Nigeria, including the military era.”

He recalled that: “ The attempt by Alhaji Moshood Abiola to be president was truncated by the military regime of General Ibrahim Babangida.”

According to him, “If Chief Olusegun Obasanjo can spend eight years as Nigeria’s president when the opportunity came to the Southwest, nothing should stop President Tinubu also spending eight years as Nigeria’s president from the Southwest region.

“It’s a general belief that for any nation to progress, such a nation must pass through a difficult reform that will eventually lead to prosperity and development.

“For President Bola Tinubu to have summoned the courage to initiate some reforms for the betterment of Nigeria, it should be acceptable to Nigerians to endure a little for the reforms to start bringing positive development for Nigeria.

“What Nigeria’s past leaders knew that would benefit Nigerians but could not summon the courage to do is what President Tinubu started doing, and Nigeria has started seeing the results of the reforms in terms of infrastructure.

“President Tinubu is doing wonders. In Osun State, the Ibadan-Ife-Ilesha Road is under construction with concrete pavement, Osogbo-Iwo-Ibadan Road is progressing speedily, and approval has been given for Gbongan-Osogbo Road, while another has been given for Ogbomosho-Ifon Osun-Ilobu Road in Osun State.”

Olohunlomerue stressed that “if all these can be done in just three years plus, definitely if given another four years’ opportunity, a lot will still be done for us in the Southwest, particularly in Osun State. In terms of appointment opportunities, Osun State has never had it so good; several heads of federal agencies are from Osun State, which invariably has led to several federal job opportunities for the state indigenes.”

He added: “Nigerians will soon feel the benefits of fuel subsidy removal. The current hardship is a global phenomenon due to the crisis in the Middle East, and that is why there were protests in several parts of Europe. Before the president finishes his second term in office, Nigerians will appreciate him for the reforms.”

The presidential campaign council (Islamic religion affairs) chairman further recalled that the support given by the president to the National Hajj Commission has always made it possible for Nigerian Muslims to perform Hajj every year with ease.

World.title: Payaza Acquires Seesail Boost  Africa’s SME Ecosystem
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Sunday Okobi

Payaza, a pan-African financial technology company, has acquired Ghana-founded small business commerce platform Seesail Technologies Limited through its commerce subsidiary, Shopaza, in a strategic move aimed at expanding access to digital commerce tools and financial services for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) across Africa.

In a statement issued yesterday by the Chief Marketing Officer of Payaza, Shola Asiru, the company said that the acquisition, whose financial details were not disclosed, would see Seesail’s entire team integrated into Shopaza, while the company’s co-founder and Chief Executive Officer, Victor Blavo, assumes the position of General Manager, Africa.

He noted that the deal is expected to strengthen Shopaza’s capacity to provide small businesses with integrated tools for selling, payment processing, business management, distribution and access to finance.

According to the companies, the acquisition builds on an existing business relationship, as Seesail merchants had previously used Payaza’s payment infrastructure to process transactions, allowing the fintech company’s leadership to monitor Seesail’s growth and operational progress.

The statement quoted Payaza Chief Executive Officer, Seyi Ebenezer, as saying that the acquisition followed the company’s confidence in Seesail’s business model and its potential to transform commerce for small businesses across the continent.

“We watched Seesail from the inside through the payments they ran on Payaza. They built real traction with very little. We believe in the dream, and we are bringing the jet fuel so they can move as fast as they can,” Ebenezer said.

Under the new arrangement, “each Seesail function will retain operational autonomy and receive a dedicated budget from the outset, while benefiting from strategic guidance from Payaza’s chief executive.”

Blavo said Seesail was inspired by his mother’s difficulties in rebuilding her business after relocating from Lagos to Ghana, where limited access to finance and basic business management tools made it difficult for her to re-establish her operations.

He explained that the experience shaped the company’s founding philosophy that providing small businesses with the right tools to sell, monitor operations and grow would ultimately improve their access to financing.

“Seesail started from my mother’s struggle. Tools come first, and finance follows. Shopaza has built strong foundations, and I could not ask for a better partner to help take them further,” he added.

Blavo, who has worked with Nigerian, Ghanaian and international companies, including Chipper Cash, established Seesail through a bootstrapped approach before building it into a growing commerce platform.

His appointment is expected to support Shopaza’s expansion across African markets, combining Seesail’s experience in serving small businesses with Shopaza’s existing commerce infrastructure.

The integration will also enable the combined platform to deepen its focus on addressing challenges confronting African SMEs, particularly limited access to digital business solutions, financing and distribution networks.

Payaza Africa, founded in Lagos in 2022, provides payment infrastructure covering collections, payouts, embedded finance and digital commerce. The company serves small businesses and large enterprises across Africa, North America, Europe, the Middle East and Oceania.

It has presence in 31 countries across the world, and operates or maintains regulatory registrations in several markets, including Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Uganda, Canada, the United States and New Zealand.

Shopaza, its commerce platform, provides small and growing businesses with tools to sell online and in physical stores, accept payments and manage business operations from a single platform.

Seesail Technologies, founded in Ghana, is built around the idea that accessible commerce tools can help small businesses establish sustainable operations and improve their prospects of securing finance.

The acquisition marks another development in efforts to strengthen Africa’s SME ecosystem through the integration of financial technology, digital commerce and business management solutions.

World.title: CeBIH, NIMC  to Deepen Digital Identity Integration in Financial Services
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Nume Ekeghe

The Committee of e-Business Industry Heads (CeBIH) has identified gaps in Nigeria’s digital identity infrastructure as a major barrier to expanding financial inclusion, strengthening transaction security and improving access to financial services.

The industry group said reliable identity verification remained critical to the sustainability of Nigeria’s rapidly expanding digital payments ecosystem, particularly as more Nigerians embrace digital banking and other financial technology services.

The Chairman of CeBIH, Mrs. Abidemi Asunmo, stated this in Lagos at a press conference to announce the 2026 CeBIH Annual Conference organised in partnership with the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC).

The conference, scheduled for December 1 and 2 at the Eko Convention Centre, Lagos, will focus on the theme: ‘Digital Identity: A Catalyst for Financial Inclusion, Trust and Growth’.

Asunmo said the collaboration with NIMC is aimed at strengthening the connection between Nigeria’s national identity infrastructure and the financial services industry, noting that individuals without adequate identity documentation often face difficulties accessing bank accounts, credit, insurance and other essential financial services.

She argued that the conversation around digital identity must extend beyond enrolment figures to address how effectively identity infrastructure is utilised across the economy.

“These are some of the reasons why we believe the conversation around digital identity must move beyond enrolment numbers to focus on utilization, interoperability, security, accessibility and the real value identity infrastructure delivers to citizens and the economy,” she said.

She also highlighted the significance of the NIMC Act 2026, signed into law by President Bola Tinubu on June 26, saying the legislation provided an important foundation for strengthening identity verification and authentication systems.

According to her, reliable digital identity systems could simplify customer onboarding and Know Your Customer (KYC) processes, strengthen confidence in digital transactions and widen access to financial services.

“Our partnership with NIMC is therefore designed to promote dialogue, knowledge exchange and stronger institutional collaboration around the practical integration of trusted digital identity into financial services,” she said.

Asunmo added that the conference would bring together policymakers, regulators, financial institutions, fintech companies, payment service providers and identity management experts to examine practical solutions to challenges affecting Nigeria’s digital identity ecosystem.

She stressed that building a trusted identity infrastructure required sustained collaboration between government, regulators and private-sector players, adding that the conference would provide an opportunity to identify areas of cooperation and advance the country’s digital economy.

The conference is expected to attract several government and industry leaders, including the Director-General of NIMC, Engr. Abisoye Coker-Odusote; Executive Chairman of the Nigeria Revenue Service, Dr Zach Adedeji; National Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, Dr Vincent Olatunji; Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service, Kemi Nanna Nandap; and Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority, Dr Kelechi Ohiri. Others expected include the Postmaster-General of the Nigeria Postal Service, Tola Odeyemi; Registrar and Chief Executive of JAMB, Professor Segun Aina; Managing Director of NIBSS, Premier Oiwoh; Director of Payment System Policy Department at the Central Bank of Nigeria, Musa Jimoh; Dr Rakiya Opemi Yusuf of the CBN’s Payment System Supervision Department; and Managing Director of Payment Processing and Switching at Interswitch, Akeem Lawal.

World.title: PAP Distributes More Laptops to Scholarship Beneficiaries
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

The Presidential Amnesty Programme (PAP) has distributed an additional 1,282 laptops to beneficiaries of its scholarship scheme in Nigerian universities.

The two-week exercise conducted this month was the fourth phase of the initiative by the PAP Administrator, Dr Dennis Brutu Otuaro.

Among the many institutions covered in the exercise were the Achievers University, Elizade University, Lead City University, Afe Babalola University, Gregory University, Lux Mundi University, Wigwe University, and Ritman University.

Commenting, Dr Otuaro noted that the initiative underscored his unwavering commitment to equipping the scholarship students with a vital tool to aid their learning, research, and academic performance.

He urged them to utilise the computer device diligently and also take their studies seriously.

He said: “Education is a critical driver of socio-economic transformation, sustainable peace, development in the Niger Delta; and a laptop is an essential tool that will enhance learning, research and academic excellence by our scholarship students.

“The computer device will also enhance their digital literacy, innovation and personal growth because, today, education and industries have become much more technologically driven across the world.

“We will continue to do our best for our scholarship beneficiaries under the mandate of President Bola Tinubu to build a solid foundation for the future of the Niger Delta and the country, knowing that education is the vehicle that will enable us to achieve it.”

Otuaro expressed appreciation to President Tinubu for strengthening human capital development, sustainable peace and development in the Niger Delta with his massive support for the PAP under his Renewed Hope Agenda.

He stated that the unmatched 13,300 onshore and more than 500 offshore scholarship deployments since his appointment by President Tinubu, and the laptops given to beneficiaries, would not have been possible without the president’s unshaken commitment to the programme.

While also extending his gratitude to the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, for his effective supervision of the programme, the PAP helmsman also thanked stakeholders for their consistent support and encouragement.

Otuaro equally reiterated his call on people of the Niger Delta to remain steadfast in their support for President Tinubu and vote for him in the 2027 general elections to continue with his good plans for the region.

Some of the students, including Aaron Ogheneruruo (Lead City University), Emikonde Cecilia (Gregory University), Ebimobowei Tamaradoubra (Achievers University), and Fuwe Oke (Ritman University), thanked the President and Dr Otuaro for educational empowerment and promised to study very well.

World.title: Tinubu Govt Determined to Deepen Relations with EU,  Says Enang
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Segun James

The Nigerian Ambassador to the Federal Republic of Germany, Senator Ita Enang, has told the leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Germany Chapter, that the President Bola Tinubu government is determined to deepen political and economic relations with the European Union.

He emphasised the importance of deepening economic relations, strengthening international partnerships, and creating opportunities that will accelerate Nigeria’s economic growth and sustainable development.

Enang, who stated this during a dinner meeting with the APC leadership, stressed that the nation has seen significant progress in the last four years.

He also highlighted ongoing efforts to attract increased European investment into Nigeria.

In his remarks, the APC Germany Chairman, Jide Fashakin, underscored the importance of closer collaboration between the party and the Nigerian Embassy, particularly in identifying and harnessing the expertise, technical knowledge, and international experience of Nigerian professionals living in Germany.

He noted that strategic partnerships could establish effective platforms for connecting skilled Nigerians in the Diaspora with institutions, businesses, and development initiatives back home, thereby promoting knowledge transfer, investment opportunities, technology exchange, and national development.

Enang reaffirmed his willingness to support broader engagement among APC chapters across Europe and promote greater pan-European solidarity.

The meeting was further enriched by the presence of other distinguished stakeholders, including the Chairman of APC Poland, Hon. Adekunle Ayoola; the National Secretary of APC Netherlands, Hon. Kayode Opadola; and former Chairman of NIDO Germany and European Director of Renewed Hope Ambassadors, Otunba Tony Akinyemi.

The gathering reaffirmed the collective commitment to constructive political engagement, community mobilisation, and support for the federal government’s Renewed Hope Agenda, particularly the Tinubu-Shettima 2027 Re-election Project, under the spirit of ‘Uniting for Progress and Democratic Strength’.

Furthermore, members of APC Germany and other distinguished Nigerians preparing to travel to Nigeria as part of a Diaspora delegation assured the ambassador of their unwavering commitment to mobilising support for the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima in 2027.

They expressed confidence in the administration’s ongoing reforms, describing them as necessary steps towards repositioning Nigeria, strengthening its economy, attracting investment, and restoring the country’s standing among the comity of nations.

APC Germany believes that sustained diaspora participation, strategic mobilisation, and collective commitment will play an important role in consolidating the gains of the Renewed Hope Agenda.

APC Germany sincerely appreciated Senator Enang for his exceptional hospitality, encouragement, openness, and continued commitment to Nigeria’s progress.

“We look forward to sustained engagement, stronger institutional partnerships, and practical initiatives that will deliver meaningful benefits to Nigeria and Nigerians at home and abroad,” it stated.

World.title: Supreme Court Revelation: Resign Now or Be Impeached, ADC Tells Tinubu
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has called on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to immediately resign from office or be impeached.

The party made the following statement by the Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, suggesting that President Tinubu may have interfered with the Supreme Court judgment in the 2023 Kano State governorship election based on the governor’s agreement to switch to the president’s party, the All Progressives Congress (APC).

In a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC said the governor’s revelations during his recent BBC Hausa interview indicate that the president may have committed a serious breach of Section 413 of the 1999 Constitution, which made “gross misconduct” the basis for the president’s removal from office.

ADC said: “No conduct can be more heinous on the part of a democratically elected president than to make the administration of justice an instrument of political bargaining. No betrayal of the presidential oath can be more profound than to pervert the cause of justice in pursuit of personal political advantage.

“In plain language, what Governor Yusuf admitted to was that the President of Nigeria, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, got the highest court in the land to award him justice in exchange for him to decamp to the APC. This is a very grave allegation that undermines every principle regarding the rule of law, independence of the judiciary, and, indeed, the fight against corruption.”

The party consequently called on the National Assembly to initiate impeachment proceedings and ensure that all parties to the alleged arrangement are made to provide evidence.

“The Supreme Court is not an extension of the APC national secretariat, and the president of Nigeria is not the proprietor of the Nigerian judiciary. With this revelation, the president has signalled to the rest of the world, including investors, that the rule of law is dead in Nigeria and that the Supreme Court of Nigeria is actually pliant to the political whims of the president. What a shame!”

The ADC, therefore, challenged the National Assembly to demonstrate whether its allegiance is to the president or to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

World.title: Alleged Cyberbullying: DSS Asks Court to Foreclose Sowore’s Defence For Exceeding Adjournment Ceiling
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

The Department of State Services (DSS) on Tuesday asked the Federal High Court in Abuja to make an order foreclosing the defence of African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, in his ongoing trial for alleged cyberbullying.

Counsel to the DSS, Akinlolu Kehinde, SAN, informed Justice Mohammed Umar shortly before adjournment, that an application had been filed to the effect.

Kehinde told the court that Sowore’s legal team had already been served with the application.

The senior lawyer, who submitted that Sowore exceeded the five adjournments he is entitled to in criminal trial by nine, said there must be an end to this.

“Before we finally draw the curtain to the proceedings, I want to bring to your lordship notice the application we filed and and served on the defendant.

“The application is that, there must be an end to all these. The defendant has since exceeded the number of adjournments as required by law,” he said.

He urged the court to allow the application to be taken.

In the motion on notice filed on November 23 by Kehinde, the DSS sought two orders.

The security agency sought an order of the court ordering the closure of the case for the defence.

It also sought an order directing the parties to file and exchange their final written addresses within such time as the court shall direct, and fix a date for the adoption of the said addresses.

Giving a nine-ground argument, the lawyer said Sowore was in the suit and was re-arraigned on a two-count charge on which he pleaded not guilty on January 19, 2026, and thereafter the trial commenced.

He said the DSS called its witness and closed its case in March 2026, and the defendant’s no-case submission was overruled on May 8, 2026 and he was called upon to enter his defence.

The lawyer said Sowore, as particularised in the affidavit in support of the motion, sought or procured an adjournment of the proceedings on at least 14 occasions.

He said eight of the adjournments were sought since he was called upon to enter his defence.

“This is far in excess of the five (5) adjournments to which a party is entitled under Section 396(4) of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, 2015.

“Since the defendant/respondent opened his defence on 6th July 2026, the trial has not progressed beyond the evidence of two defence witnesses,” he said.

Kehinde said Sowore has repeatedly filed applications and processes which had the effect of stalling the trial, including the subpoena issued against him, the lead counsel to the complainant/applicant.

He said the court had on several occasions warned Sowore against further delay.

According to him, the right to fair hearing guaranteed by Section 36 of the Constitution is a right to an opportunity to be heard, not a right to an unlimited number of adjournments.

He argued that a defendant who has been afforded ample opportunity to present his defence and fails to use it cannot complain of a breach of that right.

‘Section 36(4) of the Constitution guarantees a fair hearing within a reasonable time, and the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, 2015 requires that criminal trials proceed from day to day or, where that is impracticable, within the strict limits on adjournments prescribed by Section 396 of the ACJA.”

Kehinde urged the court to grant the application in the interest of justice.

Responding, Reuben Adakole, who appeared for Sowore, acknowledged the receipt of the application seeking to foreclose their defence.

Adakole, however, said that before the prosecution’s application could be taken, the court needs to deliver its ruling on the objection raised by Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Chairman, against their subpoena, including their preliminary objection and ex-parte motion.

“In as much as the application tends to foreclose us, there is our application which the court ought to pronounce on first. Until after the ruling, we can look at it. The application is unripe my lord,” he said.

Kehinde, however, corrected Adakole’s impression that the prosecution’s request was to get a date to hear the application seeking the foreclosure of Sowore’s case.

World.title: Former PDP Leader, Burga, Emerges Bauchi APM Chairman
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Segun Awofadeji in Bauchi

The former Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Bauchi State, Samaila Adamu Burga, has emerged as the new state chairman of the Allied People’s Movement (APM).

Burga emerged as chairman with other executives at the APM state congress held last Sunday in Bauchi, which was presided over by the National Secretary of the party, Oyadeyi Ayodele Adebayo, who served as the returning officer.

The congress, which drew delegates from the 20 local government areas of the state, affirmed Burga and other members of the State Executive Committee through voice vote.

Presenting the nominated candidates for affirmation, Adebayo called out Burga first for the position of chairman to loud applause from delegates.

After presenting all the nominees, the returning officer put the question to the delegates three times.

The delegates responded in the affirmative, shouting “Yes”.

Announcing the result, Adebayo said: “As we await the coming of the INEC representative, I hereby, as the returning officer, return all these eminent young and old men and women to serve in the Bauchi State APM chapter.”

Burga’s emergence marks a major political realignment in Bauchi State, coming after his exit as the PDP state chairman.

In his acceptance speech, the newly elected chairman pledged to serve with honesty and transparency, and never to use party funds for personal use.

“Today, before God and you all, I make these pledges: I pledge to serve with honesty and transparency. I pledge to run an open-door administration. I pledge never to use party funds for my personal use. I pledge never to betray the trust you have given me today. I pledge to carry everyone along, whether you voted for me or not,” he said.

He said the victory was not his alone but belonged to every delegate who travelled from all 10 local government areas, every ward chairman, every local government chairman, and all members that form the structure of the party.

Burga paid special tribute to the state Governor, Senator Bala Mohammed, whom he described as the great leader of the Kaura movement.

“Your Excellency, we thank you for your visionary leadership, for your guidance and unwavering commitment to peace, unity and development of Bauchi State,” he said.

He said the governor’s love for the common man and dedication to good governance have given hope to the youths, women and the entire people of Bauchi State.

“Your Excellency, Bauchi State has witnessed infrastructural development, improved education, better healthcare, empowerment of women and youths, and a new spirit of unity. You have shown that leadership is about service, not about power,” he said.

Burga said in the past seven years, Bauchi State has seen serious transformation under the leadership of Senator Bala Mohammed.

He said as the leader of the Kaura movement, the governor has built a family, not just a political structure; a family that listens, leaders who care, and a government that keeps its promise.

Describing APM as a party of the people, justice, equity, and progress, Burga said the party is where the farmer in Ningi, the trader in Bauchi market, the student in ATBU, the teacher in Misau, and the mother in Dass all have a voice.

He invited all Bauchi people to join the party, irrespective of religion or tribe.

“To the good people of Bauchi State, APM is your party. Whether you are a Muslim or Christian, Hausa, Fulani, Jarawa, Sayawa, or whatever your tribe, you are welcome here. Bauchi is one. Our diversity is our strength,” he said.

World.title: What happens if the Springboks-France final ends in a draw?
World.content:
The Springboks and France, having finished top of their respective hemisphere standings, meet in the Grand Final to determine the inaugural Nations Championship winners in London this Sunday.

Just a couple of weeks ago, France got the better of South Africa in a thrilling clash in Paris, and it is notable that five out of the last six games between these sides has been decided by a margin of five points or less.

In case Sunday’s final ends in a draw after 80 minutes, it’s worth knowing that the title decider has its own tie-break process compared to the rest of the Nations Championship.



What will happen iff France and the Springboks are level after 80 minutes?

Two 10-minute periods of Golden Point extra time will be played (with the first team to score declared the winner). If the teams still cannot be separated, the Nations Championship winner will be decided by a place-kicking contest.

Meanwhile, in the other five ranking matches, tied games go to 10 minutes of Golden Point extra time, with the first team to score declared the winner.

If neither side scores during the Golden Point period, the match is officially recorded as a draw and the Hemisphere Shield point available from that fixture is shared.

Fortune has favoured South Africa

Despite losing their last two games, the Springboks managed to still sneak into the final, thanks in large due to the shock defeat the All Blacks suffered against Wales.



On Tuesday, assistant coach Tony Brown said they knew what they had to do turn things around to hopefully win the inaugural trophy at the Allianz Stadium, Twickenham this weekend.

“It’s obviously never good to lose a Test match, and it’s not great to lose two in a row (following the defeat against Ireland), so the team is hurting and we want to perform better,” said Brown.

“At the end of the day, if you’re in a final, you’re in it, and the best team will win on the day, so our preparation and thoughts are only on Sunday and making sure we perform better than we have in the last two weeks.”



Brown shared the other coaches’ sentiments that the Boks did not perform to the best of their ability in the last two matches, but he was confident they could turn things around in the final.

“This week we’ve placed a massive focus on executing in every situation on attack,” said the former All Black flyhalf.

“We want to get back to what makes us a good rugby team — not just on attack, but being strong at set piece time, defensively, in the air, and on the ground. Every momentum shift is going to be massive in the final, and all the different parts of your game have to work if you want to win.”



The final kicks off at 18:40 (SA time) and will be broadcast live on SuperSport.

World.title: The KZN property hotspots attracting buyers from Gauteng
World.content:
KwaZulu-Natal’s North Coast is increasingly attracting people looking to relocate, buy their first home or invest in property.

The coastal stretch from uMhlanga to Ballito and further north offers a range of property options, with prices varying according to location, size and type of home.

According to property experts, one-bedroom apartments on the North Coast can cost between R1 million and R1.5 million, while two- and three-bedroom units generally range from R2 million to R3 million.



THE kzn AREAS ATTRACTING BUYERS

uMhlanga remains an established residential and investment market, supported by its proximity to shopping centres, business areas, healthcare facilities and the beach.

It also attracts people relocating from Gauteng, some of whom initially rent for a year before deciding whether to buy.

Sibaya, between uMhlanga and Ballito, has emerged as another important growth area as development expands along the coastal corridor.

Ballito, also an established residential destination, is attracting both permanent residents and people looking for coastal property.

Further north, residential development is expanding into areas including Salt Rock, Sheffield Beach, Shaka’s Rock and Tinley Manor.

Investment in infrastructure, schools, healthcare, retail and other amenities is supporting the North Coast’s shift from a largely holiday-focused destination towards a more established residential area.



What buyers should consider

The North Coast offers different entry points for buyers. According to Pam Golding Properties, a budget of around R1 million may be enough for a one-bedroom apartment, while R1.5 million to R2 million can open up options for larger two-bedroom units.

However, buyers should look beyond the purchase price and consider ongoing expenses such as levies, rates, insurance and maintenance.

Location is also important. Access to employment opportunities, schools, transport routes and everyday services can be just as significant as proximity to the beach.

For investors, the potential rental market should be considered carefully, including whether demand is likely to continue outside the holiday season.

World.title: Bad news on former Kaizer Chiefs star against FC Barcelona
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs’ former centre-back McCarthy is facing a two-match UEFA suspension.

The 22-year-old was sent off in Sabah’s 4-1 loss away to Viking FK.

McCarthy was first yellow carded in the 77th minute.



The VAR did a review to overturn the yellow into a red card.

The Kaizer Chiefs academy graduate’s tackle on Peter Christiansen had studs-up. UEFA subsequently extended his automatic one-match suspension to two games.

To his disappointment, McCarthy miss the Barcelona encounter at Baku Olympic Stadium at 19:45.

His last match to miss will be Sabah’s trip to Spain against Villarreal on 8 December.

He is expected to return against Napoli on 20 January 2027.

ADEN MCCARTHY’S RISE FROM KAIZER CHIEFS TO EUROPE

McCarthy came through the Kaizer Chiefs youth academy and the club’s DStv Diski Challenge reserve team before making his senior debut in May 2025.



Born on 4 December 2003, the 1.86-metre defender became a regular in the Amakhosi defence during the 2025/26 campaign.

He made 33 appearances across all competitions, scoring twice as Chiefs finished third in the Betway Premiership and secured qualification for the CAF Confederation Cup.

His departure also marked another chapter in the McCarthy family’s association with Naturena. His father, Fabian McCarthy, previously played as a central defender for Kaizer Chiefs and Bafana Bafana.

On 9 June 2026, Chiefs completed Aden’s transfer to Azerbaijani champions Sabah FK on a three-year contract. He became the second Kaizer Chiefs youth product to join the Baku-based club after Hendrick Ekstein.

SABAH FK FACE BARCELONA WITHOUT FORMER CHIEFS STAR

McCarthy’s suspension comes at a significant stage of Sabah’s Champions League campaign, having established himself as an important member of Valdas Dambrauskas’ defensive setup.

The South African started all four of Sabah’s opening league-phase matches and completed 90 minutes against Manchester United, Slavia Prague and Borussia Dortmund.

He also registered his first UEFA Champions League goal on 20 October 2026. The former Kaizer Chiefs defender scored with a first-half header during Sabah’s 2-1 home defeat against Borussia Dortmund.

World.title: SHOCKING: Pink effluent spills into sea at popular Cape Town swim spot [video]
World.content:
A mysterious, pink discharge was seen flowing into the sea at one of Cape Town's main swimming beaches. Image: @beradstern

A shocking pink-coloured effluent was filmed streaming into the sea at Saunders Rocks over the weekend, and concerned residents raised the alarm. Here’s what we know.

Members of a local Saunders WhatsApp group shared photos and videos of the discharge on Saturday. It appeared to flow from a stormwater outlet near the main stairway.

Saunders Rocks is a small, scenic beach with a sheltered tidal pool at the southern end of Sea Point, bordering Bantry Bay in Cape Town along Beach Road.



Adjacent to the tidal pool is a protected gully that is known as a popular swimming spot. Effluent from the storm drain flows directly into this gully.

What we know about the pink effluent

One member on the group posted: “Whatever it is…it is unacceptable!” Another asked whether the flow could be tracked, calling it “unbelievably unconscious behaviour.”

A witness left a message for Sea Fisheries and alerted the Sea Point CID. The CID, they said, had “promised to notify the authorities.”

The National Sea Rescue Institute (NSRI) was also alerted. An NSRI representative replied that City law enforcement and the environment department were “rushing to go see what it is.”

Soon, speculation was rife, with one member suggesting the pink outflow was the result of “paint being tipped down a storm water drain” by a contractor.

Another witness reported similarly-coloured water pooling at the bottom of a nearby road. Painting and renovation work appeared to be under way at a property on this road.



Eventually, a concerned resident took a sample, saying: “Will test and report back.”

After a follow-up, it was revealed that the mystery substance was in fact paint.

“It smelt of paint…it was confirmed,” the resident told The South African. “The place that caused this unfortunate toxic spill, has been located. Hopefully there will be consequences.”

A sample of the mystery pink substance was taken. Image: Supplied

Outfalls and water quality

According to locals, this is not the first time off-colour or odd-smelling runoff has reached the gully at Saunders where people swim.

It has joined the larger conversation around water quality along Cape Town’s Atlantic Seaboard.

Saunders Rocks lies between two of Cape Town’s three marine outfalls, at Green Point and Camps Bay. Together they pump millions of litres of “screened” sewage offshore daily.

Wind and tides have been known to bring this polluted water into contact with bathers.

The City insists the outfalls operate largely within regulatory limits, though activists have long challenged the practice.

Going by the City’s latest coastal water quality dashboard, Saunders’ tidal pool is rated ‘excellent’ for the summer and good over five years.

The City’s new coastal water quality sampling regime sees key recreational nodes along Cape Town’s coastline sampled weekly, monthly, or twice a month.

The raw data is presented in water quality reports, that are available on the City’s website.

A separate “Outside” sampling point for Saunders however is rated ‘poor’ over five years, with 87% compliance. It last failed a water quality test outright on 4 May 2026.

Reports have tied the Saunders poor ratings to stormwater, not to the outfalls.

World.title: HSBC Sevens: Champion Blitzboks chasing three-peat in Dubai
World.content:
The Blitzboks have a tough opening game in HSBC Sevens in Dubai. Image: South Africa Rugby.

The Blitzboks begin defending their double world champion status this weekend.

HSBC Sevens is back on 28 and 29 November, with South Africa facing a tough first game.

Here are the details on the first round of the series ahead of kickoff on Saturday.



Blitzboks ready to defend their title

The Blitzboks are chasing a three-peat after back-to-back world title victories.

Last season’s series was a testament to the resilience of South Africa’s sevens squad.

After a fifth-place finish in Dubai, the Blitzboks went on to win four of the next five events.



They claimed gold in Cape Town, Perth, Vancouver, and New York, and finished fourth in Singapore.

In the Grand Finals, South Africa won gold in Hong Kong and silver in Spain.

Despite a fourth-place finish in the final event in France, the Blitzboks won the world championship.



This marked a successful defence after powering to the title in the 2024/25 SVNS season.

Coach Philip Snyman was proud of their efforts, as quoted by South Africa Rugby in June this year:

“We did not always play our best rugby, but our effort could never be faulted.” 

Sevens season kicks off in Dubai

The new campaign begins at The Sevens Stadium in Dubai, according to the competition website.

Australia face the USA first, followed by the Blitzboks against the hard-running Argentina (09:52 kickoff).

South Africa also face Aussie 7s at 12:55 and America at 17:38 in the pool stage.



The semifinals and playoffs are all scheduled for 29 November, and the Blitzboks will be aiming to start strong.

The team arrived in the UAE this week and knows the pressure is on their shoulders.

Forward Ryan Oosthuizen said, as quoted by South Africa Rugby:



“Every match is like a final, so you cannot afford mistakes. For us, being defending series champions might put a target on our backs, but we don’t mind. We were down and out a couple of seasons back, and I don’t want to experience that feeling ever again.”

After Dubai, the next event is in Cape Town on 5 and 6 December.

This will be followed by Singapore (30-31 January), Perth (6-7 February), Vancouver (6-7 March), and New York (13-14 March).



The HSBC Sevens World Championship events are scheduled for April and May 2027.

World.title: Springboks suffer major blow ahead of France final
World.content:
Earlier this week, the Springboks named Pieter-Steph du Toit in the starting side for this Sunday’s Nations Championship final against France.

Unfortunately for South Africa, it’s now been confirmed that the star loose forward has been forced to withdraw from the matchday squad, and will head home.

The reason for Du Toit’s withdrawal was said to be due to a niggle, but it will raise questions over whether it was caused by the blow to the head suffered during the clash against Ireland in what looked to be a clear case of foul play.



MAJOR BLOW FOR SPRINGBOKS

Du Toit had to leave the field for a Head Impact Assessment as a result of a ‘cheap shot’ from Ireland centre Stuart McCloskey at a ruck when he clearly thrust a knee out in frustration, which appeared to catch the South African on the shoulder and side of the head.

Erasmus will announce the changes to the match-23 to face Les Bleus later in the week once he has decided whether to call up a replacement player to London.

Not implying Ireland didn't deserve the win…

But if the referee saw this, and didn't blow him up for it, is this not match fixing? #IREvRSA pic.twitter.com/EHckRls2ck  November 23, 2026

ANOTHER PLAYER HEADS BACK TO SA

Meanwhile, Damian Willemse will also return to South Africa. The fullback was not named in the matchday squad on Monday for the inaugural competition final due to the knock he took in last weekend’s clash against Ireland in Dublin.

World.title: ATM considering legal option after Phala Phala report set aside
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - African Transformation Movement (ATM) leader, Vuyo Zungula says they will, along with other parties, be looking at their legal options.

This comes after the Western Cape High Court set aside the Section 89 panel report on Phala Phala, declaring it unlawful.

Zungula says they will be engaging their legal teams to carve out a way forward. He says the judgment has to be appealed as it sets a "dangerous" precedent.

"The facts of Phala Phala have not yet been established," says Zungula.

"It is the duty of Parliament to establish those facts," he adds.

Meanwhile, the ANC, on the other hand, welcomed the judgment.

"It is a very clear and decisive judgment that validates the concerns we had in 2022," says the party's Cameron Dugmore.

"The President, like any other citizen, has applied his rights," he added.

World.title: Springboks' Du Toit out of Nations Championship final
World.content:
DUBLIN - Springboks' flanker Pieter-Steph du Toit has been ruled out of the Nations Championship final against France and will return to South Africa with Damian Willemse, coach Rassie Erasmus announced Wednesday.

Erasmus said Du Toit, a two-time World Cup winner and twice world player of the year, was being withdrawn from Sunday's showpiece match at Twickenham because of a "niggle".

Du Toit was involved in a clash with Ireland centre Stuart McCloskey during South Africa's 20-17 defeat in Dublin on Saturday, but Wednesday's announcement from the Springboks made no mention of that incident.

The 34-year-old had been included in the South Africa starting side for the final unveiled on Monday.

Erasmus will announce changes to the match-day 23 to face France later in the week, once he has decided whether to call up a replacement player.

Full-back Willemse was not named in the 23 on Monday for the inaugural Nations Championship final following an injury he suffered against Ireland.

The Springboks are trying to avoid a third successive loss. A 21-19 pool-stage defeat by France in Paris preceded the match against Ireland.

World.title: WC High Court rules in favour of Ramaphosa, sets aside Phala Phala impeachment report
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The Western Cape High Court has set aside the Section 89 panel’s report on Phala Phala, declaring it unlawful.

Western Cape Judge President Nolwazi Mabindla-Boqwana handed down the ruling on Wednesday, also setting aside all steps taken by Parliament’s Impeachment Committee pursuant to the report.

The court said the panel went beyond its mandate and made errors in attempting to apply the law.

The Section 89 independent panel, chaired by former Chief Justice Sandile Ngcobo, concluded in 2022 that President Cyril Ramaphosa had a case to answer over the theft of foreign currency from his Phala Phala game farm.

READ | Two accused in Phala Phala Farm theft found guilty of housebreaking

It found prima facie evidence that Ramaphosa may have violated the Constitution and the law.

Ramaphosa subsequently approached the court to challenge the findings, seeking an order to review and set aside the report. The matter was heard in September.

In July, he secured an interdict preventing the impeachment committee from holding public hearings pending the outcome of his review application.

World.title: London museum makes 'miraculous' move to former meat market
World.content:
LONDON - The London Museum, a free museum telling the story of the British capital, reopens this week in former meat market buildings transformed into an exhibition space.

The museum has relocated from a dated 1970s-era site to a 19th-century brick building formerly part of the Smithfield Market in central London, in a project costing £437 million ($570 million).

The atmospheric new space, which incorporates objects from the last 2,000 years, opens to the public Saturday.

"It's thrilling to see people in the museum," Sharon Ament the museum's director, told AFP at a press preview Tuesday.

She called the completed building "miraculous and I think, much needed: we've got this great new museum for London."

On the ground floor a huge open space with brick walls and iron columns has seating and places to eat and shop.

This is intended to be "a great big indoor public square," Ament told AFP.

"I think this is a new model for a museum, and it's all come about because of the market buildings themselves. I couldn't imagine that we would have ever designed a museum like this from scratch."

The displays reflect recent history: a bike courier's outfit, Indian ready meals and a horse-drawn coffee stall donated by the family who ran it for 100 years.

One display commemorates Grenfell Tower, a block of flats in west London where 72 people were killed in a fire in 2017, with a sign saying the community there "have yet to see the change that they are owed".

Shop signs on the walls come from businesses including Top Shop fashion retailer whose store on Oxford Street closed in 2021.

Most spectacular is the Lord Mayor's gilded coach, used for an annual parade.

"When we were offered these buildings in 2015, we thought it would be the perfect home," said Alec Shaw, the museum manager who oversaw the move.

- 'Same fears, same hopes' -

"It's this incredible set of buildings with amazing architecture but also located right in the middle of the city."

But the site had been disused since the 1990s and was "dripping everywhere", Shaw told AFP. Just restoring the glass roof took about three years.

Smithfield Market, the last major food market in central London, is gradually closing down and the last traders are due to move out in the next few years.

World.title: 'Sufficient' or 'prima facie'? The legal question hanging over Ramaphosa
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Western Cape High Court ruling on President Cyril Ramaphosa's section 89 impeachment will boil down to whether the right verbiage was used in the report's findings.

In addition, whether the Impeachment Committee understood the word 'sufficient' to mean the same thing as 'prima facie' evidence, says legal expert Jazz Vilakazi.

The Western Cape High Court is expected to deliver judgment on the President's application to review and overturn the panel's report, which found prima facie evidence that he may have violated the Constitution and the law.

The findings followed an investigation into the theft of foreign currency from his Phala Phala game farm in February 2020.

World.title: Mlambo-Ngcuka remembered for her leadership, vision and service
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Former deputy president Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka still had more to give towards the betterment of the country.

This is the view of Special Mother Dr Hlophe Bam who paid tribute to Mlambo-Ngcuka at a memorial service in Rivonia on Tuesday.

Bam praised Mlambo-Ngcuka for her skills and her leadership.

“I am disappointed; I'm hurt that she didn't get the position as president of this country. Phumzile left us so early, she had many plans [for the] country, and to make sure that we get out of this problem."

Family, friends and dignitaries gathered to remember the former deputy president and head of UN Women.

She died on Friday after complications from a medical procedure.

World.title: Malema awaits judgment in bid to gag Zille over alleged Joburg corruption claims
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Gauteng High Court in Johannesburg is expected to deliver judgment before Friday in an application by Julius Malema and the EFF to interdict DA leader Helen Zille from repeating allegations linking the party's leader to alleged corruption in the City of Joburg.

Advocate Mfesane Ka-Siboto, representing Malema and the EFF, argued that Zille’s statements undermined Malema’s dignity and reputation. He accused her of making serious allegations without sufficient evidence to substantiate them.

The applicants want the court to prevent Zille from repeating or publishing claims that Malema allegedly influenced major decisions during Herman Mashaba’s tenure as Johannesburg mayor, including allegations relating to City Power and the city’s fleet tenders.

Antony Stein SC, representing Zille, argued that political speech and public-interest debate should be protected, particularly during election campaigns and coalition negotiations. He submitted that Zille had a reasonable basis for her claims, relying on media reports and other material.

Stein further argued that granting the interdict would unduly restrict Zille’s freedom of expression and that Malema had failed to demonstrate that he would suffer irreparable harm. He urged the court to dismiss the application with costs.

The judge said he intended to hand down judgment before Friday so that both parties would know where they stood.



Report by Dikeledi Ramabula

World.title: Scammers are shopping for victims this Black Friday – and AI is helping
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - As Black Friday bargains begin to roll out, consumers are being urged to stay alert as fraudsters ramp up their efforts to exploit the shopping frenzy.

From fake promotional offers and online stores to fraudulent delivery notifications, scammers are finding increasingly sophisticated ways to trick unsuspecting shoppers into handing over their personal and banking details.

And artificial intelligence (AI) is making the threat even harder to detect.

Bonolo Sebolai, Head of Fraud at GoTyme Bank, says fake websites designed to replicate legitimate retailers have reached a new and worrying level of sophistication, with AI allowing fraudsters to create convincing platforms in a matter of hours.

READ | Spar blames KZN woes and a bad Black Friday for losses

Among the scams consumers should be particularly aware of are fake delivery notifications, which typically target people who are expecting a parcel.

Scammers send messages claiming that a delivery is waiting, often prompting recipients to click on a link to confirm details or arrange delivery.

Promotional scams are another growing concern, with fraudsters using fake bargains and special offers to lure shoppers into engaging with fraudulent websites.

Sebolai also warns that these scams are not limited to online platforms, with consumers increasingly being targeted through phone calls and text messages.

READ | Black November spending up as consumers benefit from lower costs

He identifies three common tactics: vishing, where scammers use phone calls; smishing, which involves fraudulent SMS messages; and phishing, where victims are tricked into sharing sensitive information through deceptive links or online platforms.

AI has made these tactics even more convincing, allowing criminals to produce fake websites and promotional material that look almost identical to those of legitimate businesses.

“What you would think would take years and years of development is now being done in a matter of hours,” says Sebolai.

World.title: Kenyans working in Germany increase by 2,500 in two years, Ruto says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto welcomes German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier to State House, Nairobi, during his official visit to Kenya on Wednesday, November 25, 2026. [PCS]

The number of Kenyans employed in Germany rose to 9,500 in March 2026 from 7,000 two years earlier, President William Ruto has announced.

Ruto attributed the increase to growing employment opportunities under the Comprehensive Migration and Mobility Partnership Agreement (CMMPA) between Kenya and Germany, which seeks to create pathways for skilled workers and trainees.

He also revealed that the number of Kenyan trainees contributing to Germany's social security system increased from 820 in March 2024 to 1,260 in March 2026.

The President made the announcement during a joint press conference with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier at State House, Nairobi, on Wednesday, November 25, following bilateral talks between the two leaders.

Kenya and Germany signed the CMMPA in Berlin on September 13, 2024. It came into force on October 18, 2024, establishing a framework for cooperation in employment, vocational training, skills development and the protection of migrant workers.

The agreement also provides for cooperation in addressing irregular migration and the return of people who do not have the legal right to remain in either country.

Germany has been seeking skilled workers to address shortages in its labour market as its population ages. Its Federal Employment Agency (BA) identified 157 occupational categories facing skills shortages in 2025, including healthcare, construction and skilled trades.

Ruto said the two governments had discussed measures to streamline visa and recruitment procedures, expand language training and speed up the recognition of professional qualifications to help more Kenyans access employment opportunities.

The discussions also covered vocational training programmes aimed at equipping Kenyans with skills that respond to the needs of the German economy.

The two leaders explored further opportunities for Kenyan seafarers through specialised training, sea-time placements and partnerships with German shipping companies.

Their discussions also covered sustainable shipping, maritime logistics and investment in the sector, drawing on Germany's maritime expertise and Kenya's strategic position in the region.

Beyond employment, Ruto invited German companies to increase investment in Kenya, identifying manufacturing, agro-processing, infrastructure, healthcare, renewable energy and digital technology as priority sectors.

He said Kenya wanted to deepen partnerships between local and German enterprises, including joint ventures in manufacturing and integration into global value chains.

The President also pointed to opportunities for expanding Kenyan exports to Germany and the wider European market under the Kenya-European Union Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA).

He identified cut flowers, avocados and fresh vegetables among products with export potential, while calling for efforts to address market access barriers and help Kenyan exporters meet international quality standards.

The two countries also discussed agricultural cooperation in mechanisation, irrigation, climate-smart farming, post-harvest management and food chain infrastructure.

Ruto said the objective was to improve agricultural productivity, raise farmers' incomes, create jobs and strengthen food security.

The President also announced the conclusion of technical negotiations on a mutual data adequacy arrangement between Kenya and the European Union (EU).
