He said the arrangement, once adopted and implemented, would facilitate secure cross-border data transfers, expand digital trade and strengthen Kenya's competitiveness in business process outsourcing (BPO) and digital services exports.

Ruto called for Germany's support in facilitating the adoption and implementation of the respective adequacy decisions.

He said the arrangement would create opportunities for Kenyans to access global employment through the digital economy.

The discussions also covered cooperation in digital public infrastructure, artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity and scientific research, including partnerships between universities, research institutions and technology companies.

On renewable energy, Ruto said Kenya was seeking German investment and technology in geothermal power, green hydrogen, energy storage and green infrastructure.

He described the energy transition as an opportunity to accelerate green industrialisation, strengthen manufacturing competitiveness and expand exports.

The President also thanked Germany for supporting the government's Shirika Plan, which seeks to move refugees from prolonged encampment and humanitarian dependency towards integrated settlements and self-reliance.

He called for continued cooperation in creating economic opportunities for refugees and host communities, noting that sustainable solutions to displacement must also address the conflicts and instability that drive it.

The two leaders further discussed cooperation in counter-terrorism, maritime security, military training and peace-support operations.

Ruto said Kenya appreciated Germany's contribution to peace and security initiatives in Africa and welcomed closer cooperation between the two countries.

The discussions also covered cultural relations, tourism and academic exchanges, with the President saying the two governments needed to translate their commitments into measurable outcomes for citizens.

World.title: Ledama Ole Kina court battle over Sh1.2m dispute takes new turn
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Narok Senator Ledama Ole Kina has been granted a stay of execution in a Sh1.2 million compensation dispute with former Narok County Assembly employee Zakayo Rotiken.

The court has given the senator an opportunity to raise funds and settle the outstanding amount.

The Employment and Labour Relations Court, sitting in Nairobi, issued the orders on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, and scheduled the matter for mention on February 18, 2027.

The development follows a protracted legal dispute arising from Rotiken's dismissal, in which the court awarded him Sh1,220,737.61 in compensation.

During Tuesday's proceedings, Ole Kina sought between 30 and 45 days to raise funds and settle the outstanding amount.

The court subsequently granted a stay of execution pending further proceedings in the matter.

In a statement, Rotiken's lawyer, Tonge Yoya, said the stay of execution did not invalidate, overturn or extinguish the original judgment, insisting that the senator remained legally obligated to settle the award.

The claimant's legal team also told the court that it intended to challenge pending applications by Ole Kina, arguing that some of the issues had already been determined in previous proceedings.

The lawyers said an application dated November 19, 2026, seeking to amend a preliminary objection filed on September 25, 2026, was directed to be served upon them.

Ole Kina was further directed to file and serve written submissions on the preliminary objection within 14 days.

The objection is anchored on the doctrine of res judicata, which bars parties from reopening matters that have already been conclusively determined by a competent court.

Rotiken's lawyers contend that a previous application by the senator seeking a stay of judgment was dismissed on April 24, 2026, and argue that subsequent applications touching on the same issues should not be entertained.

However, the Parliamentary Service Commission (PSC) is considering a request to release funds to settle a court-awarded compensation to Zakayo Rotiken, a former employee of Narok Senator Ledama Ole Kina, in a labour dispute that has resurfaced following a dramatic confrontation between the senator and auctioneers.

In a letter addressed to the parties in Employment and Labour Relations Court Cause E165 of 2021, Rotiken versus Ledama Ole Kina, the Commission confirmed that it had received a request seeking the release of funds to settle the decretal sum and costs awarded by the court.

The letter signed by the Commission's Director of Litigation and Compliance, Anthony Njoroge, states that the request has been placed before the Commission for consideration, with a decision expected once deliberations are concluded.

"The Commission's decision shall be communicated to you as soon as the Commission has concluded its deliberations on the matter," reads part of the letter.

The development comes against the backdrop of a viral video showing Senator Ole Kina threatening to shoot a female auctioneer who had gone to repossess a milk delivery lorry belonging to his Enkanasa Cow Milk Company over an outstanding financial obligation.

The confrontation sparked public outrage, with questions emerging over the circumstances surrounding the attempted repossession and the senator's conduct towards the auctioneers.

The dispute is linked to a labour case filed by Rotiken, who had been employed by Ole Kina before his dismissal. The former employee moved to court seeking redress over his termination, resulting in a monetary award against the senator.

The dispute stems from a court case filed by former Narok County Assembly employee Zakayo Rotiken against Senator Ledama Ole Kina at the Employment and Labour Relations Court in Nairobi. The court awarded Rotiken KSh 1,220,737.61 in compensation following his dismissal.

The latest communication from the Parliamentary Service Commission signals that the institution is considering facilitating settlement of the court award, although it has not yet made a final commitment to release the funds.

World.title: Ruto backs Didmus Barasa for Bungoma governor in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kimilili MP Didmus Barasa with President Ruto at a political rally in Mt Elgon during the President’s development tour in the Western region. [PCS]

President William Ruto has thrown his weight behind Kimilili MP Didmus Barasa in the race to succeed Bungoma Governor Kenneth Lusaka in 2027, setting the stage for a contest over the county's political leadership.

During his ongoing tour of Western Kenya, the President rallied support for Barasa, signalling his preference for the legislator in the battle for control of Bungoma County after the next General Election.

Barasa has expressed confidence in securing the United Democratic Alliance (UDA) party nomination, citing his development record and grassroots mobilisation in Kimilili as the foundation of his gubernatorial bid.

The MP has urged Bungoma leaders aligned with Kenya Kwanza to unite behind his candidature, arguing that a common political front would strengthen the region's bargaining power within the national government.

He said he intends to replicate his development model in Kimilili across the county's 45 wards, prioritising healthcare, education and youth empowerment.

“I want to take the development model we have implemented in Kimilili and extend it to all the 45 wards in Bungoma. Our people deserve better healthcare, improved education infrastructure, functional vocational training centres and quality early childhood education facilities,” he said.

The legislator pledged to strengthen county hospitals, improve the availability of medicines and expand access to healthcare services at the grassroots.

He also promised to invest in vocational training centres to equip young people with practical skills for employment and entrepreneurship, while improving Early Childhood Development and Education (ECDE).

Barasa identified agriculture, trade, infrastructure and youth entrepreneurship as key sectors requiring investment to unlock Bungoma's economic potential. He said his proposed administration would prioritise accountability, efficient use of public resources and improved service delivery.

His bid has received backing from a section of county leaders, including Senator Wafula Wakoli of Ford Kenya and Webuye East MP Martin Pepela.

However, Ruto's apparent preference for Barasa has attracted opposition from Sirisia MP John Waluke, who has questioned the endorsement and instead declared support for Westlands MP Tim Wanyonyi, who is associated with the Linda Mwananchi Movement (LMM).

Waluke argued that Bungoma residents should determine their next governor without external political influence.

“Bungoma belongs to its people, and the people must decide who will lead them in 2027. We cannot allow the gubernatorial contest to be determined through political endorsements from outside. Residents must be given the freedom to choose a leader who represents their interests,” he said.

The contest is also unfolding amid political differences between Barasa and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, adding to the competing interests shaping Bungoma's succession politics.

World.title: Shun leaders inciting you to cause chaos, PS Omollo tells youth
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Internal Security Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo. [File,Standard]

Internal Security Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo has warned young people against political violence, saying the destruction of public property costs lives and diverts resources meant for development.

The warning comes amid concerns over political violence in Embu following the September 12 incident at Nembure Stadium, where a meeting attended by Deputy President Kithure Kindiki was disrupted, leaving one person dead, six vehicles torched and three others vandalised.

Speaking during a Mass at St Thomas More Kairuri Parish in Embu County, Omollo challenged young people to question leaders who ask them to disrupt meetings, block roads or destroy property.

“Before you leave home to disrupt a meeting, ask that leader whether they would allow their own child to do what they are asking you to do,” he said.

“Ask them what they are doing to help you access education, training and employment.”

Omollo said young people should also question what political leaders were doing to improve their access to education, technical training and employment.

He said the Government was working to expand opportunities for young people through education, technical training and employment.

The PS welcomed efforts in the technical and vocational education and training (TVET) sector to equip young people in Embu with skills to pursue their ambitions.

At the same time, Omollo commended county leadership for working with the national government to combat illicit alcohol and drug abuse.

Omollo said proposed legislative changes targeting the sector had passed the first reading in Parliament and urged residents to participate in the next stages of the legislative process.

On security, the PS acknowledged calls for more police vehicles, saying the Government was investing in personnel, vehicles and equipment.

However, he challenged residents to help protect public investments, citing reports that 10 police vehicles had been burned in Embu.

“We use our taxes to buy police vehicles, build markets and construct roads. We cannot pay for development and then allow a few individuals to destroy what belongs to all of us,” he said.

Omollo warned that anyone suspected of destroying property would be taken to court in accordance with the law, where the judiciary would determine their cases.

He maintained that political differences should not be used to justify vandalism, endanger lives or disrupt public services.

“The Constitution protects the right to express ourselves peacefully and unarmed. Political differences cannot be an excuse to vandalise property, endanger lives or disrupt the services our communities depend on,” he said.

Those present included Public Service, Human Capital Development and Special Programmes Cabinet Secretary Geoffrey Ruku, Embu Governor Cecily Mbarire, Senator Alexander Munyi and Deputy Governor Kinyua Mugo, among others.

World.title: Narok Senator under fire after threatening to shoot auctioneers in Sh1.2m dispute
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Narok Senator Ledama ole Kina is at the centre of a national uproar after a viral video captured him threatening to shoot individuals during a volatile confrontation involving auctioneers and a former Senate office employee.

The dramatic standoff erupted when court-backed agents attempted to seize a milk delivery truck over an unresolved legal dispute and has since ignited intense public debate regarding political accountability and the rule of law.

The controversy surrounds long court battle after Zakayo Rotiken, who served sacked as Narok North Constituency Coordinator between 2017 and 2020, was sacked.

According to records, the claimant was illegally dismissed amidst unpaid salary arrears.

On October 31, 2023, the Employment and Labour Relations Court ruled in Rotiken's favour , a decision that was subsequently upheld when the Senator lost his appeal.

With accrued interest, the court decree now stands at Sh 1.2 million.

Consequently, when the debt remained unsatisfied, licensed auctioneers moved in to execute lawful warrants which in turn provoked a furious reaction from Senator Ole Kina, who fiercely framed the entire episode as a political witch-hunt.

The lawmaker argued that Rotiken was hired by the Narok Senate office rather than his personal capacity, maintaining that any resultant liabilities ought to be handled by the Parliamentary Service Commission (PSC) rather than attaching his private property.

Defending his harsh words in the widely circulated footage, the senator dismissed the agents as trespassers and asserted action against them.

"Anybody who trespasses will get a bullet in their head or leg because that is trespass," said Ole Kina.

“Nitakupiga Risasi!” Senator Ledama Ole Kina embroiled in confrontation with alleged auctioneers over unpaid car loan https://t.co/k4OSXpNsdi November 21, 2026

The claimant's legal team condemned the threats made against statutory court officers emphasizing that a court judgment is an enforceable command rather than a mere suggestion, calling upon the Inspector General of Police of Police and the Director of Criminal Investigatons to urgently investigate the alleged death threats.

Rotiken noted that he merely sought justice through proper judicial channels and should not be penalized or intimidated for pursuing his lawful entitlements.

"When I was illegally dismissed with unpaid salary arrears, I did not resort to violence or politics—I went to the Employment and Labour Relations Court. Nobody is above the law, and I appeal to the police to protect the officers doing their job so that justice can finally be served," he said.

Ultimately, as pressure mounts on security agencies to look into the firearm threats, the unfolding saga highlights a tense intersection between public office obligations and the absolute sanctity of judicial decrees.

While the senator maintains that his assets were unjustly targeted by political rivals, legal experts and the public continue to demand that the rule of law must prevail without exception.

World.title: Ruto defends IEBC, challenges rivals to present alternative policies
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [PCS]

President William Ruto has launched a scathing attack on opposition leaders over their demands on the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), accusing them of attempting to interfere with the electoral agency because they fear losing the 2027 General Election.

The President challenged opposition leaders to allow IEBC to prepare independently for next year's elections, saying they should instead focus on identifying their presidential candidate, developing a manifesto and presenting alternative policies to Kenyans.

Ruto accused his competitors of attempting to play the roles of both contestants and referees by seeking to influence decisions on the procurement of election materials and equipment.

He spoke a day after opposition leaders walked out of a meeting convened by IEBC, alleging bias by the commission.

“Please give IEBC a chance to arrange the elections next year. The people of Kenya will decide. You go and first look for your candidate, find your policies, agenda and plans and sell them to the wananchi. We shall meet at the ballot,” said Ruto.

Speaking during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto questioned why opposition politicians were concentrating on determining how IEBC should procure election materials instead of preparing to face voters.

“How can somebody who is in a competition want to decide where the pitch will be, who the referee will be and where the ball will be placed? Leave IEBC alone. Those who will vote are the citizens, and they are the ones who will decide,” he said.

The President accused his opponents of lacking a clear political agenda and capacity to deliver, claiming their campaigns were centred on slogans and personal attacks against him.

He challenged them to explain what they would do differently in agriculture, education, healthcare, infrastructure and employment rather than mobilising Kenyans around the slogan 'Kasongo Must Go'.

“The reason why my competitors cannot develop a plan is that they have no capacity. The reason why they have no agenda is that they have no knowledge. The reason why they cannot develop anything is that they know they have no capacity to deliver on anything that they will say,” he said.

His remarks were echoed by Kakamega Governor Fernandes Barasa and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, who rallied Western Kenya leaders behind his re-election bid and defended IEBC against what they termed unnecessary political pressure. President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [ Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Speaking in Butere, Barasa said the region's political leadership, including Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, Cabinet Secretary Wycliffe Oparanya, Wetang'ula and trade unionist Francis Atwoli, was united behind Ruto's development agenda.

“IEBC will conduct the elections according to the law. Opposition leaders should leave IEBC alone and allow it to do its work,” he said.

Wetang'ula maintained that IEBC was independent of both the government and the opposition and should be allowed to conduct its work without interference.

“IEBC is independent of the government and independent of the Opposition. You stand there to do your work fairly, truthfully and equally,” he said.

He added: “Just as Arsenal supporters cannot dictate what uniform the referee should wear, the referee's responsibility is to ensure the game is played fairly and the winner emerges through a legitimate process.”

The exchanges underline the growing political contest over the management of the 2027 elections, with the government side accusing the opposition of undermining the electoral agency before campaigns gather momentum.

Beyond the political exchanges, Ruto used his Western Kenya tour to highlight development projects, saying his administration was committed to correcting years of neglect and unequal distribution of national resources.

He also announced plans for a second phase of the Nyota programme targeting an additional 200,000 young people, each expected to receive Sh50,000 to establish or expand businesses.

The government is also targeting 100,000 college graduates for internships from January, with each expected to receive a monthly stipend of Sh20,000.

Ruto's tour comes amid growing competition for Western Kenya's support ahead of the 2027 General Election, with emerging opposition alliances seeking to challenge his influence.

World.title: Ruto sustains attacks on Gachagua, dares Opposition to name 2027 flagbearer
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto launches Matisi-Bokoli-Milani-Teremi road in Webuye West on November 19, 2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

President William Ruto has challenged Opposition leaders to name their presidential candidate and unveil a clear political agenda, accusing them of wasting time hopping from one hotel to another and holding meetings in private residences in search of a flagbearer and campaign manifesto.

The President said the Opposition was yet to settle on a flagbearer or agree on a common agenda despite the clock ticking towards the 2027 General Election.

He dismissed the rival camps' political engagements as endless consultations and manoeuvres, arguing that their leaders were more preoccupied with political meetings than developing policies to convince Kenyans.

Speaking in Bungoma during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto challenged his opponents to stop what he termed political confusion and present an alternative development agenda, insisting he was ready to face them in the 2027 contest.

"These people do not have a candidate. They are struggling, moving from one hotel to another and from one person's house to another, trying to find an agenda and a manifesto before they can start campaigning. Time is running out, yet they are still struggling to agree on an agenda," he said.

Ruto also launched a fresh attack on former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua, accusing him of promoting tribalism and hatred while questioning his remarks about relocating to Texas, United States.

The President mockingly referred to Gachagua as "Mr Chuki wa Texas", questioning why he would allegedly acquire a house in the US while engaging in politics that could divide Kenyans and fuel hostility.

"Mr Chuki wa Texas has gone to buy a house in Texas. He wants to know whether he will flee our country after spreading tribalism and hatred, dividing people and turning them against each other, before boarding a plane to Texas and leaving others to deal with the consequences," Ruto said.

He accused the former Deputy President of attempting to turn communities against one another for political gain, warning that he would not allow anyone to undermine national unity through ethnic mobilisation.

Ruto said he was ready to confront his political opponents directly but insisted that political competition should not become an avenue for spreading hatred and inciting Kenyans against one another.

The President also questioned Gachagua's allies over their reported visit to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) offices in Kizirani, accusing the Opposition of picking unnecessary fights with the electoral agency ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He suggested that politicians who begin questioning the electoral commission before elections could be preparing grounds to reject the results should they lose.

"Whenever you see someone picking a fight with IEBC, that person is already looking for an excuse to fail. Now they are coming up with all sorts of excuses, asking whether it is IEBC that votes. Is IEBC responsible for the votes?" He posed.

Ruto urged politicians to stop harassing the electoral agency, maintaining that the power to elect leaders rests with Kenyans and not the commission.

"I want to tell Kenyans to stop harassing IEBC. IEBC does not have votes. The votes belong to the people of Kenya," he said.

The President maintained that his administration was focused on delivering development, challenging the Opposition to explain its alternative plans on electricity connectivity, education, healthcare and infrastructure.

He questioned what the Opposition considered its development agenda, dismissing what he described as recycled political slogans and simplistic promises.

The President particularly took issue with promises centred on providing porridge to Kenyans, questioning whether such pledges could constitute a credible national development agenda.

He urged voters to interrogate the policies and development track records of politicians seeking their support instead of being swayed by political rhetoric and personal attacks.

The latest attack marks an escalation in political exchanges between Ruto and his rivals as competing camps intensify mobilisation ahead of the 2027 General Election.

It also comes amid efforts by Gachagua and other Opposition figures to consolidate their political formations and build a formidable challenge to Ruto's re-election bid, with Western Kenya emerging as a key battleground.

World.title: Ruto lists measures to lower cost of living, put more money in Kenyans' pockets
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his State Of The Nation Address at Parliament, Nairobi. November 18th, 2026. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

President William Ruto has outlined a raft of government interventions aimed at reducing the cost of living, increasing household incomes and creating more employment opportunities for Kenyans.

Addressing Parliament during the 2026 State of the Nation Address on Wednesday, Ruto said his administration had prioritised lowering the cost of essential goods and services while increasing earnings across key sectors of the economy.

“Our economic proposition was simple: Reduce the cost for families and increase the income from what they do,” he said.

On food prices, the President cited the government’s fertiliser subsidy programme, which has reduced the price of a 50-kilogramme bag of fertiliser from Sh7,500 in 2022 to Sh2,000 this year.

He said the government had distributed 38.5 million bags of subsidised fertiliser to farmers, contributing to an increase in maize production from 44.3 million bags in 2022 to 71 million bags last year.

Consequently, maize imports declined from 9.9 million bags to 3.3 million bags, while the average price of a two-kilogramme packet of sifted maize flour dropped from a high of Sh230 in September 2022 to Sh152 in September this year.

Ruto also highlighted gains in the tea, coffee, dairy and sugar industries, saying government interventions had helped improve production and increase farmers' earnings.

He said the Cherry Advance Revolving Fund had disbursed Sh15.07 billion to 684,000 coffee farmers, while tea export earnings increased from Sh163 billion in 2022 to Sh187 billion in 2025.

In the dairy sector, milk production rose from 4.5 billion litres to 5.52 billion litres, while average earnings for farmers increased from Sh32 to Sh60 per litre last month.

Sugar production, he added, increased by 60 per cent between January and October, with cane crushing rising by 57 per cent. The industry is projected to produce more than 900,000 tonnes by the end of the year, with Sh1.2 billion in bonuses expected to be paid to sugarcane farmers.

On healthcare, Ruto said the Social Health Authority (SHA) was designed to ease the financial burden of medical expenses on households through a shared health financing system.

In education, he said the government had employed 100,000 teachers and was preparing to recruit an additional 20,000 to address staffing shortages and reduce the burden on parents who pay teachers hired through Boards of Management.

He added that 23,000 classrooms had been constructed, while 1,600 laboratories were being built and equipped.

The President said the annual education allocation had increased from Sh521 billion in the 2022/23 financial year to Sh784 billion in the current financial year.

"These investments improve the quality of education while progressively reducing the need for Kenyans to finance education," he said.

On affordable housing, Ruto said more than 313,000 homes were at different stages of construction across the 47 counties, with over 1.37 million Kenyans registered on the Boma Yangu platform and more than 18,000 homes already allocated.

He said households could work towards homeownership through monthly payments starting at Sh4,000, which he argued would help ease the burden of rent.

The housing programme, according to the President, had also generated more than 1.1 million employment opportunities and reserved orders worth over Sh61 billion for Jua Kali artisans.

On employment, Ruto said 350,000 Kenyans had secured jobs through the digital economy programme, while another 707,000 had obtained employment abroad through international labour mobility initiatives.

He also cited the Hustler Fund, saying more than seven million Kenyans had established credit records through the programme, with cumulative borrowing reaching Sh94 billion.

Under the NYOTA programme, more than 133,000 young entrepreneurs had received training, mentorship and Sh50,000 each in start-up capital, he said.

The President further announced proposed tax measures aimed at increasing disposable incomes, including exempting workers earning Sh32,333 or less per month from Pay As You Earn (PAYE).

Other proposals include scrapping stamp duty on land transactions valued at Sh1 million or less and removing the 25 per cent import duty on mobile phones.

On pending bills, Ruto said the government had approved the settlement of 28,726 verified claims amounting to Sh27.8 billion, covering debts of Sh50 million and below dating back to 2005.

He added that Sh18 billion owed to public universities and another Sh16 billion owed to public and private hospitals under the former National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) had been approved for payment and were undergoing Treasury processing.

“These are not isolated interventions, but parts of one comprehensive undertaking,” Ruto said.

He maintained that the government's economic strategy was anchored on reducing household expenditure, increasing incomes and expanding opportunities for Kenyans.

World.title: Greek mission uncovers massive structure in Alexandria’s ancient Royal Quarter
World.content:
A Greek archaeological mission has uncovered the foundations of a massive limestone structure in the Royal Quarter of ancient Alexandria, a discovery that could shed new light on the urban and architectural layout of the historic district, the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities announced on Monday.

The mission, affiliated with the Hellenic Research Institute of Alexandrian Civilization (HRIAC) and headed by Dr. Calliope Limneos-Papakosta, has been conducting excavations in Alexandria’s Shallalat Gardens area for nearly 20 years, with funding from the Moheb Kassabgui Foundation and Reliance Egypt.

According to the ministry, the excavations revealed the foundations of a large walled structure, as well as a tunnel running beneath the building northward.

Following the mission’s report, Minister of Tourism and Antiquities Sherif Fathy ordered the formation of a specialized archaeological committee, headed by Ayman Ashmawy, head of the Central Administration for Lower Egypt, Sinai and the Northern Coast Antiquities at the Supreme Council of Antiquities. The committee included senior specialists and professors of Greek and Roman history and archaeology from Alexandria and Tanta universities.

The committee inspected the excavation site and examined the architectural features uncovered before submitting its findings to Supreme Council of Antiquities Secretary-General Hisham al-Leithy, who presented the report to the minister.

The report said the site lies within the Royal Quarter of ancient Alexandria, one of the city’s most prominent historic districts. The building’s foundations and square-shaped dimensions indicate that it once supported a large, tall structure.

The discovery is also significant for research into the topography of ancient Alexandria and the extent of the massive foundations, adding to archaeological studies of the buildings that once stood in the area, the committee said.

It noted that the structure’s nature and architectural features raise the possibility that it served a funerary purpose. If confirmed, it could be the “Royal Tombs” established by Ptolemy IV Philopator (221–204 BC), according to historical sources, and mentioned by ancient Greek geographer and historian Strabo in his description of Alexandria.

Fathy described the discovery and the committee’s initial findings as significant, saying successive archaeological discoveries in Alexandria highlight the city’s unique cultural and archaeological heritage and its potential to reveal further aspects of its history and urban development.

He reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to supporting both Egyptian and foreign archaeological missions and strengthening scientific cooperation with research institutions and specialized universities to advance archaeological studies, improve understanding of historic sites and structures and preserve Egypt’s cultural heritage.

Al-Leithy said the committee had examined the mission’s findings and the discovered architectural elements on site, adding that its preliminary conclusions confirmed the site’s importance, particularly given its location within the ancient city’s Royal Quarter.

He said the discovery opens new avenues for research into royal structures in Alexandria during the Ptolemaic period, stressing the need for further archaeological and architectural work to establish the building’s nature, function and relationship with surrounding structures.

Ashmawy said the committee had developed a preliminary hypothesis based on its inspection and study, but stressed that it remained under examination. Excavations and research are continuing to determine the building’s identity and function more precisely.

He added that the discovery represents an important contribution to the study of the structures that once occupied the Royal Quarter and their architectural and cultural functions during the Ptolemaic era. Further excavations and studies could yield additional evidence about the building and related structures.

World.title: Red Crescent delivers over 2,304 tonnes of aid to Gaza
World.content:
The Red Crescent launched on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, the 319th “Zad Al-Izza. From Egypt to Gaza” convoy, loaded with trucks of humanitarian and relief aid heading to the Gaza Strip, to continue supporting the Palestinian brothers and meeting their basic needs, especially with the approach of winter.

The Red Crescent explained in a statement that this comes within the framework of its ongoing efforts to meet the needs of the sector, as the aid included basic winter supplies, which included more than 12,320 pieces of winter clothing, more than 692 tents, and more than 17,510 blankets, to support the people of the Gaza Strip in facing the repercussions of the heavy rains and the low-pressure system.

It added that it also included more than 2,304 tons of various aid, including: more than 1,482 tons of food baskets and flour, more than 286 tons of relief and medical supplies and medicines, as well as more than 537 tons of petroleum products needed to operate bakeries, hospitals and vital facilities within the sector.

The Red Crescent has maintained its presence on the border since the beginning of the crisis, keeping its logistical centers ready and intensifying its efforts to prepare and deliver humanitarian and relief aid to the Gaza Strip, which has exceeded one million tons, thanks to the efforts of more than 75,000 volunteers in the association.

The Red Crescent has been present as a national mechanism for coordinating and directing aid to the Gaza Strip since the beginning of the crisis in October 2023. The Rafah land port has not been completely closed during that period, and it continues its readiness in all logistical centers and its continuous efforts to bring humanitarian and relief aid into the Gaza Strip, which has exceeded one million tons by 75,000 volunteers.

World.title: Egyptian, Cypriot special forces conduct joint exercise ‘Ptolemy-2026’ in Cyprus
World.content:
Egyptian and Cypriot special forces personnel conducted the joint military exercise “Ptolemy-2026,” which took place over several days in Cyprus.

The exercise included a series of theoretical and practical lectures introducing participants to the operational methods of special forces and the equipment used in the training.

It also sought to foster integration and interoperability, harmonize operational concepts and train participants in detecting and countering improvised explosive devices (IEDs).

The exercise also featured a number of conventional and unconventional live-fire drills, demonstrating the high level of professionalism of personnel from both sides.

The activities further included several practical exercises showcasing the field skills of Egyptian and Cypriot special forces personnel and their ability to carry out all assigned missions efficiently and competently.

The exercise is part of the Armed Forces’ commitment to strengthening military cooperation with friendly and brotherly countries and exchanging expertise across various military fields.

World.title: Cairo, Khartoum reaffirm commitment to restoring stability, reject threats to Sudan’s unity
World.content:
Egypt and Sudan have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening coordination to restore stability in Sudan, with Egypt reiterating its rejection of any threat to Sudan’s unity and territorial integrity and its continued support for the Sudanese people and national institutions.

The positions were outlined in a joint statement issued at the conclusion of a visit to Egypt by Sudan’s Transitional Prime Minister Kamil al-Tayeb Idris, following expanded talks with Prime Minister Moustafa Madbouly.

The statement said Idris visited Egypt on Tuesday at the head of a high-level delegation and met with President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, delivering a message from Sudan’s Transitional Sovereignty Council Chairman Abdel Fattah Al-Burhan.

Egypt reaffirmed the principles set out in the Egyptian Presidency’s statement of December 18, 2025, on the direct link between the national security of both countries. These include preserving Sudan’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, safeguarding its resources, rejecting the establishment or recognition of parallel entities and protecting the country’s state institutions.

Egypt also stressed its readiness to take all measures permitted under international law and the joint defence agreement between the two countries to support Sudan and prevent any violation of these principles.

The two sides condemned attacks by rebel militias on civilians and infrastructure in Sudan, particularly electricity stations and water facilities, using drones launched from a neighbouring country. They underscored the need to respect Sudan’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and support its national institutions, foremost among them the Sudanese Armed Forces, in carrying out their constitutional responsibilities to safeguard national security, defend the country’s borders and resources and protect its water rights.

The two governments agreed to pursue closer cooperation across economic, trade, development, cultural, social and educational fields. They also stressed the importance of facilitating arrangements for Sudanese students in Egypt and maintaining consultations through intensified contacts and official visits at various levels to advance the shared interests of the two Nile Valley peoples.

Both sides highlighted the need to strengthen trade and investment ties and increase bilateral trade in the coming period. They also discussed expanding cooperation in several sectors, including healthcare and pharmaceutical industries.

They further agreed to swiftly address the situation of detainees held by both sides, in keeping with the close historical and fraternal ties between the two countries and their peoples.

The two governments also agreed to continue coordinating efforts to facilitate the voluntary return of Sudanese nationals to their country. The Sudanese side expressed deep appreciation for Egypt’s role in hosting Sudanese citizens over the past period, in line with the longstanding bonds between the two peoples.

Egypt reiterated its full support for Sudanese national efforts to rebuild the country. Sudan, in turn, expressed its interest in strengthening its partnership with Egypt on reconstruction and opening the way for Egyptian companies to contribute to rebuilding war-damaged facilities in the industrial and agricultural sectors, as well as rehabilitating infrastructure to accelerate Sudan’s recovery.

Egypt expressed its readiness to provide all forms of support and assistance to the Sudanese government’s reconstruction efforts and welcomed joint work to support various sectors in a manner that serves the interests of both countries.

The two sides also exchanged views on ongoing political and security developments in the region and discussed ways to enhance coordination in regional and international forums on issues of mutual concern. They agreed to maintain close coordination and ongoing political consultations.

Egypt and Sudan stressed that their water security was interconnected and indivisible, agreeing to defend their full water rights and uses under the 1959 Nile Waters Agreement and reject any infringement on those rights.

The two sides said their position was based on promoting cooperation and dialogue to protect the right to life and support the right to development, while pursuing mutual benefits in accordance with international law. They welcomed what they described as African understanding of the rights of downstream countries to defend their water interests and those of their peoples, while pursuing development on an equal footing with other African nations.

They agreed to follow up on the implementation of outcomes from coordination meetings under the Permanent Joint Technical Commission for Nile Waters, established pursuant to the 1959 agreement, to develop a unified position on all Nile-related matters. They also agreed to continue meetings under the 2+2 mechanism bringing together the foreign and irrigation ministers of both countries.

The two sides reiterated their outright rejection of unilateral measures in the Eastern Nile Basin.

They also said Ethiopia’s unilateral dam, which they described as contrary to international law, had serious consequences and posed an ongoing threat to the two downstream countries. They called on Ethiopia to change its unilateral approach and restore cooperation in accordance with applicable principles of international law, particularly the principles of no significant harm, prior notification, consultation and agreement.

Egypt and Sudan underscored the central role of the Nile Basin Initiative (NBI), stressing the collective determination of Nile Basin countries to complete the consultation process and restore consensus on the establishment of an inclusive commission representing all basin countries.

They commended the work of the subcommittee overseeing the consultation process, led by Uganda and comprising Rwanda and South Sudan, as well as its report recommending that the process be completed to restore inclusiveness, including through amending and developing the Cooperative Framework Agreement to address the concerns of all parties.

The two sides reaffirmed the importance of freedom of navigation and stressed that governance of the Red Sea is the exclusive responsibility of its littoral states, in accordance with international law.

They rejected any maritime access by non-littoral states at the expense of the sovereignty, unity, territorial integrity or ports of Red Sea countries. They also opposed attempts to exploit regional circumstances to militarize the Red Sea or take unilateral measures undermining the sovereignty and territorial integrity of countries in the region.

At the conclusion of the visit, Idris invited Madbouly to visit Sudan to build on the outcomes of the talks and discuss further frameworks for bilateral cooperation and strategic issues between the two countries.

Both sides renewed their commitment to elevating bilateral cooperation across all fields to a level of comprehensive integration, meeting the aspirations of their peoples for prosperity and development.

World.title: Trump’s stunning show of raw power and what it means
World.content:
President Donald Trump’s summit last week with the tyrant rulers of Russia and China implied that powerful men can do exactly as they please.

On Monday, he proved it.

Trump described how he used his influence to restore AI king Jensen Huang to his job running Nvidia, which by most estimates is the world’s most critical company.

The president compared Huang to a baseball all-star, implying that he was just too important to the US economy and defense industry — and therefore Trump’s own political fortunes — to leave out of the game.

“The board decided to do what we wanted to do,” Trump told CNBC.

Huang’s restoration was followed by a stunning spike in share prices that eased the president’s concerns over crashing stock markets, revealed in his social media posts.

The Nvidia boss is himself a data point for the theory that great power delivers impunity, having been absolved by Trump of accusations that a woman with whom he had an affair was a Chinese asset.

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, meanwhile, said on CNN’s “State of the Union” Sunday that China had illicitly obtained advanced Nvidia chips despite US export controls meant to prevent such transfers.

The coziness between the president and a top corporation that is supposedly regulated by the government is one of many perceived transgressions the new Democratic Congress will probe next year.

“We’re living in something like a monarchical corporate state where the corporations have their way with the government, and then the president of the United States decides he’s going to weigh in on the meeting of a corporate board of directors,” Rep. Jamie Raskin, incoming chair of the House Judiciary Committee, told CNN’s Kasie Hunt. “That’s just an amazing turn of events and such a descent for us.”

Trump’s flexing of power Monday was hardly limited to Nvidia

The president made the short trip from the White House to the Justice Department to condemn California’s outgoing Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom for his commutation of hundreds of death sentences.

Trump’s anger at Newsom is not an abuse of power. There’s a legitimate debate over whether the possible 2028 presidential candidate is serving justice or whether, like Trump, he’s wielding power to boost his own political prospects. Trump also gave voice to relatives of victims of Death Row inmates who’d suffered unspeakable evil. They included Sandy Friend, the mother of 8-year-old Michael Lyons, who was raped, tortured and murdered in 1996. “You’ll never understand the unimaginable pain that you’re putting these families through,” Friend said, publicly rebuking Newsom.

President Donald Trump embraces Sandy Friend, the mother of murdered 8-year-old Michael Lyons, at the Department of Justice in Washington, DC, on November 23. Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters

But it was Trump’s choice of venue, rather than his subject matter, that was significant. His visit to the Great Hall of the DOJ seemed a deliberate reminder that he’s demolished the wall between the White House and an agency traditionally seen as dispensing justice above the political fray. And it was a clear suggestion he plans to mobilize the power of the government in efforts to destroy the prospects of Democratic 2028 hopefuls. It would hardly be the first time, that he’s weaponized the DOJ to go after perceived political foes such as former FBI Director James Comey.

And the president earned impeachment for using the inducement of military aid in 2019 to try to force Ukraine to investigate Joe Biden, and again for using the power of his office to try to overturn his 2020 election defeat.

Newsom argues that capital punishment is incompatible with Californian values and undermines the legal system. The governor said in a statement that he wouldn’t take “lectures on accountability from a President who has used the pardon power to help wealthy friends and business associates avoid accountability while victims are left fighting to recover what was stolen from them.” He added: “Justice should be about the people we serve, not the political interests of the people in power.”

Trump also flexed power Monday in a noticeably political manner in a dispute over a US Army plan to blow up nearly five tons of hazardous material in Iowa, which triggered a public outcry over fears of lead contamination. He temporarily halted the detonation — but warned that if the chemicals spontaneously combusted in the meantime, it would be the fault of incoming Democratic Gov. Rob Sand.

In another display of personal power almost designed to outrage his foes, Trump is expected to award Rudy Giuliani America’s highest civilian honor, the Presidential Medal of Freedom, on Tuesday. The former New York mayor, who announced the award on Steve Bannon’s podcast Monday, led Trump’s legal team in the bid to overturn the will of voters six years ago.

‘Sex sells, fellas’

Each of Trump’s power plays Monday would have been regarded as aberrant behavior from other modern presidents. And the Nvidia intervention might turn out to be legacy-defining.

But each reflects his vision that there’s nothing, as president, he cannot do.

Most remarkably, Trump doesn’t even try to hide his motivations. He said in a freewheeling interview with CNBC that he phoned the Nvidia board and told them that he felt very strongly about reinstating Huang — “one of our great stars.”

A sign is posted in front of Nvidia headquarters on May 21, 2024, in Santa Clara, California. Justin Sullivan/Getty Images/File Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang speaks at a Windows event at Dogpatch studios in San Francisco, California, on October 7. Heather Diehl/Getty Images/File

And he dismissed the idea that Huang’s affairs — one with alleged Chinese intelligence contact Alice Huang (no relation) and another with a subordinate — were a big deal, though at the very least they would seem to infringe the principles of good corporate conduct. “Sex sells, fellas,” he told CNBC’s anchors, explaining the reason the story took off.

The president’s cavalier attitude to the possibility that Jensen Huang might have been compromised by a foreign intelligence service was also stunning. Nvidia is, after all, critical to equipping US armed forces for a superpower standoff with Beijing. “Who isn’t in contact? I just left China,” Trump said. “I think probably China speaks to everybody. … That doesn’t make them bad.”

Democrats are questioning a DOJ determination that Huang poses no security risk. “There’s no way they could have conducted a thorough investigation already to draw the conclusion that both the attorney general and the president have made,” Virginia Democratic Rep. James Walkinshaw told CNN’s Erica Hill. Other Democrats on Monday demanded investigations into whether Trump’s decisions on Nvidia were partly motivated by his personal financial interests.

Trump has wielded aggressive power swiftly to outrun the courts and Congress repeatedly over his two terms.

But his method is especially significant now because it seems to repudiate voters, who delivered a historic midterm election win to Democrats partly because they wanted some restraints on the president.

And so many of Trump’s previous gut calls and big gambles have backfired. His use of government power for personal political gain twice got him impeached. The war in Iran looked like a spectacular short-term success when it killed Iran’s supreme leader, but inflicted high fuel prices and elevated inflation on hundreds of millions of people worldwide. And the US economy might not be quite so dependent on the AI boom were it not for Trump’s trade wars, which also hurt consumers.

Now, Trump is seeking to effectively dictate the future of AI — an industry he has refused to regulate despite fears it could threaten humanity.

What could go wrong?

This headline has been updated.

World.title: One every four minutes: 720,000 Russian soldiers killed since start of Ukraine war, new data suggests
World.content:
Almost three-quarters of a million Russian soldiers have been killed since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, equating to roughly one death every four minutes, analysis based on leaked official data has revealed.

Russian opposition outlets Mediazona and Meduza reported on Monday that by the end of September, 490,000 Russian troops had been confirmed dead by Russia’s statistical bureau, Rosstat.

But accounting for time lags in reporting and including troops who have been reported as missing in action – and are most likely dead – Russian fatalities jump to more than 720,000 since the start of the war, according to the two outlets.

That is a staggering number that surpasses Russia’s death toll from the Soviet war in Afghanistan in the 1980s and both Chechen wars in the 1990s and early 2000s – and which the Kremlin has long tried to keep secret.

Rosstat stopped publishing demographic data in 2025 to disguise the rising death toll from the war. Mediazona and Meduza, as well as other outlets, obtained the official data after two pro-Ukrainian hacker groups, Cyber ​​Partisans of Belarus and Silent Crow, managed to breach Rosstat’s servers earlier this month.

CNN cannot independently verify the figures, but the leaked data on confirmed deaths alone corroborates earlier estimates by analysts and Western intelligence – which now appear to fall far short of the likely real death toll.

Mediazona and Meduza have long been keeping a tally of Russian losses, based mostly on inheritance documents, death notices and other publicly available documents.

Ukrainian servicemen fire a self-propelled howitzer towards Russian positions in eastern Ukraine on December 28, 2022. Sameer Al-Doumy/AFP/Getty Images

But the leaked Rosstat data allowed the media outlets to go a step further, using the same methods and calculations normally employed by actuaries estimating risks and insurance premiums.

By analyzing discrepancies between reported death dates and death registration dates, and by comparing these to search notices published by relatives, the reporters were able to extrapolate the number of deaths that have occurred but have not yet been reported to be somewhere around 230,000.

Mediazona has kept a tally of troops identified as missing by their relatives from 2023. That database contains 160,000 individuals and almost all of them are likely dead. Mediazona said that based on its reporting, the rate of survival among those reported missing only around 10%.

The data shared by Silent Crow showed that the war was the fourth most common cause of death in Russia since the start of the full-scale invasion, after heart diseases; Covid; and stroke and other vascular conditions. It also confirms what has long been suspected – that the losses are not spread evenly across Russia, with poorer areas and ethnic minorities suffering significantly higher casualty rates.

In addition, an analysis by the NEST Centre, a think tank that also obtained the data, revealed the scale of Russia’s recruitment of foreign fighters. It identified 6,947 records of foreign nationals killed in Ukraine – the majority of them from the central Asian countries of Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Turkmenistan.

Like Russia, Ukraine doesn’t release official casualty data, although Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has publicly acknowledged the scale of losses in combat. The most recent research by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) estimated in July that the country has endured between 525,000 and 625,000 casualties, including 125,000 and 150,000 fatalities.

Alexander Baunov, a senior fellow at the Carnegie Russia Eurasia Center, said that the combined death toll suffered by Russia and Ukraine could exceed 1 million.

Ukraine expands evacuation orders

As the newly projected death toll underscores the human cost of Moscow’s war, fears are growing in Ukraine over a deteriorating security situation in the country’s eastern Donetsk region – an area mostly under Russian control – amid daily guided bomb and drone attacks.

All families with children still in Donetsk were on Tuesday ordered to evacuate.

Children and families in many communities in most of Ukrainian-controlled Donetsk – including the major cities of Kramatorsk and Sloviansk – were already under the evacuation order, but now the measure has been expanded to settlements further west. An estimated 64,500 civilians remain in the region as of November 2026, according to the Donetsk regional military administration.

“This is an extremely difficult but necessary decision. The Russians are shelling our cities and villages every day and bombarding the region with aerial bombs,” said the head of Donetsk’s regional military administration, Vadym Filashkin.

For months, Moscow’s forces have been inching towards Kramatorsk, one of Ukraine’s last strongholds in the north of Donetsk region. Tuesday’s mandatory evacuation order is a sign of Kyiv’s concern that an expansion of Russian attacks could further harm civilians and isolate communities, for example by blowing up bridges and supply routes.

World.title: US court convicts China’s Huawei for fraud, conspiring to steal trade secrets, in sprawling trial over Iran business
World.content:
New York Reuters — Chinese telecommunications equipment maker Huawei was convicted by a jury in New York City on Tuesday in a sprawling US criminal case on charges that it deceived banks about its business in Iran and stole trade secrets from American companies.

The verdict came in a criminal case that began in 2018, with the US government the following year placing Huawei on a trade blacklist that restricted its access to US technology amid American concerns that Huawei posed national security risks.

The jury in Brooklyn federal court found Huawei guilty on 10 of the 12 criminal counts the company faced, including bank fraud, wire fraud, sanctions violations and conspiring to steal trade secrets. The jury acquitted Huawei of conspiring to obstruct justice and racketeering conspiracy, a charge alleging the company had acted as a criminal enterprise.

The trial lasted more than two months, with prosecutors calling more than 60 witnesses and the defense calling 15. It was not immediately clear what penalties Huawei will face when US District Judge Ann Donnelly sentences it on September 14, 2027.

Reuters stories in 2012 and 2013 helped expose Huawei’s activities in Iran and were discussed during the trial.

“After the media started questioning Huawei’s operations in Iran, so did Huawei’s banks,” prosecutor Meredith Arfa told jurors during closing arguments in the case last week.

Brian Heberlig, a lawyer for Huawei, said the company was disappointed by the convictions but said the acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge vindicated its “good-faith compliance culture.”

“We fully expect to appeal,” Heberlig told reporters.

US Attorney Joseph Nocella said in a statement: “Few crimes are as serious as Huawei’s decades-long pattern of endangering US national security, violating the sanctity of US commerce, and impeding the enforcement of US laws.” China’s embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Asked how much the company may have to pay in penalties, Heberlig said it was premature to comment, but said the acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge could make a significant difference.

Experts have said the case did not undermine Huawei’s business, as the company diversified and emerged as a key player in China’s push for artificial intelligence.

Founder’s daughter was detained

In December 2018, Meng Wanzhou, Huawei’s chief financial officer and daughter of the company’s founder, was detained in Canada on a US warrant, prompting a diplomatic crisis involving the United States, China and Canada.

Meng had been secretly indicted on US charges of misleading an HSBC banker about Huawei’s business in Iran, so the company could move dollars in and out of Iran in violation of American sanctions. Meng fought extradition to the US for nearly three years, before entering a deferred prosecution agreement and flying home to China to a hero’s welcome. The charges against her were dropped.

Meng did not testify at trial, though an HSBC banker she met with in 2013 did testify.

The 2018 indictment alleged that Huawei misled HSBC, Standard Chartered and BNP Paribas about its business dealings in Iran. Prosecutors added new charges in 2020, including allegations that Huawei conspired to steal trade secrets from US technology companies over two decades.

The prosecution case

During the trial, prosecutors sought to prove that Huawei stole source code from Cisco Systems for its routers, stole wireless telecommunications company Quintel’s antenna technology, and hired a professor to gain access to a circuit board developed by semiconductor company CNEX.

Jurors watched a video that, according to prosecutors, showed a Huawei employee slipping a piece of a T-Mobile testing robot into his backpack, and heard about a Huawei engineer sneaking into a Fujitsu booth at a trade show to photograph a device.

Prosecutors gave jurors a statement attached to Meng’s deferred prosecution agreement in which she acknowledged that the company illegally conducted business in Iran.

The defense argued that HSBC and the other banks knew about Huawei’s business in Iran and were competing for Huawei’s business.

Heberlig accused prosecutors during his closing argument of having “cherry-picked” a handful of disparate incidents to support their claim of a 20-year conspiracy. Heberlig said Huawei succeeded through “hard work, innovation, and investment in research and development.”

The company has more than 200,000 employees and operates in approximately 170 countries.

World.title: This nation had a security pact with China. It’s just signed a deal with a US ally instead
World.content:
Sydney Reuters — Australia and Solomon Islands signed a security pact on Wednesday that makes Canberra the country’s defense partner of choice, marking a shift for the Pacific archipelago that signed Australia and Solomon Islands signed a security pact on Wednesday that makes Canberra the country’s defense partner of choice, marking a shift for the Pacific archipelago that signed a similar deal with China only four years ago

Under the deal, Australia will support the expansion and development of Solomon Islands’ police and border force, while Honiara will deny any request from a foreign power to establish military or security bases on its territory, the leaders of the countries said in a joint statement.

“Australia is proud to be the Solomon Islands’ main security partner, and that’s a responsibility that we take seriously,” Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told a press conference in Canberra with his Solomon Islands counterpart Matthew Wale.

The pact is a victory for Canberra, which is battling China for influence in the region and recently signed similar agreements with Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu and Fiji.

The wide-ranging treaty includes Australian funding for investment in infrastructure and education, improved visa arrangements for Solomon Islanders, and requires Honiara to consult Australia on the development of critical infrastructure.

It signals a significant shift by Wale, a long-time China critic who had appeared to soften his stance in recent years.

“Solomon Islands has been for a number of years a source of uncertainty and doubt in the region. Those days are done,” Wale said at the press conference.

Wale was highly critical of the 2022 security deal with China, echoing the United States and other Pacific nations, saying it would upset regional security and could jeopardise relationships with existing partners.

But in 2025 he led a delegation to Beijing, where he praised China’s economic development and said his party supported the one-China principle.

Australian media reported on Wednesday that Solomon Islands’ pact with China had been scrapped, though Wale declined to comment on the status of the deal, citing a non-disclosure agreement.

A spokesperson for China’s foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

“I think this deal, coupled with indications that Solomon Islands will let the China deal lapse, goes beyond the success of the previous deals” which Australia has struck in the region, said Connor Graham, a research fellow in the Pacific Islands program at Sydney-based think tank the Lowy Institute.

“It is a blow to Chinese security ambitions in the Pacific certainly.”

World.title: LPRA to Launch Five-Year Strategic Plan to Strengthen Liberia’s Petroleum Sector
World.content:
MONROVIA, Liberia – The Liberia Petroleum Regulatory Authority (LPRA) is set to launch its Five-Year Strategic Plan on Thursday, November 26, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. at the Ellen Johnson Sirleaf (EJS) Ministerial Complex in Congo Town, Monrovia.

The launch, being held under the theme “Regulating the Frontier for Lasting National Value,” marks a significant milestone in the Authority’s institutional development and Liberia’s efforts to position its upstream petroleum sector as a competitive, transparent, and attractive destination for responsible investment.

Established by an Act of the National Legislature to separate the regulatory and commercial functions of Liberia’s petroleum sector, the LPRA operates as an independent regulatory institution mandated to regulate, license, and oversee upstream petroleum activities in the country.



The five-year plan outlines a strategic framework for strengthening regulatory effectiveness, building institutional capacity, attracting credible investors, advancing petroleum exploration, and promoting strategic partnerships and stakeholder engagement.

Through its Board of Directors, experienced professional workforce, and collaboration with national and international partners, the Authority aims to establish a modern, responsive, and internationally credible regulatory institution capable of meeting the evolving demands of the global petroleum industry.

The launch is expected to bring together government officials, industry representatives, development partners, and other key stakeholders, underscoring the importance of collective commitment to the responsible management and development of Liberia’s petroleum resources.

The LPRA says the strategic plan reinforces its commitment to ensuring that the exploration and development of the country’s petroleum resources generate sustainable economic and social benefits for the Liberian people, both present and future generations.



The Authority views the plan as a roadmap for strengthening petroleum governance, promoting responsible investment, and ensuring that Liberia’s upstream petroleum sector contributes meaningfully to long-term national development.

World.title: Liberia Issues Revised AML/CFT Regulations to Strengthen Fight Against Financial Crimes
World.content:
The Government of the Republic of Liberia has announced the issuance of revised regulations to strengthen the country’s fight against money laundering, terrorist financing, and proliferation financing.

The Gazette, Vol. XXVI, No. 39, dated Tuesday, August 11, 2026, the Central Bank of Liberia (CBL) and the Financial Intelligence Agency (FIA) jointly formulated and issued Regulation No. CBL/FIA/AML/CFT/001/2026.

The regulation is titled: Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Terrorist Financing, Counter-Proliferation Financing, Preventive Measures, and Proceeds of Crime Regulations, 2026.



The regulations were issued pursuant to the statutory powers and functions of the FIA under the Anti-Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing, Preventive Measures, and Proceeds of Crime Act, 2021, the Financial Intelligence Agency Act, 2021. Also, the joint regulation considers the Amendment and Restatement of the Act Establishing the Central Bank of Liberia, and other applicable laws.

This Regulation implements preventive measures requirements which are mandatory for financial institutions as defined by Section 15.3 of the Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Act of 2021. It designates the National AML/CFT Ministerial Committee (IMC) as the central coordinating body for the formulation of national AML/CFT policies and strategies necessary to achieve the objectives of Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism and combating the Financing of the Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction.

Moreover, the joint regulation provides for the creation and implementation of internal controls and other procedures to deter criminals from using its facilities for money laundering, terrorist financing, and proliferation financing (ML/TF/PF).

Also, it adopts a risk-based approach in the identification, assessment, and management of their ML/TF/PF risks in line with the requirements of these regulations.



Accordingly, it provides for compliance without delay with requests made pursuant to current AML/CFT/CPF legislation and provides information to the Central Bank of Liberia, Financial Intelligence Agency of Liberia, and other competent authorities.

Additionally, it ensures their employees, agents, and others doing business with them clearly understand the AML/CFT/CPF program, and conduct ongoing Due Diligence and, where appropriate, Enhanced Due Diligence on all business relationships, and shall obtain information on the purpose and intended nature of the business relationships of their potential customers.

Meanwhile, the revised Regulation repeals and replaces the previous CBL AML/CFT Regulations No. CBL/RSD/002/2017.

Under the revised framework, financial institutions are required to adopt and fully implement effective internal AML/CFT/CPF control policies and procedures applicable to all customers, products, services, business lines, branches, and subsidiaries.

The revised regulations are expected to enhance Liberia’s compliance with international standards and strengthen preventive measures against financial crimes, coupled with filling regulatory parameters and international compliance requirements.

In another development, the Government of the Republic of Liberia has announced new regulations to strengthen anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing measures in the country’s real estate sector.

The Gazette, Vol. XXVI, No. 38, dated Tuesday, August 11, 2026, the Financial Intelligence Agency of Liberia (FIA) and the Liberia Land Authority jointly issued and published Regulation No. FIA/LLA/RES/001/2026 concerning AML/CFT Regulations for Real Estate Institutions in Liberia.

The regulations were issued by the FIA pursuant to its mandate and authority under the Financial Intelligence Agency of Liberia Act of 2021, specifically Section 67.3 (12), which empowers it to issue regulations, and Sections 15.2 and 15.3 of the Anti-Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing, Preventive Measures, and Proceeds of Crime Act of 2021.

The objective of this regulation is to implement Liberia’s laws and its international obligations pertaining to Anti-Money Laundering and combating the financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT), and specifically as it relates to the implementation of internal control requirements by the Real Estate Sector (RES), to enhance systems to prevent and detect money laundering and terrorist financing, as well as enhance financial integrity of the real estate sector against money laundering, terrorist financing, and proliferation financing.

This regulation shall apply to all classes of real estate institutions and professionals (real estate agents, brokers, appraisals, property managers, real estate investors, title agents/closers, mortgage, mortgage brokers/lenders, etc.) to adopt and fully implement effective internal AML/CFT control policies and procedures applicable to all customers, products, services, business lines, branches, and subsidiaries as defined by the FIA Act of 2021 and AML/CFT Act of 2021.

The publication was made by order of the President, through the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Mme. Sara Beysolow Nyanti.

The new regulations are expected to enhance transparency and accountability in real estate transactions and strengthen Liberia’s efforts to prevent the sector from being used for money laundering and terrorist financing.

World.title: Liberia: Promise of Power and Roads Collides With Warnings of Hidden Debt as Bea Mountain Deal Heads for Signing, Legislative Debate
World.content:
Monrovia- Every dry season, Monrovia goes through the same routine. River levels on the St. Paul fall, the turbines at Mount Coffee slow down, and the lights flicker and go out across the capital. Generators start up in businesses, hospitals and homes. Liberians have lived with this for so long that many now treat it as normal.

By Rodney D Sieh

On Wednesday, President Joseph Nyuma Boakai is due to sign a deal his government says will change that. The Master Infrastructure Development Agreement (MIDA) with Bea Mountain Mining Corporation (BMMC) is valued at about US$5.7 billion. The President received the agreement from the Inter-Ministerial Concession Committee. After he signs it, the Legislature must ratify it.



Within days of the announcement, the deal had become one of the most hotly debated documents in the country. Churchmen, analysts, opposition figures and columnists have warned that Liberia may be signing away its future gold income on terms that heavily favor the company. The government calls it a once-in-a-generation opportunity.

Both sides could be right. This is what the deal promises, what its critics fear, and what lawmakers need to settle before they vote.

THE PROMISE

The power shortage the deal targets is real. Liberia’s installed capacity was about 126 MW in 2024, while officials put national demand at roughly 400 MW. MIDA’s 270 MW would more than double current capacity. Only about a third of Liberians had electricity in 2023, according to World Bank data, and rural access was below 10 percent.



Under the plan, the 270 MW would come from four plants: a 100 MW hydropower plant on the Via River, a 100 MW plant at SP3 on the St. Paul River, a 10 MW plant at SP4 further along the St. Paul, and a 60 MW biomass plant near the Via dam. The reservoirs are central to the design. Three of them, with combined storage of 10 billion cubic meters, would hold high-flow water and release it through the turbines when river flows fall. That is the government’s answer to the dry-season blackouts.

The package also includes US$230 million to upgrade substations, transformers and transmission lines on the national grid, along with the 146 km Liberia Development Road linking the power plants to key facilities.

The government’s pitch rests on how the deal will be paid for. Instead of new loans, it plans to ring-fence additional revenue payable by BMMC, made possible by high gold prices. BMMC is also pledging US$500 million in bridge financing and will keep making its regular payments to the Consolidated Account. Officials call this “innovative financing” that would reduce Liberia’s debt burden. The government statement goes further, describing the deal as “the single most transformative catalyst for the nation’s development in decades.”

The schedule is ambitious. The full program is meant to take five years, with the biomass plant and transmission lines targeted within two years.

THE PRICE

Critics are not arguing about whether Liberia needs power. They are asking what the country will pay for it, and who will decide.

The most detailed objection has come from Rev. Dr. Samuel B. Reeves, Jr., President of the Liberia Council of Churches. He is urging the Legislature not to ratify the current version of the agreement. He says the copy he reviewed is missing key documents: the Annex C payment milestones, the Annex E technical specifications and the EPC contracts. Without them, he argues, no one can independently assess pricing and delivery.

His figures suggest the bill may be larger than the headline number. The eight primary projects have a base cost of US$4.4513 billion, rising to about US$5.6813 billion with additional roads and grid work. A further project ceiling of about US$2.23 billion could apply, and he says the draft sets no all-in ceiling.

The repayment mechanism worries him most. BMMC could offset its corporate income tax, royalties, withholding taxes, the dividends on Liberia’s 5% stake and its employees’ PAY against project costs. He warns that the Treasury might receive no guaranteed cash.

Independent analyst George K. Fahnbulleh reaches a similar conclusion in a briefing note to officials. He calls the arrangement “undisclosed public debt” repaid outside the Public Financial Management Act and the national debt sustainability analysis. By his estimate, the three dams would cost US$3.88 billion for 210 MW, about US$18.5 million per megawatt. He compares that with roughly US$3.1 million per megawatt for Guinea’s Souapiti dam. He projects interest of about US$282 million a year once the works are built, against total BMMC payments to government of about US$33.5 million in 2023. If the offsets cannot keep up with the interest, he warns, the balance could grow indefinitely and pass to future governments.

Reeves singles out the smallest dam. SP-4 is priced at US$634.44 million for 10 MW, or about US$63.4 million per megawatt. He concedes that reservoir and water-transfer works mean this alone does not prove overpricing, but says it warrants independent review.

Both men raise concerns about how the contract was awarded. The draft exempts the contractor and EPC contracts from public procurement law, and MAPA is the exclusive initial contractor. The Auditor General can inspect payment certificates but not actual costs. Liability is capped at 10% of the contract price, and there is no performance bond.

Writing in The New Dawn, columnist Seltue Robert Karweaye Sr. puts the central question bluntly. He argues that if the deal is financed from Liberia’s own future gold revenues rather than new foreign capital, it is a commitment of public money, not a generous investment. He also notes that Bea Mountain is a mining company, not an infrastructure developer, and asks whether there was any competitive bidding.

The political reaction has been harsher. Commentator Martin Kollie has urged President Boakai to abandon the deal. Emmanuel C.D. Gonquoi of the Economic Freedom Fighters of Liberia called it “daylight corporate robbery” under the guise of development.

THE TRACK RECORD

Much of the skepticism comes from Bea Mountain’s history in Grand Cape Mount.

Critics point to the gap between what the mine produces and what the state collects. According to the 16th EITI report, BMMC exported about 12,146 kilograms of gold worth over US$653 million in fiscal year 2023. Both Grand Cape Mount senators have demanded renegotiation of the existing mineral agreement. Sen. Dabah Varpilah describes the flat 3% royalty as inadequate and inequitable as gold values climb.

Questions over taxes are also still open. In October, a preliminary review by Sen. Amara Konneh found that Bea Mountain lifted 16.4 million gallons of diesel over nine months without paying levies.
