Freestyle: A sci-fi inspired performance to Minnie the Moocher by Cab Calloway and Over the Rainbow by Judy Garland, which Inaba praised as "beyond insane." Ravnik also blurted out, “I’m so f-ing proud” after the routine, prompting a bleep.

Fifth place: Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas

WATCH | Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas’s finale freestyle:

Score: 90/90

Judges' choice: Tango to Gallo Ciego by Orquesta Color Tango.

Instant: Quickstep to Tutti-Fruitti, Little Richard

Freestyle: An avant-garde freestyle that opened with a feather-filled moment to Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend, moved into a fog-filled clover field and finished with a ballroom-floor party to Irish folk songs The Parting Glass and Flowers of the Red Hill. Hough called it "a beautiful button on a fantastic season."

World.title: 2 men charged in break-in at country residence of Prince William, Princess of Wales
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Two men have been charged with burglary at the country home of Prince William and Princess Catherine, police said Wednesday.

The Norfolk Police force said Mirgen Doku, 34, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, were charged with entering a dwelling with intent to steal and trespassing on a protected site. They are due in court later Wednesday.

Police officers were called Monday evening to reported "suspicious activity" at an address on the royal family's rural Sandringham estate in eastern England. After a search involving police dogs, drones and a helicopter, two men were arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespassing.

No members of the Royal Family were on the property at the time.

William and Kate's Kensington Palace office declined to comment on security matters.

Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom house on the Sandringham estate, was a wedding present to the couple from the late Queen Elizabeth.

William and Kate use the secluded red brick Georgian mansion about 171 kilometres north of London as a country residence on weekends. The couple and their three children spend most of their time at Forest Lodge in Windsor, west of London, which they have described as their "forever home."

Intruders have breached royal properties several times over the years.

Britain's Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales, are shown in Mumbai on Nov. 17. The couple are now back in Britain, but were not at their country residence Monday when a break-in occurred. (Rafiq Maqbool/The Associated Press)

In October 2024, burglars broke into the Windsor Castle estate west of London and stole a pickup truck and a quad bike from a farm building. Charles and Queen Camilla weren't at Windsor Castle at the time, but it was reported that William and Kate were in their nearby house.

Three years earlier, a man armed with a crossbow was detained on the castle grounds. Jaswant Singh Chail was later sentenced to nine years in prison after admitting he had been encouraged by a chatbot to kill Elizabeth.

In 1982, intruder Michael Fagan managed to sneak into the queen's private chambers while she was in bed. The queen spent 10 minutes chatting with the burglar before raising the alarm when he asked for a cigarette.

As well, there was a security incident earlier this year at Sandringham when Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, the former prince, was allegedly threatened by a masked man while walking his dogs.

A court case for the 39-year-old man who was charged in connection with the incident is ongoing. Andrew, who was stripped of his royal titles and removed from his longtime Windsor Castle residence, now lives at Marsh Farms on the Sandringham estate..

World.title: Highest MP turnover rate in decades making for byelection bonanza this Parliament
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

A slew of MP resignations is putting this Parliament on track to have the most byelections this soon after a general election in over half a century.

It will be 560 days since the 2025 election when voters in six ridings go to the polls on Dec. 7. That will bring the total number of byelections held since the last general election to 13 — and that doesn't include the riding of Parry Sound-Muskoka where current MP Scott Aitchison has signalled his intention to resign in the coming weeks.

The last time there were more byelections in that short amount of time was after the 1949 election. That year, newly minted Liberal Leader Louis St. Laurent won his first election as prime minister and by October of 1950 he had called 16 byelections.

Jonathan Malloy, a political science professor at Carleton University, says there are some similarities between the current Parliament and the one elected in 1949, given St. Laurent and Prime Minister Mark Carney both returned the Liberal Party to power after taking over leadership.

But beyond that, he told CBC News that "the political conditions were rather different back then."

"This is a very unusual Parliament and, to me, it's because of the unexpected election results in April 2025," Malloy said, noting that Carney's Liberals were behind in the polls when he took over the party.

"In both cases you do have a prime minister succeeding another one and successfully winning elections. That's the obvious connection. But on the other hand, the 1949 election was not radically different from what people had been expecting, say a year or two before."

Ironically, there is a near identical situation between the Terrebonne byelection held earlier this year and the 1950 byelection in what was then the Nova Scotia riding of Annapolis-Kings: both results from the preceding general election were declared void due to issues around vote counting.

But besides that case, the reasons for the rapid turnover rate in the 21st Parliament appear to be quite different from the current crop of MPs who have recently left their seats.

Of the 16 MPs who vacated in the first few years following the 1949 vote, most were appointed to judicial or Senate positions. A handful of seats were also left vacant after five MPs died while in office between October 1949 and October 1950.

Éric Grenier — a polls analyst who noted the byelection trend for his publication, The Writ — told CBC News that the amount of MPs stepping down so far in this Parliament could be "just a bit of a coincidence" because there have been a variety of reasons for their resignations.

Conservative Damien Kurek was the first MP to exit to allow for leader Pierre Poilievre to reclaim a seat. Carney also appointed former MPs Bill Blair and Jonathan Wilkinson to diplomatic posts — and appointed Richard Martel to the Senate.

WATCH | More about the upcoming byelections: Our Sunday night panel dives into a discussion on the six byelections called today | Duration closed caption 6:52 Get the latest on CBCNews.ca, the CBC News App, and CBC News Network for breaking news and analysis.

Four MPs swapped their federal roles for provincial or municipal ones. Larry Brock left to return to his local Crown attorney's office. Former cabinet ministers Steven Guilbeault and Chrystia Freeland left after serving a number of years in the former Trudeau government and Conservative Cathay Wagantall had been on the Opposition benches since 2015.

Malloy said the surprising reversal of Liberal fortunes during the 2025 campaign could have pushed some of those MPs to reassess their career trajectories. He suggested that for Liberals, they may have expected to lose their seats (or move to the Opposition benches) under Trudeau and are "not really comfortable in this new situation" of serving in Carney's government — as was the apparent case with Guilbeault.

For Conservatives, Malloy said there are likely some dashed expectations of forming government.

"Elections have a habit of helping MPs make their career decisions one way or the other," he said.

Grenier said the Liberals attaining a majority in the House earlier this year may have also factored into recent decisions.

"[That] kind of sets everybody's minds to the next four years rather than the next 18 months," he said.

The current slate of byelections may not reach the same levels as seen in the early days of Parliament when MPs were expected to resign and rerun in their riding when they were appointed ministers — a practice that was ended in 1931.

Still, Grenier says it's been a significant amount of byelections so far this parliamentary session.

"It is just kind of remarkable how many there's been," he said.

World.title: Colombia’s special forces liberate hostages from Cartagena supermarket
World.content:
Colombia’s security forces liberated some 20 people who were held hostage inside a supermarket in the northern city of Cartagena after a 15-hour stand-off.

The operation ended a tense situation that began around 8AM on Tuesday when the armed kidnappers entered the Exito supermarket in La Castellano, a residential neighborhood.

According to President Abelardo de la Espriella, who led the liberation operation, the kidnappers were meant to rob an armored car that had already left with the proceeds of the day before.

The kidnappers subsequently kidnapped a group of 30 people, and demanded COP7billion ($2 million) and the possibility to escape the supermarket.

Throughout the day, at least five of the hostages were released from the supermarket cafeteria, whose windows had been covered with papers. One video showed a row of hostages sitting behind the window.

Riot police was deployed around midnight after family members and onlookers became restless.

The situation took a quick turn after 1PM when explosions were heard and special forces entered the building.

The security forces killed one of the kidnappers and detained the remaining four, De la Espriella said in a social media video.

Images that were shared on social media showed special police forces securing the Exito’s cafeteria and removing the paper from the windows.

De la Espriella said that all the hostages were released in an “extraordinary joint operation between the National Police and the military forces.”

One agent would have been injured in the rescue operation, reported Caracol Radio.

The kidnappers “were given the opportunity to surrender and release the hostages, but they rejected that opportunity, so we took decisive action,” said the president.

World.title: 22 injured after car bomb strikes central Colombia governor’s office
World.content:
Twenty-two people were reportedly injured and more than 80 buildings were damaged in a car bomb attack on the Governor’s Office of Meta in Villavicencio, central Colombia.

According to Meta’s Security Secretary, Franklin Olivos, the car that exploded carried approximately 100 kilograms of explosives and caused damage to buildings that were located more than 100 meters away from the blast.

Among the injured are five private security guards. One of them needed surgery, according to his employer.

Olivos blamed the attack on the 39th Front, a unit of the FARC dissident group EMC, which has opposed the peace process that started 10 years ago on Tuesday and controls large swathes of jungle territory in the south of Colombia.

In an initial response, President Abelardo de la Espriella said that “narcoterrorism is desperate because we are confronting it head-on. It seeks to intimidate us and force us to back down so we seek another sham peace process.”

De la Espriella, an opponent of the peace process, has been advertising an “iron fist” policy against organized crime and illegal armed groups.

The president’s alleged offensive has failed to produce any results and guerrilla groups have continued to attack State security forces and infrastructure.

World.title: Colombia strips key critics of security details
World.content:
Colombia’s National Protection Unit (UNP) has withdrawn the security details of journalist Daniel Coronell, a major critic of President Abelardo de la Espriella, after vowing to protect the freedom of the press.

Coronell’s local security detail was removed because he lives in the United States, which would make it impossible for the UNP to reassess his protection plan.

The Miami-based journalist frequently travels to Colombia for his work and was in Bogota to receive a lifetime achievement award from the national journalism prize.

While receiving the prize, Coronell sharply criticized De la Espriella for promoting self-promotion over governance. using state resources to censor critics, restricting public information to “friendly media,” and leveraging a history of aggressive lawsuits against reporters.

The journalist’s criticism triggered a clash with Interior Minister Alejandro Ordoñez, who accused Coronell of being angry for having State subsidies pulled.

After press freedom foundation FLIP responded to defend Coronell, Ordoñez claimed that “the freedom of the press enjoys full protection and guarantees from the government.”

We value and defend freedom of the press as a cornerstone of democracy. The press is free, but it is also responsible. It is not a license to abuse, slander, defame, fabricate stories, spread misinformation, or engage in politics. Nor is it a license to destroy democracy or its institutions with lies. Interior Minister Alejandro Ordoñez

Coronell played a key role in Colombian journalism since the late 1980’s and was forced to flee Colombia in 2005 after reports on the ties of former President Alvaro Uribe and paramilitary groups escalated death threats.

The journalist currently works with Noticias Uno and Caracol Radio, and has more than 700,000 subscribers on YouTube.

The UNP previously stripped former President Gustavo Petro and former presidential candidate Claudia Lopez of their security details.

World.title: Illegal armed group carries out first urban drone attack: three injured in northeast Colombia
World.content:
A couple and their 18-month-old baby were injured in a drone attack on a police station in Cucuta, the first major city to be struck from the sky by guerrilla explosives.

The attack damaged more than 60 homes near the Norte de Santander Police Department in the Tasajero neighborhood in the north of the regional capital, the province’s security secretary, George Quintero, told press.

As of now, the situation is as follows: more than 60 damaged homes located just 20 meters from the police headquarters, and three people injured. Security secretary George Quintero

The homes were hit because the police department’s signal-jamming systems reportedly caused the drones to miss their target.

An unknown number of drones were able to reach the interior of the Police Department’s compound, leaving only minor damage.

Guerrilla group ELN has been carrying out multiple drone attacks in Catatumbo, a nearby region with major coca cultivations, and exercises control in the peripheral slums of Cucuta.

The group was accused of attacking the same police department with home-made mortars in August. This attack injured seven policemen.

In a response to the guerrilla attack, President Abelardo de la Espriella in October ordered the militarization of the border city, which has been struggling with security issues for years.

De la Espriella vowed that he “will not allow narco-terrorism to continue sowing fear and threatening families” in Cucuta and the surrounding Norte de Santander province.

According to the authorities, the militarization of the city sought to “strengthen territorial control, protect citizens, and confront” the illegal armed groups that operate in and around Cucuta.

The president’s offensive against illegal armed groups and organized crime has been hampered by an increase in the use of drones that are equipped with explosives.

All kinds of illegal armed groups use the relatively new technology to push back the authorities from areas under their control.

World.title: Colombia asks X to suspend Petro’s social media account
World.content:
Colombia’s communications ministry said Sunday that it had requested social media platform X to suspend former President Gustavo Petro for “possible incitement to violence.”

In a statement that was published of X, the ministry said it reported Petro’s account to X’s Public Affairs, Safety, and Rules Enforcement Team.

According to the statement, the request to suspend the leftist former president, who has more than 9 million followers, was due to a November 21 post in which Petro asked “the people of Colombia to demand Abelardo’s resignation now.”

Petro has been trying to promote popular opposition against De la Espriella, who he has called an illegitimate president.

According to the ministry, Petro’s call to “take action in the streets” could constitute a call for violence against the government.

In a response, the former president said the De la Espriella administration sought to impose censorship on him, which is “expressly prohibited by the Constitution.”

The ministry’s request “demonstrates the extent of the current government’s illegitimacy,” added Petro.

The former president is now the leader of the Historic Pact (PH) opposition party and has actively been promoting a general strike in response to his successor’s controversial policy decisions.

Petro is a member of the PH’s more radical wing and can still count on a significant following among Colombia’s population.

World.title: The deteriorating press freedom in Colombia and the Americas
World.content:
I sat down with Joshua Collins of Pirate Wire Services to discuss the deteriorating press freedom situation in Colombia and the rest of Latin America.

This fundraiser episode seeks to lift Colombia Reports out of financial trouble. If you can, please ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠donate⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ or ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠become a patron⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠.

World.title: De la Espriella calls on US to prosecute Petro in response to call to “resign now”
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella called on the US Justice Department to “investigate, prosecute and hopefully jail former President Gustavo Petro after the latter called on the people to “rise up” and “restore real democracy.”

De la Espriella addressed the nation at the end of a day of anti-government marches that mobilized tens of thousands of people throughout Colombia.

Petro led the march in Cali and called on his supporters to “rise up,” call a general strike and force the president to “leave now,” less than four months after De la Espriella took office.

Reiterating fraud accusations and the president’s business ties to paramilitary warlords and drug traffickers, the former president told the crowd that “it is not about waiting until 2030; an illegitimate government must leave now.”

A government whose policy goes against the people must leave now. A government whose policy builds hunger and death for the people of Colombia must leave now. Life must be restored, democracy must be restored, and the slogan “Abelardo, resign now!” must become the slogan of the majority of the Colombian people. An agreement will eventually be made to transition back so that the Constitution of Colombia and the laws in favor of the Colombian people prevail. But from here on out—and that is why we must move to a national strike, that is why we must move to a general strike—within the people’s right of expression and decision, an illegitimate government that goes against the interests of the Colombian population must leave now. Gustavo Petro

De la Espriella told Petro that he would never accept they “attack democracy, promote a coup d’état or attempt to destroy Colombia, just as he did when he was a guerrilla fighter.”

The president claimed that the former President and congressional opposition leader Ivan Cepeda “have no moral authority whatsoever. However, as I tell you, I will not accept them attacking democracy, attacking institutionality, or promoting a coup d’état in an attempt to destroy Colombia.”

De la Espriella repeated his threat to extradite his predecessor if requested to do so by the administration of his ally, US President Donald Trump.

I make a direct call to the judicial authorities of the United States so that investigations related to acts of corruption, drug trafficking, or any other criminal conduct move forward with full rigor and the independence of the judicial system in the United States. Petro’s government was a criminal enterprise, and international laws and provisions were violated. The United States has jurisdiction to investigate him, prosecute him, and hopefully imprison him. Let the North American justice system act, let the whole truth be known, let the evidence be examined, and let those found responsible answer before the law without regard for anything other than the application of the law. President Abelardo de la Espriella

The president has tried to criminalize the opposition and the former government ever since taking office in August without much success.

World.title: Colombia rejects US proposal to conduct joint strikes against drug trafficking: NYT
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella rejected a US plan to conduct joint military operations, anonymous US officials told the New York Times (NYT).

According to the NYT, De la Espriella told the US government he supported working with the US military, but lacked congressional support invite US soldiers on Colombian soil.

The conversation would have taken place in the week ahead of US defense secretary Pete Hegseth’s visit to Colombia on Wednesday.

In a response, the president and the defense secretary said that the alleged US plan was “fake news.”

“I have not rejected any proposal of the Government of President Donald Trump,” De la Espriella said on social media platform X.

Colombia and the United States maintain strong and increasingly close cooperation in the areas of security, intelligence, and the fight against drug cartels and narco-terrorist organizations. President Abelardo de la Espriella

The president confirmed that congressional approval would be required for him to invite foreign troops into Colombia.

Between visits to Venezuela and Ecuador, Hegseth briefly stopped in Colombia, and met with Defense Minister Jorge Eduardo Mora and Foreign Minister Omar Bulla.

The defense secretary expressed his support for the government’s plans to combat drug trafficking.

“You, sir, are never going to have a stronger partner than President Trump, Secretary Hegseth an the War Department,” Hegseth told Bula.

Both the US and the Colombian governments have assumed a militaristic approach to drug trafficking, contrary to their predecessors.

World.title: An Excursion 30 Years in the Making
World.content:
Photo Feature by Fabiana del Valle

HAVANA TIMES – In the late 1990s, my school organized trips to the Jardín de Aspiro campground. These outings were supervised by teachers and a few parents who joined in the adventure. However, my mother wouldn’t let me go. For her, anything beyond familiar boundaries entailed a lurking danger.

It’s true that on one occasion, after much begging and pleading, she gave me permission. But since bad luck has followed me since childhood, the bus that was supposed to pick us up broke down along the way, and the trip was postponed until the following weekend. My mother saw this as a divine sign or some kind of omen and withdrew her permission.

I remember the innocent envy I felt toward my best friends, who never missed a single excursion. Every Monday, the classroom was filled with stories of swimming in the river and nights under the stars. My teenage imagination placed that spot on a par with London, a city I dreamed of visiting someday.

That little corner in the foothills of the Sierra del Rosario, in the municipality of San Cristobal, retained for me the allure of the forbidden and the unattainable. But I grew up and never had another opportunity to go, nor did I seek one. My life changed, and adulthood took me toward other horizons.

Still, that unfulfilled longing remained buried deep inside me, and my husband, knowing my story, was determined to make the trip happen. He made some inquiries, and a friend told him we could get there on our electric motorcycle without any problems. Although the campground remains closed to the public, we could go to the river or enjoy the natural pool.

The idea of fulfilling a wish nearly three decades in the making excited me. Since walking the damp streets of London remains a dream with no foreseeable prospect of coming true, at least I could immerse myself for a few hours in the natural surroundings Aspiro promised. We prepared some sandwiches, a bottle of soda, and some water to quench our thirst, and set off early that morning. What we hadn’t anticipated was the condition of the route. The steep hills and the road, deteriorated from a lack of maintenance, proved quite a challenge for our motorcycle.

Since the heat is less intense at this time of year, we hoped to find some privacy. But Cubans aren’t afraid of the cold, and as the morning wore on, other people began arriving at the pool, seeking to wash away their everyday troubles in the refreshing water.

We had been looking for some privacy in a place where we could breathe fresh air and disconnect for a while. Our dream refuge ended up crowded with people, their speakers blasting reparto music through the vegetation, disrupting the natural harmony and the haven of peace we had both envisioned for our getaway.

Despite everything, it was worth immersing ourselves in those crystal-clear, cold waters, so cold that our skin felt as though it were burning the moment we touched the water. Those natural surroundings brought us a revitalizing sense of relief. And we were only there for a few hours!

Before returning home, we stopped at the entrance to the Jardín de Aspiro campground, and I asked the guards for permission to take some pictures. I couldn’t leave without seeing the inside of the place I had so longed to visit as a teenager.

I did a little research and discovered that the campground opened in 1982. The site was chosen to take advantage of the river, the natural pool, its proximity to the waterfall, and the mountain trails with their numerous caves.

The name Aspiro is associated with the Spanish merchant Don Jose de Aspiro, who was one of the owners of those lands. The grounds of this enclave once formed part of several estates where agricultural activities were combined with botanical experimentation. I have read that in the early 19th century, a garden featuring exotic species and a wide variety of flora was established there, where the naturalist and botanist Jose Blaín Cervantes conducted his studies.

The facility was repaired and refurbished last year so that it could be operational this summer. But on this island, after 1959, objectivity was lost. A video room, a restaurant, a game room, and remodeled cabins with air conditioning, kitchens, and bathrooms.

All of this without water, since the blackouts prevent water from being pumped to the facility. The services the center was supposed to offer have been reduced to zero, and there is no hope of recovering the investment. The place possesses an undeniable beauty, and it is a shame that it cannot be enjoyed.

Although we returned home satisfied — once again managing to escape the suffocating reality we live in with very few resources — I cannot shake the sad conviction that there is no future for an island that sinks deeper into misery, neglect, and darkness with each passing day.

See more photo features here on Havana Times.

World.title: A Week of “Normality” Ended
World.content:
By Veronica Vega

HAVANA TIMES – Since everything that begins must come to an end, this morning the spell was broken and Cinderella’s carriage turned back into a pumpkin.

What I mean is that the seven days of DAF (Automatic Frequency Tripping) on the circuit to which our building was assigned have come to an end.

These circuits ration access to electricity in this new, nameless phase we are living through in Cuba. (There is an urgent need to give it a name to make historians’ work easier.)

I have no idea what DAF actually means, but in practice, it entails a week of uninterrupted electricity and a return to our lost normality.

A functioning refrigerator, food that you are not forced to pack into small containers crammed into the freezer among jars of ice. Because you have to make as much ice as possible to withstand the long hours of blackouts, maintaining a temperature that allows you to preserve your food.

That food, with its heart-stopping prices, robs you of your peace of mind three times: when you buy it, when you cook it — if you have no gas available and depend on an electric burner and whatever brief spell of electricity you get — and finally, when you rack your brain trying to fit whatever is left for the next day into a freezer that is no longer running.

That blessed week also means cooking in the electric cooker without fear that the process will be interrupted and the beans will remain hard. Or the rice half-cooked.

Feeling a strange peace that gradually begins to rock you like the waves, transporting you back to almost idyllic times, when the word “crisis” was still the subject of jokes rather than this constant tightness in your stomach, this bitter feeling of stagnation and of having lost your way.

Night falls, and the lights around you reassure you that there is life outside: televisions switched on, fans and air conditioners providing that minimum level of comfort and restoring the home to its status as a sacred refuge.

Some people play dance music, and the lights of small private businesses twinkle like costly harbors of hope, of other people’s prosperity.

When I go out to walk my dogs, I sense a kind of tranquility in the air, a feeling of shared goodwill throughout the area where DAF reigns, or a sense of relief that rekindles the memory of what a country can be, even amid shortages, if at least a basic level of functionality prevails.

But the full bliss of DAF is only achieved if you are lucky enough for that week to coincide with water flowing into the communal cistern.

Then there is no need to rush to fill tanks, buckets, and all kinds of containers in an agonizing race against the ever-uncertain hours of electricity.

You can do everything at the pace of nature, at the pace of life. Relax. Remember a way of living in which everyone can enjoy a glass of cold water, a hot meal, and a warm bath, even if they don’t have a solar panel, EcoFlow power stations, or gas paid for by a relative abroad.

You can feel that your time belongs to you again, face life’s other minor setbacks without experiencing them as anonymous and unexpected assaults.

“We used to live like this…” you tell yourself and immediately wonder how long ago that was and what we did (or failed to do) to lose the little we had.

Who marked us on the map of the world with an ominous sign? And why? After surviving the promises, the lies, and the disintegration of a fledgling society that never became prosperous, just, or equitable.

A disintegration all the more terrible because it is so inconspicuous. There are no bombs or explosions. No wounded people shedding that blood which assaults the eyes and which Facebook mercifully covers up as soon as it detects it, to protect its users’ visual sensibilities.

No, nobody sees us. Nobody hears us. The entire island could disappear, just as even the sharpest outlines are swallowed up by darkness.

As though we were being engulfed by the waters that separate us from the most powerful country in the world.

If an unspoken joy awakens with the arrival of DAF, a heavy sadness settles over everything when the day comes when the blessing shifts to another circuit that you will see glowing at night, while we return to the darkness and the wretched feeling of abandonment.

Then you console yourself by counting the weeks it takes for DAF to rotate through each of the circuits, like the hands of a clock, like the rotation of the Earth, until it is our turn once again to experience that fleeting season of normality.

Read more from the diary of Veronica Vega here on Havana Times.

World.title: AI Data Centers: Local Damage, World Threat
World.content:
Demonstrators protest against a planned data center in Decatur, Georgia. ‘Concerns over AI, rising energy costs and the environment are intermeshing.’ Photo: Erik S Lesser/EPA

By Jomo Kwame Sundaram and Rachel Gong (IPS)

HAVANA TIMES – Mass local opposition to AI data centers influenced the US mid-term elections. Perverse incentives have driven speculative investments to build more despite poor returns so far. Worse, financing investments using loans risks causing a major financial crisis.



The massive computing demands of AI (artificial intelligence) requiring hyperscale data centers have grown rapidly over the last decade, greatly exceeding traditional storage cloud providers for general web hosting or standard information technology.



The number of such data centers worldwide has nearly tripled, with most in the US, but local opposition has slowed plans to build more. It is unclear how many data centers are being built, as details are often withheld, even from governments.



AI data centers in the US have been very unpopular with local communities. They are noisy and ugly, draining energy and water resources, with most profits going to the mainly US companies building them.



They use much electricity, straining electricity grids and driving up electricity prices. Data centers largely run on fossil fuels, exacerbating greenhouse gas emissions and planetary heating.



Data centers need a huge amount of freshwater to prevent overheating. Yet, more are being built despite spreading droughts and water stress.



There are also other significant health and environmental concerns that promoters hide, claiming modern data centers use ‘closed-loop systems’ reducing their adverse impacts.

Rachel Gong

Governments claim they create employment, although only a small fraction of promised jobs have materialised. Unsurprisingly, there is growing local opposition to AI data centers worldwide.



After meeting with China’s leader Xi Jinping following the midterms, Trump threatened tough measures against building data centers abroad, deeming their US presence necessary to maintain US dominance.



AI expects AI bubble to collapse



Dean Baker asked various AI chatbots whether pension and hedge fund investment managers face perverse incentives when investing in AI-related companies.



If they did not invest in companies which have far outperformed others in recent times, their performance would fall behind their peers, costing them bonuses and even their jobs.



And if all AI stocks fell, they would not be penalised as other fund managers had done likewise. AI agreed that asset managers would keep investing in AI even though their market performance did not make sense.



They would continue such investments as keeping their jobs required following the herd and ‘riding the wave’.



Such perverse incentives may also induce similar behavior among top executives at Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle.



All of them have “committed hundreds of billions of their companies’ capital to building data centres to support the AI producers, primarily OpenAI and Anthropic”.



And what if AI companies have ‘over-invested’ trillions in data centers with limited prospects of profitability? If this view of AI’s future is widely shared, it would make sense to stop building and cut losses.



But what if AI top executives still believe it is better to continue investing? Perhaps AI will eventually pay off. And if they stopped investing to cut their losses, they could also lose trillions, probably ending their careers.



Hence, they keep building data centers even if they suspect they are pouring in good money after bad. AI generally agrees that top executives are likely to continue investing.

Jomo Kwame Sundaram

After the AI bubble bursts, it is likely there will be some obligatory investigations into how and why the AI boom became a dangerously unsustainable bubble until ‘business as usual’ resumes.



When the bubble bursts



William H. Janeway notes the notion of an ‘AI speculative investment bubble’ has recently been widely accepted. Since bubbles inevitably burst, fears are now rising that time is running out.



Janeway warns that the AI industry’s heavy and still growing reliance on borrowed money risks triggering a major financial crisis. AI hyperscalers have to keep increasing profits to justify the still rising investments and borrowings.



If generative AI delivers productivity gains across a wide range of applications, the current frenzy may be remembered as a productive bubble.



But it is unlikely these gains will be large and soon enough to justify the huge investments in AI infrastructure to date.



Growing reliance on private credit to fund current data center building, with lenders themselves borrowing from banks, implies the AI bubble is enmeshed with the financial system.



The AI bubble can still deflate gradually rather than burst abruptly. Hence, slowing AI growth and data center construction delays may actually be better for the economy.



However, the risk of sudden collapse remains. The second Trump administration’s record so far generates broader concerns about how it is likely to handle an AI bust.



Thankfully, however, history reminds us that speculative bubbles may leave behind some valuable infrastructure in their wake despite bankrupting those financing them.



Rachel Gong is Associate Director of Research at the Khazanah Research Institute studying the intersections of digital technologies, society and policy.

World.title: Those Who Really Mistreat You and Don’t Care About You
World.content:
Eggs for 130 pesos each or 3,600 for a carton of 30.

By Lien Estrada

HAVANA TIMES – In his song “La sal no sala” (Salt Doesn’t Make Things Salty), Argentine singer Charly García has a line that goes: “The girl on the corner is treating me badly, she sells me a drug I can’t afford.” When I first heard it, I found it quite amusing. I’ve enjoyed his entire discography thanks to a friend abroad who was kind enough to get it for me.

Back then, we didn’t have Internet access, and Charly García’s music wasn’t heard in Cuba because, as I understand it, like John Lennon, he had made statements unfavorable to the dictator, Fidel Castro. And, of course, he was never forgiven for that.

However, I had seen a television interview with Colombian singer Carlos Vives, who said that Charly Garcia’s music was exceptional, and that was when I asked my friend to do me the favor of getting it for me. And he did. Like Fito Paez’s music, I find it revealing. But the line that has stayed with me the most is this cheeky one about the girl who sells a product at such a high price that it cannot be purchased, and the singer interprets that as mistreatment.

Perhaps this line has resonated so deeply with me because I live in a context where buying anything is a real challenge. When you find that a package of seasoned sausages costs far more than most people’s retirement pensions. A 10-pound package of chicken costs 9,500 pesos when the minimum wage is 3,210 pesos. A piece of candy costs 40 pesos. And to think that I had naively believed that everything would improve once the currencies were unified, supposedly in 2021.

That experience with stores where prices were in US dollars, but salaries and pensions were paid in Cuban pesos was never a good one, not even for those who belonged to the country’s sole political party, which runs everything and controls everything. Therein lies the difference between Cuban reality and the line from Charly’s song “La sal no sala.”

We know that those who mistreat us with these economic measures to “save the Homeland” are certainly not the girl on the corner. Nor is it the young man with the pushcart trying to sell lemons that will eventually rot because most people cannot afford them. Those mistreating us are not the women who resell goods, because there are few other business opportunities in this land. Cuba stopped producing things quite some time ago.

Those who mistreat us are those elderly gentlemen dressed in olive green, whom there seems to be no way of convincing that building an economy is essential to saving that very Homeland they are forever mentioning in their speeches, and that our daily bread cannot be obtained by talking about ideological work among the people.

But we don’t know how to get the message across by force (through sabotage, gunfire, and bombs), and these army officers won’t listen to reason. They see no mistreatment whatsoever in their political and economic management of a country that is increasingly falling apart, but rather “decisions that are not fair, but necessary,” as the tyrant Commander-in-Chief Fidel Castro once put it.

People decide to leave. Even sensing the truth of what the French say: “To leave is to die a little.” It doesn’t matter. More than a million Cubans have decided they will no longer endure mistreatment at the hands of a government that refuses to budge and is utterly convinced that it is right. More and more people are leaving. Every day.

One thing, however, is clearer than ever: it is not the girl on the corner who is mistreating us. And that is an important fact.

Read more from the diary of Lien Estrada here on Havana Times.

World.title: International News Briefs for Tuesday, November 24, 2026
World.content:
HAVANA TIMES – We bring you some of the top international news stories compiled by Democracy Now on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Trump Intervenes

Nov 24, 2026

Image Credit: X/@aburducky

Jensen Huang is back as CEO of the chip giant Nvidia, after President Trump personally called into a meeting of the company’s board on Sunday to push for his reinstatement. Huang had resigned less than two weeks ago, after news reports revealed he had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who was allegedly in communication with China’s top spy agency. The woman worked with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company suspected of buying advanced Nvidia chips and then diverting them to China in violation of U.S. export rules. On Monday, the Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist. During an interview on CNBC, President Trump was questioned about his role in reinstating Huang.

Eamon Javers: “Mr. President, did you give the board of directors an assurance that Jensen Huang would not be prosecuted at all for any of these” —

President Donald Trump: “I didn’t use the word ‘prosecuted.’”

Eamon Javers: — “questions around export controls?”

President Donald Trump: “But I said — I said that we believe — and I put out a statement. I think you probably saw that.”

Eamon Javers: “We did, yes.”

President Donald Trump: “That we believe he’s fine, he’s absolutely fine. I gave them enough” —

Carl Quintanilla: “There was a” —

President Donald Trump: — “assurance.”

Meanwhile, President Trump used his Truth Social platform to share a bizarre AI-generated meme that altered a photo taken moments after Trump was shot in Butler, Pennsylvania, in 2024. The doctored photo depicts a bloodied Huang holding a red bra in the air, with an Nvidia flag replacing the U.S. flag behind him.

Trump’s Stake in Nvidia Grows by Up to $15 Million as Stock Price Soars on Jensen Huang’s Return

Nov 24, 2026

Image Credit: Joyce N. Boghosian

News of Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia sent share prices soaring by over 30%, recovering much of the value lost since Huang resigned two weeks ago. Among beneficiaries of the stock surge is President Trump, whose stake in Nvidia grew to as much as $62 million before the scandal broke. Trump’s net worth grew by up to $15 million on Monday. Also benefiting is Cantor Fitzgerald, the investment firm that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick ran for decades before joining the Trump administration. It’s now controlled by Lutnick’s sons, Brandon and Kyle. Cantor Fitzgerald held shares in Nvidia worth hundreds of millions of dollars, even as Lutnick made key decisions affecting Nvidia’s operations.

Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as CEO comes after Reuters reported Nvidia’s accounting practices have prompted an investigation by the Securities and Exchange Commission. Nvidia and Huang also face a class-action shareholder lawsuit in California alleging securities fraud and misleading investors. And Huang is scheduled to testify on Capitol Hill next week, both in private testimony to lawmakers and in a public session of the Senate Banking Committee. We’ll have more on this story after headlines.

Analysis Estimates More Than 700,000 Russian Soldiers Have Died Fighting in Ukraine

Nov 24, 2026

A new report estimates more than 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in combat since President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine nearly five years ago. The finding is based on an analysis of leaked data from Russia’s state statistics agency, published by a pair of Russian-language news outlets operating outside of Russia.

On Monday, the Kremlin warned that Ukraine will face “painful consequences” for drone attacks on Russian ships in Libya and the Baltic Sea. Overnight, Russian drone and missile attacks on Zaporizhzhia left two people dead and more than 40 others injured, after a guided aerial bomb hit an apartment building near a bridge crossing the Dnipro River.

UNICEF Says Russian Attacks Are Killing Three Children, on Average, Each Day in Ukraine

Nov 24, 2026

Russia’s latest deadly strikes came as the U.N. Children’s Fund said the number of children killed or injured in Ukraine is approaching levels not seen since 2022, during the first year of Russia’s full-scale invasion. This is UNICEF’s Louise Wateridge.

Louise Wateridge: “According to the Human Rights Monitoring Mission for Ukraine, at least 1,144 children have been killed or injured in Ukraine in the first 10 months of 2026. This is a higher number of verified child casualties than in any other of the previous three years here in Ukraine, and that is more than three children who have been killed or injured every single day.”

Russia Threatens “Open War” with Estonia, a Former Soviet Republic Turned NATO Member

Nov 24, 2026

Russia has threatened to attack Estonia, after the Kremlin accused the country of allowing Ukraine to launch attacks from Estonian territory. On Monday, Russia’s Foreign Ministry declared Estonia was “on the verge of triggering open war.” The threat came after Estonia announced the closure of its land border with Russia. Estonia is a former Soviet republic, and has been a NATO member since 2004.

Rapid Support Forces Launch Drone Attack on Sudan’s Capital as Electrical Grid Nears Collapse

Nov 24, 2026

Sudan’s military says it intercepted drones launched by the Rapid Support Forces over the capital Khartoum, following a series of attacks that struck the city’s main airport and several buildings, including a U.N. facility. At least four people were reportedly killed in those attacks. They came as Sudan’s power grid is on the brink of collapse following attacks on electricity stations

Yemen’s Houthis Say 41 Civilians Are Killed in Saudi Attacks Using U.S. Arms

Nov 24, 2026

In Yemen, officials with the Ansar Allah movement, also known as the Houthis, say Saudi warplanes killed 41 civilians in a single day, in a series of strikes carried out with U.S.-made ordnance. One Saudi airstrike targeted a telecommunications hub, leaving 17 civilians dead, according to a Houthi spokesperson. Other attacks targeted buses and public transport vehicles in Hodeidah and Lahij, reportedly with GBU-49 and GBU-12 bombs. The U.N. warns over 1,600 people have been killed and 300,000 displaced since the ceasefire in Yemen between the Saudi-backed government and the Houthis collapsed in July.

Oxfam Report Finds Israel’s Military Assault “Has Turned Gaza into a Toxic Wasteland”

Nov 24, 2026

In Gaza, an Israeli airstrike on a security post killed two police officers and another Palestinian in al-Mawasi, a narrow strip of land that Israel has designated as a so-called safe zone. Another strike killed three brothers traveling by donkey cart — one of them, a child. In Gaza City, Palestinians held a funeral for Adel al-Helo, an employee of the U.N. agency for Palestinian refugees, UNRWA, killed in an attack a day earlier. This is his brother, Nizar al-Helo.

Nizar al-Helo: “He was working at the water dam in Jabaliya camp, supplying the water for the people of Jabaliya camp, and have been killed by an airstrike in Jabaliya camp by the Israeli army. They doesn’t make any difference between the civilian people and other people, even the people of the United Nations.”

Meanwhile, Oxfam has published a new report titled “Environmental War Crimes: How Israel’s military assault has turned Gaza into a toxic wasteland, threatening human survival.” It finds contamination from heavy metals, explosive residue, asbestos fibers, dioxins, crystalline silica, persistent organic pollutants and biological contaminants across 99% of Gaza’s territory.

Lebanese Immigrants Are Set to Lose Protected Status in U.S., Despite Ongoing Israeli Assault

Nov 24, 2026

In southern Lebanon, Israeli forces launched a series of airstrikes, artillery and machine-gun attacks earlier today — the latest in a series of violations of a U.S.-mediated ceasefire Israel agreed to earlier this year. The violence has uprooted 1.2 million people from their homes — about one-fifth of Lebanon’s population.

Here in the U.S., a program granting temporary protected status to Lebanese immigrants and refugees is due to expire on Friday. A bill introduced by lawmakers in Michigan, a state home to a large Lebanese diaspora community, would extend TPS. It’s co-sponsored by Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib.

Rep. Rashida Tlaib: “Without temporary protected status, our neighbors are at risk of being deported to Lebanon, where the ongoing Israeli invasion — illegal Israeli invasion — and ethnic cleansing campaign has already killed 4,000 people this year. I introduced the Lebanon TPS Act because the safety of our neighbors cannot be left up to the whims of Trump and Stephen Miller.”

Mexico to Try Alleged Drug Kingpin “El Chapo Isidro” After Denying U.S. Extradition Request

Nov 24, 2026

Mexico’s military says it captured one of the leaders of the Beltrán Leyva cartel and two of his lieutenants during an operation in Sinaloa state on Friday night. The arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores sparked a wave of armed ​clashes between Mexican security forces and cartel members, who set up flaming roadblocks in some areas. Meza Flores is known as “El Chapo Isidro” and is one ​of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives. His arrest reportedly came in coordination with U.S. intelligence agencies. Mexico denied a U.S. request to extradite him, saying he will be tried in a Mexican court. The Trump administration has threatened to take unilateral ⁠military action inside Mexico after accusing the government of failing to halt narcotrafficking.

Alarm Grows over U.S. Army Plan to Explode Lead-Containing Munitions on Wednesday

Nov 24, 2026

The U.S. Army is proceeding with plans to blow up a stockpile of toxic explosives at a munitions plant in southeastern Iowa. The acting Army secretary said late Monday the “extensively mitigated, carefully controlled detonation” would occur on Wednesday morning, based on forecast wind conditions. The statement came hours after a federal court denied a request for an emergency stay from environmental groups who warn the plan could send a plume of toxic lead up to 100 miles away. In response, Senator Tammy Duckworth, an Army veteran whose home state of Illinois is potentially downwind of a lead-release disaster, wrote, “The Army still has failed to explain to the public why this detonation needs to happen this way — and too many people fear for their family’s health and safety. This is an extreme failure of communication, planning and leadership. And they must be held accountable for the harm done.”

Pete Hegseth Faces Call to Resign from His Former Chief of Staff

Nov 24, 2026

A former top aide to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is calling on him to resign, saying he has badly mismanaged both the Pentagon and the ongoing war in Iran and let showmanship get in the way of doing his job well. Joe Kasper, Hegseth’s chief of staff during the first three months of the second Trump administration, told Politico, “Pete’s been belligerent in his stewardship of an office that will outlive him or any memory of his service.”

Jimmy Gomez Quits Congress as Ethics Committee Finds Evidence of “Unwelcome Sexual Conduct”

Nov 24, 2026

In more news from Capitol Hill, outgoing California Democratic Representative Jimmy Gomez announced he’ll resign from Congress next week, after a House Ethics Committee report found substantial evidence that he had engaged in “unwelcome sexual conduct” with a female aide. The report determined Gomez’s behavior might have constituted a “criminal misdemeanor sexual abuse.” Gomez is the third congressman to resign over sexual misconduct allegations this year, following Democrat Eric Swalwell of California and Republican Tony Gonzales of Texas.

JD Vance Faces Senate Scrutiny for Allegedly Helping Campaign Donor Secure Venezuelan Oil Licenses

Nov 24, 2026

Image Credit: Reuters/Juan Carlos Hernandez

A Senate committee is investigating whether JD Vance used his position as vice president to help a major political donor secure lucrative business opportunities involving Venezuelan oil. That’s according to Reuters, which reports Vice President Vance met in December 2025 with John Addison, a trader with the commodities giant Vitol whose company went on to land ⁠special licenses to sell hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of Venezuelan oil following the January U.S. military operation that abducted President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores. Reuters reports Vance and Addison met at Montana’s Yellowstone Club, an ultra-exclusive ski and golf resort. Both Vance and Addison have denied having the meeting, but in a letter to Vance, New Hampshire Democratic Senator Maggie Hassan writes, “Despite denials from your office and Mr. Addison, flight records place his private jet and ⁠your government plane at the same Montana airport on the day of the reported meeting.” John Addison had been an early backer of Vance, contributing $300,000 to Vance’s successful 2022 campaign for an Ohio Senate seat.

Read more news here on Havana Times.

World.title: Falklands, growing interest in adjacent areas to Navitas Sea Lion
World.content:
Falklands, growing interest in adjacent areas to Navitas Sea Lion

25th Wednesday, November 2026 - 11:21 UTC Full article

The Eco Atlantic farm in is in PL001, adjacent to PL032, where Navitas is expected to begin operating next March

Exploration Company Eco (Atlantic) Oil & Gas has farmed into Israeli group Navitas Petroleum's PL001 license block off the Falkland Islands. The move comes after Eco purchased JHI Associates Inc. (JHI), giving the company a 35% working interest in the block, with Navitas holding the remaining 65%.

Exploration Company Eco (Atlantic) Oil & Gas has farmed into Israeli group Navitas Petroleum's PL001 license block off the Falkland Islands. The move comes after Eco purchased JHI Associates Inc. (JHI), giving the company a 35% working interest in the block, with Navitas holding the remaining 65%.

According to Brazil Energy Insight, Navitas itself farmed into the block at the start of the year when it bought its stake from JHI. The acreage is adjacent to its upcoming Sea Lion development at PL032.

The company is preparing to commence development drilling for the first phase of Sea Lion in March 2027 expecting first oil in mid-2028.

According to its presentation Eco Atlantic operates in the Toronto Venture Exchange Stock Exchange and London's Alternative Investment Market, AIM, with a strategic portfolio of offshore projects in Guyana (South America) and Namibia and South Africa in partnership with major energy companies and large independents.

According to Eco, Navitas is considering drilling two oil exploration wells during the first phase of the Sea Lion NDA1 drilling campaign expected to start in 2027.

One of the wells under consideration is a multi-target exploration well on PL001 that would target Chatham, Poseidon, Rhea, Selene and Tyche.

Meanwhile, Eco added that the exact timing of drilling the potential PL001 well has yet to be confirmed and the company will announce it in due course.

Similar to other licenses adjacent to the Sea Lion project held by Navitas, should a discovery be made in PL001, it may also be developed, among other options, through a tie-back to the floating production and storage facilities as planned for the Sea Lion project.

Under the PL001 farm-in agreement, Navitas will fund Eco's 35% share of the first US$40 million of gross expenditure on the license through a carry loan capped at US$14m net to Eco.

The loan is repayable from 85% of the free cash flow attributable to Eco's interest in any future production from PL001.

World.title: Falklands at JMC: UK steps up security support for British Overseas Territories
World.content:
Falklands at JMC: UK steps up security support for British Overseas Territories

25th Wednesday, November 2026 - 11:20 UTC Full article

Uma Kumaran MP – UK Minister for the OTs and David Burt JP MP – Premier of Bermuda and President of the UK's Overseas Territories Association (UKOTA)

The UK government and elected leaders and representatives from the Overseas Territories are meeting in London, beginning this Monday until November 26, for the annual Joint Ministerial Council (JMC). The JMC is a chance for UKOT leaders to come together to celebrate partnerships with UK and tackle the major challenges of our time.

The UK government and elected leaders and representatives from the Overseas Territories are meeting in London, beginning this Monday until November 26, for the annual Joint Ministerial Council (JMC). The JMC is a chance for UKOT leaders to come together to celebrate partnerships with UK and tackle the major challenges of our time.

The Territories are custodians of extraordinary biodiversity and marine environments, which includes some of the most extraordinary places on Earth – from spectacular coral reefs to huge penguin populations and vast protected ocean like the Sargasso Sea. Preserving this natural heritage is not just good for Britain it is of crucial importance for the whole world's climate ambition.

In an increasingly volatile world, security is also closely connected too. Malign states, criminal gangs, cyber hackers – each seek to exploit weaknesses for their own gain. By working together to protect our communities and respond to emerging threats, the UK and Overseas Territories are more than the sum of our parts.

Working on this objective, people across the British Overseas Territories will benefit from greater protection as the UK steps up security support for the Territories. UK is committing £18m in new funding to tackle organized crime, violence and emerging security threats.

New support will focus on policing, criminal justice and prisons, maritime security, cyber and safeguarding capabilities. It will also draw on UK expertise to enable increased information sharing and cooperation between the Territories.

The four-day Joint Ministerial Council is an annual event to celebrate the modern partnership and explore closer collaboration on shared key priorities, including security, economic growth and climate.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said that the “Overseas Territories are an essential part of the British family of nations, and in a more dangerous world, our security is increasingly bound together.

”Through improved policing, justice and security, today's funding will help to protect us all from malign actors that would do us harm, from organized crime to cyber hackers and hostile states“.

Minister for the Overseas Territories Uma Kumaran pointed out that, ”The Joint Ministerial Council is an important moment for the UK and our Overseas Territories to come together and tackle head-on the key issues of our time.

“The strength of our relationship lies in our ability to tackle challenges around security, growth and climate together, drawing on our respective expertise, experience and global connections.

Furthermore ”when the Territories prosper, Britain prospers too. By standing together, we are stronger, safer and better prepared for the future”.

In effect the Territories are also crucial to Britain's prosperity by supporting investment, jobs and economic activity. Trade between the UK and the Territories is worth around £17bn. Taken together, that puts them among Britain's top 25 trading partners, ahead of major economies including South Korea, Brazil and South Africa.

This is what Britain's relationship with the Territories is about – communities standing together, protecting our shared environment and standing up to the threats we face. It is something we should all value, invest in and be proud of.

The Minister for the Overseas Territories will also use the summit to announce a new safeguarding partnership between the FCDO and the London Borough of Camden.

This will see the exchange of expertise and best practices between the UK and the Overseas Territories, strengthening safeguarding across communities through shared learning.

This year's Joint Ministerial Council is centered on advancing a modern, equal and forward-looking partnership based on mutual respect, shared responsibility and ensuring Overseas Territories voices are heard in decisions that affect them.

The event is expected to focus on wide-ranging discussions on security and resilience, sustainable economic growth, climate and nature, AI, tech and more.

Discussions are also expected on a shared commitment to tackling Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG), recognizing the challenges of this in isolated communities and the collaboration between the UK and Territories in this area.

The meeting builds on the recently agreed Charter for UK Government Engagement with the Overseas Territories. The Charter recognizes the UK's responsibilities towards the Territories and commits to championing Territories' voices and interests.

Falklands and self-determination

The Falkland Islands as a UK Overseas Territory is represented by the Chair of the Legislative Assembly. In a brief statement MLA Ford underlined the significance of JMC and UK's support for self-determination, which is “enshrined in the UN Charter as a fundamental right, yet one we must continually defend. While our freedom was restored by the taskforce in 1982, our right to determine our own future remains challenged by Argentina.

”The cross-party support of MPs and peers is therefore invaluable and we are deeply grateful. Today, our diverse, welcoming community remains united in its determination to shape its own future“.

MLA Ford also recalled that in 2013, 99.8% of Falkland Islanders, on a 92% turnout, voted in an internationally observed referendum to remain a self-governing Overseas Territory of the UK. ”This was self-determination in action”.

Argentina interested in purchasing three Italian made built light frigates

25th Wednesday, November 2026 - 11:19 UTC Full article

FCX20's combined diesel-electric and diesel (CODLAD) propulsion system comprises two main diesels, two electric motors and two reduction gearboxes

Argentine defense minister Lieutenant General Carlos Alberto Presti and his Italian counterpart Guido Crosetto framed in November in Rome, a Letter of Intent for the purchase of Italian built corvettes or light frigates.

Argentine defense minister Lieutenant General Carlos Alberto Presti and his Italian counterpart Guido Crosetto framed in November in Rome, a Letter of Intent for the purchase of Italian built corvettes or light frigates.

According to Infodefensa and Navy Outlook, the Argentine government described the agreement as naval cooperation, joint training and closer ties between the two countries' defense industries.

Fincantieri identified the FCX20 as the frigates involved and confirmed that Argentina wants an integrated logistics support package. Neither government so far, has announced a contract, a price or a delivery schedule.

The FCX20 is based on the hull design of the Italian Navy's new Ugolino Vivaldi-class offshore patrol vessels, although Fincantieri offers a considerably heavier armament for the corvette. The 95-metre ship displaces about 2,300 tons and has a complement of 93. The builder gives a maximum speed of 25 knots, a range of 3,500 nautical miles at 14 knots and an endurance of 20 days.

The advertised armament includes vertically launched MICA missiles for air defense, Exocet anti-ship missiles, a 76mm main gun forward and two cannon amidships, possibly Leonardo Lionfish 30 X-gun mounts. Fincantieri also lists two 12.7 mm machine guns, an anti-air warfare decoy launcher and a torpedo system with two launchers. The specification gives no missile load, tube count or sonar fit, leaving the ship's ability to detect submarines independently unclear. Precise weapons and sensor fit would have to be defined by the customer.

World.title: British heritage in Chile, 1858 Catedral de San Pablo, refurbished in city-port Valparaiso
World.content:
British heritage in Chile, 1858 Catedral de San Pablo, refurbished in city-port Valparaiso

25th Wednesday, November 2026 - 11:17 UTC Full article

Catedral de San Pablo brought together the early immigrant British community which settled in the central port city of Valparaíso, 120km from the capital Santiago.

Chile's oldest Anglican church will be preserved as a museum to celebrate the role of the British Anglicans building religious tolerance in Chile. St Paul's Cathedral, (Catedral de San Pablo), brought together the early immigrant British community which settled in the central port city of Valparaíso, 120km away from the capital Santiago.

Chile's oldest Anglican church will be preserved as a museum to celebrate the role of the British Anglicans building religious tolerance in Chile. St Paul's Cathedral, (Catedral de San Pablo), brought together the early immigrant British community which settled in the central port city of Valparaíso, 120km away from the capital Santiago.

After years and years of attempting to repair the church which has stood since 1858, a cultural center has been transferred into management of the building.

Destino Valparaíso, which has the Immigrant Museum in their building across the street from St Paul's Cathedral on Cerro Concepción, will take over the cathedral built on a centerpiece hill in the port city.

“Chile didn't have freedom of religion when the British arrived in the 1820s, and they wanted to practice their faith, which was Anglican,” Eduardo Dib, executive director of Destino Valparaíso, told Religion Unplugged.

As the Chilean independence movement from Spain began, and free trade was declared in Valparaíso by the First Junta Government in 1811, a wave of immigration built and peaked in the second half of the 19th century.

British immigrants were the most influential immigrant group in the city, and started building a cemetery in 1823. The “Dissidents Cemetery”, as it was known, was the only place where Protestants were allowed to be buried.

St Paul's was built to be discreet with no main entrance, small windows and no spire, cross or bell tower. A Lutheran church was built later on in the 19th century by Germans 41 years after St Paul's, and became the first Protestant church in South America with a bell tower. The Church and State were later separated in Chile's 1925 constitution.

St Paul's was designed by British designer William Henry Lloyd and was a place of worship under the Diocese of the Falkland Islands, like most South American Protestant churches, until 1963. The cathedral now belongs to the Anglican Diocese of Valparaíso.

Michelle Prain, a professor at Universidad Adolfo Ibáñez, said: “St. Paul's is a witness to the tensions between a clerical state that gradually became liberalized, and people of different faiths.”

It was declared a historic monument in 1979 by the Chilean government and became a cathedral in 2016. The neo-gothic cathedral will be handed over to Destino Valparaíso on 30 November, and before then, the roof, floors, pews and stained-glass windows will have been restored.
