World.title: Spain: Catalan separatist Puigdemont sets date for return
World.content:
Former Catalan leader Carles Puigdemont plans to return to Barcelona on December 12 after nearly a decade in exile. Spain's Supreme Court has dropped the criminal case against him, clearing the way for his return.

Catalan separatist leader Carles Puigdemont said he would return to Spain on December 12, nearly a decade after fleeing the country following a failed independence bid.

The announcement comes just days after Spain's Supreme Court closed criminal proceedings against him under a controversial amnesty law, removing the last legal obstacle to his return.

Speaking at a televised news conference in Brussels, Puigdemont said he would return to the Catalan parliament in Barcelona.

"I left as President of the Government of Catalonia, and I will return to the place where Catalan democracy elects or dismisses its presidents: the Parliament of Catalonia. I will do so on Saturday, 12 December, at midday, and that very night I will be able to sleep at home, with my family," he said.

Puigdemont also announced plans to present a proposal for a renewed push for independence of Catalonia on December 17.

Who is Carles Puigdemont?

Puigdemont is a former president of Catalonia, a wealthy region in northeastern Spain with its own language, culture and a strong independence movement.

He led Catalonia's regional government in October 2017 when it organized a referendum on independence from Spain that Spanish courts had declared illegal.

The vote and the subsequent failed attempt to break away from Spain triggered the country's worst political crisis in decades, deepening tensions between the central government in Madrid and Catalan separatists.

Thousands of Catalan independence supporters gathered in Barcelona in September 2017, weeks before the disputed independence referendum [FILE: September 11, 2017] Image: Reuters/S. Vera

Puigdemont fled to Belgium that same month to avoid arrest and has lived in self-imposed exile ever since.

His "Junts per Catalunya" party remains an important force in Spanish politics and played a key role in securing the parliamentary support needed for Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez to remain in power in 2023.

Why has Puigdemont now been cleared to return to Spain?

Spain's Supreme Court on Monday shelved the criminal case against Puigdemont after applying an amnesty law passed by parliament in 2024.

In a ruling dated November 20, the court determined that the amnesty had extinguished any potential criminal liability for Puigdemont and two other separatist figures.

Puigdemont briefly returned to Barcelona in August 2024 to address supporters before leaving again without being arrested, despite an outstanding arrest warrant [FILE: August 8, 2024] Image: Manaure Quintero/AFP

The decision followed a Constitutional Court ruling in October that extended the amnesty to cover embezzlement allegations linked to Catalonia's independence bid.

The Supreme Court had initially ruled that the law did not apply to those investigated for embezzlement, including Puigdemont.

Following the Constitutional Court's intervention, the Supreme Court lifted the arrest warrant against him. Monday's decision to close the criminal proceedings completed the legal process, allowing him to return without facing detention over the 2017 case.

Why is Spain's Catalan amnesty law controversial?

The amnesty was a key concession by Sanchez to Catalan separatist parties, including Puigdemont's Junts, in exchange for their support following Spain's inconclusive 2023 general election.

The agreement allowed Sanchez to secure another term as prime minister but sparked strong opposition from conservative parties and critics who accused him of putting his political survival ahead of Spain's interests.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez secured the support of Catalan separatist parties in 2023 in exchange for an amnesty law [FILE: October 16, 2026] Image: Stephanie Lecocq/REUTERS

The conservative Popular Party (PP) and far-right Vox opposed the legislation and unsuccessfully challenged it in parliament and the courts.

The controversy intensified after Puigdemont said in a recent interview with Spanish newspaper El Mundo that his party had exploited Sanchez's ambition to secure concessions for Catalonia.

"We had to test how far we could go," Puigdemont said, calling Sanchez "an amoral person with an excessive thirst for power".

"We have exploited this excessive ambition for power to inflict certain defeats on Spain that we would otherwise not have been able to bring about."

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez (front row, left) applauds as parliament approves a controversial amnesty law for Catalan separatists [FILE: May 30, 2024] Image: Bernat Armangue/AP/picture alliance

His remarks became a flashpoint in the campaign ahead of Spain's snap general election on November 29.

Polls suggest the Popular Party is likely to win the most seats but fall short of an outright majority, potentially leaving it dependent on Vox to form a government.

World.title: US Army to detonate unstable lead-based explosives in Iowa
World.content:
The Army says a controlled blast is the safest way to deal with explosive chemicals that began crystallising in storage, but residents say changing guidance has left them confused about where the lead dust will go.

The United States Army plans to detonate about 5 tons of aging lead azide at an Iowa ammunition plant on Wednesday, saying the explosive chemical has become too unstable to store.

The controlled blast is set for 9 am local time (1500 GMT) at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, and will destroy the country's entire stockpile of the chemical.

The US army has said residents of a small town and other nearby areas should leave "out of an abundance of caution."

"We don’t believe that the public should be in a panic," said acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle. "Our goal is to keep as much of it as we can here on our Iowa Army Ammunition plant to prevent it from traveling."

What do we know?

The material was moved to Iowa for storage from bases around the country in 2009.

But a March inspection found that it had partly crystallized, which makes it sensitive to friction and cold and could set off a spontaneous explosion.

"Inaction is no longer an option," said Major General Eric Shirley, who leads the operation.

Rob Cekada, director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, told reporters: "It's not a matter of if, it's a matter of when, and that would not be a great place for us to be in."

Is it safe to detonate the chemical?

To limit toxic lead dust, the Army has built barriers around the bunkers holding the material and will use foam and water to trap particles.

Reuters reported that Army projections show dust could settle up to 40 miles (64 km) southwest, reaching northern Missouri.

Officials expect the wind to carry the plume away from Burlington, a city of nearly 25,000 people.

The date of the planned explosion has been changed three times over public backlash Image: Austin Johnson/AP Photo/picture alliance

While residents within 5 miles (8 km) were encouraged to evacuate, the Federal Emergency Management Agency has also advised people 5 to 20 miles away to stay indoors with windows closed.

How have people reacted?

The date of the detonation changed three times after public backlash. A federal appeals court cleared the plan on Monday after environmental groups sued.

Farmer Jill Holler, who organised a protest, told Reuters: "I'm not opposed if this is the only safe option."

"What I'm saying is that it's been so mishandled that people are confused and don't trust anything they're saying," she added.

World.title: North Korea expels Swiss envoy over sanctions on camp accused of indoctrinating Ukrainian children
World.content:
North Korea has ordered Switzerland to close its newly reopened diplomatic office. The dispute centers on Swiss sanctions against a camp accused of indoctrinating Ukrainian children from Russian-occupied territories.

North Korea has declared Switzerland's top diplomatic representative in Pyongyang persona non grata and ordered him to leave the country within 48 hours, state media reported on Wednesday.

The North Korean Foreign Ministry also called for the closure of Switzerland's diplomatic office in the capital, less than a month after it reopened following a lengthy shutdown during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Swiss Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis met with senior North Korean ruling party official Jo Yong Won during his visit to Pyongyang in October [FILE: October 30, 2026] Image: KCNA/KNS/AP Photo/picture alliance

According to the state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), Pak Hyon Su, director general of the ministry's European Department, summoned Swiss diplomat Sylvain Astier and handed him a memorandum demanding the office's closure.

Pyongyang said the decision was in response to Switzerland's sanctions against a North Korean children's camp, describing the move as an openly hostile act.

"Any act of violating the sovereign rights of the DPRK and the interests of its citizens can never be welcomed by us," KCNA reported, using the acronym for North Korea's official name.

Why did Switzerland impose sanctions on North Korea?

Switzerland placed the Songdowon International Children's Camp in the coastal city of Wonsan under sanctions on November 4.

Swiss authorities accused the camp, which also hosts Chinese and Russian students, of participating in the "transfer of Ukrainian children from temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine" to North Korea.

They also said the facility contributed to "efforts aimed at the ideological conditioning and russification of Ukrainian children".

Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, condemned the Swiss sanctions [FILE: August 10, 2022] Image: Korean Central News Agency/Korea News Service/AP Photo/picture alliance

On Tuesday, Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, condemned the sanctions arguing that the measures violated North Korea's sovereignty by interfering with its responsibility to provide children with cultural and recreational opportunities.

How has Switzerland responded to North Korea's decision?

Switzerland's Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday that reopening its diplomatic office was independent of its sanctions policy.

"The reopening of the Swiss diplomatic office in Pyongyang is in line with our universalist foreign policy. Its aim is to maintain channels of dialogue, including with states with which we have differences on certain issues," the ministry said.

It stressed that this approach applied regardless of Switzerland's participation in UN sanctions over North Korea's nuclear program or EU sanctions related to Russia's war against Ukraine.

Swiss authorities were not immediately available for further comment on Wednesday.

South Korea proposes talks to officially end war with North To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Switzerland has maintained diplomatic relations with North Korea since 1974 and has long served as an intermediary between Pyongyang and Western countries.

Its office in the North Korean capital closed during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. Swiss Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis formally reopened it during a visit in October, when he discussed normalizing relations.

It was the first visit by a Swiss government minister to North Korea since 2003.

The office operates under the Swiss Embassy in Beijing, which handles diplomatic and consular relations with North Korea. Pyongyang also maintains an embassy in Bern.

Only a few European countries have diplomatic missions in North Korea, including Sweden, Poland and the Czech Republic.

What does North Korea's move mean for relations with the West?

Experts say the expulsion is intended as a warning to other Western countries, including the United States, which has been seeking to reestablish contact with Pyongyang.

"North Korea is using Switzerland as a test case to show that sanctions and dialogue are incompatible," Lim Eul-chul, a professor at South Korea's Kyungnam University, told news agency Reuters.

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has expressed a willingness to expand diplomatic ties with countries that respect North Korea's sovereignty [FILE: October 23, 2026] Image: KCNA/KNS/AFP

Ahn Chan-il, a researcher originally from North Korea, told agency AFP that Pyongyang, backed by its allies China and Russia, wanted to make an example of Switzerland.

Earlier this week, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un personally received credentials from the new ambassadors of 10 countries, including Russia and Sweden, in a rare diplomatic ceremony.

Kim said Pyongyang was seeking to expand relations with countries that respected its sovereignty but would oppose attempts to restrict the rights and development of sovereign states.

World.title: Australia, Solomon Islands sign sweeping pact seen as countering China
World.content:
Australia will become the Solomon Islands' primary security partner, while the archipelago will reject any foreign power trying to "interfere" on its "sensitive" infrastructure.

Australia and the Solomon Islands signed a security pact on Wednesday that makes Australia the archipelago's main defense partner.

This came four years after the Pacific islands country signed a similar deal with China.

The deal ‌is a win ⁠for ⁠Canberra, which is battling China for influence in the region. It also recently secured similar agreements with Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu and Fiji.

With the deal, Australia will support the expansion and development of the Solomon Islands' law enforcement.

It also includes Australian funding for investment in infrastructure and education, improved visa arrangements for Solomon Islanders, and requires ‌Honiara to consult Australia on the development of critical infrastructure.

Solomon Islands' "sensitive" infrastructure will also "remain free from militarization, foreign interference and unauthorized access".

This covers airports, ports, energy and telecommunications infrastructure, sectors where China has invested through million-dollar loans since the Solomon Islands switched diplomatic ties from Taiwan to Beijing in 2019.

How Pacific islands beat the China-Australia power struggle To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

"Australia is proud to be the Solomon Islands' main security partner, and that's a ​responsibility that ‌we take seriously," Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told a joint press conference in Australian capital Canberra with his Solomon Islands counterpart, Matthew Wale.

Albanese also said the Solomon Islands would also be required to consult with Australia before striking deals with non-Pacific Island Forum countries on critical infrastructure or security cooperation.

"Solomon Islands has been for a number of years a source of uncertainty and doubt in the region. Those days are done," Wale told the press conference.

Will the China deal be affected?

Wale has been rebuilding diplomatic relationships with Canberra and Washington since he was elected in May. His predecessor Manasseh Sogavare had built closer ties with China since coming to power in 2019.

Asked whether he had ended the 2022 security pact with Beijing, Wale told journalists that he could not comment due to a non-disclosure clause in the treaty with China, set to expire in April 2027. Discussions with China were "ongoing," he said.

Taiwan minister to DW: 'You cannot be naive' with China To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Asked the same question on Wednesday, China's Foreign Ministry did not confirm whether the deal had been scrapped, news agency AFP reported. However, ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun warned Australia and the Solomon Islands that their cooperation "should not target any third party."

“I think this deal, coupled with indications that the Solomon Islands will allow its agreement with China to lapse, goes beyond the success of previous deals Australia has struck in the region,” Connor Graham, a research fellow in the Pacific Islands Program at the Sydney-based Lowy Institute, told Reuters news agency.

He said it was a "blow to Chinese security ambitions in the Pacific."

World.title: Fact check: Deepfakes and 'US abandons Taiwan' claims spread ahead of vote
World.content:
Ahead of local elections, AI-generated falsehoods targeting Democratic Progressive Party mayoral candidate Puma Shen have surged in Taiwan, alongside disinformation claiming the US is pulling back support for the island.

On November 28, Taiwan will hold local elections that could reshape power dynamics between the sovereignty-leaning Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) and the Beijing-friendly Kuomintang (KMT). The outcome could influence relations between Taiwan and China, as well as regional geopolitics and ties between Washington, Beijing and Taipei.

A month before the election, there was a spike in AI-generated content featuring DPP Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen. Claims that the US is abandoning Taiwan also increased during the same period. Experts say that fake quotes and misleading clips are being used as part of a campaign to weaken trust in US security commitments .

Did Trump offer to sell US arms to China? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Research by DW Fact check found that identical disinformation headlines claiming US troops were withdrawing from Taiwan repeatedly appeared as both articles and videos on Chinese clickbait platforms NetEase and Sohu. The V-Dem Institute at the University of Gothenburg ranked Taiwan "the country most severely targeted" by foreign disinformation for eleven consecutive years – from 2014 to 2024.

The Taiwanese Ministry of the Interior has stated that foreign actors are increasingly using diverse methods to interfere in elections. That includes manipulating election betting, inviting Taiwanese citizens to China, using donations from Taiwanese business people to organize events, such as banquets, and leveraging temple and religious activities, to mobilize and win over supporters. Taiwan has functioned with de facto independence since 1949 despite Beijing's decadeslong claim to the island as a province and repeated vows to annex it.

DW Fact Check examined viral claims that have circulated online since September during the run-up to the election.

Deepfake audio, video target pro-sovereignty candidate

Claim: Puma Shen takes drug and receives kickbacks through arms purchases from the US.

DW Fact check: Fake

AI-generated audio recordings attacking DPP's Taipei mayoral candidate circulated on Facebook one month before Taiwan's local elections Image: Facebook

An audio clip posted on Facebook on October 29, claims to show Puma Shen, the DPP candidate for Taipei mayor, admitting to receiving kickbacks from US arms deals.

The recording is heavy with background noise – a method used mask synthetic manipulation in AI-generated audio. Multiple deepfake detection platforms, including Is this AI and Undetectable, flagged the audio as likely AI-generated.

The Facebook account that posted the audio was created on October 29, 2026 – the date the audio was also published. The account's followers are mainly profiles using languages, such as English, Arabic and Thai. That points to possible bot activity.

Another Facebook account posted an image of Puma Shen taking drugs. Apart from the "AI content" label on the post, multiple AI detector tools identified this photo as likely AI-generated.

Taiwanese independent media platform Watchout discovered that the advertiser behind this Facebook account is located in China Image: Facebook

The account was created in March 2026. Since then, a lot of AI-generated content mocking Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te and his pro-sovereignty party has been posted. It is occasionally interspersed with posts praising the development of Chinese cities.

This account's profile indicates that the primary country location for people who manage this page includes China and Taiwan.

Taiwanese independent media platform Watchout investigated the account's advertising activity and found that it had previously run at least five Facebook ads. The advertisers were identified as Peng Zhiwei and Guo Yang, both based in China. The findings suggest that the account received financial support from individuals in China.

The AI detection tool "AI or Not" indicates that this photo is likely AI-generated Image: aiornot.com

The Taipei mayoral race is a key battleground in Taiwan's upcoming local elections. As of mid-November, polls showed a neck-and-neck contest between Puma Shen and his opponent, Chiang Wan-an, who claims to be a great-grandson of Taiwanese leader Chiang Kai-shek.

Chiang Kai-shek was a leading figure of the Kuomintang and relocated with the party to Taiwan in 1949 after losing the Chinese Civil War to the Chinese Communist Party.

While the Kuomintang was historically staunchly anti-communist, critics argue that it now promotes closer ties with China. For example, they point to senior Kuomintang figure's proposed 10-year unification framework as evidence that its stance runs counter to mainstream public opinion in Taiwan. Although Kuomintang subsequently stated that this framework is entirely unrelated to the current party leadership , it has sparked controversy in Taiwan.

Sensational headlines on Chinese platform

Claim: 500 US troops urgently withdrawn from Taiwan.

DW Fact check: Misleading

A post in Simplified Chinese on Sohu , a popular mobile news platform in China, claims that 500 US troops stationed in Taiwan were to be withdrawn rapidly.

An automated translation of a misleading article on alleged withdrawal of US troops Image: sohu.com

According to a March 2026 report by the US government's Defense Manpower Data Center, 45 American military personnel are currently stationed in Taiwan.

Retired US Navy Rear Admiral Mark Montgomery stated during a hearing in May 2025 that 500 American military personnel were providing training in Taiwan.

DW Fact check reached out to Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense, which declined to comment. The US Department of Defense and the Pentagon did not respond to requests for comment by the time of publication.

Distorted quotes and misleading clips

Claim: A TikTok video claims to show US president Donald Trump saying the US is abandoning Taiwan.

DW Fact check: Misleading

In this TikTok video, Donald Trump's response in an interview was interpreted beyond what the US president had actually said Image: tiktok.com

The original video was from a Fox News interview ​​​​​​​Fox News interview with Trump on May 16. The interviewer did not ask whether the United States would defend Taiwan, and the US president did not comment on the issue.

Trump said he did not want Taiwan to become independent or for a war to break out, adding that the status quo should be maintained to allow tensions to de-escalate. He also clearly stated that his policy toward Taiwan "has not changed." Washington has long maintained a policy of strategic ambiguity toward Taiwan – neither explicitly guaranteeing the island's defense nor ruling out the possibility of doing so.

World.title: Houthis claim attacks on Saudi refinery, financial district
World.content:
Iran-backed Yemeni Houthis say they carried out fresh retaliatory attacks in Saudi Arabia. A fire was reported at Ras Tanura oil refinery and Riyadh's financial district was attacked for the second time in a week.

Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen say they are continuing their attacks on Saudi Arabia, claiming to have damaged a key oil refinery as well as the petromonarchy's financial district in the capital Riyadh.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree on Wednesday said that "accurate and direct" attacks targeting Ras Tanura — Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery and a major export terminal for crude — had "caused fires to break out at the facility."

Saree said an attack on Saudi Arabia's financial district, located in the capital Riyadh, was "carried out in three phases, with strikes hitting their targets accurately."

Saudi capital has been repeatedly attacked by Houthis

Saudi defense officials said that air defenses in the kingdom had taken down four Houthi drones at Ras Tanura and that 11 people had been injured when a tower in the financial district was hit.

The building in question was also targeted on November 19, but no one was injured in that attack.

The Houthis and Saudis have been fighting for over a decade as part of a civil war that has become a regional conflict with increased significance as a result of the ongoing conflict in Iran and the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Climate loss and damage fund exists, but the money doesn't
World.content:
Climate-vulnerable countries fought for years to create a loss and damage fund. Four years on, demand far outstrips funding, pledges are scarce, and disaster-hit nations are still waiting for support.

On the sandbars and river islands of Bangladesh's Brahmaputra and its branches, families have little to fall back on when the water rises.

"The floodwater swallows everything," said 16-year-old Rasel Babu, who had traveled to Antalya, Turkey, to speak to delegates at the UN climate conference.

Created after years of pressure from vulnerable nations, the loss and damage fund was designed to help countries recover from climate disasters and irreversible climate impacts. This includes extreme weather events such as floods, heat waves and wildfires as well as slow-onset impacts such as sea level rise, desertification and damage to infrastructure and crops.

But the fund is already struggling to meet demand. It received $2.8 billion (€2.56 billion) in urgent requests in a first call for funding, with only $342 million available at the time.

Even the money promised has not fully arrived. Only about half of the money currently pledged had been received by this summer.

While the European Commission signed a €25 million ($27 million) contribution agreement to the fund on the margins of COP31, formalizing an earlier pledge made at COP28, and Spain pledged an additional €15 million, other contributions to loss and damage remained scarce.

First payout will go to Nepal after glacier collapse

The fund's first emergency response is going to be paid out to Nepal. The board of the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage had provisionally set aside $21.6 million following the catastrophic glacier collapse that triggered flash floods in August, killing more than 1,500 people with 5,600 more missing.

But the money has not moved yet. Nepal must first submit a funding request setting out how it will be spent.

"It's asking for a country that is dealing with the climate emergency to work on a proposal," Nepali climate finance expert Bibek Raj Kandel said, adding a layer of bureaucracy inefficient to address the urgency.

UN warns climate change could force millions to move To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Nepal is already waiting on another request, filed after floods in Kathmandu and landslides in the eastern hills. "There's already one pending proposal sitting on the table," Kandel said. Unless the fund speeds up, he warned, it's "going to disappoint many, many countries."

Pakistan which led the push for the fund in 2022 after floods affected 33 million people and killed more than 1,730, also hasn't seen any of the money yet.

"Pakistan was one of the countries which really spoke up and managed to get the loss and damage fund on the climate agenda. But it takes a long time," Pakistan's Minister of State for Climate Change, Shezra Mansab Ali Khan Kharal, told DW.

In 2022, monsoon and floods killed more than 1,730 people in Pakistan, with 33 million people affected Image: Akhtar Soomro/REUTERS

"We have still not really got anything. We haven't seen anything on the ground at all as yet," Kharal said. Pakistan has submitted two projects and was told the cap is $200 million.

Other forms of aid often come in the form of loans.

"These promises, they are hollow promises," said Abid Qaiyum Suleri, Executive Director of the Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI) in Islamabad, adding that for a heavily indebted country, the form of the money matters as much as the amount.

"We do not want that a climate disaster in Pakistan should translate into further debt for Pakistan," Kharal said, calling for grants rather than loans.

World.title: Germany's women's football team take stand against domestic violence
World.content:
Germany's women's football team are to wear UN Women badges in games against Argentina and Peru, as domestic violence hits a record high in Germany.

Domestic violence has reached a record high in Germany, with 16 women subjected to physical abuse behind closed doors each hour.

UN Women Germany is one of 13 UN Women national committees worldwide, each an independent, non-profit, non-governmental organization committed to gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls.

Their current campaign "Orange The World" runs from the start of International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women on November 25 to December 10, International Human Rights Day. It is designed to raise awareness around violence against women in the country and worldwide. The 2026 campaign's focus is particularly on men's responsibility in ending gender-based violence.

"In these 16 days of activism, we can deliver a lot of information. Survivors of gender-based violence can find out where to get support and be reminded that they are not at fault," UN Women Germany chair, politician and long-standing campaigner for women's rights Elke Ferner told DW. "The debate helps and it's a chance to change consciousness about the topic."

Germany captain Giulia Gwinn said in a statement via the German Football Association (DFB): "Violence against women and girls affects us all and must have no place in our society. As the women's national team, we therefore want to once again use our reach to create awareness for this important issue and jointly set a visible sign against violence."

The campaign with the women's team is not new. Two years ago, the team joined the campaign, delivering a moving video that saw players reveal the truth of statements by crossing out words.

During Germany's upcoming South America tour — part of their preparations for the 2027 World Cup in Brazil — they are to wear special UN Women Germany badges on their sleeves in their games against Argentina and Peru.

Role models pivotal for the campaign

Ferner believes the work with role models is pivotal and that the campaign is powerful, especially in a football context. A 2022 study from Warwick Business School in the UK revealed alcohol-related domestic abuse rises by nearly 50% after England's men's football team win a World Cup game, never mind lose.

Currently, there is no data on domestic abuse during Germany games, however during the 2026 World Cup last summer, Berlin police recorded a 31% increase in domestic violence compared to the week before.

Ferner is encouraged that sport has understood the importance of the issue, and that the German Olympic Committee (DOSB) and other sports clubs and organizations are helping move the conversation forward.

In sport, this is particularly important given the problematic nature of dependency relationships that so often exist in high-performance environments. But violence against women is really a societal issue that is not specific to class, origin, religion or societal space, such as sport.

"Violence against women has structural origins and to change that you need to change the structures," Ferner said. "You just need to do it. I always say, this isn't about a lack of knowledge but rather a lack of action."

Performance is an integral part of sport, but a multi-dimensional understanding of it might help shift perspective in a country that remains driven by a performance culture.

"What is performance? Higher, faster, further? Or is it managing to look after a family of three?" Ferner asked. "Why do people who repair washing machines earn more than those looking after your kids in nursery? This is about changing business culture, but also awareness around the role men play at home and in the family.

"The picture boys and young men get of girls and women in school is a problem that needs addressing. We can't wait for generational change. This is about saving lives. We need to change societal structures."

Male power structures a problem

Sports structures are also in need of reform. Non-profit organization Safe Sport provides independent support for people affected by sexual, physical and psychological violence in both amateur and professional sport in Germany.

They are the only organization with a specific focus on violence in grassroots sports in Germany, and one of only two in professional sport in the country. They also have to contend with structures, in a sporting context, that make spaces less safe for women.

"Gender roles have become more fluid in the last few years, but in associations and clubs management positions are still occupied by men, regardless of the sport," Safe Sport manager Ina Lambert told DW.

"In professional sport, there are a lot fewer women involved in training and so the space remains male dominated, and, as a result, so do the power structures.

"We have people in search of advice, men included, who see the problems and want to enforce change, and we offer them support so they are not alone," Lambert said. "But whether in a big association or a small club, perpetrators are frequently protected, incidents are ignored and so the people who want to enforce change are often prevented from doing so."

Safe Sport, which provides free psychological and legal support, has only been in action since July 2023, but in that time the number of support requests they have received continues to grow. Psychological violence in sport in Germany is the most common case they are faced with, but sexual violence is also a major problem.

"There is finally recognition of the problem and there is a seriousness about tackling it," Lambert said.

"There is a lot of good work being done in the right direction, with many good concepts for prevention, intervention and processing violence, as well as more education, holistic training and focus on women's menstrual cycles."

Germany is backing UN efforts to highlight that more must be done to tackle violence against women Image: imago images/Lucca Fundel

Comprehensive support on the way

Germany's Interior Ministry is leading the process with participants from the country's states, organized sport, affected parties and academia to create a central hub. The center for safe sport was founded in July 2026, but investigative and sanctioning work is expected to begin in the spring of 2027.

Support from leading figures clearly makes a huge difference, but it's also clear that more data is needed. Addressing the underlying issues, such as social norms and gender stereotyping, is a must.

After all, as UN Women Executive Director Sima Bahous said: "No country has yet eliminated violence against women. Ending it requires transformative action — greater investment, innovation, and unwavering political will."

This article was originally published on November 28, 2024, and updated on November 25, 2026.

World.title: Llega el apagón de encuestas: ¿Qué dice el promedio con las últimas?
World.content:
Esta es la última actualización del promedio de EL PAÍS, del 23 de noviembre. Además, construye tu propio promedio

Se publican decenas de encuestas en una campaña. Son el mejor instrumento para predecir unas elecciones, sobre todo cuando las miramos juntas: eso hace nuestro promedio. Combina todos los estudios dando más peso a las encuestadoras que más aciertan. En su última actualización, ese promedio sitúa al PP con el 31,4% de los votos, unos 2,5 puntos por delante del PSOE (29,1%), y con Vox alrededor del 18%.

En el gráfico puedes elegir entre tres promedios. El “medio” es el que usamos habitualmente; los otros dos sirven para comparar: “agresivo” (que reacciona antes a los cambios pero tiene más ruido), y otro “cauto” (que se mueve menos).

Los sondeos se han movido desde la convocatoria del 6 de octubre. El cambio más claro es la subida del PSOE, que estrecha la ventaja del PP: era de 6 puntos y ahora es de menos de 2,5, y bajando. Nuestros cálculos dicen que el PSOE tiene al menos un 25% de probabilidad de ser primero.

Algo que también ha cambiado es la izquierda del PSOE. Las últimas encuestas estiman un 6,8% de voto para lo que hemos llamado Frentes (Frente Amplio y las coaliciones con Podemos, Compromís, Ara Més o Unidad del Pueblo Canario) y un 1,1% para Podemos en solitario. Juntos rondan el 8% de voto, lejos del 12,3% que logró Sumar en 2023.

La suma de izquierdas y derechas

El número clave de las elecciones es el resultado por bloques. Al cierre, la derecha suma el 51,1% de los votos (PP, Vox y SALF) y la izquierda, el 38,7% (PSOE, Frentes, Podemos y Adelante Andalucía). Son 12,4 puntos de distancia, cuando en las generales de 2023 casi empataron, con 45,6% y 44% respectivamente. La suma de PP y Vox tendrá seguramente la mayoría si supera el 47% de votos.

La ventaja de la derecha creció entre 2024 y el verano de 2025, cuando sus votos pasaron del 48% al 52%. Pero en campaña se ha reducido unos tres puntos. Se ha cumplido nuestra hipótesis inicial: la izquierda, que partía desmovilizada, ha recuperado terreno con la convocatoria electoral, aunque siga por detrás.

El promedio también constata que las encuestadoras discrepan. Casi todas ponen al PP primero, pero con ventajas distintas: desde menos de un punto, según 40dB. o Ipsos, hasta los casi siete de Hamalgama. Solo SW Demoscopia y Cluster17 sitúan al PSOE por delante, además del CIS. Pero el dato de este último es poco informativo porque el centro sobrestima a la izquierda desde 2018.

¿Y si corregimos los llamados sesgos? Algunas encuestadoras se desvían hacia la derecha o hacia la izquierda. Nuestro promedio no lo corrige por un motivo: esas desviaciones cambian de una elección a otra y casi nunca son sistemáticas. Pero podemos ver qué pasaría si lo hiciéramos: el siguiente gráfico permite corregir cada encuesta con el sesgo histórico de su casa.

El resultado depende de qué elecciones miramos. Con los errores de todas las elecciones desde 2018, generales y autonómicas, la ventaja del PP sobre el PSOE sube de 2,5 a 3,5 puntos: en conjunto las encuestas se han quedado cortas con la derecha. Pero en las generales ha pasado lo contrario: subestimaron a la izquierda. El caso más recordado es 2023: las últimas encuestas daban a la derecha 5,4 puntos de ventaja, y en las urnas sacó solo 1,6. Si ajustamos las encuestas con sus sesgos solo en las tres generales desde 2018, la ventaja del PP baja a un punto, aunque la suma de derechas sigue claramente por delante.

Todos estos números son tentativos. Primero, porque las encuestas son una aproximación. Y segundo, porque entre las últimas encuestas y el 29-N hay seis días. La izquierda venía recortando distancia. Esa tendencia podrá seguir o no, pero ya no podremos contarlo aquí con sondeos públicos: la ley impide publicarlos en los cinco días previos a la votación.

¿Cómo funciona el promedio?

Un promedio de encuestas suele ser más preciso que cualquier encuesta aislada: suma la muestra de todas y compensa en parte sus errores, porque mezcla la “cocina” de cada encuestadora. El nuestro funciona así:

1) Todas las encuestas. Usamos las de voto al Congreso publicadas desde las generales de 2023, salvo las encargadas por partidos y las que no tienen trabajo de campo propio. La mayoría las tomamos de Wikipedia.

2) Con distinto peso. Cada encuesta importa según su encuestadora, su muestra y su antigüedad. La nota de cada casa sale de nuestro comparador, que valora su error, su sesgo y si publica sus microdatos (las mejores pesan el doble que una casa normal). El peso de una encuesta se reduce a la mitad cada diez días y desaparece a los 30.

3) Cada casa cuenta una vez. De cada encuestadora pesa su último sondeo, para que no mande quien publica más.

4) Mira hacia atrás. El promedio de cada día solo usa las encuestas con el trabajo de campo terminado hasta entonces. Si una se publica con retraso, la línea de esos días se corrige un poco.

5) Tres ritmos. El promedio central y dos para comparar: el agresivo reduce el peso a la mitad cada 8 días y corta a los 14; el cauto, cada 30 y a los 60.

6) Las listas del 29N. Desde el 14 de octubre medimos las candidaturas nuevas, y las encuestas anteriores se traducen a ellas. SALF y Adelante Andalucía entran en el promedio poco a poco, a medida que las publican las encuestadoras.

7) El sesgo, aparte. La corrección del interactivo usa el error de cada casa en la ventaja entre bloques desde 2018, entero: enseña qué pasaría si las casas volvieran a fallar como de media.

8) El promedio es sólido, pero no infalible. Lo hemos probado con 41 elecciones desde 2018: cinco días antes de votar, falla 1,5 puntos por partido de media. Cambiar la ventana o los pesos lo mejora una décima como mucho. Cuando falla es porque fallan todas las encuestas a la vez, algo que ningún promedio puede corregir: por eso nuestro modelo añade esa incertidumbre.

Todas las encuestas

World.title: La industria de las mil pantallas: los cambios que han transformado el mercado audiovisual
World.content:
Pocos hubieran imaginado hace dos décadas que una incipiente plataforma de vídeos caseros como YouTube sería la cantera del nuevo talento de Hollywood, o que las producciones extranjeras vendrían a España por sus paisajes y por sus profesionales altamente cualificados. Así ha cambiado este sector que ha convertido a España en el primer productor de contenidos de la Unión Europea

La forma de consumir productos audiovisuales que conoció el empresario barcelonés Juan Carlos Tous hace 20 años, cuando creó Filmin, tiene poco que ver con la de hoy. Tanto es así, cuenta, que entonces nadie confiaba en su proyecto, que en la actualidad es una de las principales plataformas españolas de películas y series en línea. “Nos decían que no funcionaría porque nadie pagaba por ver cine en internet, pero sabíamos que el futuro del sector sería la distribución por internet”, contaba en el último capítulo de El poder de las empresas, el pódcast de los que hacen, de Banco Sabadell.

Actualmente, vemos muchísimas películas y series desde la televisión inteligente, el canal más usado, aunque el consumo audiovisual en móvil crece, especialmente entre los jóvenes. La mitad de la población no va a las salas, aunque el 13% acude al menos una vez al mes, según la Asociación para la Investigación de Medios de Comunicación (AIMC). Una situación que está cambiando, pues muchos joven están redescubriendo la experiencia de ir a una sala. Al mismo tiempo los exhibidores han recurrido a la tecnología para aumentar su atractivo proponiendo que la película sea no solo un viaje emocional, sino también físico gracias al sonido envolvente o las butacas que se mueven. Innovaciones que no existían cuando Tous inició su aventura ni en 2008, cuando Ignacio Segura, director ejecutivo de la productora y distribuidora DeAPlaneta Entertainment, llegó a esta compañía.

El consumo doméstico y la experiencia en la sala son parte de la respuesta a los nuevos retos de la industria. A ellos se suman el impacto de la IA, la llegada de talento procedente de nuevos formatos digitales y redes sociales, y la consolidación de España como destino para rodajes. Un escenario de desafíos, pero también de oportunidades para quienes quieran emprender en una industria que, en 2025, convirtió a España en el mayor polo de producción de la Unión Europea (UE), con 423 producciones, un 31% más que el año anterior.

La sala de cine como experiencia

El público acude hoy a la sala de cine como parte de una experiencia compartida. Incluso el más joven, que ha crecido con miles de películas al alcance de un clic, señala Juan Carlos Tous, consejero ejecutivo de Filmin. “Para ellos es un descubrimiento. Les ayuda a romper con una rutina, salir de casa, encontrarse con sus amigos y hacer algo a una hora concreta, cuando ellos están acostumbrados a tenerlo todo cuando quieren”, justifica. Al mismo tiempo, las empresas exhibidoras han enriquecido su oferta con formatos que permiten vivir una experiencia radicalmente opuesta a la doméstica, explica Borja de Benito, responsable de marketing de la Federación de Cines de España (FECE).

De Benito menciona tres innovaciones tecnológicas que cada vez se ven en más salas: el 4DX, que sincroniza una serie de efectos, como el viento o la percepción de olores con lo que sucede en la pantalla; el D-BOX, que busca transmitir físicamente los movimientos de la película mediante balanceos y vibraciones en la butaca; y el Dolby Atmos, con sonido envolvente que imita la manera en que le llegaría al espectador si estuviera dentro de la película.

Otros cines ofrecen opciones prémium con gran acogida entre el público, explica el portavoz de FECE. Son las salas con butacas reclinables y servicio de restaurante, también los espacios júnior, adaptados alas necesidades del público infantil. “Cuentan con entretenimientos alternativos, como toboganes,y ofrecen un parón a media película para que los niños puedan ir al baño”, explica. En 2024 en España había 729 salas con alguno de estos formatos prémium y se habían invertido más de 150 millones de euros tras la pandemia para acondicionar salas tradicionales, de acuerdo con el Dossier de datos de 2024, de FECE. Y se prevé que la cifra siga creciendo, completa De Benito.

Consejos de Empresario Si empezara hoy, crearía una empresa con visión europea y con presencia en varios territorios Ignacio Segura, director ejecutivo de la productora y distribuidora DeAPlaneta Entertainment

España como destino para rodar (y producir) cine y televisión

La industria audiovisual española ha apostado por convertirse en destino habitual para las grandes producciones extranjeras, señala Juan Manuel Guimeráns, presidente de la Spain Film Commission, organización dedicada a atraer rodajes de otras partes del mundo. Esfuerzo que ha dado sus frutos: en las últimas dos décadas han tenido lugar en España rodajes de sagas como Star Wars y Los Juegos del Hambre y series como The Crown o The Walking Dead. Que Hollywood elija España para rodar no es una novedad, ya en los sesenta se rodaron multitud de wésterns, pero puntualiza Guimeráns, ahora ya no desembarcan con todo el equipo humano, sino que contratan empresas y profesionales de una industria local extraordinaria que cada vez es más internacional, valora.

El Gobierno presentó un proyecto en 2021 para convertir al país en un polo de producción audiovisual, inversión internacional y talento. Uno de los elementos centrales del plan eran los incentivos fiscales, de manera, señala Guimeráns, que las productoras extranjeras ahora se encuentran en España una combinación de ahorro fiscal, profesionales especializados y gran variedad de localizaciones. Un estudio de la consultora Olsberg en colaboración con Spain Film Commission señala que el 70% del gasto de las productoras extranjeras hasta 2022 no se habría producido en el país sin esos incentivos. Las empresas que tengan una visión internacional del negocio, añade Segura, de DeAPlaneta Entertainment, tienen más posibilidades de prosperar. “Si empezara hoy, crearía una empresa con visión europea y con presencia en varios territorios”, puntualiza.

Consejos de Empresario La industria española está produciendo más que nunca, una inercia que da la oportunidad a los empresarios de mostrar su trabajo al mundo y hacer crecer el negocio Juan Carlos Tous, cofundador y consejero ejecutivo de Filmin, compañía española de 'streaming' de series y películas

Este dinamismo se ha traducido en un aumento de la capacidad de las empresas españolas para crear contenidos, explica Tous, de Filmin. “La industria está produciendo más que nunca, una inercia que da la oportunidad a los empresarios de mostrar su trabajo al mundo y hacer crecer el negocio”. Ese empuje se observa en la reactivación, tras años de inactividad, de la Ciudad de la Luz, en Alicante, un complejo cinematográfico donde se han rodado taquillazos como El cautivo, de Alejandro Amenábar, y donde Disney filma ahora la adaptación con actores de Enredados. De ese auge también es consecuencia Madrid Content City, un recinto multiempresarial, impulsado en 2025 por el grupo español Secuoya, donde ya se ha instalado Netflix. Ambos complejos destacan por reunir en un mismo recinto empresas de toda la cadena de valor, lo que multiplica las oportunidades de colaboración.

Los ‘youtubers’ son los nuevos creadores

Ignacio Segura, director ejecutivo de DeAPlaneta Entertainment, apunta a un cambio importante en la industria audiovisual: las redes sociales están dejando de ser consideradas como una cantera de aficionados para convertirse en una fuente de talento que Hollywood empieza a tomarse en serio. “Estos creadores de contenido han sido mal vistos en el mundo serio del cine. Ahora dos de los grandes éxitos de este año, Backrooms y Obsession, son responsabilidad de youtubers”, afirma el empresario.

El creador de Backrooms es Kane Parsons, un joven de 20 años que comenzó publicando en la red vídeos sobre espacios laberínticos y desiertos que han acumulado más de 190 millones de visitas. Parsons trasladó aquel ambiente a un largometraje que ha superado en la taquilla al último estreno de Star Wars, The Mandalorian. Obsession está firmada por Curry Barker, 26 años, que se dio a conocer con cortometrajes de terror en YouTube. Rodó su cinta con 750.000 dólares — unos 684.000 euros al cambio actual— y superó los 365 millones de euros en recaudación. Llevar el talento de YouTube a la industria del cine permite probar nuevas ideas y lenguajes con poco presupuesto y contar con creadores que llegan con una audiencia creada, lo que facilita la promoción.

La industria española también cuenta con experimentos de trasvase entre YouTube y el cine, aunque mucho más discretos y menos convencionales. La webserie Malviviendo fue el punto de partida de la carrera como director y productor de David Sainz, que desde entonces ha dirigido tres largometrajes. El youtuber Míster Jägger llevó a la gran pantalla el universo surrealista de sus vídeos y Wismichu presentó en el Festival de Sitges una cinta que consistía en una escena repetida en bucle con la que pretendía provocar al público para grabar sus reacciones.

La IA como vector de crecimiento

La irrupción de la IA está cambiando la manera de crear, producir y distribuir películas y ha abierto debates sobre el futuro de los profesionales y sus derechos. El reto en este sector, indica Guimeráns, va a ser gestionar la propiedad intelectual de todas las creaciones, de la imagen de las personas a los guiones y la música.

Esta tecnología que plantea retos, ya ha sido abrazada por la industria. La IA se emplea a lo largo de toda la cadena de valor, especialmente en la preproducción y la posproducción. No solo sirve para crear imágenes, también se utiliza para gestionar los planes y agilizar procesos al automatizar tareas técnicas.

El proyecto piloto Film Data España, impulsado por la Spain Film Commission, por ejemplo, propone un motor de búsqueda de localizaciones, que será actualizado por los propios usuarios, y que permitirá conocer las características, los servicios del entorno y qué películas ya se han rodado en cada uno de los lugares.

Guimeráns cree que la IA abre nuevas e interesantes vías de negocio a las que los emprendedores deben prestar atención. El estudio El impacto de la IA en la industria audiovisual en España, de la consultora Public First y Google, estima que esta tecnología disruptiva en el audiovisual puede aportar hasta 9.400 millones de euros anuales al producto interior bruto español (PIB) en 2035. Permitirá a los profesionales hacer más en menos tiempo, como señaló Johann Choron, responsable de Alianzas e IA generativa para Cine y Televisión de Google, en el festival de San Sebastián del año pasado, aunque también hará que muchos empleos se transformen.

World.title: El profesor que enseña cocina tradicional a través de las recetas familiares de sus alumnos
World.content:
El chef y docente Ricardo Fernández ha impulsado en el CIFP Carlos Oroza, en Pontevedra, una iniciativa que anima a sus estudiantes de FP a recuperar las elaboraciones culinarias de sus madres, abuelas y vecinas. El objetivo, en línea con el proyecto ‘Gastronomía para una Inmensa Minoría’, es preservar la memoria cultural

En el Centro Integrado de Formación Profesional (CIFP) Carlos Oroza, de Pontevedra, los alumnos de la asignatura de Cocina Tradicional recopilan recetas familiares transmitidas de generación en generación. En los últimos siete años han reunido cerca de 600 elaboraciones procedentes de madres, abuelas, vecinas... Además, junto a las instrucciones de preparación, los estudiantes incluyen las historias personales de las mujeres que han compartido sus conocimientos.

El proyecto recoge el testigo de Los recetarios, una iniciativa dedicada a recoger, localizar y digitalizar estos platos tradicionales —especialmente los transmitidos por las mujeres—, con el objetivo de proteger la identidad culinaria de un territorio. El profesor Ricardo Fernández encontró en esa propuesta, creada por periodistas y expertas en gastronomía, una fuente de inspiración y una oportunidad para mostrar a sus alumnos cómo las técnicas y costumbres que han dado forma a la cultura popular ayudan también a comprender la evolución de la cocina.

Fernández, profesor y chef, reflexiona sobre el proyecto junto con los también cocineros Verónica Gómez, formada en el Basque Culinary Center y conocida por su paso por MasterChef; Javier Olleros, fundador del restaurante Culler de Pau, en Reboredo (O Grove, Pontevedra); y Manuel Costiña, responsable de Costiña, en Santa Comba (A Coruña). Los dos últimos, reconocidos con dos estrellas Michelin, destacan la importancia de iniciativas como la que se desarrolla en el CIFP Carlos Oroza. “Son fantásticos para, desde la memoria, preservar y avanzar”, insiste Olleros.

Esta es una de las iniciativas que forman parte de Gastronomía para una Inmensa Minoría, el proyecto impulsado por Cervezas 1906, que nace con el objetivo de poner en valor propuestas auténticas, que no siguen modas, que parten de la tradición para innovar y que son una defensa del territorio y origen. Gracias a su apoyo, las recetas recopiladas en el CIFP Carlos Oroza han podido digitalizarse y ponerse a disposición del público: de este modo, el patrimonio culinario sale del aula y queda disponible para cualquier interesado en conocer o preparar estos platos caseros.

World.title: Apalabré con el casero una subida de la renta antes de la aprobación del decreto de vivienda. ¿Puedo acogerme a la prórroga de dos años?
World.content:
Pregunta. Mi contrato de arrendamiento de vivienda vence, por cumplimiento de los cinco años, el 31 de diciembre de 2026. En septiembre de este año, antes de aprobarse los decretos de vivienda, mi arrendador y yo habíamos apalabrado que al finalizar el contrato celebraríamos uno nuevo incrementando la renta. ¿Puedo acogerme a la prórroga extraordinaria de dos años o, por el contrario, el arrendador puede rechazar la solicitud. J. C. Villanueva.

Respuesta. Una de las excepciones reguladas en la Disposición final quinta del Real Decreto-ley 29/2026, de 6 de octubre, por el que se adoptan medidas urgentes para la protección de la función social de la vivienda y la ampliación de la oferta de vivienda asequible establece que la prórroga extraordinaria no será aplicable “salvo que se hayan fijado otros términos o condiciones por acuerdo entre las partes, o que se haya suscrito un nuevo contrato de arrendamiento”.

En su caso indica que, al vencimiento del contrato, lo acordado verbalmente fue la firma de un nuevo contrato con una nueva renta. Si dicho acuerdo no ha llegado a formalizarse por escrito y no se han concretado los nuevos términos y condiciones del arrendamiento, sí podría solicitar la prórroga extraordinaria de dos años, que deberá ser aceptada obligatoriamente por el arrendador.

El acuerdo verbal alcanzado en septiembre no invalida, por sí solo, su derecho legal a solicitar esta prórroga extraordinaria. Para que la excepción relativa a la fijación de “otros términos o condiciones por acuerdo de las partes” resulte vinculante frente a una prórroga legal impuesta por una norma de orden público, el acuerdo debe ser inequívoco y formalizarse expresamente por escrito. Un mero compromiso verbal previo o el hecho de haber dejado “apalabrada” la firma de un futuro contrato no supone la perfección de un nuevo acuerdo que extinga el contrato vigente.

Por tanto, entendemos que sí puede solicitar la prórroga extraordinaria de dos años, siempre que cumpla, además, con el resto de los requisitos establecidos en la citada disposición.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: DNB warns AI, cyberattacks and debt could rock financial system
World.content:
The Dutch central bank DNB has issued a new warning that a convergence of risks is posing a severe threat to the country’s financial stability; namely, the power of AI cyberattacks, the possibility of an AI economic bubble, and the fact that only a small number of cybersecurity companies are protecting financial institutions.

At the same time, interest rate rises are putting increasing pressure on government debt.

“The systemic risk lies primarily in the potentially dangerous confluence of shocks, such as cyberattacks, a stock market correction, or the impact of higher interest rates,” DNB president Olaf Sleijpen said in a statement on Tuesday.

“Moreover, the ability to absorb setbacks has diminished now that government fiscal space is limited. As a result, shocks can spread more quickly and widely throughout the financial system.”

There is widespread fear that massive global investments in AI infrastructure could cause an economic downturn. The DNB notes that the Dutch investment exposure here is around €13.5 billion (compared with global AI investment of around $1 trillion this year, according to Goldman Sachs).

While this amount is relatively limited, complex financial structures and the use of leverage (borrowing money to fund investments, which amplifies gains and losses) mean impacts can spread fast and are hard to predict.

Interest rates around the world have risen sharply in recent months, to their highest level since 2000, DNB said. That makes it more expensive for governments to borrow, and harder for countries that are already deep in debt to pay it off.

Governments also have less money to spare for a new crisis than they did during the coronavirus pandemic, the bank said.

DNB said banks, insurers and pension funds should keep investing in protection against cyberattacks and in back-up systems. They should also hold regular crisis drills with other key sectors such as energy and telecoms.

It also called for better crisis planning across Europe and closer ties between EU banking and investment markets, so companies can make more of opportunities such as AI. That, the bank said, will take “political will and courage”.

World.title: MPs vote to remove “remigration” from language of Dutch law
World.content:
Dutch MPs have voted to change the name of the Remigration Act to a more neutral term amid warnings that the term has become a rallying cry for far-right groups.

The law was passed in 1999 to allow benefits to be paid to migrants who return to their country of origin voluntarily, but no claims have been processed since the start of last year.

The English term is widely used on government websites such as the social security bank (SVB) that advise Dutch residents on how to claim benefits.

Security services have warned that “remigration” is increasingly by far-right political parties as a euphemism for enforced deportation.

“If extremist ideas and language are normalised and the boundaries shift, it can have implications for people’s safety,” the intelligence agency AIVD and anti-terrorism co-ordinator NCTV warned in a recent report.

The three coalition parties D66, VVD and CDA supported a motion by the left-wing opposition party Pro on Tuesday that would remove the word “remigration” from the name and text of the 1999 law.

Payments to Syrians

The right-wing party JA21 and independent MP Mona Keijzer tabled a motion calling for the government to start funding the payments again so the law could be reactivated, but the plan was voted down.

The VVD succeeded with a motion to offer Syrians a one-off payment of €10,000 to leave the country if they agree to return home voluntarily.

The government says large areas of Syria are safe to return to, even though the Dutch embassy in Damascus remains closed and the official travel advice says it is “too dangerous“ for visitors because of the “unpredictable” situation.

Parliament also passed a motion by the far-right PVV which would allow dual nationals to have their Dutch passport cancelled if they join proscribed organisations such as Al Qaida or Islamic State.

World.title: Prosecutors demand life sentence for Tarwekamp mastermind
World.content:
Prosecutors have called for a life sentence for the man accused of masterminding the Tarwekamp explosion in The Hague in 2024, which killed six people and collapsed a part of an apartment complex.

The public prosecution service (OM) told the district court on Tuesday that the defendant, Moshtag B., came up with the “insane plan” as revenge against his ex-girlfriend. He sought to blow up the bridal shop she ran on the ground floor of the building, it said.

The OM wants 30 years for Mourad ben T. (31), who they say carried out the attack, and 28 years for his cousin Ilias B. (31), who took part but didn’t come up with the plan. Adil A. (34) faces a possible four-year sentence because he was involved in the plan but pulled out beforehand.

According to the OM, the attack was planned for months in advance. The men allegedly looked up how flammable wedding dresses were and worked out in a group chat how to best burn the shop down. On the day, they used high-powered fireworks and around 175 litres of petrol.

The blast hit the Mariahoeve district at around 6.15am on December 7, 2024. Besides the six who were killed, it also injured five people and left a row of homes in ruins.

Three of the six people who died were from one family: a father (45), a mother (41) and their 17-year-old daughter. Their 8-year-old son was the only one of them pulled alive from the rubble. The others killed were two men aged 44 and 63, who also lived on the Tarwekamp, and a 31-year-old man from Voorburg who was staying with a friend in the building.

Within a fortnight, B. had been identified as the ex-partner of the shop’s owner. Broadcaster NOS reported that he was in London when the explosion happened.

At a pre-trial hearing in March last year, B. told judges he was “so unbelievably sorry”.

NOS said the four men barely reacted when the sentences were read out. Victims’ relatives were split: many thought the demands were tough, but some had hoped for heavier ones.

World.title: Amsterdam poverty rate double the national average, CBS says
World.content:

Amsterdam has the highest share of people living in poverty in any of the major cities in the Netherlands, according to new figures from national statistics office CBS, which also show over half a million people are below the bread line.

Some 6% of Amsterdam residents were classed as poor in 2025, double the national rate of 3%. The national figure was unchanged on 2024. The Hague (5.9%) and Rotterdam (5.6%) were close behind.

The CBS counts someone as poor if they do not have enough left to live on after paying fixed costs such as rent, energy and health insurance. Nationwide, 521,000 people fell below the line.

Only Vaals in Limburg had a higher rate than Amsterdam, at 6.4%. Tubbergen in Overijssel had the lowest, at 0.9%.

When Amsterdam first had the biggest share of poverty among big cities, its then poverty chief Marjolein Moorman said the figures ignore local support such as the Stadspas discount card and free laptops, Het Parool reported.

CBS economist Peter Hein van Mulligen told the paper that was possible, but that the effect is unknown because some other councils have similar schemes.

The figures more people might be missing out on that help. A third of people in poverty nationwide now live mainly on income from work.

Poverty among workers rose from 1.9% to 2.1%, driven by the self-employed. Freelancers (zzp’ers) without staff have a poverty rate of 4.3%, compared with 1.7% for employees.

“People with a job who live below the poverty line are often invisible to the council,” Van Mulligen told Het Parool.

World.title: Bosz says PSV were “trampled” after Real hit five in second half
World.content:
PSV and Feyenoord face an uphill task to reach the group stages of the Champions League after defeats on Tuesday night saw them drop out of the qualifying places.

PSV briefly threatened to cause an upset in Madrid as they took a 1-0 lead into the half-time break. Ivan Perisic’s penalty after 32 minutes was their only reward for a courageous first-half display in which Ruben van Bommel and Sven Mijnans also missed clear chances to score.

But the introduction of Jude Bellingham at half-time changed the picture as Real’s superstars regrouped to score five goals. The England midfielder’s dazzling volley was the pick of the bunch, while Kylian Mbappé bagged a double and Vinicius Junior also got on the scoresheet.

Head coach Peter Bosz admitted his team had been “trampled underfoot” in the second half. “I think you had to be there to see how big the difference was between the first and second half,” he said.

“In the first half we were brave, put our opponents under pressure and had three big chances in the first four minutes.

“When you look at the second half, they scored quickly and the tempo of their game was much higher. That’s the quality they have with the players they can bring off the bench.”

Feyenoord beaten

PSV’s next match is a home tie against Real’s city rivals Atletico on December 9, before they travel to Stavanger to take on Viking in January and round off the group stage at home to Stuttgart.

Feyenoord suffered a narrower defeat at home to Porto as they were unable to recover from an own goal after two minutes by Oussama Targhalline.

Goalkeeper Florian Kastenmeier vindicated the decision of Giovanni van Bronckhorst to replace the out-of-form Tjark Ernst by making some vital saves to keep the Rotterdammers in the game.

Feyenoord staged a late rally, with Gjivai Zechiël going close and Targhalline striking the crossbar from long range, but they were unable to breach the Portuguese side’s defence.

The fans in De Kuip were briefly celebrating after a bizarre incident when referee Irfan Peltjo’s watch told him a header by Nacho Ferri had crossed the line, but video replays clearly showed it bounced off the post and into the hands of Diogo Costa.

Feyenoord have just three points from their five matches so far, one less than PSV. Their next two matches are away to Viking on December 8 and Galatasaray on January 19, before they close their campaign in Rotterdam against RB Leipzig.

World.title: Appeal court rejects state bid to pause Bonaire climate ruling
World.content:
The Netherlands has to draft binding national targets, the Court of Appeal in The Hague has ruled, after the state requested a suspension of its obligation.

The ruling is another step in the Bonaire climate case, which was taken to court by Greenpeace on behalf of the residents of the Dutch island in the Caribbean, where climate change is destroying the coral reef.

That case was won in January, and the court found that the government in The Hague had acted in a discriminatory manner to its people there.

Part of the ruling was that the Netherlands must set binding emissions targets for the whole economy in law by July 28, 2027, as well as draw up an adaptation plan for Bonaire that can be implemented by 2030. The ruling must be carried out even while an appeal is under way.

The government appealed the ruling in April, requesting a suspension. The Court of Appeal has largely rejected that request, but said international air and maritime transport can be left out of the targets but the government must move otherwise forward.

Marieke Vellekoop, director of Greenpeace Netherlands, said in a reaction: “The state has once again been reminded of its responsibility. Executing the judgment is not a non-binding ambition, but an obligation.”

Vellekoop said it was “incomprehensible that the state is doing everything it can to delay climate action,” while the consequences of the climate crisis are becoming increasingly severe. “On Bonaire, but also here in Europe. The cabinet must stop delaying and get to work now.”

World.title: Erasmus MC head of intensive care steps down over safety report
World.content:
The head of intensive care at Rotterdam’s Erasmus Medical Centre, Diederik Gommers, has stepped down in the wake of a damning report into a “culture of fear” that potentially compromised the safety of staff and patients.

The healthcare inspectorate IGJ said the situation in the department, the largest in the Netherlands, amounted to “a serious threat to the safety of patients or care”.

Gommers, who became one of the public faces of the Netherlands’ coronavirus response in 2020 when he was a member of the government’s Outbreak Management Team, quit his post with immediate effect when the findings became known this week.

The department’s board of directors has been placed under heightened supervision after the report said the psychological safety of staff was compromised by a management that did not accept being challenged or criticised.

The Erasmus MC hospital said in a statement on its website that it accepted it should have recognised the warning signs and taken action sooner.

“We are sorry that some colleagues did not feel safe enough to voice their concerns. Everyone should feel free to express their views, challenge each other and share signs.”

The hospital added that there was no suggestion patients had received substandard care as a result of the problems in the department.

18-month investigation

Inspectors began investigating the ICU 18 months ago after a whistleblower raised concerns about the workplace culture.

NOS late-night news show Nieuwsuur and regional news channel Rijnmond said they had seen hundreds of internal emails and documents going back five years and spoken to 26 current and former staff about the situation.

Doctors said “tensions” between medical specialists deterred staff from speaking out if they were critical of or worried about their colleagues’ decisions.

Jan Maarten van den Berg, a former healthcare inspector who specialised in intensive care, told Nieuwsuur: “These conclusions are very severe. There needs to be a breakthrough in the situation at Erasmus for the sake of the patients.”

Nieuwsuur earlier reported that Gommers did not have the legally required qualifications to carry out medical research on patients. The hospital said Gommers had not done any clinical research since 2023 and had started studying to obtain his certificates.

World.title: Juice and milk bottles to join deposit scheme in 2027
World.content:
Dutch packaging trade association Verpact has announced it will begin a deposit return system for plastic juice and dairy bottles on its own initiative, according to broadcaster NOS.

Plastic juice and dairy bottles of up to three litres will carry a deposit (statiegeld) from next year. Verpact said it is preparing a phased rollout in 2027. Labels, return machines, IT systems and logistics will all have to be adjusted.

The move follows pressure from climate and green growth minister Stientje van Veldhoven, who wants 90% of plastic bottles sold in the Netherlands to be collected by January 1, 2028. According to NOS, that target cannot be met without juice and dairy bottles.

In September, Van Veldhoven proposed making deposits compulsory on all plastic bottles up to three litres and banning the sale of bottles and cans without a deposit.

Dairy bottles have so far been exempt because producers say they are hard to clean, and the minister has made hygiene measures a condition. Many juice producers already charge a deposit voluntarily.

Poland and the United States have signed an agreement on defence research, development, testing and evaluation, concluding 17 years of negotiations and opening the way for deeper technological cooperation. The agreement establishes a framework for joint defence projects, as well as the exchange of technical data and expertise, giving Poland – which is already a major importer of US arms – a formal role in the development of American defence technologies for the first time. Under Secretary Emil Michael (@USWREMichael) and Mr. Cezary Tomczyk, Poland’s Secretary of State at the Ministry of National Defence, signed the Agreement Between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Republic of Poland for Defense Research,… pic.twitter.com/7EAgK3nD2i — Department of War CTO (@DoWCTO) November 23, 2026 The agreement was signed at the Pentagon by Poland’s deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk and US under secretary of war for research and engineering Emil Michael. According to the Department of War, the deal will help “turn research and development into validated military capabilities to jointly support US and Polish warfighters”. Tomczyk said the agreement would allow Polish universities, research institutes and companies to participate in joint research and development work on defence technology with US partners and would enable such technologies to be tailored more closely to the requirements of the Polish armed forces. During a briefing in Washington, Tomczyk admitted that the agreement had been negotiated for what he described as a “probably record-breaking” 17 years, but he noted a “significant acceleration in relations” between the US and Poland over the last six months. General Marcin Górka, who oversees innovation in the Polish armed forces and accompanied Tomczyk to the United States, likewise welcomed the agreement, which he said would “open the doors to American military laboratories for our scientists and engineers”. Górka also said the agreement would enable Poland and the United States to jointly develop anti-drone systems and advanced drones, with testing taking place in both countries. Poland is a major importer of US military hardware. Between 2021 and 2025, it was the biggest overall importer of arms in NATO, with around 44% of that equipment coming from the US, including F-35 fighter jets, Abrams tanks, Patriot air defence systems and HIMARS rocket launchers. But Poland has recently sought to move from being a client of the US defence industry to more of a partner. Earlier this month, Polish defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth signed a declaration on expanding bilateral defence-industrial cooperation. Poland and the US have signed a statement of intent on strengthening defence industry cooperation. Polish defence minister @KosiniakKamysz said his country would be "the US ambassador in the EU", including seeking EU funds for jointly produced equipment https://t.co/SKHrxTEKIW — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 11, 2026 Last month, Poland was chosen as the location for a planned Patriot missile maintenance and servicing facility, the first of its kind outside the United States. In May, an agreement was signed to establish a centre in Poland for servicing the engines of Abrams tanks. This year, Polish state defence group PGZ was chosen as the first European producer of American Barracuda-500M cruise missiles, while US defence giant Northrop Grumman and Polish arms manufacturer Niewiadów-PGM announced plans to jointly produce artillery shells in Poland. Poland is also seeking to host a new permanent US military base, with Tomczyk reiterating during his Washington visit that a decision is expected from the Trump administration in early December. NATO has approved the deployment of an Airborne Warning and Control System to Poland in response to three Russian missiles striking Polish territory last week. Hours after the decision was announced, Poland’s airspace was again violated by a Russian drone https://t.co/gudQJsPlQ5 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 24, 2026 The new agreement on defence technology was signed amid heightened tensions with Russia. On Friday, three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles struck separate locations in southeastern Poland, near the Ukrainian border. Tomczyk said the Polish delegation had briefed Pentagon officials on the missile strikes, which he described as a “provocation” by Russia. The Polish minister was also asked about US President Donald Trump last week calling Russia’s Vladimir Putin his “friend”. “One thing is certain: Vladimir Putin is not our friend; he is a threat to us,” replied Tomczyk. “This is the most important message that should come from Poland and resonate with the people of the United States.” Subsequently, on Monday night, a Russian drone entered Polish airspace from Ukraine for a few minutes before turning back.
