NEW DELHI: India's national pavilion has won the Visitors' Lion for Best National Participation at the 61st Venice Art Biennale, marking a major international recognition for the country's contemporary art scene.The award was decided through votes cast by visitors from across the world, rather than by a traditional jury.Union minister for culture and tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat announced the achievement in a post on X on Wednesday, calling it a "moment of immense pride".He said the recognition reflected India's growing cultural influence and the international appeal of its artistic heritage."Under the visionary leadership of Hon'ble PM Shri Narendra Modi Ji, India's cultural and artistic heritage is receiving renewed global recognition, while contemporary Indian creativity is finding its rightful place on the world stage," Shekhawat said.The minister said India's national pavilion, titled 'Geographies of Distance: Remembering Home', was presented by the ministry of culture in collaboration with the Nita Mukesh Ambani cultural centre (NMACC) and serendipity arts.The pavilion showcased the works of five Indian artists, Alwar Balasubramaniam, Ranjani Shettar, Sumakshi Singh, Skarma Sonam Tashi and Asim Waqif.Shekhawat described the award as a testament to the talent of Indian artists and the vibrancy of the country's contemporary art scene.He said the recognition celebrated how India's traditional artistic heritage could find contemporary expression and resonate with audiences across the world.The recognition is particularly significant as India returned to the Venice Art Biennale after a gap of seven years, having last participated in 2019.The 61st edition, titled 'In Minor Keys', brought together 100 national participations and attracted over 7 lakh visitors.Shekhawat concluded his post with the slogan "Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi", saying the honour would inspire future generations of Indian artists to engage with the world with greater confidence and creativity.

World.title: Iranian delegation meets MEA officials to discuss multilateral ties
World.content:
NEW DELHI: An Iranian delegation met officials from the ministry of external affairs (MEA) in New Delhi on Wednesday to discuss multilateral cooperation under the framework of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA).

According to news agency ANI, the Iranian delegation was led by Alireza Tootonchian, director general for multilateral and International economic cooperation. He met Thelma John David, MEA joint secretary (Indo-Pacific), in the national capital. Both sides exchanged views on strengthening cooperation through the regional grouping.

In a post on X, the Iranian embassy in India said that Tootonchian and deputy director general Abolfazl Azizi Panah held discussions with David on multilateral cooperation under the IORA framework.



The meeting comes ahead of the 25th IORA Council of Ministers meeting, scheduled to take place in New Delhi on Friday. Foreign ministers from member countries are expected to attend the gathering to discuss regional cooperation and strategic priorities in the Indian Ocean Region.

India is also hosting the 29th IORA Committee of Senior Officials (CSO) meeting ahead of the ministerial gathering. The two-day meeting began on Wednesday.





The council of ministers is IORA's highest decision-making body and comprises foreign ministers of member states. It provides strategic and policy direction to the association, reviews progress in regional cooperation and identifies new areas of collaboration.

The committee of senior officials is the organisation's second-highest decision-making body. It comprises senior government representatives who oversee the implementation of ministerial decisions, review recommendations and coordinate IORA's work programmes.

Meanwhile, the European union (EU) and IORA held their first high-level roundtable on maritime security in New Delhi on Tuesday. Representatives from several Indian Ocean countries participated in discussions on improving maritime surveillance, tackling piracy and trafficking, and protecting important shipping routes.

The European union organised the event with support from its project 'Enhancing the EU's security cooperation in and with Asia and the Indo-Pacific' (ESIWA+) and in coordination with its Delegation to India.

Addressing the gathering, EU ambassador to India Jean-Eric Paquet reaffirmed the bloc's commitment to expanding security and defence cooperation with regional partners. He also stressed the importance of sharing information to tackle maritime threats.

Paquet said maritime security was a shared priority for the EU and IORA, adding that regional cooperation was essential to addressing maritime crime and other challenges at sea.

He also highlighted the Indian ocean's importance to global trade, warning that maritime insecurity could disrupt international supply chains and affect economic growth across the region.

Representatives from IORA member states and dialogue partners, including India, Australia, Sri Lanka, Kenya, Mauritius, Mozambique, Seychelles and Saudi Arabia, attended the roundtable.

The discussions also covered the European Union naval force's operation ATALANTA, which works to improve maritime security in the western Indian ocean and red sea. The operation focuses on deterring piracy, protecting vulnerable vessels and monitoring illegal maritime activities.

World.content:
The AIADMK, on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), issued an advisory to its office-bearers, district secretaries, spokespersons and party functionaries at all levels to obtain the party leadership’s approval before issuing press releases, giving interviews or expressing views on social media regarding party affairs and events.

The party’s advisory comes a few days after senior AIADMK leader and former Minister S.P. Velumani took to the social media to make certain remarks, in an apparent response to comments made by AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami to a question related to Mr. Velumani during an interaction with journalists.

World.title: BIM students excel at Global Capsim Challenge 2026
World.content:
Bharathidasan Institute of Management (BIM), Tiruchi, has secured the first place globally in CapsimCore and second place in Capstone at Global Capsim Challenge – Fall 2026, an international competition featuring business schools from around the world.

In the CapsimCore category, first-year MBA students A. Deevananth, V. Nakul, T.S. Srivatsan and S. Vignesh emerged as world champions with a score of 722.4. They finished ahead of the team from Bowling Green State University, USA, which secured the second place with a score of 655.6.

In the advanced Capstone category, second-year MBA students S. Adithyaa and P. Jerald Immanuel secured the second position globally with a score of 750.5. Bar-Ilan University, Israel, finished ahead of them with 751 marks, while the team from S.P. Jain Institute of Management and Research (SPJIMR), India, secured the third position with a score of 628.9.

BIM Tiruchi has consistently secured top global positions in both categories for the past three years.

Asit K. Barma, Professor and Director of BIM Tiruchi, in a press release, said business education should focus on enabling students to apply their knowledge in complex, unfamiliar and uncertain situations rather than merely imparting information.

He said the institute aimed to provide students with practical exposure to boardroom decision-making and help them understand the consequences of business decisions before taking up managerial responsibilities.

World.title: Drought threat looms over Keralam as 27 rainfall stations cross Trigger-1 drought threshold
World.content:
A drought vulnerability assessment conducted by the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) has revealed that 27 of the 59 rainfall monitoring stations for which the India Meteorological Department (IMD) provided long-term data have reached the ‘Trigger-1’ threshold, an indicator used for drought monitoring.

The worsening situation has necessitated the disaster management authority to hold a meeting based on the assessment that the State is likely to face a significant reduction in water availability during the upcoming summer, driven by the failure of both the southwest and northeast monsoons to deliver expected rainfall, compounded by the influence of the El Niño phenomenon in the Pacific. The agency also directed various departments to begin preparations and preventive measures to proactively address potential drought scenarios.

In 11 districts

The 27 stations that met the Trigger-1 conditions are spread across 11 districts—Kasaragod, Kannur, Wayanad, Kozhikode, Palakkad, Thrissur, Idukki, Alappuzha, Pathanamthitta, Kollam and Thiruvananthapuram as the State recorded rainfall deficits of 28% during the southwest monsoon and 26% during the northeast monsoon (up to November 21, 2026).

During the four-month southwest monsoon season, the State received 1,446.4 mm of rainfall against the normal of 2,001.1 mm, marking a deficit of 28%. The worst-affected districts were Wayanad (53% deficit), Idukki (46%), Kollam (38%), Alappuzha (32%), Palakkad (30%) and Thrissur (30% deficit).

The rainfall deficit during the ongoing northeast monsoon season stands at 26%, with the State receiving only 321.1 mm against the normal of 434.6 mm as of November 21, 2026. The rainfall deficiency in Ernakulam, Idukki, Kasaragod, Kollam, Malappuram and Thrissur ranged between 30% and 42%. The irregular rainfall pattern, characterised by short-duration spells interspersed with prolonged dry periods, has affected soil-moisture replenishment and groundwater recharge, resulting in poor inflows to reservoirs.

Water kiosks

The meeting, chaired by State Relief Commissioner, directed the departments concerned to revive water kiosks and, if necessary, utilise the VB-G RAM G (employment guarantee scheme) workers to set up additional kiosks. District Collectors were also asked to adopt the Kareepra model of quarry pond rejuvenation in Kottarakkara, Kollam, and utilise the restored waterbodies for agricultural purposes and local groundwater recharge.

The Water Resources department has been directed to ensure that sluice gates of barrages are repaired promptly, wherever necessary, to prevent water loss, while the Agriculture department will also prepare contingency plans at least at the block level, in convergence with VB-G RAM G, to address the emerging drought situation.

KSDMA Member-Secretary Sekhar Kuriakose told The Hindu that the authority was closely monitoring the situation and had completed the first round of drought assessment based on rainfall deviation, the Standardised Precipitation Index (SPI), and dry-spell analysis. The next stage of assessment (Trigger-2), scheduled to be completed by the end of this month, will incorporate remote-sensing indicators such as the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Normalised Difference Water Index (NDWI) and Vegetation Condition Index (VCI), along with crop conditions, soil moisture and hydrological indicators, (RSI, GWDI and SFDI). A detailed report will subsequently be submitted to the State government.

As per the prescribed procedure, the Trigger-2 assessment will be followed by ground truthing, involving field-level verification, to establish whether the features identified through satellite imagery correspond with actual conditions on the ground. This exercise was essential for enabling districts to access additional funds to tackle the emerging challenges, Mr. Kuriakose said. The evolving situation points to the possibility of early summer-like conditions setting in across Keralam as early as the end of January 2027.

World.title: Students educated on solid waste management
World.content:
Tiruchi Corporation organised an exposure visit for school students to educate them on solid waste management and the importance of environmental conservation.

During the visit, Corporation officials explained the importance of segregating waste into biodegradable and non-biodegradable categories. They also highlighted how proper waste management could help prevent environmental pollution and the role of students and the public in keeping the city clean.

The students visited the Corporation’s micro composting centres (MCCs), where they were given practical demonstrations on the processing of biodegradable waste and its conversion into organic manure. They were also briefed on the technologies used to convert waste into useful resources.

The initiative aimed to familiarise students with scientific waste management practices and encourage them to adopt waste segregation and responsible disposal habits at home and in their neighbourhoods.

They were also urged to spread awareness of environmental protection, among others.

Corporation Commissioner N. Ponmani said such initiatives would continue to be organised to create environmental awareness among students and the younger generation and encourage their participation in maintaining a clean and sustainable city

World.title: Brahmin scholars examine Big Temple premises
World.content:
A team of two Brahmin scholars inspected the ashtadhik balagar sannadhi at Sri Brahadeeswarar Temple, Thanjavur, popularly known as Big Temple, on Wednesday as a fall out of an order of the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court.

The team members, Sivasri K. Pitchai Sivachariyar of Pillaiyarpatti and Sivasri S. K. Raja Bhattar of Thiruparankundram, inspected the eight sannadhi of ashtadhik balagargal . There were no idols at ‘Indhiran’, ‘Yaman’, ‘Niruthi’ and ‘Guberan’ sannadhi., and the idols at other four sannadhi were damaged.

The inspection was sequel to the Madurai Bench’s direction in a 2019 case filed by Kaliyamoorthy of Thanjavur, Chinraj of Tuticorin and Azhagarsamy of Bhudhanendal, Ramanathapuram district, seeking directions to authorities managing the Big Temple to install new idols and replace the damaged ones.

After hearing the arguments, the Bench comprising Justice C. V. Karthikeyan and Justice R. Sakthivel in September this year directed the temple authorities to initiate steps for installation and replacement of idols at the eight sannadhi within three months from the date of issuance of the order and completion of the exercise within 12 months.

World.title: The Hindu’s coffee table book on exploration of the Western Ghats released
World.content:
The Hindu launched a coffee table book titled, ‘Mountains of Our Destiny: The Western Ghats, A Journey Through The Southern Monsoon Mountains’, on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Authored by Vrinda Ramanan and J. Ramanan, mountaineers, writers and photographers, the book was launched by Tamil Nadu Forests Minister R.V. Ranjith Kumar. The first copies were received by Rohit Ramesh, Director, Suresh Nambath, Editor, and L.V. Navaneeth, CEO, The Hindu. The book is a sequel to ‘Mountains of our Destiny: An Expedition to the Indian Himalaya’, also by the same authors.

Speaking on the occasion, the Minister noted the importance of the forests, rivers and mountains to sustaining agriculture, livelihoods and ecological balance. He highlighted the need to ensure forest conservation, spoke of the measures taken by the government to improve upon work being done, such as AI technology to prevent elephant deaths on railway tracks and in the control of forest fires, and congratulated the authors on their work.

Author J. Ramanan explained that the two mountain ranges: the Himalayas and the Western Ghats formed the bedrock of India’s existence. Without them, he said, we would not have had our rivers. The 1,500 km Western Ghats in particular, recognised as a biodiversity hotspot, was one of the richest ecological resources in the country, sustaining thousands of lives. The monsoon in India, Mr. Ramanan said, is shaped by the Western Ghats and the Himalayas. The book was an attempt to create awareness about, and educate people on the importance of maintaining ecological balance through their preservation.

Through more than 400 photographs, field experiences and narratives, the book explores the geology, wildlife, plants, indigenous communities and the intricate web of life that sustains these mountains. It also examines the growing pressures of plantations, invasive species, tourism, dams and other human interventions, highlighting the urgent need for conservation.

The book is available at The Hindu’s online bookstore: https://publications.thehindugroup.com/. The cover price of the book is ₹2,999. At present, the book is available at a special launch offer price of ₹2,249 for a limited period of time. Those interested can also scan the QR code to buy a copy.

World.title: Tamil Nadu’s water dispute with Karnataka: Palaniswami, Dhinakaran criticise TVK government
World.content:
AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) strongly criticised the Congress government in Karnataka for reportedly moving the Supreme Court seeking a stay on several irrigation projects that will impact Tamil Nadu, including the ambitious Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar river-linking project.

Mr. Palaniswami accused the Congress of consistently acting against Tamil Nadu’s interests and questioned whether the TVK government, which is aligned with the Congress, would take a firm stand to protect the State’s water rights. He recalled that the Cauvery-Gundar river-linking project was formulated during his tenure as Chief Minister under the AIADMK government.

Describing it as one of south India’s largest river-linking initiatives, he said its completion would significantly improve water availability for agriculture and help address water scarcity in several regions. Mr. Palaniswami also alleged that Karnataka had sought restrictions on several other Tamil Nadu irrigation projects.

Taking a swipe at Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, Mr. Palaniswami said the Karnataka government’s move reflected its perception that the Tamil Nadu administration was weak. He also criticised the government for not convening an all-party meeting despite his demand. He urged for initiating all possible legal measures to safeguard Tamil Nadu’s water resources.

Meanwhile, AMMK general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran urged the Tamil Nadu government to legally challenge Karnataka’s move seeking a ban on several irrigation projects being implemented across the State along the Cauvery. Citing a report published in The Hindu in this regard, Mr. Dhinakaran said Karnataka has approached the Supreme Court seeking to stall projects, including the Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar river-linking project and the Sarabanga lift irrigation scheme.

Accusing the TVK government of failing to protect Tamil Nadu’s water rights, Mr. Dhinakaran sought transparency on the funds allocated and work completed under the river-linking project.

World.title: At least 1 dead, 10 injured after under-construction building collapses near Karachi's Baloch Colony
World.content:
KARACHI: At least one person was killed and ten were injured on Wednesday after a six-storey under construction building collapsed near Karachi’s Baloch Colony, as rescue teams continued searching the rubble for people feared trapped.

A Rescue 1122 spokesperson said teams had recovered one body and rescued one person alive from the rubble. An urban search and rescue team was present at the site, the spokesperson added.

Emergency in-charge at the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC) Dr Irfan Siddiqi, told Dawn that 10 injured individuals were brought to the hospital. He added that nine were discharged after receiving first aid, while one was admitted for treatment and is now stable.

Meanwhile, Sindh Inspector General of Police Javed Alam Odho directed police officials to immediately reach the site of the building collapse and assist in rescue operations, according to a statement issued by the police spokesperson.

He directed officials to ensure close coordination with Rescue 1122, the fire brigade and other relevant agencies, and take necessary measures to secure the site, remove obstacles to rescue efforts and maintain the flow of traffic.

The IG also ordered that all available resources be used to rescue people potentially trapped under the rubble and that assistance be provided to ensure the injured receive immediate medical attention.

He directed the traffic police to clear roads, maintain an uninterrupted flow of traffic and make arrangements for alternative routes.

Relevant police officials were also instructed to personally supervise rescue operations and provide regular updates on the situation, the statement said.

SBCA planned to demolish building: Mayor Wahab

Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab, speaking to the media at the site, said that the Sindh Building Control Authority had planned to demolish the building previously; however, he said the authority had been unable to do so due to a stay order.

“If there had been no stay order, this building would have been demolished,” he said, underscoring the need to “exercise responsibility”.

“The portion mafia and corrupt elements have caused many losses to this city,” he said. Wahab also acknowledged that there was “political influence” behind the construction; however, he regretted that when the administration tried to take action, a stay order came from the court.

The Karachi mayor said that he would discuss the matter with the Sindh chief minister and local government minister.

“Strict action must be taken to prevent this in future.”

Sindh CM directs SBCA to examine possible negligence

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah also took notice of the incident and directed the relevant authorities to reach the incident site and expedite rescue operations, said a statement from the Chief Minister’s House.

The chief minister directed Rescue 1122, the district administration, police and other relevant agencies to coordinate and complete the rescue operation.

He ordered that all available resources be utilised to rescue people potentially trapped under the rubble, added the statement.

The chief minister also directed the authorities to ensure immediate medical assistance for the injured and make emergency arrangements at nearby hospitals. Hospital administrations were told to remain on alert and ensure that no negligence occurred in the treatment of the injured.

The statement also said the chief minister instructed the relevant authorities to immediately inspect nearby buildings for safety.

Murad said any potential risks posed by the collapsed building’s debris and the surrounding area should be assessed to ensure the protection of citizens’ lives and property.

The chief minister directed the Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA) to examine the building’s approved plans, construction standards and any possible negligence.

The administration was also ordered to determine the cause of the collapse and identify those responsible in case of negligence or illegal construction.

All relevant agencies were directed to ensure safety measures for buildings in a dilapidated condition, the statement said.

“Protecting the lives and property of citizens is the government’s top priority. No one can be allowed to put human lives at risk,” the chief minister said.

He also directed the Karachi commissioner and relevant agencies to continuously monitor the rescue operation and submit a detailed report on the building collapse.

President Asif Ali Zardari expressed sorrow at the incident and called for a comprehensive investigation to determine the cause of the building collapse, as per a statement issued by his office.

He added that the investigation should examine construction standards, building plans, and oversight provided by relevant authorities. He directed the Sindh government to take action against those responsible.

President Zardari directed all available resources to be utilised to recover individuals trapped under the rubble and accelerate the rescue operation. He also directed the best possible medical care for the injured.

He further instructed that a safety assessment should be carried out on the surrounding buildings.

“There is no room for any lapse in the discharge of duties by relevant institutions regarding the construction and safety of buildings,” the statement said.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also expressed sorrow at the building collapse and offered condolences to the bereaved family, Radio Pakistan reported.

He directed the authorities to ensure priority medical treatment for the injured, the report added.

Roof and building collapses are common across Pakistan, mainly because of poor safety standards and the use of shoddy construction materials. But Karachi, home to more than 20 million, is especially notorious for poor construction, illegal extensions, ageing infrastructure, overcrowding and lax enforcement of building regulations.

In September, five people were killed and two others injured when a wall of the dilapidated building of a government school collapsed on them in Orangi Town.

Earlier this year, at least 15 people, including women and children, were killed, and 18 others were injured after a gas explosion caused part of a residential building to collapse in Karachi’s Soldier Bazaar area.

World.title: ‘A new era begins’: Pakistan’s Zeeshan Ali enters new frontier as Shenzhou-24 docks with space station
World.content:
China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, carrying 40-year-old Pakistani astronaut Zeeshan Ali, successfully docked with the Tiangong space station three hours and 38 minutes after liftoff, the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) confirmed on Wednesday.

Ali became the first Pakistani astronaut to enter orbit after the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft successfully reached its preset orbit following liftoff from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre earlier today. And he is also the first foreign national to board the Tiangong space station.

A Long March 2-F rocket was used for the launch. It took off in a cloud of flames and smoke at 8:18am Beijing Time (5:18am Pakistan Time) under a pink sky, video from state broadcaster CCTV showed.

A send-off ceremony was also held for three astronauts who make up the mission’s crew at the launch centre before they entered the spacecraft capsule.

The spacecraft successfully separated from the carrier rocket roughly 10 minutes after lift-off and entered orbit, the CMSA said.

“The spacecraft is functioning well. I declare the Shenzhou-24 launch mission a complete success,” an official at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre announced.

90 experiments

China’s Tang Hongbo is commanding the mission, with Wu Yi serving as mission pilot and Ali as payload specialist.

Ali is expected to spend around a week in space, conducting various experiments alongside the Chinese crew. Pakistan’s space agency, Suparco, said Ali would conduct experiments in orbit, including cultivating microalgae as a potential food and oxygen source for future space missions, and testing the effects of spaceflight on quinoa seeds.

Meanwhile, the CMSA said the crew would conduct around 90 experiments during the mission.

The agency said the mission’s objectives included conducting an orbital rotation with the crew of the earlier Shenzhou-23 mission, carrying out routine operations and maintenance of the space station, and continuing space science research, including experiments involving space payloads.

‘Pakistan begins its journey beyond the stars’

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif congratulated the nation on astronaut Zeeshan Ali’s departure for the Tiangong space station aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 mission, saying Pakistan had begun its journey “beyond the stars”, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.

In a statement, the prime minister said the “journey was not just that of one astronaut but of 240 million Pakistanis, particularly the younger generation, scientists and their dreams”.

He said Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud had completed their training in China with hard work, discipline and dedication.

Shehbaz said Pakistan would become the first country after China to travel to the Tiangong space station, calling the development a reflection of the “ironclad friendship” between the two countries.

He thanked China for making Pakistan part of the historic mission, adding that the two countries were now working together not only for peace and development on Earth but also in space.

The prime minister also paid tribute to Suparco, universities and scientists involved in the scientific experiments being sent into space.

The premier said the combined efforts of the armed forces, national institutions, scientists and young people were helping Pakistan make progress in space research and advanced science.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar also congratulated the people of Pakistan and China on the successful launch of Shenzhou-24.

“This historic mission marks a significant milestone in our all-weather strategic cooperative partnership as we commemorate 75 years of diplomatic relations.”

“I thank President Xi Jinping and the Chinese leadership for their support and commend the teams of both countries for this achievement, which reflects our enduring friendship and commitment to the peaceful exploration of space,” he posted on X.

Dar said it was a “proud moment” for Pakistan, and this mission would inspire the country’s youth and advance its aspirations in science and technology.

“My best wishes to our astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and the Chinese crew for a safe journey and a successful mission,” he concluded.

The military leadership has congratulated the nation, the Suparco and the scientific community on the historic launch of Pakistan’s first astronaut to China’s Tiangong space station, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a press release.

Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf, Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu, and Commander National Strategic Command General Syed Aamer Raza extended felicitations on behalf of the Armed Forces of Pakistan.

The ISPR said the journey of Zeeshan Ali, Pakistan’s first astronaut and the first foreign astronaut to travel to the Chinese space station, marked a defining moment in the country’s scientific and technological advancement and was a source of immense pride for the nation.

The military leadership commended Suparco’s scientists, engineers and technical teams for their dedication, professionalism and sustained efforts in achieving the milestone.

It also appreciated the leadership, government and people of China for their support and cooperation in enabling Pakistan to achieve the milestone.

The ISPR said the friendship between Pakistan and China had reached new heights, extending beyond the frontiers of Earth into outer space.

It added that Pakistan’s entry into human spaceflight reflected the potential of its human capital, scientific ingenuity and technological capabilities, and would inspire future generations to pursue excellence in science, technology and innovation.

The armed forces also wished Zeeshan Ali success and a safe return to Earth.

Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, who is in China, witnessed the send-off and the mission’s launch.

Later, he posted on X: “As Shenzhou-24 lifts off this morning, Nov 25, carrying Zeeshan Ali, Pakistan’s first astronaut, a new era begins for Pakistan’s space programme. With him, the Pakistani flag rises into orbit, lifting the hopes and aspirations of 260 million Pakistanis for technological advancement and space exploration. From highways to information super highways to skyways, Pakistan-China friendship and CPEC rises higher than the skies.

“This is Pakistan’s URAAN (flight) into space, and it is only the beginning of a brighter and more glorious future.”

Zardari, Xi exchange letters

Meanwhile, the Presidency in Islamabad said in a statement that President Asif Ali Zardari had exchanged letters with his Chinese counterpart on the “landmark Pakistan-China space cooperation achievement”.

The statement said the two leaders congratulated each other on the “historic milestone in Pakistan-China space cooperation, marked by the first spaceflight of a Pakistani astronaut to China’s space station aboard the Shenzhou spacecraft, making him the first foreign astronaut to enter the Chinese space station”.

President Zardari extended felicitations to the government and people of China and expressed his “profound appreciation” for selecting Pakistan as the first foreign partner in China’s manned space programme, the statement said. It added that he further acknowledged the “invaluable support, professionalism and dedication” of the CMSA and the Astronaut Centre of China in making the collaboration possible.

President Zardari said the achievement “reflects China’s remarkable progress in space science and technology as well as its commitment to international cooperation in the peaceful exploration and use of outer space”.

He said the initiative embodied the “vision of building a community with a shared future for mankind, based on mutual progress, shared opportunities and collective advancement”.

He further wrote: “Pakistan takes immense pride in this historic achievement, which stands as another testament to the enduring friendship, mutual trust and close cooperation between the two countries.”

The president noted that collaboration between CMSA and Suparco had opened new avenues for bilateral cooperation in science, technology and space exploration.

He expressed confidence that the “achievement would inspire generations of young Pakistanis to pursue excellence in scientific research, innovation and technological advancement”.

In his letter, President Xi congratulated the government and people of Pakistan, the astronauts of both countries and their teams in the space industry.

President Xi said the astronauts from both countries “joining hands in the quest for the universe represents a living testament to their deep-rooted friendship and a new and significant outcome of bilateral cooperation”.

He noted that exploration was never-ending as the cosmos is boundless.

“The Chinese space station is an ark of peace, friendship and cooperation. China, together with [other] countries, including Pakistan, stands ready to hold high the banner of peaceful uses of outer space, deepen international space cooperation and improve global outer space governance, to ensure that outer space exploration delivers greater benefits to the humanity,” he added.

‘Carrying hopes of 250m Pakistanis’

In April, Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud were chosen from Pakistan to start training in China. Pakistan’s space agency Suparco and CMSA signed a cooperation agreement in February 2025, under which two Pakistanis were to train in China, with one joining a mission on the Tiangong space station operated by Beijing.

Eventually, Ali was chosen to join the Chinese mission.

Speaking at a press briefing in Jiayuguan on Tuesday, Ali said he was “deeply grateful” to the Chinese government for helping “us realise our dream of going into space”.

He said he arrived at the Astronaut Centre of China a few months ago, carrying with him the hopes of 250 million Pakistani people.

Ali said he believed that “what comes after this flight matters more than the flight itself”.

“This mission is not a finish line; it is a launch pad. And I hope the next chapter of China-Pakistan space cooperation will grow from one astronaut, one flight to multiple joint flights, to the Moon, Mars and beyond.”

Addressing Pakistanis, he said: “I now feel the true weight of the words of our Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, when he told me that we were about to write a new chapter in Pakistan’s history. I want to assure you that I am not flying for myself. I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulders, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis.

“To every child who is watching while I am in orbit, just look up at the sky and remember that I am up there with your dreams.”

In his message to his family, he said: “I want to say that I will travel farther from home than ever before. But I promise you one thing: whenever I look back at the Earth for the first time, I will always search for the light of our home before I look at anything else. No matter how far I fly, we will still share the same Moon, and I will still be looking back at the same Earth.”

Stay at Tiangong

China’s self-built station, named Tiangong or Celestial Palace in Chinese, has been fully operational since late 2022. It can host up to six astronauts during handovers when an arriving three-person crew overlaps with the departing crew.

This time, the handover will be different.

Shenzhou-23 commander Zhu Yangzhu ​will stay on to support Beijing’s study ​of how the human body copes ⁠in space — a crucial step towards a planned crewed mission to the moon and a potential journey to Mars. The rest of the Shenzhou-23 crew will depart Tiangong alongside Ali.

Zhu, who will stay for a year, will hold the record for the longest single ​stay in orbit by a Chinese astronaut by the time he leaves.

Beijing has poured billions into China’s space programme as it aims to land astronauts on the Moon before 2030, a race in which the United States is also competing with its Artemis programme.

Additional input from Reuters and AFP

World.title: £190m corruption case: Imran, Bushra's counsel says transaction caused no loss to exchequer
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: In the £190 million corruption case, counsel for PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, argued that the transaction had caused no loss to the national exchequer but had instead proved financially beneficial.

The couple is serving prison sentences in the £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case. On January 17, 2025, an accountability court in Islamabad sentenced Imran to 14 years in prison and Bushra to seven years in the case. Both subsequently challenged their convictions before the IHC.

The development came as the Islamabad High Court (IHC) resumed hearing appeals filed by Imran and Bushra against their convictions on Wednesday.

A division bench comprising IHC Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and Justice Muhammad Asif heard the appeals.

At the outset, Barrister Salman Safdar, counsel for the appellants, sought live streaming of the proceedings, arguing that the facility was available in courts across Pakistan and in other countries.

He said the request was aimed at ensuring transparency in a case involving matters of public importance. The counsel clarified that he was not seeking a telecast of the proceedings on Pakistan Television but wanted them to be live-streamed for public access.

Barrister Safdar pointed out that the trial had been conducted behind closed doors inside Adiala jail, arguing that open, live-streamed proceedings before the IHC would help address the lack of public access during the trial.

Justice Dogar observed that arguments concerning the May 9 incident and other general matters were irrelevant to the proceedings. He advised the counsel to focus on the pending application and the legal issues involved in the appeals.

Justice Dogar also pointed out that the IHC proceedings were already open to the public and that the courtroom was crowded.

When Barrister Safdar mentioned that Imran was 74 years old and incarcerated, the chief justice advised him to advance legal arguments rather than refer to general information about the appellant.

The counsel cited the case of former military ruler General (retd) Pervez Musharraf and read excerpts from Indian court judgments in support of his plea for live-streaming.

However, Justice Dogar observed that rules governing live-streaming were yet to be finalised and that the application could not be allowed at this stage.

Barrister Safdar requested the court to adjourn the application until the rules were framed, expressing hope that the matter would be resolved soon. He said that, as an advocate, he considered it appropriate to advance legal arguments even if the judge was initially reluctant to accept his request.

The chief justice observed that the conduct of proceedings was at the court’s discretion.

Arguing the main appeals, Barrister Safdar said the prosecution had produced 35 witnesses during the trial and Imran had been convicted under various provisions of the National Accountability Ordinance.

He elaborated that Imran was formally arrested in the case on November 13, 2023, while Bushra was convicted of abetment and arrested after her conviction.

The counsel pointed out that several individuals, including former accountability adviser Mirza Shahzad Akbar, property tycoon Malik Riaz, his son Ahmed Ali Riaz, Zulfikar Bukhari, Farhat Shahzadi and Ziaul Mustafa Nasim, had been declared absconders in the case.

Reading from the charge sheet, he said Akbar had produced a letter from the UK’s National Crime Agency (NCA) regarding the freezing of accounts belonging to Riaz and his family members.

He said the accounts had been frozen in three phases and maintained that the alleged financial benefits to Imran and Bushra had been extended before the accounts were frozen.

He also referred to the prosecution’s allegation that Bahria Town had extended financial benefits to Imran and Bushra through Bukhari in April 2019 under the guise of donations.

However, he pointed out that Riaz’s money had been frozen on August 12, 2019. Initially, the allegation against Imran was one of abetment, but Imran was subsequently made the principal accused, the counsel added.

According to the prosecution’s case, Imran allegedly approved the transfer of the frozen funds to an account maintained by the Supreme Court in violation of the Rules of Business. The funds were linked to Rs460 billion that Riaz was supposed to deposit in connection with the Bahria Town land dispute in Karachi.

Barrister Safdar argued that the amount had been transferred to the SC account even before the Federal Cabinet’s approval.

He alleged that Akbar and Nasim, both absconders in the case, had played a role in placing the relevant summary before the cabinet and facilitating the transfer.

The counsel further added that the prosecution’s case was that the amount should have been deposited with the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) rather than the apex court account to settle a civil liability.

Referring to the Al-Qadir University land transaction, he said the land had been transferred in January 2021. The prosecution had alleged that Riaz provided Rs285 million for the university’s building and furniture, but the amount was never transferred to Imran or Bushra’s personal accounts, the counsel argued.

The counsel said Imran was accused of chairing a cabinet meeting on December 3, 2019, and misleading its members into approving the transfer to benefit Riaz.

He maintained that the funds were deposited in the SC account and subsequently invested in profitable ventures, generating substantial returns.

“The amount remained with the Supreme Court for four years, and everyone knew about it,” he argued, adding that the funds had yielded significant profits.

Barrister Safdar further argued that Akbar had held multiple positions, including special assistant to the prime minister, chairman of the Assets Recovery Unit and adviser on accountability. He alleged that Akbar, in connivance with others, had played a key role in signing the confidentiality agreement that paved the way for the recovery of the frozen funds.

He contended that there was no evidence establishing Imran’s active knowledge of any alleged wrongdoing and that neither Imran nor Bushra had signed the confidentiality agreement.

He also questioned how Imran could have been aware of any alleged irregularities when the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) itself was part of the Assets Recovery Unit.

When Justice Dogar observed that the Assets Recovery Unit was an independent entity, Barrister Safdar responded that it comprised officials from NAB, the Federal Investigation Agency and SBP.

“If these officials were unaware of any wrongdoing, how could Imran Khan have known about it?” he questioned.

The counsel argued that the transaction did not cause any loss to the national exchequer, as the amount had remained within the banking system and had almost doubled through investments.

He maintained that the case could not be characterised as one involving a financial loss to the national exchequer, arguing instead that the transaction had generated profits. He also argued that the costly prosecution itself had burdened taxpayers.

Questioning the prosecution’s reliance on alleged collusion, he said the trial had concluded while several key suspects remained absent and had been declared absconders, raising questions about how the alleged conspiracy and connivance had been established.

Regarding Bushra, Barrister Safdar argued that she had no direct connection with the transaction and that neither the investigation nor the trial court’s judgment had clearly explained her specific role in the alleged offence.

He further contended that there was no evidence establishing that the money frozen in the United Kingdom represented proceeds of crime. If the funds were illicit or proceeds of crime, there could be legal consequences; otherwise, their owner was entitled to deal with the money at his discretion, he argued.

The counsel described both the reference and the charge sheet as vague, maintaining that the prosecution had failed to establish the essential ingredients of the offences against the appellants.

The court adjourned further hearings of the appeals until next week.

World.title: Rawalpindiz secure Matthew Short as direct signing; Hyderabad Kingsmen opt out
World.content:
Rawalpindiz have confirmed the signing of Australian all-rounder Matthew Short as their marquee direct signing for the 12th edition of the Pakistan Super League (PSL), which is scheduled to run from March 18 to May 2 next year.

The franchise announced the deal on Wednesday, with Short joining for a reported fee of Rs9.15 crore.

The 31-year-old, who captains Adelaide Strikers in the Big Bash League (BBL), becomes one of the highest-paid direct signings for the upcoming season.

A two-time BBL Player of the Tournament, Short is known for his aggressive top-order batting and useful right-arm off-spin.

Short has previously featured in the Indian Premier League, The Hundred and Major League Cricket.

He was selected by Islamabad United in the Platinum category for PSL 10 but was forced to miss the tournament due to a recurrence of an injury sustained during the ICC Champions Trophy 2025.

He will now make his PSL debut with the Rawalpindi-based side.

Under PCB regulations, each franchise is permitted one direct signing of a marquee player who did not appear in PSL 10 or PSL 11.

The player auction is scheduled for January 23 next year.

Meanwhile, Hyderabad Kingsmen have decided against utilising the direct-signing option for the upcoming season.

The franchise, in a post on X, confirmed they would focus on the auction and retention strategies instead of securing a high-profile overseas player through the pre-auction window.

Defending champions Peshawar Zalmi have yet to make an official announcement regarding their direct signing.

Reports have linked the side with England’s Ben Duckett, but no confirmation has been forthcoming from the franchise.

Other teams have already completed their direct signings, including New Zealand’s Matt Henry (Islamabad United), England’s Adil Rashid (Karachi Kings), Australia’s Lance Morris (Multan Sultans), Sri Lanka’s Kamindu Mendis (Lahore Qalandars) and New Zealand’s Lockie Ferguson (Quetta Gladiators).

World.title: PM approves NCCIA restructuring, orders overhaul of cybercrime prevention system
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday ordered the modernisation of the system to prevent cybercrime in the country and approved the restructuring of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA).

A meeting, presided over by the premier, was held to review the NCCIA’s performance, administrative structure and future strategy.

Speaking at the meeting, the prime minister said efforts to prevent and investigate cybercrime should be modernised in line with contemporary requirements.

“Protecting the public from cybercrime is among the government’s top priorities,” the prime minister said. “Restructuring of the NCCIA should be expedited to transform it into an effective, proactive and modern institution.”

The premier directed the appointment of information technology (IT) and artificial intelligence (AI) experts at the NCCIA and all its subordinate offices. “The NCCIA should recruit the best available workforce strictly on merit,” he said.

The prime minister said the agency’s restructuring should focus on the use of AI and modern technologies. He added that all available resources should be utilised to resolve pending cybercrime cases.

He also ordered the formation of a committee comprising Federal Ministers Mohsin Naqvi, Azam Nazeer Tarar, Muhammad Aurangzeb and Shaza Fatima Khawaja to review the reform proposals submitted by the NCCIA.

The committee will submit its recommendations to the prime minister by the end of this week.

The meeting was informed that a proposal had been made to transform the NCCIA into a national-level Pakistan Cyber Police, with recruitment based strictly on merit. A dedicated system for national security in relation to cybercrime has also become operational.

The meeting was further told that all possible measures were being taken under the existing system to resolve cybercrime cases.

The NCCIA’s performance, administrative structure and future strategy were also reviewed.

Federal Ministers Azam Nazeer Tarar, Musadik Malik, Ahsan Khan Cheema, Muhammad Aurangzeb and Mohsin Naqvi attended the meeting.

Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry, Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kiani and senior officials of relevant institutions were also present.

On Friday, NCCIA claimed to have uncovered an extensive alleged financial network involved in illegal online gambling, fraudulent business operations and suspected money laundering, with an estimated transaction exposure of up to Rs1 trillion.

Earlier this month, the agency called for stricter regulations governing company registration and bank account verification, warning that loopholes in the existing system are being exploited by illegal call centres, online betting operators and international fraud networks to launder money and defraud victims.

Earlier this month, Naqvi sought the premier’s help in addressing the acute shortage of staff in the NCCIA.

World.title: California grand jury indicts Meghan Markle's estranged father on child porn charges
World.content:
The estranged father of Meghan Markle, wife of Britain’s Prince Harry, was indicted by a California grand jury on Tuesday on two counts of possession of child pornography.

Thomas Markle, 82, who is already in custody in Florida after removing the ankle monitor that had been attached as a condition of house arrest, is expected to be arraigned in the United States District Court in Los Angeles in the coming weeks.

The indictment alleges that Markle had 35mm negatives showing child sexual abuse, including at least one image involving a prepubescent minor.

Court documents allege Markle had illegal photographs both in the Philippines, where he had previously lived, and in two rented storage facilities in Los Angeles.

Prosecutors said FBI agents seized dozens of images on slides, film negatives and in books, including two that appear to depict Markle with children who are either naked or in various states of undress.

A Florida judge this month ordered that Markle undergo a psychiatric examination after finding “reasonable cause to believe” that he was suffering from a condition “rendering him mentally incompetent to the extent that he is unable to understand the nature and consequences of the proceedings against him or to assist properly in his defence”.

Philippines seeks charges

Philippine authorities filed criminal complaints against Markle last week in Cebu, where he is said to have lived for over a year, regional prosecutor Graeme Elmido said.

Police recommended that Markle be charged with two counts of distributing child sexual abuse material and one count of possessing such material under Philippine law.

“The complaints will go through preliminary evaluation,” Elmido said.

“If the evidence warrants… a regular preliminary investigation subpoena will then be sent to Markle Sr to answer the charges.”

Markle’s legal troubles began in October when the British tabloid The Sun reported that his son, Thomas Markle Jr, had discovered child sex abuse images while going through boxes found in his father’s former home in the Philippines.

Markle had been living in Cebu until reportedly returning to the United States earlier this year.

Meghan Markle said last month that she was “deeply distressed” by accusations that her father possessed images of child sexual abuse.

She said she had blocked contact between him and her children over previous “troubling and disturbing” allegations.

Harry, the second son of King Charles III and estranged brother of the heir to the throne, Prince William, married Meghan, an American former actor, at Windsor Castle in May 2018.

The couple left Britain and quit royal duties in 2020 but made an unexpected return with their two children to live in the United Kingdom in August.

World.title: ADB okays $250m loan to strengthen Pakistan’s public-private partnership system
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Wednesday approved a $250 million policy-based loan to help Pakistan strengthen its public-private partnership (PPP) system and advance a pipeline of bankable and sustainable projects that can attract private capital and support the country’s economic growth.

In a statement, the Manila-based lending agency said the financing will support reforms to help the government prepare market-ready projects, particularly high-quality, cost-efficient infrastructure, and improve fiscal risk management.

“Rigorous project appraisal, transparent disclosure, and sound management of fiscal risks are essential to translate Pakistan’s PPP pipeline into sustainable infrastructure investment,” ADB Country Director for Pakistan Emma Fan was quoted as saying.

Fan added that the programme demonstrated ADB’s commitment to supporting the Pakistani government in strengthening public investment and financial management, improving infrastructure development, and mobilising greater private sector investment through PPPs.

The ‘Promoting Sustainable Public-Private Partnerships Programme’ builds on the first phase approved in 2024, which strengthened the legal and policy frameworks for PPPs, the statement said.

It added that under the second phase, the government had taken steps to bring federal PPP and privatisation functions together under a unified platform.

It said that the programme also supported dedicated PPP units in four line ministries and agencies and a national framework for monitoring and disclosing PPP-related fiscal liabilities.

With support from ADB, the government approved a medium-term PPP pipeline for 2026-2030, the statement said.

The ‘National PPP and Investment Knowledge Hub’ will provide training and tools to federal institutions, while provincial governments will also be able to benefit from its knowledge resources and peer learning activities, the statement added.

“The programme integrates inclusivity and resilience into PPP planning and procurement,” it said.

The programme is supported by $1.1 million in technical assistance from ADB’s Technical Assistance Special Fund and $950,000 from the Asia Pacific Project Preparation Facility.

“This support has strengthened institutional and project-preparation capacity for federal PPPs, including through professional certification, knowledge exchange, and the development of fiscal risk assessment tools,” the statement concluded.

On Monday, the ADB said it invested an undisclosed amount in Neem, a Pakistan-based B2B fintech company that helps businesses receive, manage, and pay out money digitally.

World.title: 'Let’s not blow it out of proportion': De Villiers urges cricket to move on from 'Sandpapergate'
World.content:
Former South Africa captain AB de Villiers said lessons must be learnt from the 2018 ball-tampering scandal involving Australia but urged the sport to move on from “Sandpapergate”.

The debate was reignited this year after Australia batter Usman Khawaja alleged in his book that knowledge of the plan to use sandpaper on the ball in the test series in South Africa extended beyond the three players who were punished, Cameron Bancroft, David Warner and Steve Smith.

“Let’s not blow it out of proportion. Let’s move on now. But also we need to take learning from that,” De Villiers told reporters during a virtual roundtable organised by Test Twenty20, a new format of cricket played across genders using both red and white balls.

“A mistake was made. We can’t hide from that fact. And I think it affects the whole cricketing world, not just Australia,” De Villiers said.

“We all want the game to be in a good position, right? But let’s remember these things have happened in the past as well and we found a way to move on.

“So let’s now move on and the youngsters take responsibility to bring great energy and great integrity into the game of cricket.”

Australia won the opening test in Durban before South Africa claimed the next three matches to seal a 3-1 series victory.

Reverse swing under threat

De Villiers scored an unbeaten century to guide South Africa to victory in the second test in Port Elizabeth and was at the crease when Bancroft was caught on camera using sandpaper on the ball during the third game in Cape Town.

“As long as the players don’t step over the line, we all know where that line is,” De Villiers said.

“Sometimes it’s a little bit grey, and that’s where the administrators come in. They need to clear it up completely and find a way for reverse swing to survive and still be around for many years to come.

“I feel it’s part and parcel of the game, and it’s great for the bowlers to have that. It really speeds the game up.”

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.

The suspended solar projects must also be revisited. A total of 31 solar power projects, with a combined capacity of more than 3,000 MW, were previously suspended or cancelled. Many were being developed by foreign investors, with more than USD 200 million reportedly already invested. If implemented, these projects could save around BDT 10,800 crore annually in energy import costs. They should be reassessed and revived quickly.

Energy storage is another missing pillar. Solar and wind need storage support to become more reliable. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and other storage systems should be reduced to zero. This will help stabilise renewable power and support future grid flexibility.

Electric vehicles can also become part of the solution. In China, Japan, and the United States, EVs are increasingly seen as mobile energy storage systems. A typical EV battery has a capacity of 40–70 kWh, enough to power an average household for 1–2 days. If Bangladesh had 1 million EVs, the country would have 40–70 GWh of distributed storage. This is several times higher than the daily peak demand gap. Solar-powered EV charging, vehicle-to-home, and vehicle-to-grid systems should be included in future energy planning.

If Bangladesh had 30–40 percent of the grid powered by solar, along with solar-powered EVs, the country would be far less exposed to global fuel market shocks. Long fuel lines, online schooling, shorter office hours, and industrial disruption could be reduced. Solar, storage, and EVs should now be planned together.

Finance will decide how fast this transition happens. Renewable energy projects cannot grow at interest rates below 10–12 percent. Long-term financing should be available at an interest rate of 3.5–4.5 percent. A 10–15-year financing facility at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent should be introduced. Bangladesh Bank’s green refinancing fund should be expanded. Rooftop and residential solar customers should be eligible for collateral-free loans. The LC margin for renewable equipment should be limited to 5%.

Net metering must be simplified. Approval should be completed within 15–30 days through a one-stop service. Approval, interconnection, inspection, billing adjustment, and utility coordination should all be simple and time-bound. Wheeling charges for renewable energy should also be kept reasonable and low. The Merchant Power Policy should be clear, simple, and investment-friendly so that industries and commercial consumers can directly procure renewable electricity.

Agriculture should also be included in the solar transition. Bangladesh can set a target to convert 1.5 million diesel irrigation pumps into solar pumps. This will reduce diesel imports, lower farmers’ production costs, and protect the environment. The program should include duty-free facilities, low-cost loans, investment support, and local service networks.

Waste-to-energy should also receive policy support. City corporations need clear rules, easy financing, and private-sector participation to enable urban waste management and distributed power generation to work together.

Bangladesh now needs a phased national roadmap for renewable energy.

In the short term, within 0–6 months, customs duty, VAT, and taxes on renewable energy equipment should be reduced to zero. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and energy storage should be withdrawn. Approval for net metering should be obtained within 15–30 days. Industrial and commercial solar installations should be eligible for special incentives. The 31 suspended solar projects should be reassessed. Wheeling charges should be rationalised. Solar, storage, and EV charging should receive urgent policy support. Collateral-free lines of credit should be introduced for rooftop solar. NBR should quickly implement assessment reform and a 0 percent duty.

In the medium term, within 1–3 years, renewable energy financing should be available at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent for 10–15 years. The LC margin should be limited to 5 percent. Land banks and grid infrastructure should be developed for utility-scale solar. Merchant Power Policy and MPPA should be simplified. Rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, and hybrid solar-storage projects should receive a 10–15-year tax holiday. A national program should convert 1.5 million diesel pumps into solar pumps. Rooftop solar should be made mandatory or incentive-based for government buildings, industrial zones, EPZs, economic zones, and large commercial buildings. EV solar charging and distributed storage policies should be developed. Renewable energy skill development and employment programs should also be launched.

In the long term, within 3–10 years, Bangladesh should aim to reach more than 10,000 MW of solar power by 2030. Offshore and onshore wind should be developed. Floating solar, river-based solar, and agrivoltaics should be implemented. A National Energy Storage Strategy should be prepared. Smart grid and power sector digitalisation should be accelerated. Local assembly and manufacturing of solar panels, inverters, mounting structures, battery packs, BMS, and EV charging equipment should be encouraged. Regional power trade should be expanded. The Renewable Purchase Obligation should be introduced. Fossil fuel subsidies should be gradually redirected to a renewable energy transition fund.

Image Visual: Anwar Sohel

The benefits can be large. Energy import costs will fall. Pressure on foreign currency reserves will decline. Industrial production costs will reduce. Export competitiveness will improve. The subsidy burden will decrease. New investment will grow. Renewable energy can create 20–25 jobs per MW through rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, solar pumps, EV charging, battery storage, smart grids, manufacturing, installation, operation, and maintenance.

The government may worry about revenue loss from tax and duty exemptions. But this should be seen as an investment. In the short term, there may be a limited impact on revenue. In the long term, Bangladesh can save far more by reducing fuel imports, lowering subsidies, saving foreign currency, strengthening industries, and attracting new investment.

Bangladesh’s energy crisis is a major challenge but also a historic opportunity. The crisis is not only a supply problem. It is a policy framework problem. Renewable energy, especially solar power, storage, and EV integration, can be among the most practical solutions for the country.

The question is no longer whether Bangladesh should adopt renewable energy. The real question is how quickly, how systematically, and how boldly the country can complete this transition.



Mohammad Ataur Rahman Sarker is a renewable energy entrepreneur and the secretary of the Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association.

Md. Tanvir Siraj is a renewable energy researcher.

World.title: The forgotten art of Bengali advertising
World.content:
I have never seen someone at a rustic village market, anklets jingling, shouting slogans for "Khol Company’s Ringworm Ointment." No smooth-talker has ever leaned in, fanning out thin booklets like a deck of cards, whispering rhythmically, "Here are the mysteries of Gopal Bhar, and here—the secret love letters."

I never hid colourful s of a reclining Gauhar Jaan, cigarette in hand, between the folds of shirts in my drawer. I did indeed rummage through my grandfather’s pockets to collect old tram tickets, but none of them bore that curious notice for "Ashtavakra Toothpowder." Perhaps the elders of the house witnessed a tram tearing through the heart of a half-awake city, bearing the Khadi Pratisthan’s pledge for cow protection—but there was no question of me witnessing such a sight.

An iconic early 20th-century  for Bukhsh Ellahie & Co., featuring classical maestro Gauhar Jaan holding a cigarette to promote their brand

Someone’s great-grandfather might have known which drummers came beating the kara and nakara to announce, "Tonight at seven, the Chaitanya-lila folk play commences." I never heard the name of a young "lad" like Dhiren Bal, who reportedly painted the  for "Himkalyan Hair Oil" at a three-way junction in Dinajpur.

While searching the Panjika (almanac) for the auspicious moment of a wedding, I never had the chance to chuckle at the suggestive illustrations for "Libido-Enhancing Tablets." On a morning shortly after Mahatma Gandhi’s assassination, I didn't sit with a newspaper wondering which artist, known only as "Munshi," had used swirling brushstrokes to sketch a portrait as a final tribute on behalf of some bankrupt cotton mill.

I saw none of this because I hadn't been born yet. Most of those who witnessed it are now gone forever. Yet, even without being born in that era, I have managed to 'see' it all. The old, withered newspapers and digital archives acted like Alibaba’s cave, revealing to me a lost jewelry box.
